in recent years i've been fearful of cleveland clinic due to past bad experiences. i'm glad i took a leap of faith to try cleveland clinic fl a try again.  the improvements they made has recaptured my confidence and trust in cleveland clinic.  i would recommend cleveland clinic to anyone and you can be sure they have the best doctors and specialist you can find.

tl;dr:  mt sinai's er doctors refused to provide me with care for excruciating pain and as a result i nearly lost my life to sepsis. months after this experience, i finally have the presence of mind to post this review as a warning to others.

i visited this er at the urging of my doctor, who is affiliated with mt sinai. he feared that i might have an infection in my spine and wanted me to have some imaging and blood tests done because they didn't feel it could wait until the next week. my partner drove me to the er and we were seen very quickly - it was very quiet and we could only see 3 or 4 patients with relatively mild issues. we met with a resident, erik sherman, who did not listen to my situation at all, saying flatly that there wasn't much they could do for back pain. we asked again for an mri and the resident said "well, mris are very expensive and you might be waiting for hours," and my partner replied that our insurance would absolutely cover it and that we were fine with waiting as long as needed. 

my partner asked to speak with the attending, bess storch, and we again explained the entire situation and serious concerns our doctor had that led him to us to the er. dr. storch repeated that they were unable to do imaging and that i should follow up next week because this was "an in-office case."when she left the room, my husband called my doctor's answering service, yelled for the attending to come back, and he handed her his phone and begged her to speak with him. my doctor confirmed everything we had told them, and asked for the same tests we had asked for. begrudgingly, the attending allowed me to have an x-ray only.

we waited for a few hours for the x-ray and by the time they wheeled me back (i couldn't walk) a nurse came and said they had already discharged me. we waited for another 2 + hours and then we were handed the imaging report, which showed that i had a compression fracture on one of the vertebrae in my upper back. they said it was common and not a concern so we just left, completely demoralized and just happy to be out of there after more than 8 hours. a few days later, i was taken to another er by ambulance and was diagnosed with sepsis caused by a severe infection and an abscess that was pushing against my spine so hard that it caused a fracture. i needed emergency surgery and i spent months recovering inpatient. if mt sinai's er doctors had just listened to us and run tests, we might have known about the abscess sooner and my life would not have been put in extreme jeopardy. i nearly died. you should all be ashamed to call yourselves doctors.

review:
i have a love hate relationship with kaiser. the doctors here generally have good bedside manner and getting tests done is quick, much faster than ucsf and other hospitals because everything is done internally. it's like the walmart of hospitals... although there is a lot of convenience, just like walmart, there are some bad sides. 

getting real medical help for complex and unusual problems will send you to the grave... possibly. i've been to the er so many times and seen a variety of doctors for my atypical symptoms. because i keep getting new conditions on top of another, my doctors keep thinking i'm coming back with the same problem and have put me under chronic pain. 

i had to do my own research and i know that's a doctors worst nightmare because i don't have a md. but i am not ignorant (i only research at trusted sources like pubmed and i have an education in dissecting research papers). i am the only one who can advocate for my health. and found that i had to push for very specific tests before getting anywhere.

for privacy reasons i will not name specifically the tests i pushed for but i was extremely lucky after being rejected by three specialists. my fourth specialist agreed to the test and we found my symptoms 100% matched up with what the test showed. such a rarity, statistically speaking getting 100% on any test, the odds of that happening is almost nil. 

that's not the end of it. recently i've been struggling new symptoms and because of my history all my doctors yet again though quick and courteous, would not and was firm about avoiding getting referrals. i did see a specialist but that specialist is now putting a foot on the ground about no referrals to a surgeon who could potentially help me. my new diagnosis is something that is atypical and from what i researched, every scholarly sources mention that although surgery comes with risk, with this condition you don't want to delay as it drops remission probability to low numbers. i get that my doctor is worried about surgery but if it is something that is needed to fix the root problem, i have no idea why i'm constantly rejected for a referral. at least a consultation would be helpful but my doctor nipped that prospect out.

i'm considering seeing a specialist outside of kaiser but i know they will never cover my outside referral if i go out on my own accord. i can't even afford the surgery on my own but i'm hoping if i see a outside doctor who can vouch for surgery, maybe just maybe kaiser will agree to cover and do surgery within their network.

i'm currently writing this in the recovery room, having just delivered my second baby (first one with el camino, first was with ucsf in the city). i just wanted to use this moment to rave about my experience this time around compared to ucsf.

from triage to l&d to recovery, all the doctors and nurses here are by far the most experienced, kind, knowledgeable and kind people i have ever met. due to covid i never got a chance to do a hospital tour, so i had no idea what to expect when i checked in 2 nights ago after laboring for 24h at home.

at triage i was greeted by nurse melissa, who checked me and i hadn't progressed enough to be admitted. instead of just sending me home, she asked me to walk the hallway for 1h to see if it'll speed things up. and it did, i went from 3cm to 5cm during that hour and was admitted right after.

the rest of the nursing team were all super pleasant, knowledgeable and explained every little thing to me without me having to ask. there's a really positive energy and rapport between the nurses so it carries through the whole bedside manner. my iv drip at ucsf last time was a traumatic experience, they couldn't find my vein and blood kept spurting everywhere. this time at el camino, they had a nurse who specialized in iv insertion and she did it painlessly and perfectly in one to without any blood. 

i knew i wanted an epidural this time, and instead of dictating to me when i should get it, they told me to tell them whenever i wanted it. i decided to walk for another hour before asking for the epidural. now let's talk a bit about the epidural. i had dr. k (forget the full name) and he was so good. no pain, super calm, and the meds took effect almost immediately. with ucsf i was in so much pain and the injection didn't even work the first time, i had to wait 2h for the anesthesiologist to come back to up my dosage. this time, the dosage was perfect because i had no pain but eventually i could feel the pressure as i was nearing 10cm. i could move my legs and could feel the pressure of contractions so my pushing was super effective. i'm told this is the perfect dosage and that the doctor is really good.

now onto the pushing phase. at ucsf (since it's a teaching hospital) there were 10+ people in the room while i was pushing. some were helping while others were just spectating. this time, i had one nurse stay with me the whole time helping me push, and once it got to a certain point she called my ob and she came and took it to the finish line. hardly tore, got 2 stitches and no hemorrhages. i tore second degree and hemorrhaged pretty badly with my first.

once baby was here, they moved us to the mother & baby section. since the epidural wore off rather quickly i was able to pee way faster than with my first, and the nurses in recovery were all super nice and accommodating. i also had a fabulous lactation consultant help me with breastfeeding, who really gave me the most helpful pointers that i never got with my first. when i was at ucsf with my first, i had a lot of pain in latching and the lc there told me that nothing was wrong and a "little" pain is normal. basically made me feel like a wuss. turned out my firstborn had a tongue tie and lip tie but i didn't get that diagnosed til she was already 3mo. of course by then my breastfeeding journey was already a hot mess and did not go well at all. the lc at el camino (stacey was her name) took her time to teach me how to latch and basically said that proper breastfeeding should never hurt. after 30min of training i was able to find a good latch and now my baby is breastfeeding really well. night and day.

anyways, i just wanted to take the time to give credit to an incredible group of staff. it's seriously night and day to my experience at ucsf and i wouldn't have known unless i had something to compare against. 

thank you for such a pleasant birthing experience. i never knew i would ever use "pleasant" to describe labor and delivery.

this place does not want you to get better. they only want to make money, and it's obvious at every level of care.

it started when i was encouraged into going in to "learn about the programs" in a very normal setting, but then as i told them the full extent of my depression which included suicidal ideation (but not plans) i realized that they tricked me into involuntarily staying there and my life was about to get a *whole* lot worse.

but maybe it was fine because there was individual therapy there right? no. absolutely none. the only thing close to therapy is a group session where you check in and no matter how badly you need help the therapist just smiles and nods. they don't even put all the mental health patients together, i was one of the only ones in a mostly substance abuse program, so i had trouble relating to everyone else. you never get any real help, the whole place is just a giant waiting room for the psychiatrist who only sees you for a few minutes a day, barely cares about your situation, and prescribes everyone the same medication no matter what, but you have to beg constantly to let you leave.

i should also mention that if you're stuck there involuntarily or ever sign out they place you on a 72-hour hold (business days btw, for weekends you're out of luck), and they lie to you about what happens afterwards. they say it doesn't matter anyways because they'll file for probate at the end of the period and you'll probably be out before the court hearing anyways. that's completely wrong... i learned later that they rarely ever do this. so that's another waste of 5 days because they straight up lied to me.

they keep everyone way longer than they should and the only reason anyone gets "better" here is you practically have to pretend you get better or they'll never let you go. i was kept an extra 3 days after i met all my treatment goals just to try a new adhd medication. a completely non essential purpose. have i mentioned they don't value your time one bit?

now onto the outpatient partial hospitalization program, which i told them i would go to only so i wasn't stuck for another week. a complete waste of time and every minute was excruciatingly boring. the "therapists" only read off a paper the whole time of really basic information. any actual input from the patients was met with, you guessed it, a smile and nod and no actual therapy. my depression actually got worse during this time because i was forced into such an upsetting, non-helpful environment. oh yeah and they kept me several days longer than they said they would...

outpatient psychiatry: i really should've left the hospital altogether at this point, but here i still was, going in to see dr. rahman. as time went on it became painfully obvious he doesn't care about helping you improve. i would go in and talk about how my meds are doing nothing for me and all he'd do is slightly increase the dose. he won't ever refer treatments that actually do something different like ketamine, and i wouldn't dare mention any suicidal ideation in these appointments in case they try to trap me here again.

bottom line: run. very far away. go to the lindner center, or literally anywhere else. this is the worst mental health facility i've ever had the displeasure of dealing with, and i've dealt with a lot. they do not care about helping you one bit.

  eight times the normal level  is anything besides a "little wonky" especially after telling her that my symptoms had gotten progressively worse over the previous 48 hour period and i was worried as i was leaving for college in less than12 days.  not being a doctor, and never being told just how "wonky" my lab results really were, i unfortunately trusted the doctor and followed the doctor's directive to go home not knowing any other option and not realizing i could object and that she was just "practicing" medicine.  if i had not been discharged and would have been admitted and started on iv antibiotics that day, i am certain that i would not have had to suffer another two days at home hoping that what the er doctor prescribed was going to eventually help, when in fact it did not and i was back at the er on 2 days later, to then be admitted and be charged yet again!  it was my primary doctor's office that called my mom to check on me on monday and was appalled that i was sent home with the lab results that they saw.  my primary called and talked to the head of the er and i was told to immediately return to rch to be admitted and stayed for 2  1/2 days on multiple iv doses of antibiotics.   i had no problem having to pay my $575 co-pay from when i was admitted but then i received another bill for my first er co-pay another $250 which would not have had to be paid if i was admitted the first day as i should have been.

review:
i just woke up from a ptsd nightmare from some staff cauding me a panic attack, and then when i went in with my counselor they told me i wouldn't get in trouble. i was threatened with detention, state sanctioned child hostage taking, for being late to school. 

i was convinced i was being gaslit. i had a huge panic attack and they kept telling me to breathe. while i'm literally screaming for them to stop. screaming to go home. i ended up running outside terrified crying. i watched criminal minds and this was like being unsubbed, or held captive by the bad guy. 

i now have nightmares because their staff doesn't understand what no means? i was dissociating after being told i shouldn't be late again. i would be fainting from exhaustion every day in school trying to not be late. it was torture. when someone tells me i'll be punished for not forcing my body to do what it can't, it is the stuff of horror films. then they made it worse, how can i believe i won't get in trouble when all my life has been being punished.

they must have some sort of assembly line protocol there, because i don't know why they believe instilling a sense of being held captive benefits anyone. i said i was afraid of dogs, they put me with a blind woman with a helper dog. i have nothing against people with disabilities, but really? it's not an uncommon fear right? 

i just don't want anyone else having to wake up in fear because when they go to get help, they're met with the exact psychological abuse that required them to need help.

i also remembered the person telling me during a panic attack i wasn't a survivor. my father held me a prisoner to his anxiety about me growing up. he wanted me to stay a forever child so badly he had me misdiagnosed as autistic. i had nowhere to go, because i could only have "safe" friends. to take that from someone, to tell them they haven't suffered enough to be a survivor. well that's why i self harmed in school. mental health shouldn't be a matter of how much you suffered, just that you're suffering. 

to gaslight someone and say the abuse they endured was insignificant. why would they hire someone so cruel? and i'm used to it. what if the next person tries to end their life? after all every time they turn for help they're told your pain is meaningless.

review:
i've lost all faith in doctors. my brother is in icu in this hospital right now and has been since last friday. he has cirrhosis of the liver, kidney issues and diabetes. he spent a day at home in bed with a stomach ache and the next day woke weak, disoriented and confused. the ambulance was called and he ended up here. not sure what protocol is...if it's to start completely over as if they have no history about the patient or what. we were told by one of his nurses, we're treating him for his current issue not all of his historical issues. to not consider his historical issues (which are actually current issues) and how they are impacting his immediate health is plain stupid. they can't seem to figure out why he's unresponsive. maybe it's because his liver is shutting down. and, be straight up with the family. if the prognosis isn't good, say it instead of making us try to guess what is going on. there have been multiple "we think it's this, it looks like it might be that, it could be this...." he's been tested for everything from cocaine to hiv. from what i see, everything points to his liver shutting down. i'm not a doctor and if anyone can add any insight i'd really appreciate it. i'm very emotional right now because my brother is going to die. if not in this hospital, it will be soon in hospice. and, it seems like precious days were spent focusing on needless tests while today the nurse advised they didn't do any blood tests?? i would think platelet counts, ammonia levels in his blood, and many other things in his blood should be monitored closely. unless the medical staff is at the point where it's not worth monitoring anymore. and, if that's the case, they should tell us instead of making us wonder why they are a bunch of idiots!!!

not to mention, we just found out he had cirrhosis a couple months ago. my brother gets his blood check every two weeks, has been in and out of the hospital over the last few years, and sees multiple doctors regularly. 

in fact, he was in this same hospital last october and they couldn't figure out what was wrong with him. a liver test was done at that time but it was "unremarkable." so apparently not the correct type of test to show if there was any liver damage and they didn't dig any deeper. 

my sister has gone to most of his appointments with him and he provided her with access to his medical records. this most likely is not something that developed overnight so you tell me...how did no one figure out he had cirrhosis sooner?

they've always done right by me whenever i've gone here for medical care. last month when i broke my wrist, the nurses took good care of me. the same applies to the doctors, i've always found them to have good bedside manner and care about their patients. the only suggestion i would make for improvement is their billing practices, sometimes it's very confusing the way everything is itemized on your bill including your insurance company payouts. the people in the billing department were okay, not necessarily rude, but not as helpful as the doctors and nurses. but overall, this is a good hospital to receive care at. i've been to both here and nearby saint francis, both are pretty good. but for some reason, i'm more preferential to hartford hospital, mostly because i feel like their technology is more up to date. plus, also let me give a big congratulations to one of the nurses there, i think her name was like tori or toby... or something like that, anyways she was super helpful and made me laugh a lot when i was in pain after my wrist surgery. so yeah, that's all i really have to say, but i like this hospital and would recommend them. oh yeah... let me not forget to mention they are doing a great job of keeping everything sterile, especially during the covid-19 pandemic. maybe some would consider it a bit 'overkill' how strict their policies are regarding cleanliness, and quarantine and sanitation... especially in how they limit hospital visitors into your room when you're being treated. however, honestly wouldn't we all rather be safe than sorry...

a really great hospital!!! located close to downtown stamford, this hospital is essential to the surrounding community. you can tell it's brand new and that there was a lot of thought put into the design of the floors. there is a conference room on each floor for the staff to use. a few rooms have extra private rooms for family to stay overnight in and keep youthe company. the views from the windows overlooking the rest of stamford are breathtaking. 

the entrances can be confusing as the er entrance is on one side and the main entrance along with valet parking are on the other side. 

the cafeteria is actually the most confusing place to find i'm this hospital because it is located in what used to be the "old" hospital so unless you have been there many times before you can get lost. the easiest place to get food while in the new hospital is from the cafe downstairs in the lobby, freshii's, located right next to the gift shop.

the staff is very friendly and patient and this is a great hospital to be a patient at!

if you have a choice, pick another hospital. i lived a block away from the stamford hospital and when it came time to choose a place to give birth i drove 20 minutes farther to a different hospital because i was terrified that i would receive poor service at the stamford hospital.

i went to the er at the stamford hospital with stomach pains. it took a while but they finally thought that i might have an abnormal presentation of appendicitis. they told me they were going to check it out laparoscopically and if they were right they would take out my appendix. the surgery itself went well but it took hours for me to get my question answered of "did i have appendicitis?" and "did they remove my appendix." hours. many nurses and many residents later they finally tracked someone down that knew what surgery had been performed on me. then i was discharged with the instructions to make an appointment to see my surgeon in a week's time to verify that i was doing okay and my stitches were healing. and also to discuss pain management. great in theory, but i never got the name of my doctor and when i called to make an appointment per the hospital's instructions, i kept getting routed to a bunch of operating services. i finally just gave up and went to my primary physician.

my husband had his own issues with the stamford hospital that made us regret that we hadn't driven the 20 minutes to be seen at a different hospital. when giving us part of my husband's diagnosis, it was done as a "drive-by" by a resident that had thought the doctor had come it to talk to us already. when he realized he was breaking news to us for the first time he apologized and ran out, leaving us bewildered and worried, waiting for hours for my husband's doctor to stop by and give us further information.

it seems like they are just really bad at communication. having three hospital stays at two different hospitals after my experience at the stamford hospital, i now realize just how important communication between hospital staff and their patients are and how much better other hospitals are at providing timely and accurate information.

yesterday i was seen in the er for potential appendicitis, the hospital staff was very efficient upon my arrival all procedures were taken for my safety as well as theirs. i had the pleasure of being treated by lp vanie mangal let me just say she was amazing from start to finish. i never had the pleasure of meeting the nurse assigned to me but vanie mangal made sure i was completely taken care of. thank you vanie mangal you are truly 1 in a million

the er, with breathtaking negligence, almost killed me. i'd wanted to write the administration at the time but was experiencing a major illness so could not. another recent reviewer stated the er's decline has been recent but no, this happened back in mid august 2014, so it's been going on a long time. so im writing yelp, at this point im sure the administration is well aware of their own problems, my letter i'm confident would have fallen on deaf ears anyway 

   i had a large tablet lodge in my throat at home when i tried to swallow it, and barely had an airway. it was like trying to breathe through a coffee swizzle stick.  i was losing oxygen, and seeing glimmering floaters in my vision and couldn't feel my fingertips. and was starting to pass out. luckily i am an rn myself and am very good at handling emergency situations, and through the grace of god, managed to keep a cool head. 

  i knew i didn't have time to wait for an ambulance, and after failed self heimlich attempts, signaled my friend with my hands to grab her car to drive me directly to the er. as i was reflexively trying to cough and breathe, the tablet shifted to a spot where it completely blocked my airway, and i fell to all fours and almost passed out in the driveway. luckily it shifted back to the "swizzle stick" position, but then just continued to alternate between swizzle stick and complete obstruction. 

  "fortunately " i made it to the er. my friend drove straight up to the front of the building and burst through the doors with me in tow, explaining that i was choking and didn't have an airway. 

   i was handed a clipboard, "please fill out this paperwork (asking for name, address, insurance info etc)."  i desperately wrote "cant breathe - pill" in jagged, panicked handwriting and pointed (as in "please let me go there") to the er patient area behind her.  "no, we can't help you until you fill out the paperwork."

  at this point an rn walked behind the desk, and i showed him my note, and pointed to the door that lead into the patient area with the most imploring look of my life, and he begrudgingly let me in. 

  he told me he was going to take me to a room and let me wait there.  afraid to be left alone and knowing i needed immediate attention or could die, i grabbed his upper arm. i didn't think it was too tight, just really really scared and urgent. he immediately spun on his heels and reprimanded me like a 4 yr old, "no no no! do not touch me like that, or i won't be able to help you. you are still breathing mam, you can wait until we're ready for you." 

  i tried one more note in the presence of an aide, who looked at me pie eyed because he got what was happening. but he was too low on the totem pole, and his own attempt to say anything to the additional nursing staff outside was ineffective, and i was left alone. 

  realizing that the only thing that was going to get them to respond was my impending cyanotic collapse, i decided to try and help my own self one last time (because even at that point, by the time they perked up and eventually intubated me - if they could even handle that - i would have sustained permanent anoxic brain damage, if i survived it at all). all by myself, i found an empty gurney. the guard rails were at a better height apparently than the chair i used at home, and after another round of heimlich attempts, the tablet flew out (along with blood - the tablet was a prescribed digestive enzyme, and after such an extended amount of time, had started to dissolve and "digest" my throat). 

  their response still blows my mind. day 1 of nursing school, we're taught our "abc's", where "a" stands for "airway", the number one thing in need of protection to keep someone alive. for pete's sake, 16 yr old lifeguards are taught this. 

   shaken, the anger now starting to kick in now that i wasn't wholly absorbed with saving my own life, i walked straight back out of the double doors.  "i'm leaving now, it's out - thanks for nothing!!!!" as the nurses' station, full of qualified staff standing behind the counters doing god knows what, looked back at me with slightly confused but mainly empty, "just another day" stares. 

   i shudder at the number of people that must have died at this er's hands. i think of all the poor family members who have been told, "i'm sorry, we did all we could."  so i'm writing this yelp review to let you know - they didn't.  avoid this er at all costs.

*** edit: in case this makes a difference, i did also write in my note to the multiple staff "airway obstructing". i couldn't have been any clearer. from one er rn to another, what was happening was virtually mapped out to them in written form, since they couldn't see, or refused to see, what was happening in front of their own eyes

so why the low rating? once we had her moved to telemetry, the hospitalist was abusive screaming at me instead of giving facts or letting me check with the experts that i needed to verify risk versus reward in what was being requested. i fired her. then i got the grim reaper dr. binesh. he spoke fatalistically and pushed hospice on us when we didn't have a terminal diagnosis. when we said we didn't want it, he also sped up discharge to less than 24 hours but notified us on a saturday evening when we couldn't get in home care set up because it was after business hours. i had expressed to them that my mom's wishes was after she was stable enough, her transition goal was to be cared for at home. when my mom was able to talk she told the doctor that she wanted to go home as her next step. so why weren't they helping us?

this review is for the birthing center at sequoia hospital. like several other yelpers here, i too, had a wonderful experience delivering my baby at the birthing center a few weeks ago.

leading up to the birth, sequoia gave us all the information we needed. we attended a helpful orientation one month before the birth, and pre-registered ourselves so the hospital knew our due date and when to generally expect us. 

i began labor two days past due, and gave sequoia a call at 2am to let them know that i thought i was in labor. they were clear, calm, and provided instructions on coming to the hospital, where to park, etc. 

as soon as we got to the hospital, we were greeted and they had very short paperwork for me ready. after a few quick forms, they got me into a room and checked out a few things. once it was confirmed that i needed to stay, they got me settled into the room and we finished up the paperwork.

i'll spare readers my long birth story, but the major takeaways were-- sequoia has amazing nurses. literally, the best. i was at the hospital for a total of 96 hours and had several different nurses (they work in shifts of 12 hours each). each nurse was extremely well trained and highly competent in their respective area. i felt very well taken care of and appreciate that each nurse that clocked in took the time to read my birth plan and get familiar with my wishes. a special shout out to nurse ute who was my nurse during delivery. after a long and frustrating time laboring slowly, ute started her shift by instilling the confidence in me to have a baby that day. sure enough, my baby was delivered just as ute's shift was ending... and she stayed with me the whole time i was in labor.

sequoia also has fantastic doctors. my regular obgyn was out of the office during my delivery, but the other on-call doctors, dr. kassis (who delivered my baby and was super encouraging) and dr. rao, were absolutely fantastic. the anesthesiologist, dr. bradley, was also extremely skilled and delivered my epidural quickly and efficiently.

lastly, sequoia gave me everything i needed to take care of myself and my baby when i got home. as a first time mother, i had no idea what i needed to take care of myself. in the blur of labor, i didn't realize that sequoia had packed several bags of "after care" materials for me. it wasn't until i got home, i realized sequoia had given me everything i needed to heal at home.

thank you to all the nurses, doctors, cleaning staff, culinary staff, and others at sequoia for making this a memorable experience.

i had a negative experience at the er. i had never been to sequoia or used dignity health before, and *only* came here because it was the closest hospital near where i was. i came in with some of the most frightening symptoms of my entire life, that i had never experienced before, and that were horrifying. could not breathe. body was going numb. lightheaded and dizzy. felt like i was going to pass out. 

as soon as i got there, the doctor labeled me as an "anxiety" patient right away, upon my arrival, even before any tests were done. he even said things to me like "you are agitated and argumentative just like my other anxiety patients" all while i was frantic about not being able to breathe and was begging for help. i couldn't believe he called me those words; i was going through such an awful experience, he could have been more empathetic. the doctor seemed irritated that i was there, and discriminated against me using this label, as if having "anxiety" was my fault, that i could control what was happening to me, or as if these physical symptoms were not 100% real. 

so during my er visit they ran several blood tests and the doctor gave me ativan eventually. the ativan did help a little bit to calm me down, but my symptoms were still there (i had been having them for about a week). the doctor came in and was adamant that i had to see a psychiatrist. his tone in telling me this was condescending and rude. he made all of symptoms out to be a mental illness, and i 100% know that they are not. perhaps having these ongoing symptoms for an extended period of time resulted in anxiety, but this is not all due to anxiety. i was trying to explain my core symptoms to him - but he kept interrupting me. he treated me like i was not worthy of his time, like i was some sort of drug addict looking for pills (in this case just a human being looking for a diagnosis). 

the er doctor made it sound like i just hop around from er to er wasting everyone's time, even asking me "how many times have you been going to er's for your anxiety" and "when was the last time you went to the er for your anxiety" and trying to reprimand me and shame me for going to the er. well guess what, i don't regularly go to the er. i went one time recently, in the prior week, when all of this started, for similar symptoms. but that's it. and nobody at that time said anything about it being anxiety. they actually encouraged me to go back to the er if i didn't feel better...which is what i was doing! 

so bottom line i left the er after about an hour with the same underlying symptoms that i had and have been having for over a week now. it has been several days and i have the same symptoms 24/7 but they have gotten worse. i'm fatigued and out of breath. i can't even fold my laundry without taking naps every 10 minutes. i am very athletic and in shape but can barely walk without wheezing and gasping for air. 

i feel traumatized now that i was shamed for going to the er, and labeled and treated as an "anxiety patient". i know something is wrong with my body right now. i have a serious chronic health condition already, and i went through years of symptoms where doctors like this one labeled me as an anxiety patient. i was told that everything was anxiety. well, it wasn't. the doctor was quick to judge and overconfident in his diagnosis (after seeing me for such a short period of time). if its not a heart attack or a blood clot then...it's...anxiety? no, not in all cases.

the doctor that initially encouraged me to go to the er said to go to stanford. she never mentioned this hospital, even though it is closer to where i live. now i know why.

edit: i spoke with a psychiatrist who urged me to get medical attention. he said he could only prescribe me medication to calm me down as a result of my stress in having to deal with this, but my core symptoms are not due to anxiety. i am working with my doctor to figure out what this is. it could be gi related, heart related, or lung related. so, nope, not anxiety. it causes anxiety, but my severe ongoing shortness of breath from the last couple of weeks is due to something else. the er doctor at sequoia hospital refused to listen to or believe any of my symptoms. my doctor was pretty shocked when i told her what happened there.

review:
if i could give this facility a negative 10 star rating, i would! this hospital may give one the illusion of excellence because of its name, but it is anything but excellent!  

the negligence that is occurring at this facility that is "committed to providing you with the highest quality of treatment and support" is downright disgraceful!  they have no respect for patients or family wishes, and actively prevent families from being proactive with the care of loved ones.

our family's story as briefly as possible:  my 79 yr. old father fell at home and fractured his hip.  he was taken via ambulance to our small town local hospital.  of course, during these times of covid, none of his family were permitted to be with him.  he has quite a list comorbidities, so our small town hospital deemed his situation too critical to treat.    they recommended we transfer him to hmc for surgery, post surgery care and then on to a rehab facility.  to say we were relieved was an understatement but unfortunately, that feeling left quicker than it came.  our father was taken into surgery without notifying any of his 6 daughters, 2 of which are his medical poa's.  the first call one of the poa's received was that our father was out of surgery, he did fairly well, but his bp was critically low so he would spend the night in icu.  oh, and by the way, can you complete these consent forms with me!  yes, if you're following, this was after surgery, not before.  this was unsettling but fortunately, it wasn't "another type of notification call" and we just wanted to start the road to recovery.  well, i'll spare you all the emotional, in between details, but basically our dad laid in a hospital bed incoherent and non-responsive from thursday until the next tuesday when we had him transferred to another hospital!  i can't even describe the fear, frustration, and heartbreak my siblings and i endured during these 5 days.  we couldn't see him.  we couldn't talk to him.  to say we were living in hell is not an exaggeration!  we fell apart every time our phone rang thinking it was going to be "the call"!   and if this stress level wasn't enough, hmc has the absolute worst staff i've ever experienced in hospital care.  the nurses are incompetent, lack compassion and are plain unprofessional!  we were lied to, repeatedly, hung up on repeatedly, (yes, you read that correctly) and told by one nurse carly, "i'm at lunch right now, i can't help you"!  after staying in icu for 2 days, he was transferred to a step down floor.  we asked if we could facetime with him.  when they finally "found an ipad", we were told it only had 18% battery so not sure how long it would last.  then a person who announced to us she wasn't his nurse, laid it on his stomach and walked out.  he was so weak and disoriented, he couldn't hold it so we couldn't see him.  we tried talking to him over facetime but if he tried to speak, we couldn't understand him.  between 6 of us, we are rarely speechless or unable to come up with some type of solution; but there is a first time for everything.   we tried begging, pleading, crying, and yelling to get care for our father but we were hung up on, ignored and dismissed; all while he continued to lay in a bed deteriorating.  the doctor experience wasn't any better and the patient-care advocate/liaison, who is supposed to advocate for the patient, basically declined to address the matter and began "circling the wagons" once we told them we were initiating a transfer.  when they heard this, they then tried to threaten and scare us that a transfer would be a lateral move so insurance would likely not pay for his stay and we'd be responsible for over $200,000 in medical bills!  well, if the man laying in the bed wasn't practically comatose and able to communicate, he would reply, oh, the hell you say, just try to get blood out of this turnip!  i sincerely hope that another human never has to suffer the way my father and my siblings and i have over the last 5 days.  i'm so thankful that 3 of my sisters are nurses and knew he would not last much longer with this substandard care.  we advocated every minute of those 5 days to get get my dad transferred.  my heart hurts for those patients who do not have 6 relentless daughters in their corner as advocates!

you can do better than this hospital. i delivered my baby here in jan 2020. he's my first child, so i don't have other experiences to compare this one to. while i generally had decent care, there were many things about inova alexandria that were not as advertised, and as a result, we struggled on a few fronts. 

first, they actively advertise that they provide nitrous oxide to laboring mothers. this was one of the reasons i chose this hospital. they do not. i was already well into labor by the time i was told that there was no nitrous available at the hospital. i had mentioned this several times prior, had discussed it with my physician/midwife practice (who exclusively delivers at inova alexandria), and it was in my birth plan-- no one thought to tell me that there was no nitrous until go time. 

second, once i decided to get an epidural (given that there was no nitrous and i'd been induced a long time prior), the anesthesiologist clearly messed up as he was setting it up. to the point where he apologized to my doula-- not to me or my husband mind you. thank god i didn't end up with something terrible happening on that front. 

third, since i was induced, i was in the hospital for longer than expected before delivery. they had the most uncomfortable bed known to man. i got no sleep, and both my husband and i went into the delivery completely exhausted as a result. birth plan basically went out the window. 

fourth, this hospital prides itself on breastfeeding support. it's everywhere on the walls, the literature, you name it. but guess what-- their support is lousy. i had to request help multiple times. it got to the point where i had to beg the head nurse to ask a lactation consultant to sit with me and make sure he was latching. breastfeeding is hard regardless- but at a "baby friendly" hospital where they tell you about their fabulous lactation support, and i did literally everything in my power to flag that there was a problem and i was struggling, they failed me. i saw at least four different lactation consultants. there was a lot of happy talk, but very little practical help. when it wasn't working, they couldn't help me, and i left the hospital basically hopeless. i had to hire a lactation consultant to come to my house the next day and by that point my baby was a big fan of formula. 

fifth- as it turns out, part of the reason breastfeeding didn't work for me was b/c i had severe postpartum preeclampsia that went undiagnosed while in recovery, even though we spent extra days at the hospital because my son had jaundice. my body was busy trying to keep me from stroking out rather than producing milk. thank god i was told by a midwife to make an appt within 48 hours of discharge to have my blood pressure checked. i might very well have died in my sleep otherwise. 

sixth, i had the worst experience with a nurse of my life there. one particular nurse insisted on drawing blood from my days old son in the most painful way possible while he screamed as i've never heard a baby scream before. she was ignorant, ill-trained, and thinking of her to this day makes me furious. other blood draws were a breeze compared to this because they were done properly and he never screamed again. she clearly had no idea what she was doing. 

seventh, my baby had jaundice and they did a terrible job of giving you any option but to have a giant, drafty, old school light machine wheeled into your room so that you- in a hospital with trained staff and having had no sleep in days- have to make sure that a tiny baby who cannot have a blanket doesn't take off the thin fabric that protects his eyesight, etc. it was awful. 

eighth, there is not really a nursery here. they make this clear on the tour, but you might want a hospital with a decent nursery. what they have is makeshift, drafty, and not appropriate for proper care. 

ninth, they literally never let you sleep. i'm not talking about the baby keeping you up. they come to check vitals constantly at all times of the day even when there's a do not disturb sign up. we went home having not slept in basically five nights, which led to a nightmare scenario for a brand new family of three. despite all of this checking, they still didn't catch that my body was shutting down. maybe that wasn't possible to do-- but it is notable that i kept alerting nurses to classic preeclampsia symptoms and i was repeatedly told that those were normal after having been pumped with fluids during labor.

tenth, i left never wanting to come back to this place ever again. it was a miserable experience despite the fact that there were some staff who were helpful and tried their best. unfortunately, i had to go back to their er two days later because they had all of my recent birth records and health history on file. here's where they actually saved my life, and i had a generally good experience with excellent staff- save for the lactation consultant who was horrible, insulting, and should be fired.

this review is not about the care for my loved one, but about the protection of his identity and personal belonging while in the care of inova alexandria hospital. my brother was admitted and went straight to icu on a ventilator from the emergency department. his friend was with him and asked for his wallet that included his identification, medical cards, money and precious memories, his cellphone and his keys. since she is not his wife or family member, the ed nurse would not give them to her. there is video of the nurse giving his bag to a security guard. the story told to our family is that guard put the bag down as he was called away and another came behind him and threw my brother's personal belongings in the trash. over a 23 day period, i spoke with the icu nurse, patient relations, icu unit director, left a message for emergency room director, emergency room manager, head of security, security director, back to patient relations and ed manager. i left messages with the admin asst. for dr. rina bansal, president of alexandria hospital as well as the admin for john gaul, chief general counsel for the hospital to receive no return call. 

patient relations and the ed manager were the chosen ones to deal with me by finally requesting we provide an itemized summary and cost for replacing my brother's personal items, offered us $100, 1 year of identity theft protection and provided a "memo" with someone who had not been involved with this issue as the point of contact. this memo is to be used as supporting documentation for trying to obtain hard copies of the items they threw away. they agreed to give us copies of the cards on file, but provide no additional assistance. my nephew who is my brothers "legal next of kin" is expected to pay for these items and submit an invoice while he is unemployed and caring for his family during the covid-19 pandemic. to make matters worse they will then issue a check in my brother's name. he asked for a final settlement using a good faith estimate so that our family can move on and focus solely on the care for my brother which has not been responded to. he has gotten no acknowledgement or response to his email. 

i could go on and on, but i think you can get the message that inova alexandria hospital has taken no real responsibility in their negligence and failure to fully protect my brother while he was in their care. they continue to demonstrated the utmost disrespect to my brother and our family at such a crucial time in the world. 

let me end by saying my brother is no longer at that hospital and as expected, patient relations has gone silent as it pertains to this issue.

review: i took my dad to the er here 2 years ago because we believed he was having a stroke (which he did). as we were waiting for results from the dr., a male intern randomly walks in and starts asking my dad, who's still in shock, questions about how his stroke started and then started rambling about how it's probably not even a stroke but the test results will be ready soon. i instantly interrupted the male intern and told him that my dad is still in shock and that he can't really speak in-depth the english language so he can ask me any questions and i'll be happy to answer. the male intern automatically assumed and called us vietnamese and asked why he doesn't know how to speak english. i was definitely surprised by this statement and explained to him that we're not vietnamese, we're hmong and so on... the male intern then pushed the side panels on the bed down ( what prevents patients on the bed from falling off) and makes my dad get up for no apparent reason and then tells him to just lay back down.  after telling my dad to lay back down, the male intern didn't even put the side panels back up to prevent my dad from possibly falling. he then walks out and i never saw him again. my family and i felt like this male intern definitely violated safety hazards towards the patient, he was being very stereotypical and prejudice and disrespectful. overall, i did not appreciate this man's attitude, presence, and awful statements towards my father and my family. as a minority, i've never personally experienced racial and discriminating actions from others, especially in a healthcare facility where we're emotionally distressed and my dad is sick, which really put me in shock and blurred out some of the things that i should have done in the moment. for instance, i should have gotten this male intern's full name and reported him, as well as telling others at the hospital of this incident at that specific moment. nonetheless, i do not recommend this place at all. it sucks because sheboygan is a small city where only 2 hospitals exist and hshs st. nicholas is one of them.

whomever you have as an "operator" is completely rude and careless. answers the phone as "hello", then as you are trying to get your message across so she can help you find your daughter who just got admitted to er and is now in a room, she rudely interrupts to ask "what's the last name" the transfers. this is the kind of person you hire to assist people whose family or friend is admitted at this hospital? unbelievable. i didn't get her name but i will tell you that i just called at 2:46 pm today, 3/18/20. pathetic & terrible service! deserves a serious conversation from her supervisor. if i could rate her a double zero i would. it's unfortunate that the hospital itself earned only a 1 star due to her. i bet no one monitors their reviews, so this is for reviewers to be aware. however - when i head over there today i will go out of my way to find out who their supervisor is!!!

review:
due to covid19 i had my eyes set on delivering at queen of the valley hospital originally since it was a whole separate building. eventually i changed obgyns and this became my delivery hospital. it is one of the best things to happen.
labor and delivery has always been amazing to me. went several times for monitoring due to a risky pregnancy. every time we went i was treated wonderfully and had all my fears put at ease.

i'm very disappointed with the er medical staff at mercy gilbert. i've heard all great things about them. however when i was checked in at this hospital on tuesday, march 24, i had a completely different experience. 

it all started when i was told by the covid 19 hotline, that i could go to the banner urgent care on higley, to get tested. i waited a good hour before getting called back. (no it wasn't busy) appointment was @ 11:30, i checkin 11:15, called by 12:16pm. once i entered the back room, my legs gave out on me and i ended up collapsing. the nurse helped me to the room and onto the bed. at this point my fever was 102.6 and my body started to have convulsions. the banner urgent care called 911 and i was sent to this hospital. i wasn't tested  for covid 19 with banner urgent care.

we quickly arrived (which felt like forever) and i was taken to a room where i was met by er dr. kent first,  then by nurse rene a little later. and i was asked again the same list of questions from each. i just wanted to pop my head off from body at this point because the pain was so unbearable.

dr. kent became very short with me and slightly raised her voice and seemed very irritated because i wanted to know about getting tested for covid 19 (which the next day my doctor now tested me and i was indeed positive). she was so concerned about state regulations and not admitting me to the hospital, that she sent me home with antibiotics after my xrays showed i had  community-acquired pneumonia and i was told i could return back to work after 3 days if symptoms improved. and when she told me about the pneumonia, dr. kent stood by the curtain and quickly walked away. really?!?

i recently reported monterey park hospital to the joint commission, the agency that accredits hospitals. i had many reasons, but here's a snapshot: 

 my mother was released from monterey park hospital on 5/24/2020. i just received the discharge summary today, june 2, 2020.
 a typical discharge summary is written with 24-48 hours of a patient's release because the information contained in it will be vital to the patient's aftercare. time, therefore, is of the essence.
 to obtain the ds (and address other concerns) for my 87-year-old mother, i had to write many emails--all unanswered--and in the final one, threaten to get "legal representation" to force the hospital to release a ds.
 my mother's attending physician explained the delay by stating that he had been on vacation. he also complained that he hadn't had a vacation in ten years, and that he and his wife had planned one for march/april, but those plans had fallen through.
 he further explained that when a doctor takes a vacation, he is allowed additional time to write a ds, which sounded to me like a bad excuse for turning your homework in late. 
 no provisions or safeguards are made for patients at monterey park hospital whose doctors go on vacation. my mother's attending physician insisted that the task of writing a ds could not be assigned to another doctor.
 the day after her discharge, my mother went to the emergency room due to pain from a leaking catheter. we had no idea why she had been catheterized in the first place. discharge papers from monterey park hospital did not explain the catheter, so emergency room workers were reluctant to remove it. a ds would have been helpful in that moment. a ds was also the first thing my mother's primary care doctor asked for when we took her in for follow-up care four days after her release from monterey park hospital. however, we had none to offer.
if the ds debacle were the only issue with monterey park hospital, i wouldn't be writing this review. however, there's more, which is why i contacted ericka smith, the coo, to alert her to the many wrong things that occurred during my mother's 5-day stay. but ericka smith was completely unresponsive. completely. she didn't even acknowledge that she had received my emails. she is either indifferent, incompetent, or reflexively anticipates lawsuits and stays silent as a matter of protecting herself.
leadership is reflected in the good and bad practices of any institution, so i don't think my mother's situation was an outlier, or the problem with monterey park hospital is due to individual "bad apples." i think the problems are systemic, and leadership is mute. this is why i alerted the joint commission. when lives are at stake--as my mother's was, and still is--a hospital can't be allowed to operate in this way.

review:
my husband was diagnosed with parkinsons and we have been so thankful for the excellent service that we have received from the va family.

from office staff, to nursing, to the doctors, each person has truly cared about my husband and the best way to treat his disability.

there were no knee-jerk decisions to just throw medication at him. they performed a dat scan and had him meet with the movement specialist. 

although the diagnosis was not what we were wanting to hear, it was so nice to finally know what was going on. 

he has been on meds now for about two months.  the difference is truly night and day.

we know that the disease will continue to evolve but we're thankful that the va will be there with us.

i am proud of the men and women who have served and i'm glad that there is a place that values them for what they have done.

review:
2 different experiences at this er. fyi, i have now changed my insurance due to these experiences.

first experience:
back in january i was sick and had a high fever. i usually do not go to the hospital unless it's an emergency, so i stayed home and tried to treat myself. however, my fever did not get better and i started to get bad headaches, chills and couldn't keep anything down. i finally decided to go to the er when my body started to feel numb. i couldn't feel my face, my fingers or feet. i was in so much pain, i had to have a neighbor drive me. i arrive at the er with a very high fever and my body hurt so much (it's hard to describe, i've never felt anything like it). the nurse tells me to calm down and tells me i'm having a panic attack. i wanted to tell her that i've never had a panic attack in my life and my body has been in pain for about 3 hours. what they did was give me an iv and some medicine. my temperature was still high, but they told me to go home and rest. which i understand, there's nothing you can do at this point. 

later that day i ended up coming back and getting treated again by someone else. that rn actually did listen to me and helped me. 

second experience:
came to the er because i passed out at home after work. i came into the er and they checked my vitals. my bp was lower than usual and my heart rate was high. i thought it was weird and i tried to ask them more questions about why this happened and they told me it was due to work fatigue (i had 12 hr shifts). i knew that wasn't the reason; however, the md and rns didn't want to listen to me. they sent me home with some meds and told me to rest. 

the next couple of days was brutal. i couldn't go to work bc i had no energy and i wasn't myself. the next week i pass out again and go back to them. i get checked by someone else and i have the same low bp and high heart rate. i then get an ultrasound of my abdomen and it turns out my stomach was bleeding. i was so mad that i was left untreated for a week bc they did not want to listen to me. 

1 star is for the rn and md who actually helped me and made sure i was taken care of. 

if you come to this er it's a game of luck if you get someone good.

i gave birth to my daughter crystalli rose one week ago and had to share our stay while in kaiser. as a first time mom and having to give birth during covid 19 of course i had so many worries and fears. i was pleasantly surprised with how calm, clean and attentive everyone was. from hard working cleaners, maintenance workers administrators, food handlers, nurses and doctors. i felt completely safe and well taken care of.

04/02/20: dr. nelson and rn debbie explained every treatment and made sure i was as comfortable and cleaned up as possible.

within minutes the anesthesiologist kevin was there! he was very good at explaining the process to me and coached me to relax my body before placing the epidural. he gave me breaks in between the most intense contractions and checked on me in 20 minutes to make sure i was okay and feeling better! i was able to get sleep, drink fluids and still move around in bed but was numb in all the right places.

dr. fernandez explained me options to help assist my delivery. i was scared, exhausted and feeling overwhelmed but she gave me her opinion and understood my wishes( no episiotomy) 

rn velvet was wonderful teaching my husband and i how to feed, hold, burp, clean and bathe our. velvet worked with us to get discharged and back home as quickly as possible. she gave us formula to help the baby urinate and we were finally headed home. our daughter was born completely safe and healthy thanks to the amazing team at kaiser santa clara's l&d department!!

review: it's kaiser so what can you really say? i go here through my work so at least i have health coverage. the facility is nice and as long as you're relatively healthy you can come here every so often, get your check up or minor issue appointment and be on your merry way. but if it's something more serious and you have to go through the army of ninjas to see a specialist or want to see one urgently, good luck! not bad, not great. truly the shining beacon of mediocrity.

review: this review is for the cardiology department at kaiser santa clara. about three weeks ago i had there a quintuple bypass surgery. i'm now in the process of healing and recovery. needless to say the operation went well and i'm happy how the whole process was conducted. i had a first class operation. i'm tremendously appreciative to the surgeons, doctors, nurses, assistants, nutritionist and everyone that participated in it.  their work was simply amazing.

review: do not go to the er here!!!!!! i just spent an hour on the phone trying to figure out why i was charged close to 6000 dollars for a ten minute visit. the hospital billed my insurance, but they let their physicians charge patience independently from the er visit. they did this by charging through a different state. i have ohp and i was sent an 1800 dollar bill on top of the (already covered) er bill... i have since gotten it taken care of, but fuck that shit. this is criminal. plus it was quarantine and the doctor didn't wear a mask.

the outpatient surgery staff was polite. the security staff, a woman, was rarely at her desk and was eating while on shift. their billing practices are outrageous. they charged over $200 thousand for an outpatient toe procedure. so ridiculous. can't even get a call back from a billing supervisor. they service mostly accident and personal injury cases. no wonder their fees are out of this world. shame on you hrh.

if i could give this facility no stars i would. my husband was released from this facility without notifying our family. my husband also has a conservator and they did not speak to her about any of his medications. they released him unstable and put him in a ride share. that does not only endanger my husband but also the driver. 

i called to speak to the nurse and to find out if my husband was still there. she said he was discharged. she said he was there voluntarily, no, he was there on a 5150. they let him go without a discharge plan, no outpatient appointments set. nothing! i told her he was not stable and her response was that she's only the nurse. no! you are the advocate during this time. people come to this hospital for treatment and to get better. it is the nurses job to tell the social workers and the doctors how the patients are doing. do youre job! help the patients get better. if you don't like working in behavioral health then go to a different department.  yes behavioral health is a difficult field to work in but these patients need just as much attention. 

this place makes me sick. i hope to never have to deal with this facility again, and i hope that no family struggling like mine ends up here.

today i had an echocardiogram and the technician was expecting, i think her name was brittney. her technique for doing the procedure was compassionate, thorough, and supportive. in the past, the technicians and even doctors have pressed so hard as to cause additional discomfort; today, i didn't experience that. thank you, wellstar, for an employee that matches your trademark.
maronica is the best rn in 4th floor. she's very caring and understand the patient and family situation and give the best advice on how to move forward after discharge.

i found at my aunt who has raised me went to the hospital i went to the  the 2nd floor she was  moves 3 different times.i asked the young asian  woman siiting there she spoke so fast and you could see she was overwhelmed took her 3 minutes to even acknowledge me and she said go to other station wow ok i saw. lady in housekeeping really she directed me to the "other station" that's how i found out where to go  is like 5 nurses sitting  around mind you i ask. for help and they  are speaking to each other in there language which i find it not professional. language is beautiful i don't speak to others in italian at work its rude the one gets up annoyed asks what i needed. i told  her we hav e been calling 4 times hung up 2 times my aunt needs help or please give me what she needs and i can help her she turns and talks to the others in their language again it is middle eastern (india) i am not prejudice at all my family is mixed race and so am i .by now i'm pissed. she said she would send my nursing assistant my jaw dropped there are 5 chatting away not 1 just 1 could. help. what's going on. by the time i went back to the room she had a accident a mess . my aunt kept saying she was sorry ! really for what i thought ! never ever will we take her there again  the seniors, management, where are you!!!! you should be ashamed off yourself

well i had major abdominal surgery  that was supposed to be day surgery and turned out more serious --during my stay they took good care of me , kept  me clean ,and majority of the staff are as nice as can be ! -as are the cna s who come around to help ,they make you feel better with they're bubbly personality's . on my last day i had a rn by the name of nicolette who was so disrespectful ! she  told me i couldn't have my pain meds when it wasn't her call and gave me a lot of attitude about it -i was completely confused and hurt and i couldn't understand why she acted like that towards me and me being in so much pain and emotional strain i just broke down crying , after she talked to me ugly and walked out of my room - i then spoke to a charge nurse and she was understanding and apologized for the situation -she handled it -and switched my nurse ... i had a really good experience up until the nurse that treated me so mean that day ! thanks for everything christus spohn. overall it was good experience thanks for taking care of me  please  get rid of nurses who are mean to us patients for no reason  i was completely confused as to why she acted like that and hope nobody else has to experience that . nobody should be treated the way nicolette treated me .
