review: i can't even start without crying. any lawyers out there? can anyone explain how a cardiac hospice patient gets no meds for 3 days after their doctor examination by their doctor. i have scars all over my body and am still in pain. do the as promised investigation and show me all the factors that caused it.

i have a relative in trinity hospital who is very sick. please avoid this place at all costs. drive the extra distance if you want good care. he hit the call button when his iv fell out. they came in after a few hours cleaned the floor. did not talk to him or fix the iv.  some clothes were dropped off for him that are badly needed. they took the clothes out them in a patient bag and said they would be delivered. 4 hours later he never got them.  went back to hospital the guy outside the er was extremely rude to us and said the nurse picked everything up. not so.  he said everything was logged except for his belongings.  we called the number back that called about him and it just rings no answer. i called manager on call absolutely no help.  this hospital needs to look at leadership starting at the top and resolve the terrible conditions at this hospital. i am terribly disappointed and will 100% of time find care elsewhere. please 
update son in law got released to quarantine at home. was told no need to get checked again to see if covid19 is gone. what hospital in it's right mind would even think of saying something so stupid in this world at this time. find care elsewhere

the er doctor is callous and his bedside manner lacks basic manners. he doesn't listen to patients convey their complete medical problems and he is too quick to jump to conclusions. rural hospitals struggle to obtain qualified medical staff. however, the other members of the staff appear to be highly qualified and caring.  most er doctors work in high-stress situations. they are under pressure to save lives and often have to break the bad news to loved ones. their patients are usually scared and in some of the most traumatic situations of their lives. this means that er doctors have to remain calm under stress, as well as have a warm personality when talking with patients and their families. this doctor lacks warmth, patience, empathy, and other essential interpersonal skills required for an er doctor position.

i wish i could give negative stars. i am 33 weeks pregnant with covid-19 symptoms and they won't have me tested because they claim i don't have symptoms and that my symptoms are pregnancy symptoms (coughing ??) so if i'm positive for this and my baby suffers they are to blame. worst experience ever

i was there from 4 26 20 to 5 1 20 and there was a lot of things lacking. for instance the nurses didn't wear watches. there was never paper towels or soap in many of the restrooms. on the 3 to 11 shift tony is just plain unfriendly and favors females.  but tico who comes in at 3 is very professional and superbly respectful. he helped me make a smooth departure. chelsey smith and sierra graham came in but didn't speak.  neither did joyce. they all work in outpatient therapy. debra gill is very professional. the cafeteria experience is second to none but they play games with the food. the food and drinks served are great but i do think that they should allow the staff to eat for free. ashley and kyle are very friendly. donald seemed bent on proving that he had a cold. no place in metro memphis is a better place to go to when you are a threat to yourself or someone else. kimberly rickels is just plain too busy. one of her therapists spent 20 minutes of every hour using the bathroom. the same therapist lost her keys so they searched me.

why do these places even exist? i am sure some people really do need mental health treatment, but these places are all too often used as prisons to house people that are wrongfully committed. the worst part is when someone like me is wrongfully committed and i make the people who work there look like they should be patients. i was committed because there are way too many zealous, bigoted, and transphobic assholes in this world who have way too much power. i hope everyone who pathologized me and co-signed my commitment gets the help they need, because if they can't tell that i am a healthy person then it's probably because they are not doing any better than i am. actually, everyone who co-signed my commitment is probably rotting to their very soul. there was no reasonable cause to involuntarily commit me. what was done to me was a heinous act of transphobia committed by my local government. i would even go as far as to label what was done to me a hate crime. the system truly embarrasses itself the way it serves disturbing injustice to every day citizens. it is so terrifying to me that lesser people who are dumber, less happy, less healthy, and all around less of a person than i am get to have so much authority over me. this place should be shut down.

i filed multiple grievances about transphobic staff members here and i absolutely did not file enough. i tried to hand one of my grievances to a nurse only to find out a couple of days later that the patient advocate never received my grievance. luckily, i had photocopies made in advance so i was ready to hand my grievance directly to the advocate. there would have been no justice if i had not made sure they got my complaint because the nurses would rather coverup wrongdoing than do the right thing. 

and at the very end of my false arrest and imprisonment i found out that they had lost all of my belongings including a rare pair of nike tennis shoes, multiple pairs of underwear, and pajamas.

the creepy nurses who worked here also loved to watch me undress in my room at night.

this place should not exist.

i wish i had never known this place existed.

i should have never been here.

what an awful experience for everyone involved and me especially. 

psychiatry and psychology are pseudosciences systemically backed by preposterous amounts of authoritarian power. i don't think most people would really believe all of the horrible things these people with degrees and lab coats can do to them and i am quite sure most people would agree it is wrong.

i can only review the university of kansas medical center based on my experience with them this week. multiple phone calls and hours on the phone simply trying to know why my out-of-pocket responsibility will be for a very routine procedure. i get tossed back and forth between ku and my health insurance plan. both refuse to give the actual allowed out-of-pocket costs... the only thing the person will tell me is that i should know that my insurance will be billed $6500 for a 10 minute procedure. ridiculous, obviously and extremely unhelpful. alicia in "financial counseling" should understand that this is not helpful and put forth a bit more effort in actually matching the simple requests of patients. why is it difficult and next to impossible to know an assumed out-of-pocket cost? why the smoke and mirrors? why the games? ku should know by now the world is changing and this money game you are playing with patients is ridiculous.

on that note, i love my pcp - however, i'm taking his referral to another facility because ku can't seem to answer one simple question.... think twice folks!

my wife came here with a pregnancy complication at 20 weeks. dr fox properly diagnosed the issue but said she'd lose the fetus and to terminate - no other options presented. 

after a rough night thinking we'd lose the kid we went for a second opinion at uw valley. they presented other options and while they weren't likely to work we tried them. btw this wasn't revolutionary stuff, a google search can find studies of treatment options swedish failed to present. 

13 weeks later my son was born at uw valley and is healthy. needless to say i'm very displeased with the quality of care here after needlessly suggesting terminating my son and being less useful than google. i'm sure for routine things swedish would be fine, but no way i'd entrust my family here again.

this hospital is a joke. none of the doctors seem invested in their patients and their health and they just pass you around to as many specialist and tests as your insurance will allow and nothing actionable seems to come from their results and diagnosis. the doctors are asked to see too many patients, and they don't listen to what you have to say they are just in a hurry to collect on their next appointment. i've spent a lot of time and money seeing doctors here and am ready for a practice that actually will help. i've gotten similar opinions from people without expressing my own first. 

on top of that they've been cancelling appointments for the last two months during this covid issue, which imo you can take precautions but you're a hospital that is probably well equipped and are leaving people with serious conditions out to hang. shame.

my experience with the three doctors i see that are associated with swedish hospital has been ten stars. the one star rating is for a very profit oriented upper management with policies that appear to have little regard for patient or staff needs. i've been told that they can not make color copies on the 4th floor of the hospital because they do not have a color printer available, even though staff has made administration aware of the need. so my doctor received a black and white copy of a color coded test that was difficult to decipher. i have requested that appointment reminders be sent to my home phone and other (medical related) calls use my cell number. i am told that their system will not allow this. as a result either automated reminders interrupt my workday or i miss important calls from my doctors and their assistants. that is not my biggest complaint. i had two tests at swedish hospital. both times the technicians made mistakes that were not minor. one error rendered my test results inconclusive, the other exposed me to twice as much radiation as was necessary. after submitting a written complaint about the first test i received a letter from heidi bain, in the patient complaint department. i called the number beneath her signature to discuss the cat scan mishap. someone in her department returned my second call and said they would email my call back request to her. i later spoke with a hospital operator who said she was not provided with a way to connect me with any hospital administrator. after leaving 3 messages over 2 weeks with no response, i gave up. the administrators of this hospital clearly value one thing- and it is not the welfare of their patients or staff.

not how i planned to spend a saturday night in bethany beach, but here we are.  

my husband knocked his head on a beam in the attic while opening up a client's beach house.  he ended up with a bit of goose-egg knot on his head.   he did not think much of it at the time but the next day, he came down with an excruciating headache, unlike anything he has ever experienced.   worried it was related to the head injury the day before, we decided not to take a chance and took off for what siri told me the closest er to our location.  

i had to wait in the car due to covid restrictions but hubby kept me informed by text throughout the process.   luckily it was only the after effects of a mild concussion and not a more serious head injury (according to the ct scan).  he was pleased with the md he saw and follow-up instructions he received.   he was in and out of there in about an hour too!  hard to believe for a saturday night.

from now on, i think i will make him wear a bike helmet when he is in a low clearance attic.

the rating for this hospital is a negative. i never spend time on writing reviews but this experience was awful. the physicians and nurses are completely incompetent. my fiancé had a bad case of food poisoning and was vomiting from noon to 10pm. i finally was able to convince him to go to the er. he wasn't able to hold any fluid down since he began vomiting at noon. as soon as we got there they said he didn't need iv hydration that they would do a po challenge after giving him sublingual zofran to see if he tolerates the fluids. based on his vital signs he was stable meaning he was asymptomatic from signs of dehydration..but why wait to be symptomatic when you are told a person has been vomiting all day unable to keep fluids down! obviously he tolerated little sips after the zofran it's antiemetic and makes you sleepy. they discharged us with a prescription and said to come back if he continues to vomit. during the night of course he began to vomit. i called the ed and explained what happened and the apparent hospital supervisor "betty" said well bring him back in but there is no guarantee  what the doctor will order him maybe more zofran maybe iv fluids. does this make any sense? completely incompetent providers. if you want to live do not go there because they don't care!

dr. del vecchio was awesome! the best er physician ever! not only is he knowledgeable but he actually cares about your health.  from his bedside manner to follow up, he's top shelf.  you're lucky if you get him to treat you.

please do not come to this hospital.

they do not deserve the one star. 

if your elderly do not stay at this hospital

i had bariatric surgery preformed by dr james atkinson, pa marc washington at desert springs hospital. the medical staff was amazing. my caregivers when i first got out of surgery will forgive me if i do not remember their names because i was so groggy, however the attention they gave to me throughout the day and night was nothing less than superb. no matter what i needed they were there and made sure i was comfortable. during one of the shift changes lead rn helen took over, along with jovian and jianwea. again, impeccable care, patient oriented. caring staff. i recommend desert springs and their amazing rn, nursing assistants,doctors and pa's.

review:
we were visiting the area, my wife got sick while we were there. she was afraid she had the flu. we were flying out the next day and she wanted to know so to protect others on the plane. we went to st anthony outside frisco co at about 9:00pm so she could be tested for the flu. nice place & professional nurses & staff.
then the bill arrived !! 
er visit: $13,801.20 yes thirteen thousand dollars !! billing had coded it wrong. 
the corrected bill is now $7290.94 
seven thousand two hundred + dollars to be tested for the flu !!! 
then the kicker, the doctor's bill was an additional $974.00. thousand dollars to read flu test, order a iv and o2,
i still owe them close to $3000.00 after insurance. after insurance this 30 minute er visit cost more than my entire trip !! 
this is crazy 
please try to find a urgent care before you go here. if it is late at night, rough it out until the morning then find a urgent care or dr office.

edit: a personal reply would be nice not the meaningless automated reply.

do. not. go. here. 
i went here because i thought i might've had the flu and it was a huge mistake. the doctors were fine but the billing system which is through centura health is a joke/scam. i paid a $60 copay at the end of my visit and they handed me papers basically saying if i get another bill in the future it's from ventura and not st. anthony's itself. i thought that was sketchy and i was right. a month after my appointment i get a bill for the same doctors visit for $200. i spent hours contacting both centura and my insurance just to find out that centura billed my insurance as an "emergency room visit" rather than the urgent care. my insurance company assured me that the copay for urgent care was $60 flat which i had already paid the day of the appointment. i thought everything was handled after that. nope, 3 months after that i got another bill this one for a random total of $147. at this point i'm livid because i know i don't owe a cent and they're just throwing random numbers at me now hoping that i pay. well i called and made sure they understood i owe them nothing and they better fix it and send me a new statement of $0. that was today i'm sure i'll be back in here in a few months to update this when they will probably send me another random bill. save yourself the trouble and don't go



update: just got another bill for $147 from them, at this point it's a joke. i would love for them to contact me and explain what a joke they are.

i called bryn mawr ed to notify them of my brother being on his way via ambulance to them so they knew exactly what was going on with him. he was a danger to himself, not stable, and the charge nurse working whom i spoke with was rude, condescending, inconsiderate, and made it obvious she is suffering from compassion fatigue. (this charge nurse was working on 5/17 day shift). she showed no interest in hearing of my families' concerns for him, the medications he has been taking, or the substances he has been using, which would allow for her and her team to treat him more efficiently. i called back about 2 hours later, to speak with whoever what taking care of my brother, and a woman who did not say her name when she answered the phone said, "he is no longer here, he eloped." how this happens, i do not know. i myself am a np, and would personally do everything in my power to persuade a patient in need of medical and psychiatric care to stay. this woman made no mention that they tried anything, and left me feeling that they pretty much allowed him to walk out the door. main line health has a whole typically has a great reputation from what i hear, however this experience showed nothing but unprofessional behavior, negative attitudes, a perception that depicted these health care professionals to dislike their jobs and have no patience or compassion for those suffering from psychiatric and addictive disorders or their concerned family members. i work in the field, and i would never treat anyone's family like bryn mawr ed staff treated me today.

review based on blood donation.

i saw something online about children's reaching out, so i called and they returned my call with a near immediate time/day slot that became available. 

it was easy to find, wasn't busy, and the staff was available to direct me where i had to go which was not too far from the front entrance. 

i liked they had movies playing! great idea! why don't more blood donation centers do this? just gives you something to do besides just sitting there while your waiting to give blood, during giving blood, and after as you're making sure you're alright and snacking. makes total sense! i'd donate here again in a heartbeat.

review: they have an amazing blood donation center. clean and comfortable with knowledgeable and caring staff. if you can please donate blood or plasma. blood donation are less than 15 minutes and for plasma donation you have a nice recliner to relax during, watch some tv and snacks after.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review: high concentration of overconfident yet demonstrably incompetent providers. lots of big fish in a small pond who have conflated their outsized presence in a medium sized city with actual world class medical care.

review:
i've been in their er twice in the past couple of years, once with pneumonia, and once with severe, crippling migraine pain.

both times they essentially saved me -- from dying of pneumonia, and were very kind and concerned for me.  the migraine they helped me with very swiftly, understanding i was in terrible pain.

so... take the negative reviews with a large grain of salt.  usually the folks who're helped with a smile don't bother to review a place.

well, they saved my life.  i'm eternally grateful to a great team of medical personnel.
st. joe's sucks. if you have a major medical issue, lay in misery, wait 8 hours* and you will get sub-par treat meant or airlifted somewhere else.

real review!!!! read this before considering admitting yourself of a loved one here!!!
i came here right before thanksgiving of 2019. i admitted myself because i was having suicidal thoughts and i needed help. i went in about 9am to get an evaluation done. sat in the waiting room for about an hour after filling out paperwork. 
got escorted to a office type thing where a nurse evaluated me and asked me handful of questions (as they should). with one of the questions, he asked if i ever had any plans on killing my self , to which i said "i have in the past" and he put "within the past week" (which of course i didn't know until i got in there but that's later!) once again after waiting to hear back from this "dr" on what i should do, i waiting for another 5 hours!! by this time it's about 3pm , i haven't had any lunch. refused to give me food , even though they knew i've been in there since 9am!! doctor tells the staff that i should be admitted and i am high threat, and i'm not really sure why because i never had any intentions of hurting myself right then and there....
get put into a room and had to get naked and searched....everywhere!! like i was in prison!!!!! i was so shocked!! by this time it's about 7pm and i'm having a panic attack because i don't know what's going on , no one is telling me anything, it's "shift change" so i can't get my medicine that i need. no water, no bed. i had to sit on the hard cold chairs with a gown on cause they took my clothes (once again i have no idea why they did that till this day). 
after speaking with the doctor the next day to explain to him that this was a mistake, considering i admitted myself and i'm not doing anything these people said i'm doing, he refuses to let me go and keeps me for another 3 days!!!!
they don't do anything. no group sessions, no therapy. you sit in a room with a bed and a bathroom , can't color, can't read cause they have no books. the only thing you can do is smoking cigarettes every hour....

please save yourselves!!!!

i'm not going to exaggerate anything that occurs at this facility and just give you the breakdown of what happens from the time you arrive to the time you leave. first you get into the main lobby and depending on how you came (whether through ambulance or self-admittance) you're either going to be wearing a gown, scrubs, or random clothes that they'll have to check (no laces or strings). the food is decent, the workers literally don't care about their job and it's like staying at a sketchy 2 star hotel. they do have books, coloring worksheets, and television. but that's it there's nothing else after that. you'll do maybe a few group sessions but i can hardly even count that as something you do there on a regular basis. as far as i'm concerned i feel like i'm giving an unbiased review considering the fact that i was lied to by the doctor himself. yes, i'm talking about dr. singh and the nurse practitioner that was on duty. i'm not even going to mention in detail about how the workers ignored my request for no blood work and no pork in my meals. let's just talk about what the doctor did there. dr singh is good when it comes to prescribing medications but when it comes to being an honest guy, not so great. him and his assistant literally said i couldn't get discharged unless i did bloodwork yet i ended up leaving 3 hours later without having to do it. but that's not the worst part. the worst part was that i was having anxiety attacks the entire week and hardly slept because i kept fearing they would ask me repeatedly to do bloodwork which they did. honestly if you need to go to rehab for an addiction just stay at a 4 star hotel instead. they'll actually take care of you there. just call it a vacation and bring your medicine with you.

disgusting! unprofessional. they discharged my husband without his shoes or wallet before i arrived even though i spoke to them earlier and said not to. he walked home in socks!!! blood on the waiting room floor when i was trying to pick him up was still there the next day when i tried picking up his belongings which they lost. horrible place. my husband is more traumatized from staying here 5 days than he was before being admitted. avoid this place!!!

beware!!!

the care my intellectually-challenged daughter received at paoli emergency room over her weekend stay was poor. aside from the guards/nurses stationed outside of her room each night (each was kind and attentive) most of the numerous staff we encountered were disinterested and even unkind. her vitals were rarely taken throughout the two nights, and it took a crowd of five nurses several attempts to draw her blood (she looked like a bruised pin cushion the next day). we could clearly overhear the staff discussing my daughter's and other patients' sensitive medical information.there was also inaccurate information listed on her discharge papers- thankfully my husband noticed so that i could have it corrected. i have learned a valuable lesson for the future- read reviews before choosing your emergency room. we do it before dining out, but who thinks to check online in the event of an emergency? lesson learned!

i won't go anywhere else.  they've cleaned up the er and the wait was minimal.  the doctor was thorough and the nurses were great. 

thank you so much for being there for us!

it doesn't matter if it flu or just a everyday medical issue. i have waited 4 to 5 he's on fast track only to find out i needed to stay for a week.  why because i have pancreas problems.

this place was the worst place you could ever go to or send your kids from personal experience it took them 2 hours to get us signed in and none of the workers act like they know what they are doing the nurses always have attitude and don't care and this is in the youths they are nowhere near emotional support and that do not help you they just give you medicine if your parents allow and that's it they don't know how to handle people correctly and they act as if they don't care when you are triggered they don't  do anything about fighting all they do is break it up and lock us in the rooms if someone steals your stuff they do nothing about it at the end of the whole experience i never got back two pairs of pants and an inhaler the pants were stolen and they did nothing and an inhaler and an chapstick that they took they never gave them back i hope they go out of business because they are truly the worst there are a few very nice techs who help and do there job but the nurses and the other techs are horrible if i could i would give them zero stars but i can't they don't even deserve one dont go here ever!!

unfortunately had a medical emergency while i was with family. no better time to have a random ailment strike than during a pandemic, said no in the world, ever, at all, in the history of time.

was taken here and seen immediately by staff, who were all in face masks. they made me hand sanitize before entering. i could see the parking lot immediately outside of the hospital main gate was set up for drive-thru covid-19 testing. 

i was taken to rush care and put in a room where the nurse came promptly and dr. brian park came shortly after that. there was a ton of waiting in between, but understandable due to the current condition of things. they assured me that the covid patients were seen in another wing of the hospital, if that was something i was concerned about.

i was in and out in about 5.5 hours, with almost no time spent in the waiting room. while this was an experience i definitely did not want to have, and almost did not review, i wanted to take the time to thank our healthcare heroes who are working tirelessly to help with covid and all other emergency situations at this time. you are appreciated.

except for the hospitals covid 19 ... management best practices .... which is totally understood & appreceiated  .... 

it's the best hospital in atl

if i could give this hell house zero stars i would. terrible practices, rude treatment from start to finish, impatient nurses, and horrible customer service. run far, far away. take your health needs anywhere else. pretty sure china or mexico is a better bet then this place.

review: i went in for a procedure in 2019.  when i woke up i was told my heart beat went from normal to 35 to over 120 beats back to normal beats per minute several times.  they put me into a hospital bed for 24 hours to monitor me.  did a mess of tests was sent home and told to go see a cardiologist.  my stay in the hospital was excellent.  the nurses were fantastic, the food was great.  three months later i got a statement from our "insurance" company, they weren't going to pay on the 24 hour stay in the hospital bill because neither my wife or i had called them.  i called the "insurance" company, but wasn't able to work anything out. we went to the hospital billing department to set up a payment plan.  was told not to worry they deal with insurance companies every day.  ten months later got a statement from the "insurance" company, good to go, paid in full.

doesn't even deserve the single star. a horrible facility which traumatized me much more than helped. i had to stay here for five days when i was seventeen and i'm nineteen still trying to recover from what i went through here. i had a bacterial infection and wasn't given a physical exam or my medicine for it. they tried to get me an outpatient therapist when i already had one. they tried to give me my sleeping medicine in the morning. the psychiatrist called me promiscuous and told me ocd is normal for women. this is not a healing environment and the doctors/nurses don't know what they're doing.

not a place of healing

this place is a scam/honeypot/government subsidized trap house. patients are treated like animals, given no guidance or support, and forced to rely on each other for any real therapy. requests to staff will be brushed off, or you will be given a name (good luck remembering anyone in this super high turnover job) and also they are all wearing covid masks right now).  many of the people behind the nursing station are esl speakers from varying backrounds. they had difficulty speaking to both their coworkers and their patients. 

near the end of my stay i reported that i was having some paranoia and asked the "patient advocate" if there was a therapist i could speak with, i was dismissed with a wishy-washy aswer and left. i never heard from her again. this self-snitching was enough of an excuse for them to keep me another day ($$$) 

i finally managed to get a room all to myself for what i hoped was my final night, however in the middle of the night was awoken to the sound of med techs dragging a new roommate in. the new guy in my room apparently thought he was a snail ("i'm a snailor" - direct quote) and acted like the bug guy from men in black. he was removed from the wing shortly after breakfast and chucking a few full cops of coffee into other peoples rooms and trying to eat his food by spiting all over it like jeff goldbum in the fly.

i still had a spring in my step because of my excitement over going home, only to be told that i had not slept enough last night so i had to stay another day.

yet how can i sleep under this conditions? i felt like i was being blamed for factors outside my my control.

luckily i was able to finally sleep and overcome the many many obstacles, unwritten rules, unfollowed policies, disgruntled employees, etc. etc. etc. and prove that i could take care of myself like an adult (hygiene, laundry, etc) and finalize an outpatient treatment plan.

unless its a last resort, never send anywhere here

my 88 yr old mom was brought to er and was seen right away. x-ray and ultrasound completed within an hour. dr rothkin was so nice! he called and thoroughly explained what was being done and even sent photos of her x-ray. she'll be discharged soon.  couldn't be happier with the nurses and doctor today, esp during these crazy corona times.

i've never had any issues or complaints with the service kaiser provides.  amidst all the chaos and scare of the covid-19 they are doing their best to keep the public calm and safe. i appreciate the containment of the entrance into the facility.  wash stations immediately placed outside the door.  nurses and doctors on duty screening all who enter the facility.  you couldn't turn a corner without an employee present to answer any questions.  they are being proactive professional and patient. accommodating and kind during this time.  this is why i still chose kaiser.

review:
this is my very first review of any kind but i had to do it because of how unsettled i feel. had to bring my elderly mother to the hospital, hesitantly because of the current global health crisis. she needed to come into the orthopedic department to have her cast removed and see a doctor for her injury.

we took the necessary precautions to minimize our possible exposure by wearing a mask and gloves. upon arriving at orthopedics and checking in an older heavyset man by the name of "rick" called my mother into the department. he told us that he will be cutting off her cast and walked us down a hallway to the cast room. he than told my mother that he will be using the "cast saw" to remove her cast, turned it on without warning us of the loud noise it made and how safe it was. but what i found most disturbing was that he handled the machine with his bare hands (no gloves). he proceeded to put the saw blade to his hand and stated "it won't cut". he continued to remove the cast off my mother while touching her bare handed no gloves!!! he never washed his hands before or after handling my mother!

i looked at his badge to check for his title and shockingly he is a "sr. orthopedic tech". this is very disappointing, that someone who appears to have the experience needed in order to have that title is that incompetent and ignores the simplest of personal protection such as gloves. 

it is very troubling that during this time of global health crisis kaiser allows people like rick to hold a job at a place where you would expect the highest level of safety. no apology needed kaiser, save it for the next person one of your employees hurts.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Leandro Medical Center

review: i took my 89 year old mother to get a tb test as we are putting her in a nursing home.  she has dementia.  the test was done wednesday and we went back friday so they could read the test,  the clinic is on the 3rd floor.  they called my mom in pretty quickly and the test should have taken just a couple minutes.  after a long wait i asked the receptionist to check on her. when mom went in i stood up and directed her to go inside as she is very confused.  the gal that took her in came out to tell me mom said she was alone (although i was right there telling her to go in) so she put her on the elevator!  of course i panicked and went down the elevator to find her.  when you first come off the elevator there is an injection waiting room.  luckily my mom was sitting there totally confused why i was there.  she had even pulled a number for her turn but she didn't need an injection.  i logged into mom's kaiser portal to let the corporate office know what happened and wanted an answer why,  hopefully someone could do a better job so this doesn't happen to anyone else.  the next day i got a very nasty email telling me i am not authorized to use mom's portal,  i use it to make her appointments and communicate with her doctors.  my name is listed in her file.  no apology nothing.  they put it all back on me.  mom could have walked outside and gone who knows where.  you can just look at her and know she is confused.

i was air lifted to this hospital from parker on april 2nd as a trauma patient caused by a truck roll over accident... at the same time i became a potential for covid-19 due to ct scans showing "glassy characteristics" which relate to covid-19. although it was likely due to the blunt trauma caused by the airbags which led to me coughing blood, the hospital still deemed it as a potential- which i totally understand... needless to say it was a scary experience and through it all the entire staff was amazing... upon my isolation in the negative pressure room my limbs were previously relocated.. i was in mass amount of pain and unable to maneuver out of bed, let alone use the bathroom or feed myself.. despite the pain medications administered.. my very first nurse assigned to me that night.. took care of me like a mother would! despite the covid-19 potential on my chart, she tended to my needs beyond expectation while of course wearing appropriate gear.. silvia f. was on her name tag.. after she helped me relieve myself of urine as i was unable to use my hands or get out of the bed, she was able to get me food and then spoon fed me!! amazing, caring soul. i never got the chance to thank her after that night because i assume she was relocated, but i hope she sees this.. furthermore as the days went on, each nurse and doctor i encountered was amazing and made my stay tolerable through the pain... i just want you all to know how much i appreciate you taking care of me and keeping me alive when i was at critical condition 86% oxygen while on three liters...

i am a 72 year old woman, staying in palm springs for the month of march. on march 8,2020, my husband took me to desert regional er with horrific abdominal pain. the dr. ordered a ct scan with contrast. while waiting, i was given a shot of morphine.  the wait lasted about 2 hrs, so they gave me another shot of morphine.  after the ct, the dr read it an diagnosed me a constipated.  when i assured him that was not the case, he would not listen. my husband said he could not take me home in such terrible pain. the dr then ordered another, stronger, pain shot and a bottle of liquid laxative.  i took it and suffered excruciating pain and diarrhea for 30 hours. my husband then took me eisenhower er. they also did a ct scan and could not figure out how they could have missed, a perforated duodenal ulcer. after a week in the hospital and 3 weeks of iv antibiotics,  i'm feeling much better.  would i recommend desert regional hospital ,  not if my life depended on it, again. account #243870003

i went out to the back yard with my dog so she could relieve herself - it was approximately 6:00 am. i then got the urge to use the bathroom, then rushed upstairs. i was sitting on the toilet and instantly began sweating out of every pore of my body. i was weak, scared, nauseated - so i did what many of us do and called 911. got in the ambulance to go to the emergency room. i was only there for help.
i don't currently have insurance so i don't go to the e.r. unless i'm really worried that i need professional support. i was discharged with no covid-19 test,i was still vomiting i was given no iv support. i had to ask for anti nausea drugs - they did give me one round but i was still vomiting and the rudeness from the nurse was off the charts. and most the rest were not to much better. the overall compassion and level of care was obsolete. i am hopeful that they will wake up and do their job or better yet find a new one. shame on you for treating the members of your community so poorly when they are there for your help. yes, i totally understand that a pandemic is underway. however, this is the third time in a row i have endured the same treatment from the staff of the er. they said the only reason they didn't give a covid-19 test was my current lack of fever. after i got home, my temp was 100.1 and climbing. nope, not going there again.

this is one of the best emergency rooms i have ever had to visit. they were extremely professional, very quick, friendly, and efficient. the hospital is also very clean. i went in for some stitches on my knee and was out within 20 minutes. 
thank you to all of the staff, doctors, and nurses for your constant hard work and dedication. special thanks to dr. michael ward for the beautiful stitches he did on my knee! i'm on day 3 of healing and my knee looks great! if i ever find myself or a friend in the position of needing an er while in az, i will be coming back to this specific one.

i had coronavirus symptoms 8 days ago (started on thursday 3/12), i've been to the emergency on friday 3/13 at 8:30am to get tested, so i can let know my employer, co-workers and family.
i've been waiting for 3.30 hours, and for some time outside, on a rainy day, with high fever and flu symptoms.
they told me i should wait 4 to 5 days to get my results, so i called 5 days later, then they told me one more day, so i just called them and now i should wait for them to call me back and that, if i gave them accurate information, they "should" call me back... and actually, they looked pretty confused and non organized when i get the test and they collected my information.

i love being here , not only do i always get awesome service but the nurses go above and beyond. when i had my twins they made me cry in that floor because of how well they treated me

one of the worst hospital i ever been in. 
it is a money making machines. i have full coverage insurance. i had abdominal pain, needed to have my gull bladder removed, after all test have been done. big day at 12 noon. 1130was at the front desk,sorry your surgery is postponed to 3pm, thanks i reply no one can call and tell me so i can stay at home i tell then ,no she said like if i was in fault. long story short at 2pm in to be prepared 2 nice nurse trying to do their job with what they have on hand with broken tools. i laid on the bed til 330pm,one dr walk up to me explain the situation tel me to hung up it goin to be a wild,before i have a chance to ask any questions he left. 4pm the nurse come up i said can i ask a question?she replied i have no answer for you,i am sorry i need answer what time is my opperation? she call the dr after i insisted and the answer was. there is an urgent matter if we don't operat on you tonight  we might operat tomorrow afternoon. 
oh thanks lady can i have my clothes, i will try my luck at metrohealth tomorrow. ok thas your right she replied. gave me my stuff showed me the way out without singing any paperwork and i left.

review: i went to their er and was seen quickly and was thoroughly evaluated. they were so efficient and organized. thank you baylor scott & white mckinney! i would highly recommend them.

review:
in may 2019 a nurse in the er struck a nerve in my arm attempting to insert an iv and i'm still suffering after a year of treatments that i have had to pay for myself. it's a shame such damage can happen in the hospital and no one will take responsibility. this is not the first issue i've had with baylor. in 2016 i had major surgery at another facility and there were major complications, bmy surgeon left the state and no one knew who was supposed to tend to me. thank god the doctor my surgeon he had to call to help repair the damage he did during surgery was there to save my life. he even has to take me back to surgery. i didn't think i would leave alive. it's such a shame. it's not just one location, it seems their whole system is flawed. my surgery in 2016 has been so hard to relive, but now with the injury to the nerve in my arm it's my duty to let potential patients know what could happen if they have to visit a baylor scott and white hospital.



it's so funny that they responded to my post 6 hours after i posted, but it's been 6 days since i submitted my contact information and i have not heard from anyone representing baylor scott and white. as i said their doctors and nurses do great damage and this hospital doesn't care. by the way, the radial nerve was damaged in my arm.

review: wife and i had a terrible labor & delivery experience at this facility.  i was personally mocked and chastised by several nursing staff members from the labor & delivery unit.  this is completely uncalled for and beyond unprofessional.  extremely disappointed in how we were treated here.  i would like representatives from bs&w to follow-up with me for further details.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - McKinney

review: i never write reviews but this place is awful. the staff is always so rude, i dread coming here over getting sick because of how terrible of a staff is there. get a different job if you're not there because you don't care about the people coming in. worst place ever.

one of the finest nonprofit healthcare systems in massachusetts. my mother in law and sister in law have both been admitted 3-4 times over the past few years due to elderly related and other issues. the staff overall provided professional and compassionate care. both of them required physical therapy. mrmc advocacy team made the transition from a hospital stay to a rehab facility a smooth process. this eliminated the worry families experience regarding loved ones care.

during the covid-19 crisis, the staff was very creative with addressing protective wear shortages. they made plastic gowns from huge rolls of plastic sheeting donated by local businesses. an assembly line was setup in the cafeteria area where the gowns were made.

visited the emergency dept many times.  great staffing, nice people, great  professional communication between staff and with patients very respectful. . clean and sanitized well especially with covid 19 and their extra precautions in place. 
been admitted to a nice private room which the whole floor was private rooms.  very attentive respectful staff.  kept you well informed. great experience with many depts.  and interactions.
every time i go there the staff are amazing, wait times are short and they take every measure to diagnose and treat me. thank you milford regional!

once again, huron valley saved my life....literally.
after my pcp dismissed my intense arm pain, stomach pain. sweating and nausea and sent me home, the pain became unbearable and i went to huron valley. in less than 30 mins i was in surgery to clear two arteries...i was having a heart attack.
last year i had severe pneumonia and the care was superb. the nurses are efficient and compassionate.
i switched all my care to dmc because of my experiences- pulmonary, cardiac, and primary care.
i love this hospital.

are all ers notoriously bad, or just this one. should it really take 2.5 hours to see a doctor, get a diagnose a uti and give you antibiotics?  brought my child here at 11:00 pm and didn't leave until nearly after 1:30 am. i had this diagnosed within seconds through the mayo clinic website list of symptoms. saw the doctor for less than a minute at 12:10. at 1:10 he popped back in long enough to say its a uti and here's a pill until you can get more at the pharmacy later in the morning.

i had an injury where a large portion of my finger was removed by a power tool. dmc was the closest er. i sat in the waiting room for over an hour before even being registered. then i waited another hour after to get called into the er. i was actively bleeding. i got into a room, met the rn and md, got a tetanus shot and then didn't see either for 2 hours. no pain medication, no wound care, nothing. i finally asked another rn if they were too busy to see me. she said i'd only been waiting an hour and 8 minutes. i corrected her that this was only reflective of my time in the exam room. i asked her if i was getting anything for the pain. they said they gave me tylenol. i said for losing the tip of my finger that's it? she then went to find the dr. 20 minutes later the dr- who was a resident- not a physician- a student- and who should have been practicing under an attending physician told me i didn't need anything and to call their plastic surgeon in the morning. she didn't clean the wound that required a surgeon, stop the bleeding or even clean the blood which ran down my arm. as i departed the rn said "here's the pain medication you wanted" and gave me a pill. i then went to st. joseph's who took appropriate care of me, cleaned my wound, taped it with a splint, gave me medication, and coordinated a surgeon. i would avoid dmc at all costs.

i had to go to the er this past weekend for a non covid-19 related issue.
the care itself was very good, nurses and doctors compassionate.
i was however, surprised that one nurse used no gloves or mask. i was sick in the restroom and it was not cleaned up in the several hours that i was there...which was most concerning, even though i alerted them immediately.  so the sanitary conditions were the concern.

my nina stayed at this place she slipped and they never filed a report . she was in room 109 before they took her to the hospital and she had back surgery due to the fall my nina says . please watch your loved ones when left here
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Las Vegas

review:
worst hospital ever! my daughter has been in there 8 days! (she has crohn's disease) they are slow, it takes days to get x-ray, cat scan, or any lab work back, she has a abscess in her pelvis and they let her lay there for 7 days before they took her in to clean it out. drs don't start work till after 12:00. if you ask me they are more concerned about sucking as much money out of you then giving you the proper medical treatment. when the ambulance came to get her my gut told me not to take her to this hospital ( i read reviews before ) but she was in so much pain she just wanted to go. ( we live out of town too) they wouldn't take her to loma linda. my advice is do not go to this hospital it will be worth it to drive yourself or your loved one to loma linda. 
worst experience ever! 
there were some pretty awesome nurses but the care system needs some serious work!

i wouldn't even give one star but i have to. i only went because i needed immediate help. i had to have my appendix removed and i was in desperate need of help. first night was ok. the next day everything changed. nurse would ignore me for hours no one would answer the call button. they put my iv into my tissue and my arm swelled up huge, when they finally took it out so much fluid leaked for the site that i needed a towel. blew out my veins in both arms. forgot a machine was running and let it for over 5hrs causing my legs to swell up. the list goes on. i am young and healthy enough to stand up for myself and demanded to be discharged the day after surgery. i feel horrible for anyone who is timid or can't speak up. they probably are treated very poorly.

this establishment treats patients like cattle. they do not care about service or well being. the outpatient clinics might have good dr. care but front staff violate hippa and make policies to get big corporation money and little sensitive care.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Temple

review:
while the doctors who work in leased offices at this location are amazing - my review is based solely on ordered imaging i had done here. do not do it!  
they max bill your insurance, even my insurance company was completely dumbfounded with how much they billed. it was $500 for 2 hip extras, total time 2 minutes, i waited 2 hours to have these 2 images taken. 

after the fact, the employees in payments are beyond rude. i have not had one good call with them. 
even today paying my bill off the representative started with attitude. 
i've asked for a note to be made - never let me be a patient in this facility again. in an emergency transfer me somewhere else as soon as possible.
fac_name: CHI St. Luke's Health-Sugar Land Hospital

review:
i still give a 2 star for the gal at the admitting desk in the lobby...awhile back...grrh

but the er...during this time of pandemic, and restricted hospital entry, i had to rush my husband in and my goodness they were spot on, with a wheel chair at the car to get him...yay.
and larry rn was there got the info and whisked him away...every half hour he was checked...right now you can not go in with your loved one, so we both were worried, but my goodness they were amazing, calling me and being so attentive to him...he knows them all by name is at ease, and slowly recovering yay!!!
i can not say enough good...and thank you all...

to whom it may concern,

on behalf of our family, i would like to thank your rehabilitation center for providing great care by your delightful employees, namely: tyler, dobrina, eliza, hanna, aline, charlotta, jennifer and angel.  on november 19, 2019 my dad was transferred to your facility from sutter medical center in modesto. when we found out that he needed to complete a full physical and mental rehabilitation, we were told that he would be transferred to your facility. we were a bit skeptical, due to some reviews that we have read from yelp. however, after listening to some feedback from doctor behremian's office (my dad's surgeon), my family decided to take a chance. it was one of the most painful experiences that our family went through for 2 months, however, your awesome employees made a huge impact. our experience in your facility was nothing but great. your employees started to diminish the anxious feeling that we were having little by little from day one. we had witnessed my dad's progress as days went by. the care that your staffs provided was exceptional, and even up to now my dad still remembers every single one of them. you all treated my dad as if he was part your family. 

thank you sincerely. may our lord bless your facility and employees as you continue to grow financially and to keep up the exceptional care that you are providing for your patients. people need people like you. 

ps. dad wanted to extend his regards especially to tyler and hanna.

review:
as a patient having had to stay here for 2 weeks, i would say everything looks good from the outside. the nursing care is not as good as you would expect. i waited on a bedpan for up to 25 minutes more than once. i had a nursing assistant tell me my bottom was yellow from urine staining it.you might get a shower once a week. the physical therapy department is good, but they seem to be limited on treatments to help you get stronger.
the one good thing about this place is the private room all patients receive. the bathroom is big and accommodating. the food is not great and definitely not healthy. i would recommend this place only because of the private room.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Modesto

review:
i am giving this business five stars but these five stars are all negatives stars. this business is something else. while the staff who are directly involved in the care and rehab of their patients were more than just efficient and actually were above and beyond in their care of their of patients. no complaints there. 
the problem was with my husbands discharge and needed medical supplies which weren't given to him and what was ordered and arrived before his release was not something we are able to use. my husband had his leg amputated after 8 months of infections and gangrene. he had been sick for so long he had no strength left which pt had just began to help him. the case manager, manbir khatkar, is one of the worst humans i have ever had the displeasure to have to deal with. husband was released with one sock(shrinker) which is necessary to shape his limb in preparation for his fitting for a prosthetic limb. sock he has falls off. potty chair is unusable in my home mostly because of size. it's a free standing chair. he had told khatkar that it would not work but she refused to listen to him and ordered it anyway. i had called her on tues. the 24th and explained our situation to her and she told me she had to get it approved by mr roget, medical director.  waited for her follow up and thursday evening i called khatkar and left a message inquiring the outcome of her conversation. this morning i received a call from khatkar telling me that she had never said that she was waiting for approval and that she had told me i was to contact our primary care dr for anything i may need. that alone was no problem but her yelling at me and just being downright rude but don't you think that i would have called our dr sooner if this info had been given to me on tues.  and i know why she was yelling because she had been caught in a lie. what a piece of......, well you know. she was the only staff that i had to deal with, thank god, but if the office staff is anything like her i would not give them the time of day. so since all of this i still have nothing he can use to help him in the bathroom and because of no support system he has fallen twice, totally breaking open his stitches and bleeding everywhere, why he needs a second sock so i can soak the blood out. if he does get infected or has problems healing i am going to blame it directly on khatkar and will be named as such on any legal action taken. lucky for her i am really good at my job, taking care of my husband, but will not be happy until she is dealt with.

review: great hospital that gave my wife and i great care during separate stays. my wife had surgery for an intestinal issue and i had heart valve replacement, both in 2014. we're alive and kicking and i credit the doctors, nurses and other staff we had at gateway. we live in sc now but i still miss having that hospital nearby.

had a collection show up april 2020 on my credit report. called and they stated it was from 2013 at bartow regional!! 2013. i never got a letter or a call. shame on you for waiting 7 years when i never knew that i owed a balance. for all that i know it was probably an error on your billing departments **update: as you can see below someone commented on my review, i followed through and no one has contacted me still.

we just had our first baby here at northside one month ago. i cannot say enough good things about our experience at northside during this corona virus situation. very pleased with how they protected us.

amazing labor and delivery. i was in labor for 48 hours and i can't say enough good things about the nursing staff. i was pleasantly surprised by how amazing each and everyone of them were. after l&d we were in mother baby for another 48 hours. they did a great job checking in when needed and making us feel comfortable. each nurse and tech in mother baby did an amazing job. highly recommend.

i was just released today from northside after a 6 day stay for a lung operation. this review is about the food and food service. i have had hospital food while visiting friends over the last 20 years in different hospitals around georgia so i expected cold, cheap, poorly cooked meals.
from the first meal i was served that night, i was surprised at how good it was.
every single meal from then on was well balanced and and tasty. i was quite shocked at how good they were flavor wise. i never in a million years expected any thing like what i ate while i was there this past week. it was all good quality, well cooked, healthy food.
ok, food is one thing and service is another. the food server on the floor i was on was unbelievable, nina knew what foods i liked after the first day, always got all the little things i like to go along with my meals and took special care of me the whole time. today when i told her i was leaving and did not want lunch, she brought me the most amazing chef's salad anyway and asked me if i wanted it.  heck yea nina! she was great and it was so good.
shoot, i can't get service like that at most of the higher end restaurants i go to.
my name is bryant baker and i using my wife's yelp to post this.

i went on a friday evening and am shocked how quickly i got seen . they literally had a bed for me after they saw my heart rate was up . the tech , x-ray tech and nurses well all so kind. even the doctors! eventually i got admitted into the hospital and the care i received was amazing. the nurses and techs were so patient with me and understanding . i am not used to that, i am used to people getting mad etc.  really enjoyed my nurses the first two days i was there. my tech was also amazing and brought me anything i needed . they work on unit 72 and if i ever have to come back i am going to ask to go back to unit 72. thank you guys for everything , out of all my years of living i never received great service from a hospital.

well they could not locate my baby for three hours but assured me he was somewhere upstairs. that's a good feeling after you give birth. 

while i was in labor the charge nurse was discussing a hispanic patient and said, "it's probably her tenth baby. you know how mexicans are." i won't deliver here again.

the billing office has guaranteed that i will never use or recommend any northside facility. i work in healthcare and had a marginal experience with the care provided here but it was made worse by the treatment received after discharge. the billing dept was rude, aggressive and lied to me. a manager called a week later to apologize for the employee but i would not recommend coming to northside for any treatment.

my mom has always bragged on northside hospital for all there wonderful staff . she was fortunate enough to have a great deliver with my little sister in 2013 at north-side women's center atlanta by her obgyn doctor. 
i myself being a 1st time mother and might i add that i'm a younger mother. this now being 2 weeks ago on march 31st. so during this time of the covid-19 and living in tn 2 weeks prior. i decided i needed to be near my mom if they put the stay in shelter, in place in which case they did. also i would need her for all her support for delivery. she was not aware of the decision i was making so i showed up and she was not impressed with the decision. being that my doctor was in tn. at this point she was seeking a home birth. i insisted to just get my records transferred . in which case i did contact a obgyn that's close in the area. i was able to get authorization documents signed to transfer doctors. but by me not making a 1st appt  which was 3 days away from the day my contractions and pre labor started i had not yet been approved to have that obgyn assigned for the delivery.

   i waited until i'm 7 cm and could go no longer managing the contractions on my own . i requested an epidural. this was the best decision . but right after it started to cause my blood pressure to rise and had to be medicated. prepped and i'm meet by my delivery midwife.in which my mom reiterates to the midwife  m.d claire a parker  that i am requesting delayed clamping of umbilical cord . i notice her demeanor towards us change." future notice pay attention to the spirit in which the delivery doctor is in" in my culture a new mothers aura should be one that is at peace and love for her newborn.''it wasn't''. i started pushing at 4:56pm .mind you i'm still on epidural drip . which should have been stopped the time i started pushing. i've looked into the normal push time for a 1st time mom and its estimated average 45 min to 3 hours . i was not ready for the stress that was put on me which helped spike my blood pressure to 168 while pushing, the mid wife m.d claire a parker  was horribly mean, no compassion. no understanding.  i was not given a chance to breath during the next push i mean she was not allowing me a chance. i would push be told to catch your breathe then push. but i'm literally wore out from the inability to pause for 1 minute to catch my breathe...she was over demanding. very rough on my vaginal she pushed on my stomach and vaginal with force when my baby was making his way . she even reached for scissors which were so not needed. i couldn't believe the moment i'm in . and i'm only 15 min into pushing . i stared at 4:56 and delivered at 5:22. my health was put at risk for the stress the midwife put on me. not being able to gather myself or strength for the next push. 
without my mom and very nice nurses kind touches assisting me i don't know what the outcome would have been. my vaginal was treated like who cares if she ever wants to look at herself in the mirror again. of course with the force used to push my sons head out which i did not push him out the doctor used both her hands around his head and push him out.even one of the nurses stated that hes doing it on his own " meaning he was at that point forcing himself out with the contractions and the push i was giving. that was not needed.
doesn't end there. she didn't want to allow him delayed clamping past 2 min i insisted 5 min.

horrible experience.

review:
this review is dedicated to my son, who is now at home and about one week-old.  looking back as parents who started a bit late in life, the decision to start a family, the actual pregnancy process, and labor and delivery all take a mental, physical, financial and emotional toll.  covid-19 does not make it easier for anyone.  in the end, it was all worth it! 

stanford valleycare was there for us all the way through, and i'm happy to give 5-stars for the ob (dr. adey) and labor and delivery department, especially all the nurses and assistants.  because of them we have our son!  shoutouts to india, jacque, brianna, jennifer, judy, geri, dr. phillips, dr. silverstein, kristen, suzanne, emily, maddie, elena, elaine, heather, yuke, lang, beth, kim,  becky, and lizet.  sorry if i left anyone off, since lots of folks helped out.

delivery room: why so many people to acknowledge?  my wife went through 4-days of labor induction that needed 24/7 care.  based on some recent blood tests, the doctors recommended we induce labor some 4-weeks ahead of the due date.  when there are conditions that can potentially harm the baby at full term, an ob may elect to use drugs, foley bulbs, and combinations to help dilate the cervix and trigger active labor.  they monitor fetal heart rate and mom's contractions continuously during this process.  the process is uncomfortable and sometimes painful, and can range from 2-hrs to 3 days, since every woman and pregnancy is different.  our efforts did not work out as expected, so we went for the c-section, regarded as a "nuclear option". the 4-day induction period was not a total waste, since baby still had time in the womb to grow and develop.

c-section: its sounds scary, but the planned c-section was fast (5-10 mins) and painless according to the wife.  the pain and recovery comes afterwards, since it is a major surgical procedure.  dr. adey did her magic to ensure a smooth delivery.  recovery is lots of rest and otc painkillers followed by light exercise and returning to a normal diet.

recovery: we got 3-days for recovery in the hospital, which gave me a bed to stay as well.  all meals for mom is free and delivered by room service, while for me it was $10/meal using vouchers.  it is during recovery where the baby rooms with us while mom recovers.  here, the baby will be poked, prodded, and tested to ensure good health prior to release.  as for the parents, you get a 2-3 day crash course in newborn care.  surprised we learned diaper changing, installing baby in car seat, burping, blanket swaddling, holding the baby, and feeding (finger feeding, breast feeding, breast-feeding with supplemental tube, and bottle formula feeding).  you'll learn how often and how much to feed.  for breastfeeding, they'll offer excellent lactation consultants and nurses who can also provide breast pumps.  don't worry if you have't picked out a pediatrician yet - the visiting staff pediatrician will help you administer tests, answer questions, and schedule postpartum tests until you choose a permanent one later.

overall:  highly recommend valleycare for labor and delivery.  free and fast wifi great to pass time during labor, and the nursing staff here is amazing.  pregnancy, labor, and delivery do not always go according to plan, so have faith and put your trust to the experts at valleycare.  thanks again to dr. adey for working her magic to deliver our son!
