just talk to your drawn station they need to draw when people show up for this is not the safe place to be or keep coming back too.  not only it's scary cause of the virus but i don't see anyone wipe down the chairs people sit in.  i will not sit in those dirty chair.  i'll stand.  the hospital should be spotless at all time and that means chair also.  i done and so over it!!
fac_name: St David's North Austin Medical Center

review:
after speaking with them about my review, nothing was resolved.  as you can see in the x ray, it is clearly a screw that can not be pushed back in, as it is threaded.  as a doctor, you should know the difference between a screw and a pin.  her trying to push it only caused extreme pain and was a stupid thing to do.  yet is was worth billing me $525?

the second pic of my leg shows how far it had backed out and why i went to the emergency room to have it removed.  i am now told such a thing was not an emergency..
fac_name: St David's North Austin Medical Center

review:
my daughter suffers from medical trauma so obviously the last place in the world that she wants to go to is the emergency room- especially during this time of covid-19. yesterday she was having severe chest and abdominal pain, something that she had been experiencing off and on for the past week, but it had reached such a point that she couldn't take it anymore. it was clear that she had a hernia (there was an obvious bulge). the doctor was an older man who did not take her seriously and repeatedly told her that she'll better if she stops drinking alcohol and eating fried food. she told him multiple times that she doesn't touch alcohol or fried/processed food. she stressed how worried she was and how much pain she was in and the doctor released her without any form of pain relief or information on what to do about the hernia. luckily tomorrow she will be seeing her family doctor who informed surgery may be required. 
this neglect is disgraceful and dangerous.
fac_name: St David's North Austin Medical Center

review: i'm grateful for the care i have received at st. david's medical center, 4th floor north. during this trying time i want to thank the doctors, nurses and additional medical personnel and staff for their service to our community. also maria for her exceptional cleaning skills and friendliness! she is a gem. please stay safe and healthy.
fac_name: St David's North Austin Medical Center

review: they have the worst customer service in the registrars office. they let the phone ring forever and immediately hang up without talking to you when they do pick up the phone. they never filed with the ss administration when my baby was born even though they are required to by the state of texas. they are paying people to do a job and billing patients thousands of dollars for it, but they don't even do the basics.
fac_name: St David's North Austin Medical Center

review: dr. arkadiy s stolyar......recently featured on the netflix documentary, "dirty money" for his part in extorting millions from an elderly man in belmont, ma.  if this place had any sense, they would fire him immediately.

this is a superb hospital. most staff are amazing. there are a few, very few that prevented the five star rating. the emergency department does an amazing job and considering the virus, kept everyone separated. the floor staff is phenomenal on all shifts. the meals are made to order and they do things beyond what's on the menu. i love their cheese omelet although their menu doesn't mention an omelet. just ask. when i had a 911 emergency i requested to be brought here.

i would rather die than have to deal with this hospitals billing department again. insurance paid in full and the lazy worthless billing department of this sub par hospital can't seem to get it sorted out. no level of customer service at all with these folks.

my mother has had to be seen in the er for heart problems several times. even before covid-19, the wait times were awful. she went in today for an injury. despite her asking them to call me with information, and my own attempts to call them, i got no information  even after 6 hours. the communication at this place is the absolute worst, and i can say that because i'm a medical professional myself (over 30 years) and i know what the standard is. avoid.

nurses and anesthesiologists at labor and delivery where wonderful. thank you to cathy, gizzel, baby nurse caisa who was the main reason we were able to leave the hospital early since we needed our son to have one more test before we could be discharged, and she cane and did it herself and made sure the results where processed fast! they have honestly been the sweetest and most caring nurses i've ever had.. 

only wish the hospital could provide them better ppe.. for being a trauma 4 nicu, not one of them where given n95 masks... hence the 4 stars.. st david's needs to take better care of their wonderful staff!

this review is not about quality of care. if it were a life-or-death situation, i would go to st. david's if i was nearby. 

this review is about customer service and billing. i had an elective and scheduled surgery at st. david's in dec. 2018. the surgery was considered preventative, and under the aca should have been covered at 100%.

i called both my insurance and the hospital ahead of time to confirm.

well, the surgery was covered, but st. david's snuck in a whole bunch of facility fees and charges for routine but mandatory tests (i.e., a pregnancy test) that they require before performing a surgery. the charges came out to almost $3,000 for an out-patient operation that my insurance had already paid 10's of thousands of dollars for. 

i sent my bill back for review multiple times, but finally set up a payment plan for it, because it seemed like i had no other recourse. over a year later, i've barely scratched the surface of paying it off even though they did reduce the amount some based on my income.

customer service has been no help at all. they tell me to call my insurance. my insurance tells me to call the hospital. and no one i talk to seems to have any answers at all.

this seems criminal to me. st. david's has found a loophole in the law and they are exploiting it. they were paid for my operation. yet they are holding me hostage for an amount of money that is trivial for them, but massive for me. my only option is either paying money i shouldn't owe under the law or having that debt sent to collectors that could harass me for the rest of my life.

it's absolute madness, and i blame st. david's for engaging in this type of billing scheme.

my boyfriend had a heart procedure by dr. gallinghouse(he did wonderful ..thank you from the bottom of my heart)on june 17th and stayed the night at this location. i wish i wrote down all of his nurses names, but if you were on room 688 on june 17th-18th you were all so amazing, kind, helpful, gracious, had good personalities, knowledgeable....i could go on and on! i told one of the girls how impressed i was by her and the other girls that i'd met and she replied "we really love our job" and i believe her. thank you ladies!!! i was also nervous being in an hospital during these weird times, but from the second i pulled up...the valet, temp taker, security, front desk, cafeteria staff, random nurses i'd ask directions from....everyone was so pleasant and you'd never know they were probably exhausted and on edge(i know i would be) thank you everyone at this location for making a very uncomfortable situation comfortable

hi everybody... so yesterday i drove in to austin for pre surgery with my surgeon dr elizabeth potter plastic surgeon and wow what a righteous bitch. i knew she thought she was the best surgeon and had a complex of being superior but i let that slide until yesterday. i went into her office and told her how i was feeling about my implants how they didn't look good. now this is after my total dmx a year ago and six months after she put these horrible silicone implants in. i was now going for another surgery which would make six surgeries in one year complications infections blah blah blah. and i wanted to let her know how i was feeling and she took it so personally which she should and got so defensive. she looked at me and said i think they look great... and then i said to her elizabeth potter and she freaked out and said what do you say? i then said dr. potter and she goes ok! so then she proceeds to say i think you should come back again next week and we can revisit all that we have said today a week before surgery. i told her i live in houston and i rented a car to drive to austin for this appointment and she said well i guess you'll have to do it again. so needless to say i am furious at this moment and made the appointments and left. as i'm driving home i'm thinking this is bullshit i don't have to use this doctor i know i was excited to switch these implants out in two weeks but fuck i'll find a doctor in houston which is a really better for me anyway because i live there. i was just using her because when i had cancer i was in austin. anyway... i just thought st david's hospital should know what kind of doctor is  practicing there!!  please avoid dr. elizabeth potter at all costs!! on an up note... st  david's hospital is a wonderful hospital and they have treated me well.

this is one of the worst hospitals we've ever used. we will never go back. my wife has been neglected for hours at a time. using call button does nothing. a few of her nurses have been nice but still don't help her when she needs it. it reminds me of those nursing home horror stories.

just called to check on having blood work done the guy i talked was rude and really ignorant!!!! get some decent people to work there would not recommend this place to anyone period. not the first time this has happened.
worst hospital i've ever been to. their staff don't give a shit and don't care about the patients here. there's barely anyone here! why?? because they know not to come here or they might die.
such a disgusting facility.  don't even bring people to die here, the staff and antiquated facilities are deplorable.

my family loves having a hospital close to us.  we have utilized the hospital multiple times for my husband and myself.  there is one thing that we would like them to change.  the tv channels are very limited and actually doesn't have very good programs for families.  the news channels is cnn which is not preferred in this area.  fox news is what most like here.  please consider adding more family programs & the fox news channel.
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: i used to live in florida, and this was the closest, a couple of times i had to go there, in the er they rarely checked on me. one time i was admitted for a night because they thought i had a mini stroke, they did not even check on me. they even put on an intermittent pneumatic compression (ipc)  and it was never turned on. yep, good ol' times! my then boyfriend now my husband had to go there several times, and i went to accompany him, the treatment for him was 5 stars!!!! i had several opportunities to make sure it was not a "well maybe they were having a bad day" excuse. now, this is the kicker we are both hispanics both college educated, he is white blue eyed with an english last name and good health insurance. and me well i look different and at that time for a few months had medicaid. things have changed now, my insurance is amazing and so is my job and he is under my insurance. i often wonder if moved back to florida and i went there what would happen. again i had plenty of chances to compare! and oh by the way no neurologist ever saw me ‍
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review: i was a patient here for 3 days and two nights last july.  during that time i continued to wear the clothes i came in wearing.  i was not offered a gown or any personal care items.  the nurses were very mean.  i was hooked up to an iv and asked for assistance to use the restroom.  the nurse came in and yanked the machine's plug out of the wall and told me to go into the restroom.  i am not a medical professional; how was i to know the machine could be unplugged?  hire some nurses that are not afraid to smile for fear of cracking their faces.  get rid of the hospitalist archibald.  she basically does not have time for patients either.
fac_name: St. Vincent's Medical Center Clay County

review:
i was taken into emergency room, becuase i  flipped riding a atv and had  pretty bad scars. my right shoulder was extremely injured. i wanted to say thank you to the staff, as soon as the registration began the transition was smooth. going from my bed then to take my ct scans and x-rays. every department was friendly and they made sure  that i wasn't in any pain.. and yes i did break my collar bone. kristine my charged nurse was very passionate and i appreciate her nurse etticit!

thank you again kaiser!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Moreno Valley Medical Center

review: the worst care i've experienced. they just discharged my 89 yr old mother with her foley catheter still in place, no discharge papers or instructions, she has bedsores on her back and ankles and after a shit show of a discharge we get home and she still has a pic line in her arm. it's bad enough you can't be with your loved ones but worse when you find that the care they got was inexcusable
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Moreno Valley Medical Center

review:
my friend (transgender woman with bipolar disorder) stayed at cedar hills hospital. they are terrible. their staff has clearly had zero training on how to treat transgender patients. my friend was denied medical care because she spoke up when a doctor misgendered her. the following day, a patient called her the f-slur and still the staff suggested she needed to "use her coping skills." thankfully she spoke up, refused to stay another day, and we got her out before they could do any more damage.

staff has a high turnover and are not paid enough. the food is made with exploitative prison labor. their coronavirus safety procedures are almost nonexistent. every therapist is a contractor from somewhere else. just a complete shitshow all around.

my friend would likely be dead from her time at cedar hills if it weren't for her pre-existing coping mechanisms and her wide support network. fuck this place. if your friend is having a mental health emergency, please do not send them here.

every worker at this hospital needs to go on #generalstrike, and the bosses who run this place should be tried in criminal court.

i wish i could put zero stars. dr neha gauri held me against my will agter i came in voluntary and was told i could leave at any time if i decided their facility wasn't right for me. against my will and against the entire staff of rns, she placed me on a medical hold without ever examining or talking to me because i asked to leave! upon arrival we were told many things and they were all false. the nursing staff was very nice and helpful, and they were just following orders, but "dr" gauri went out of her way to be spiteful and make my life hell. threatened me and hung up on my wife. absolutely ridiculous. i came in looking for help and was dismissed and essentially kidnapped for 17 hrs. when a real dr showed up the next day, it was determined in less than 5 minutes that it was the wrong fit for me and i was released shortly thereafter. she should have her medical license revoked and should not be allowed around patients. this was a horrible and traumatic experience for me, and soured me on the entire mental health system. pretty sad when i needed help and was treated so poorly. very disappointed doesn't even scratch the surface.

worst hospital experience.  left in more pain than i came. nurse straight up lied to me.  "you will get something for the pain before you leave.  as i'm leaving "no we would never allow that for that procedure"..... then don't tell me... on top of being told i would be conscious for the procedure . . they put me to sleep!

.... get this when they brought me into the exam room.  they forgot i was there till after shift change

is there no chain of command? 

is there no notes? 

does everyone get to say whatever they want?

5/19/2020: i went up there for my medications, and what an awesome l.a. day, and everything went so smoothly. i even found someone who hadn't heard one of my corny jokes. :-)

5/19/2020: although they said they'd remove the paranoia note, they didn't. if they think i'm delusional about a danger here with a prowler going through my mail and all the rest back to when i moved in (the ransacking 'plumber' the lady next door gave me the number for, the guy across the way w/ intimidation after the flood, my brother yelling and breaking stuff, him jumping my locked gate, the handsome undercover felon/cop from al-anon, the beautiful al-anon thief, cops with my dad setting me up for an abusive psych. hold + "cracker" at my birth hospital,... ), why do they choose to believe that i'm not honest about the obvious lack of safety? my feeling of lack of safety is up to an unsafe hospital?

-----------"bradly g smith, a 58 y.o. male, presents with chest pain (and palpitations. sent by dr. r. johnson pgr 34295. +nausea ); psychiatric evaluation (paranoia, (not feeling safe at home)); and diarrhea (hx of c-diff)"-----------------

this is far and away the best care i've had. they figured out some stuff that has been vexing my doctors for a very long time, and they figured out what works to make it better, and i will continue that as an outpatient. 

i met some truly amazing employees and assistants that made the long stay less difficult, and of course nothing's perfect. 

these are the issues i ran into:

the worst were that they took me off of an important antibiotic before my course here was done and the bad infection came back, and i told them how many i had left, but they said i tested 'negative' for c. diff, so they didn't know what was causing symptoms, so in preparation for a colonoscopy/biopsy to find out, i had to go through the empty, super-sweet 'calories' only to find out it was hiding all along (as they do if not fully treated), and because of admit and delay, i had to have two covid tests, and the second one was pushed harder than the first and i bled like the dickens, and it was totally unnecessary since the procedure was cancelled due to the c. diff misdiagnosed/'hiding' as 'negative'; they immediately took me off of my heart pill because they thought i was bleeding (?), but when they realized i wasn't it wasn't restarted, so i needlessly went into afib for the third time at three hospitals;

strike that, my mistake, starting at a hospital very near where i live almost exactly one year ago, it's been four needless atrial fibrillations (plus a hypovolemic shock) at three hospitals. i still wonder if my healthcare killed partner is in there keeping my ticker going with love. four plus the shock in one year - jeez! 

[cont.] the menu doesn't match my super healthy diet causing some digestion issues; the night crew made it needlessly impossible to sleep (ignoring alarms...), it was not possible to heal like that, but the good people's work is not in vain: we know mostly what is wrong and what works, and i hope to get infusions whenever needed (i don't mind driving, & i'll bite the bullet on parking), w/ appropriate follow up w/ teams.

lastly, and this is minor, in my online portal for results, programs, ... there is a mindfulness research project with an upcoming webinar series that is advertised as open to the public, but when i go through all the pages to get to the registration page, the page fails with just blank, no error, so i looked under and it says an internal server error, but if i clear the cache while there and refresh, bam! the page loads for about one second and is of course unusable - the 'errored' server can serve, just too reluctantly.

what is with healthcare anymore? some incredible wonderful lights surrounded by the worst most abusive 'humanity' has to offer. i thought i missed a call from the main coordinator, dr. napolitano, but to just leave a message was difficult with multiple calls and numbers, and bad phone people, and again a woman giving me a hard time about my last name. i'll start faxing my birth certificate in advance.

best surgeons in the world!! yet, recovery on 2nd floor was like being in a 3rd world country, frightening.

nursing staff is negligent and indifferent.  it was a surreal experience.  

we had been warned that ucla ronald reagan hospital is as bad as the reviews, but didn't believe it,  given that ucla santa monica surgical center is a+

i believe my husband's recovery was set back by the poor care he received on 2nd floor overnight stay. 

by the way ucla admin, care partners were caring and kind.  care partners were working very hard to do the job of cnas and cover duties which are beyond their training.  

while nurses are laughing loudly and literally on fb huddled up making in appropriate jokes about covid-19, care partners are checking ivs,  monitors, vitals, responding to alarms, and answering nurse call buttons??? 

this is a management problem, it comes from the top.  hospital administrators are weak and incompetent.  

the best surgeons have no support.  shame on hospital administrators at ronald reagan ucla hospital.  how many bad reviews do you need to see before believing the patients?

the worst place to be. literally feeling suicidal and they just letting me go. they literally have a floor for mental patients and instead they rather have that patient go home. they could at least that person stay in the er over night then send them up in the morning . they don't care about other people only their wallet. how can this place say they care for other people. literally the worst hospital ever. they make ucla look bad. they don't take mental illness serious.

huge shout out to dr. kuo for masterfully orchestrating a tee and an electrical cardioversion with incomparable bedside manner. he devoted a great deal of time, effort, and care to ensure that everything was executed flawlessly and he succeeded. thank you from the bottom of my heart, pun intended.

like almost every other person who has written about ronald reagan medical center i am disgusted and disappointed. after being treated there for 18 months for a rare cancer they literally can't get a simple but extremely important imaging test scheduled. even while they are madly advertising and sending emails to their 'loyal patients' that it's safe to get care there during the covid 19 pandemic we aren't buying. we've learned your organization is cold and utterly devoid of any humanity. i'll find another hospital to perform my routine follow up pet scan while i search for another oncologist. since no one at ucla health cares about anything but their phony reputations i thought i'd direct my comments to the absentee hospital and health system leaders.

i was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis and itp at 19 in 2014. was in and out of the hospital for 5 years, recurved my liver transplant there in 2018. that next year i had a splenic infection and typhoid cancer removed. i was treated with more care than i could have ever hoped for. the nurses felt more like friends. doctors went above and beyond for me. still they follow up with me with care and concern. i will forever be biased that this is the best hospital in the world and saved my life numerous of times. yes, the er can be slow to get into sometimes (which hospital doesn't have a long er wait) but once you're in, it's the best care.

we had a horrible experience in the er a few weeks ago.  the manager of the er, claudina torres, spoke pejoratively about patients in spanish as she walked down the hall.  she was very rude and abrupt as she spoke to the filipino patients.  she obviously does not like filipinos.  after waiting in the er for nearly 24 hours, she offered me a bed in the 10 bed unit.  when i refused, she became hostile and aggressive.  there is a blatant racial problem within ucla.  her last name had tape over it, but an employee told me her name was claudina torres.  claudina torres is a racist and she is being supported by the people she works for who allow her racist behavior to continue.  all minorities should stop getting healthcare at ucla.  the er needs a new manager !!

i searched her name and she's done the same thing before.  she received a previous review on yelp.  on may 15, 2019 cyndy s. wrote the following:

we were disappointed with our er visit.  we understand that there are more patients than beds, doctors, and nurses.  it is a busy hospital, so we knew we would have to wait, but we did not appreciate the lack of respect we received.  the manager of the er, claudina t. (i got her name from an employee) was walking through the hall and said to another employee in spanish that, "we have too many filipinos here tonight." how can people get quality healthcare while being blatantly disrespected.  someone needs to explain to her the enormous amount of money that ucla gets from the filipino community each year.  we have other choices for our healthcare; therefore, we will not be spending our money at ucla for future healthcare needs.  further, someone needs to tell the idiot, claudina t., that many people speak spanish.  this is not a magnet hospital.

i feel very conflicted about my experience as a patient at ucla in the epilepsy monitoring unit nearly twenty years ago. because i had just had a brain injury i don't remember much and i tried to get a copy of my veeg because i noticed that the doctor's written report didn't look right. they only had the tracing, but no video portion. those records need to be kept longer for situations like mine because it looks like the doctor lied because his verbal statements to my parents at the time and the eeg don't match his written report or the eeg during the pet scan or my symptoms at the time or for the past twenty years.

i had my liver transplant there 17 years ago and had no complaints - except i thought the food was terrible. i spent 6 months there - several weeks here and there, but mostly there. a few years later i had part of intestines and appendix removed and had a good stay. still bad food. haha.

i honestly have never written a negative review. however; i am so completely disappointed in the way we were treated at tri-city hospital. i birthed all 3 of my kids at this hospital.
this week one of my adult kids had a traumatic scooter accident. we got our services at the er. my son ruptured his achilles tendon severely! the impact was so bad that the skin burst open on impact. this is a 6'3" young man, athlete. dr. amory did not prescribe pain meds, my son had to ask for help with his severe, 8,9,10 pain level! he cleaned the rupture and sewed the skin shut and sent him home. after this accident, as my son did not have a primary dr. due to the fact that he 'healthfully' has never needed to use those services. as we circled back around to establish a primary dr. and urgently trying to get him into surgery for this achilles tendon complete tear, we were lost on an island with zero support, call back, checking on pain meds and level of pain. zero support! when i called the dr. office of dr. amory i was met with a no, i cannot get a call back from dr. amory, he is not on call and your son is not one of his office patience. yes, i agreed, however; could he please call me for a minute consultation as a dr. who saw this trauma and wound. i was told from the oportator at his practice that he was not on call and if he called dr. amory when he was not on call, 'he would be so pissed off'. wow, every option we had to contact, er. dr. amory's office, primary care dr. and the pending orthopedic office for surgery was literally shut in our face! in the meantime, my sons pain medicine was down to the last dosage, and he was in writhing pain. we had exhausted all the medical support we never had. we had to resort to calling a friend who had some pain medication to get my son through the night without tears. i will never forget how unhelpful all these professionals treated us! 

i hope nobody else in trauma and pain has to experience this horrible service and apathy, where not one professional was willing to do anything but pass the buck and offer zero comforts and support, complete apathy. this is a zero star rating!

to summarize before you read the following book- i, a pregnant woman in my second trimester with a serious heart condition, was blatantly disregarded and lied to for 6 hours.

went in for severe cramping (14 weeks pregnant) and heartbeat abnormalities (heart disease)

when we arrived we were told to find a friend to watch our daughter because covid, but that spouse could stay with me. found friend to watch daughter. came back two hours later and "rules" had changed- now spouse could not come in with me (so daughter could have stayed with him outside instead of us running around trying to find childcare. that's pretty f'd up.) okay, fine. but there were other couples together inside (?!?!) then, they didn't tell me how to check in so i sat inside for 30 minutes without anyone taking my information. okay... fine.

an hour went by, they took my blood and sent me back outside. (edwin, staff member, is amazing. he is half the reason this isn't a 1 star review.)

two hours went by and i had an ultrasound. (julianna, staff, is the other reason this isn't 1 star. she may be the kindest person i've ever met.)
back outside.

five hours later no one had checked my heart. we watched patients check in and be discharged while we just sat there and at no point was the emergency room busy. i've been to packed emergency rooms and never experienced this.

after being asked for insurance details for the third time (tricare, pretty simple stuff) we left. we asked if they would give us a call if they found anything serious and they said no... but they did call! to ask if we left.. an hour after we'd left.

i'd quite literally rather die on my way somewhere else then take my chances here again.

note: tri city hospital itself is a fine hospital. however their er is outdated in the way it treats patients. wait times usually exceed 4 to 7 hours as you suffer in need of a doctor. everything about this er is dissapointing. triage & intake is so unprofessional.  
scripps encinitas on the otherhand is a welcoming er with a caring triage & intake second to none and wait times often less than an hour to 2 hours. private rooms and a great staff. clean and modern surroundings. they care about you & for you!!!!

i want to thank all the staff for making my horrific pain feel better.  all the staff from the ones that first check you in, the ones who drew my blood, the nurses for being so kind . i had a great experience.  tri city has a bad reputation but you can't go by what other people say.  i will definitely recommend this hospital to anyone.  thanks again to all of you who are putting your life's at risk during these harsh times to make everyone feel better. you sure made my life better.

amazing maternity! wow 5 out of 5. they were an all star staff. i loved it here! i had such an amazing experience. i had an emergency c section and the surgeon even sewed my ab muscles back together. she saved me thousands of dollars in cosmetic fees. i am so grateful i came here. i loved everyone. i felt so great during my time here. they treated me with so much kindness and love.

if i could give a zero i would. well i understand all the necessary coughing due to the covid-19 i do not understand how they cannot keep a spouse updated. i also understand hipaa regulations however i dropped him off at the emergency room left my phone number have called twice for an update and being told that they can't give me any information. so i can't stay with him his phone is at home because it was an emergency i wasn't thinking about getting a cellphone. common sense would tell you if i dropped him off and i was with him mind you i would have stayed if it wasn't for all the precautions right now i would be in the room with him so i can talk to the doctor. all it takes is for the nurse to get up off her ass and go ask him if it's okay to give me information.

prior to covid-19, we have had a lot of interactions with tri-city medical center and they all have left us wondering what "po-dunk" "back-water" "c-hole dump" do we live in?!?  this "medical center" was built over 50 years ago.  much of it will collapse in a moderate earthquake (well known). the horrific past and current management spent over $30 million building an office building they can't use. we have had experience with many departments and many doctors and many in the er and both in- and out-patient surgical areas.  sadly, there are a good number of very good doctors and nurses, but there are way, way too many other horrific providers and nurses.  sadly, the best and brightest are the folks they bring in on temp contracts - the "traveler" mds and rns are awesome! then you have the horrific whack-job nutters with personality disorders and clearly show psych issues who turn out to be hired directly by the hospital.  after five years of this we have had so much experience that it is clearly a dump!  when the er rn's (it may take 8-12 hours to get in pre-covid 19) say "oh no, i'd go someplace else" that says a lot.  this place is a dump and pick an insurance and provider and medical group that does not work with this dump!  it is horrific!  five years of horror stories. want to hear them, can tell you a lot more!

i gave birth to my son at this hospital in february and would 100% give birth here again. every nurse that i had made this experience as comfortable as possible for me and listened to my needs. dr. mccullough delivered my baby and did such an amazing job. she made the entire birth experience enjoyable and thrilling by being upbeat and positive the entire time.

the other thing i enjoyed was the blueberry pancakes from room service! the chef made really good food which is rare for a hospital! 

littleton adventist was great and i will definitely consider delivering at this hospital again with my future children.

was not impressed with the level of service at lah. sent to er for a cat scan when i had a ski accident at keystone & was determined i had a fracture. sent to lah er as keystone can't do cat scan. was determined multiple fractures, er doctor who i saw for maybe a minute and was not very forthcoming with info (and found out when i got the bill was out-of-network). needed overnight hospital stay turning into 2. arrived in er at 6pm finally in bed at 10pm; was offered a snack so i could take pills. next morning was never offered a menu; after not eating all day the day before because of tests i was fairly hungry, at 9:30am i asked do they offer something to eat here? shouldn't that be part of the nurses duty to make sure you are fed? was told that the assigned doctor would come and see me the next morning (i never saw him but in notes it indicated he evaluated my case and spent time with me, i wanted to see him but he never stopped in). instead a team of a few came in and in front of me were discussing my injuries and were disagreeing amongst each other in front of the patient, does not give you a warm fuzzy. the occupational therapist who assisted me with a shower gave me wrong instructions for my injury of a position i was not supposed to do. i had to stay an additional day since i was not able to complete my pt successfully. i asked the next day again to see the doctor, instead his pa came in and was very thorough but still did not understand that i had 4 fractures, not 3 (why am i explaining this to the pa)? the doctor that discharged me (wound up being out-of-network, extra cost to me) after i had just saw a pa in-network?? why do i have to pay out-of-network costs, it was during the week and i just saw a pa that was in network? i was shocked at the costs, the bills keep pouring in. kind of strange the total amount and of that how much is over the customary acceptable charges (don't get that). the positive experience was i had a great physical therapist; most of the nurses provided good care and a couple not sure why they are in nursing.

i had the absolute best experience at this hospital giving birth to my 2nd baby on april 1, 2020. with all this craziness going about the pandemic, i was super nervous to (1) give birth in general (2) not be able to have a support person due to visitor restrictions (3) be in the hospital amongst all the sickness and whatnot. 

i got there at about 10:15am, got screened right at the entrance, got wheeled up to the 3rd floor and brought straight to my room where i was monitored and checked to see how far dilated i was. regina (i don't really remember if this was her name but i hope it is - it for sure started with a r) was my labor & delivery nurse and she was there with me through my entire labor & delivery and she was amazing. she was very attentive and caring and made me feel very comfortable in a very uncomfortable situation. i could go on and on about how great it was to have her as my nurse because she really was just the sweetest person. 

i gave birth around 2pm and got transferred to the recovery wing around 4pm. i had amazing nurses over there as well. melissa, fe, jordan, shawna are the names that i could remember and they were all extremely nice and took very good care of me. they made sure i always had anything that i needed and also took care of my fiancé's needs as well. 

i'm honestly so happy that i chose scripps mercy as my hospital to give birth. i had a better experience here than i did when i gave birth to my 1st child.
i just delivered my baby at this hospital and it was amazing.the all nurses and doctors in labor and delivery and postpartum were so nice and professional.

while i've found an incredible doctor at scripps mercy, (sup, dr p?!), it hasn't always been my favorite when it comes to physicians. i've had some decent ones in the past and i had one in particular that really got under my skin - moving on...

all in all, great hospital that has always been very quick to accommodate and get me in as fast as they can. whether that's to see a doctor, a np, or to get an x-ray, it's never been a long process. 

parking is free when validated if you park below the facility and there are several pharmacies that surround the hospital making meds easy to receive in one quick trip.

the er was so great to me in the early hours of this morning. i apparently have a kidney stone and they were so kind and efficient. my doctor dr. remington explained what was going on and was so compassionate. nurse iday was tireless i'm getting me everything i needed to feel comfortable. everyone else was great too - from admitting nurse mary and her team of chris and jacob at the front desk to the helper lorraine and the registration rep janet everyone was terrific. i was very impressed and grateful. thank u team so much!
i also wanted to give a thank u for another dr. who came into specifically explain what a kidney stone was and it's likely process. he was so clear and easy to understand i felt i could have written a paper on it after he was done. i don't remember his name but he deserves to be given a shout out as well.

quite a dirty place, actually, filthy! having been to various other hospitals, i can make a comparison on how dedicated each is to providing a safe environment for patients. scripps mercy comes short. bathrooms: gross; floors: looks like they don't mop. floor was so sticky in areas, my shoe stuck. this is important because we are in the middle of a world wide pandemic where sanitation is key to containing the spread of covid 19. if target, costco & supermarkets can see the necessity to continuously disinfect during these days, then why can't this hospital? after all, isn't  this the place where people go when they are sick and contagious? a close look will reveal that the grime isn't new, but rather built up over time, clearly indicating neglect. they need better housekeepers!

in spite of the above, the medical & nursing care was actually good and am pleased with the outcome. recovering well.

be careful with your possessions at this hospital. my father was admitted due to a dangerous drug interaction. thankfully, medical treatment was good, but the costco gift card that was in his wallet was missing. his driver's license was not returned to him before leaving the hospital, so we were told it would be mailed to us, but never received it. disappointing to know, when you're in a debilitated state, in a hospital, your possessions can just disappear.

so my mom was in the er earlier this week while simultaneously my dad was having serious symptoms of covid 19. i called several times to warn to them that my mom may need to be tested and to take proper precautions. the operator had a serious attitude with me. as my dads symptoms progressed the next day to shortness of breath he called to see how he can safely arrive to the er without possibly infecting anyone else. they gave him another number to call the next day and very rudely asked if i was a health care professional. they deterred my dad from getting treatment and then called him to pick my mother up. he let them know he was sick and they insisted he come get her. guess what he was admitted to another hospital with pneumonia and tested positive for covid the next day. they never tested my mother. this is very poor decision making on their part. very disappointed in the attitude we received and lack of information or help.

worst hospital i have ever encountered and believe me when i tell you i've dealt with most . there actions today towards a client who was transported by ambulance was grossly mistreated and discharged . complete negligence on there part yet they never take responsibility . you call trying to talk to someone in charge, someone emphatic but all you get is people completely desensitized to human suffering . and when you call them out they make it clear they dont care.  they shift blame on to the medics or the doctor and in the meantime you have a 66 year old patient in terrible condition fall between the cracks.  that person is an alcoholic who is now facing the physical consequences of that drinking . but in no way does that make her less worthy of the proper care . even when you send detailed msg to relay to the doctor or nurse it gets shoved off to the side . they consider that person a frequent flyer and dismiss them. what they did today to this person is uncinsiouable and negligent yet they not only refuse to take responsibility , they get an attitude as if your bothering them yet someone that needs assistance gets none . i'm so disgusted with this hospital and it's not the first time or even the third time .... it's an ongoing issue with scripps mercy and the lack of empathy and medical attention and details they care nothing for.  i'm horrified by this hospital and there staff. one bad experience after another and there actions today were pure negligence . please if you have a loved one that needs care, avoid that hospital if you can. ucsd is around the corner and the difference is day and night. i have expressed gratitude towards those on the front lines but i have no respect for this hospital, the majority of the staff and the complete lack of professionalism of there staff . i keep filing complaints on behave of my friend but nothing changes . worst hospital ever

truly the worst experience of my life at this hospital. i had a vitamin lodged in my throat. emts who originally picked me up we're extremely rude and gave me major attitude. all they did was check my vitals and scold me for coughing on one of them. told me i didn't have a pill lodged in my throat, just the sensation of one. that it had probably dissolved and that it was just a scar from when it was there. they told me my heavy breathing and coughing was making it worse. when i finally was admitted to the hospital, they told the nurses this. instead of listening to me (ya know the patient in pain) they took their word. i could tell they weren't taking me seriously and laughing at me. until, they tried to give me medicine with water and i couldn't swallow it. must have been there for at least an hour before they realized this. then suddenly, they realized maybe i wasn't exaggerating. after a cat scan, they did see that i had a pill lodged in my throat still. they performed an emergency surgery to have removed. i went into the emergency room at 2am, didn't see the doctor until 7am and i didn't have the surgery to remove it until 8am. woke up at 8:45am and they had finally removed it. they told me the doctor wanted to see me and she would discharge me. she never even showed up to talk to me. finally at 1:30pm my girlfriend and i made the nurse discharge me. now i have an outrageous bill that i have to figure out how to pay and i actually have decent insurance. can't imagine what this would be like for someone with terrible or no insurance. it could bankrupt you. anyways all this is to say the fact that i didn't have the emergency surgery i needed earlier is true disgrace. i'm lucky i could hold on and breathe (though it was like death) the entire time. i could have died and it was sad, i should have felt properly cared for and not like everything was taking so long. i hope i never have to go back to this hospital.

at first they pretended to care! but beware of the phony two- faced lying girl they'll send in the end to be the final blow. the er " dr" was absent at best,useless is a better fit. they gave me bad medicine it almost killed me.the nurse was pretty good, but they were giving her a hard time for not having their obnoxious attitude. this hospital had dust and dander (or whatever it was)visible on the tv screen and the hazardous materials were hanging out of the trash can in the room! so they are not even cleaning the rooms. don't trust this place.  the "dr" must be trying to make up some credits doing his intern at the er and acted like he could care less. they over medicated me and i nearly had a heart attack. you leave feeling worse then when you made the horrible mistake of ending up at scripps mercy. i think they tried to kill me. so if your feeling ill, any other hospital would definitely be a wise choice. unless you are someone who is a glutten for punishment. thank you everyone for taking care of me tonight. the staff was exceptional. tonight was the first time i went to henry ford wyandotte er. i felt the care i received was top notch quality. everyone, including the techs, registration clerks, rn, and the doctors, were all friendly and professional.  i appreciate you. air hugs all around. stay safe.

i would give them a negative score if i could.  
if you are going there without good insurance, don't go there. they don't inform or explain the total cost of my surgery before i pay. i went there for a surgery knowing that my insurance wouldn't cover me and inquired about the full price of the surgery multiple times before i went there. the day i went to have the surgery i asked the check-in assistant three times (during check-in, before i pay, and after i pay) about the total expenses giving that i don't have insurance coverage, she told me i only need to pay $850 upfront. six months later, i received another billing from the hospital asking for $900+ more. i called them and filed a dispute. however, the administrative staff of this hospital were not very helpful in explaining and getting back to me during the dispute. firstly,  they asked me to call (not transfer) three different places/departments to find people to talk with. secondly, they consistently asked me to call my insurance company after i told them that i knew my insurance doesn't cover the surgery, and even after i explained to them via the phone. thirdly, they never apologized to me for not providing the whole picture of the billing before my surgery. instead, they held a very condescending attitude and said to me there was no point arguing about whether they told me the whole price or not, i still owe them money and have to pay. i had no choice but paid them the other $900+.  
in summary, this hospital tends to persuade their patients to do a surgery without telling them how much they should expect to pay. i am very disappointed about my experience there and i will never go back there again. please consider my experience if you are thinking about going to this hospital.

my husband at 56 years old has a major heart attack. his heart stopped 12 miles from the hospital. the paramedics were amazing. dr. robert wang, the interventional cardiologist was amazing. the er staff was amazing, the local ambulance, green pond, the paramedics, the nurses the cardiac icu....were all providing top notch care for which i remain grateful. my husband is fine thanks to their speed, sense of urgency and professionalism. i have never experienced anything less there and i will be grateful forever. never underestimate this hospital because morristown is close. i felt i had the same physicians, closer to home, and the skill and talent level was without comparison. thank you st. clare's, thank you dr. wang, thank you to his assistants, the paramedics and the local ambulance. you are amazing

yesterday at the request of my mother's doctor my mother and i donned our masks, got her wheelchair, and went to the east doors to take her for her infusion. we were met by a nurse and security guard both without any mask or gloves, the nurse leaned over my very ill and aged mother breathing on her, while the unprotected security guard insisted only he could take her upstairs. i can understand my not being allowed in right now due to covid-19. however, when her appointment had run 5 hours instead of 2-3 i went back to the doors to inquire as no one on at the cancer center was answering their phone, and they had a message setup that they aren't taking voicemail messages to call anyone back. two different people without protective equipment are present. not only that, but when i got upset that no one can find out anything for me, he throws me out and calls for more security. i had already explained that my mother's memory is shot and she can't remember my cell number to call me in the parking lot when her appointment is over. i had also explained that her cell phone had been left in the car, but was dead and she wouldn't be able to call it either, and there is no one else she can call. the staff couldn't care less. the extra security rolled up in an suv, as i am walking to my car to do whatever they thought they would do. that security person was able to do what the guy inside insisted is not possible...find out why my mother's appointment had run so long and find out was she hospitalized now. however when my mother was returned about an hour later, the person bringing her wore no protective gear. this placed both me and my mother at risk and i am very disappointed. i called the security desk this morning to file a formal complaint and i will take video of all future interactions. a very poor experience indeed!
just an update, i never received my medical records even after filling out the form on their website. shocker.

i visited a close friend there about a month ago.  they allowed me a 1-hour visit, where i had to empty my pockets and hand over my phone to reception before going in.  visitors are allowed in a lobby that looked like a cafeteria with a lot of tables and chairs.

when talking to my friend in the lobby, she said that her roommate was on her 4th week of ect (shock treatment) that was administered 3-times a week. she stated that her roommate was screaming mad that she could not remember anything, and the only emotion she could feel was anger.  i saw 3-patients in the visitation room sitting in a semi-fetal position with their visitors - their heads curled down with visitor stroking their heads lightly. scary place to be with an active shock treatment ward in place.

this was my very first psychiatric hospital i was ever in-patient about one year ago. i was hospitalized for suicidal ideation. despite the fact that the nurses who interviewed me were very nice i unfortunately cannot say about the other healthcare workers. i was put in the lowest functioning unit; basically i feel as if i were put with other patients who had more severe mental disorders than i did so i felt like my safety was at risk. my roommate suffered from severe psychosis. now, i know that the nurses cannot control whom you are paired with as your temporary roommate but i feel like they should group certain people with alike mental disorders. my roommate was so scary, i requested a room change. yet, they ignored me. and in general, the staff kept treating me with a very stigmatizing atmosphere. kept avoiding me like the plague as if i were to go mental and kill them, and they treated me with a very mock-like tone as if i were a baby. it eventually drove me nuts. and i was not ok with them putting me on a. 52/50 instead of the usual 51/50 so i was supposed to stay there a whole two weeks. mind you, this is my first mental hospital they never read me my rights or even explained what a 52/50 was. i eventually bailed myself out by making contact with a lawyer. also, i must add the nurses overdid my medication that was making me very slow and speak with a slurred voice. poor service, if suffering from any mental health issues please seek them elsewhere.

sjbh's iop and php programs are exceptional resources for people struggling with depression, anxiety, and other issues. the outpatient staff are extremely attentive, warm, intelligent, and respectful. i recommend their programs to anyone looking for support in these hectic times. group therapy gives connection and essential coping skills. jun, manya, and nia are rockstars.  jasmin is a passionate and caring addition to the staff. jennifer is the head of the program and you can tell why. she goes out of her way to make each patient a priority. it was difficult to leave but i've been given the tools and a blossoming sense of self to be able to start living my life again. thank you, san jose behavioral health.

i enjoyed visiting the cmhip museum recently. colorado mental health institute at pueblo museum is located in the former superintendent's residence at 13th and francisco streets in pueblo, colorado. their mission is to collect, preserve, interpret and exhibit artifacts and archives from the mental health institute (formerly colorado state hospital). the museum was developed to ensure that the history of cmhip is not forgotten and that future generations will gain a better understanding of the treatment of the mentally ill in colorado.
fac_name: Colorado Mental Health Institute at Pueblo Museum

review: ok let me start off by saying i've been to many psych wards in seattle and at first site or intake may be a little rough around the edges i was in 3w which is a pretty hectic place but there was gems within this unit including the loving staff that actually care.  i would like to point out that i wasnt in a good shape so my perception may be different from today.  looking back i'd like to say that my overall experience on 3w was rough its loud and there are many sick ppl so its not a hilton hotel so the expectation should be different right, well being hospitalized during corona virus makes everything 100% worse no going outside for one month! but through it all i made it with the help of the great staff and supportive doctors who understand how to care for you...was this place perfect no! but it allowed me the space to heal from my illness they respected my privacy and allowed me to go through the motions which is huge.  when i asked the staff that i needed something every one helped and if they couldnt they asked someone.   for example i needed clothes and the nurse made it a point to get me clothes if i needed a different diet they made sure it was done.  i was then transferred to 2w which was 100% better this floor allowed me even more space to heal its a less hectic unit and the surrounding helped me along further.  i was able to use the computer and have alittle bit more freedom.  no one likes to be hospitalized but when you have staff that actually cares for your healing they dont judge you and  dont make fun of you it makes healing 100% better.  staff comes from all walks of life which i love the diversity no one turned their back on me and that's important. they definitely don't throw you out on the street thanks to the wonderful social workers and doctors.  from the moment you walk in there is a plan and work as a team to get you there. thanks cascadia for all your help!! i will list cascade in my wrap plan as this is my hospital of choice for mental health

i wish i had some sort of way to get this place investigated. no staff member there had any care for my well being. and i clearly was not safe to leave but i had to anyway, to protect myself. it was so unsafe in so many ways. i was threatened to be sedated against my will just because i was crying, but i was completely cooperative the entire time. i was put in the wrong wing and neglected the entire time. they only ridiculed and mocked me when i started scratching up my own legs to self harm, and still let me leave the next day. the food was disgusting. the staff would not listen to me. i was terrified. i am completely traumatized and i left there feeling worse than i did when i came in. i am now scared to ask for help that i clearly need, for fear that i'll end up there again. other psychiatric units i've been to weren't great either but this one was the only one i've been to where i felt unsafe and terrified, alone, and unable to fend for myself.

just fyi, when i recently looked to read more reviews on cascade behavioral health i notice they changed their website to cascadebh.com to escape all the horrible reviews on this website.  i think anyone that has had a bad experience should post it to their new website.  www.cascadebh.com
close to death!!! i almost died at this place
i am not a "baby that did not finish the program", as some of the 5 star reviews say.  in fact i have been in aa since 1986 and have worked the steps multiple times as well as sponsored people and all the other things we do to stay clean and sober.  i had to take opioids because i broke my femur, and i self admitted myself to cascade to detox, feeling it would be safer than trying to do it alone at home with my sponsor an aa friends.  boy was i wrong about that!  the worst 7 days of my life!!!
i would give this place no stars if it would allow it.
the day i got there they rushed me through the paperwork, strip searched me and stuck me in a freezing cold room with none of my belongings.
the nightmare began.
i lay in my bed for 7 days with absolutely no help or human contact other than the nurse that took my blood every day, and another nurse that gave me a couple of pills(which i thought were my antidepressants).
when my doctor ordered a copy of my medical records from cascade, ( 5 pages were missing),it showed  that they took me off all my medications including the anti depression medicine and so i could not eat, drink or sleep.
this will be hard to believe but they gave me a hallucinogenic drug.
i really thought i would die in there.  the only person i spoke with was my 2nd roommate for little short spurts while she was getting ready to get up and go sit at the table.  she was told not to talk to me.
there is an evil man that was the director of the facility (he used to be at milam in kirkland until he was fired)and the last night i was there he was upset because he realized i was there for only 7 day detox(all my insurance would pay for).  he threw an absolute fit throwing stuff around and then cut off all meds that night for me and my roommate.
that next morning an intern(doctor) came in( i could see his desk from my bed), after looking at my chart he yelled "how can you treat people this way?!!!  i am calling 911.  the director came, there was another doctor and they were all arguing about it.  no one called 911.  i could see he was alone at his desk for a moment so i summoned all the strength i could and used a walker to get to his desk and asked him "do you believe in your hippocratic oath"?  he said "yes".  i then said "please help me",
and went back to my room.  about 5 minutes later there was arguing the doctors and director again and somehow my roommate had gotten her hands on a cell phone and i could hear her say "if you don't call 911, i will right now." 911 was called,  they made me take a bunch of pills before i left and i went to highline hospital for fluids because i was so dehydrated from not being able to drink anything for 7 days. i then was taken to uw hospital and remember nothing of the 1st 4 days i was there.
i had a stroke either while in treatment, or at the hospital and i had a psychotic break (most likely it was lsd mixed in with the pills they made me take before i left cascade), at uw they found an unknown substance in my blood, (lsd is not traceable).
please don't go here. there are doctors that can help you detox at home and can give you non-addictive drugs to help with the symptoms.
or go to a 12 step group like aa or na, there are people there that can help you too.  you are putting your life in the hands of insane, evil, money mongers that do not care about you.  please do get help if you are suffering from addiction, read the reviews about the place you are going.
i talked to a lawyer once i recovered from my stay, but he wouldn't take my case because he said because their were no lasting injuries i didn't really have a case. that was 5-6 years ago.  
if there are enough of us willing to work together i am sure we could get something done.  post if interested.

well i got to the point where my contractions were coming too rapidly and lengthy (coming every 30 secs for at least 45secs to 1 min each) for the only 4 cm i was dilated. so i elected to get an epidural being that the contractions were strong and i was dilating super slow; i went in already dilated to 3cm. fast forward and things started to move faster after the epidural and dialing the pitocin up quite a bit. the attending nurse was so sweet that she hung out slightly after her shift because she was determined to see my baby girl. unfortunately she couldn't hang out to that point since she was born at 9pm and her shift ended at 5pm i believe. 

fast forward again to postpartum. everything started out good.  but the reason i gave 1 star starts now. the room was freezing cold, i informed the nurse that it was super cold and the thermostat was not working. i was told that they would contact engineering and have them check it out. 2 hours later and freezing, nothing was done. i called again and finally a different person contacted someone who fixed it... temporarily.  of course after delivery things can be "less than tidy" and i consider myself a pretty clean person. well the cleaning crew did absolutely nothing but empty the trash in the bathroom. no one checked the bed/changed the linen, swept or mopped the floor or actually cleaned the bathroom. and unfortunately i had to be there for 2 days since my discharge time would have been too late in the night because of the required 24hour stay after delivery. 

the following day the lactation specialist, nicholette, came in to go over breast feeding with me. not once did she ask me about my personal situation e.g.) personal life and whether i have a partner to assist,  medical history, potential work schedule, nothing i think would be important to establish my personal feeding plan. i had a pacifier for my daughter because i couldn't stop her from crying. the first thing she did was tell me her name and write it on the board. the second was to take the pacifier out of my daughter's bed and throw it in the drawer and tell me "she doesn't need this, these are terrible" i was in disbelief and speechless. she never asked why i had it out but just shut down the use of it. she asked me to try to breast feed her so that she could see how things are going. i obliged and picked her up and attempted to latch. i explained to her that i was having some issues getting her to latch because of the shape of my nipple so i was going to try using a nipple shield that my doula suggested may help.  she asked if i tried different positions, which i had and told her.  i said i was going to try using a nipple shield to help with latching and again shut me down saying those are terrible and she will latch i just have to make her. keep in mind, i've just had a baby, i'm exhausted, i've been trying to breast feed, and my baby was crying quite a bit. now she's come in and told me that everything i've been doing is wrong. so finally my daughter latches, she asked me if she could help out. i said "sure." so she starts aggressively massaging my breast while my daughter is latched and i'm just sitting there because i can't get a word in because she's over talking me. a nurse comes in to ask me a question and suddenly she storms out of the room. she goes and tells the attending nurse, wendy, that i was "non compliant." wait... what?!?! she starts immediately asking me why i didn't want to work with her without asking me how i felt, if there was an issue, if i felt comfortable... none of that. just basically that i was wrong. luckily the pediatrician on call came in to take a look at my daughter and he asked about breast feeding and how it was going. i explained to him that she hadn't urinated and she was crying a lot. he suggested supplementing her with formula because she was likely hungry. well he was right! she sucked down 3 ounces of formula in no time which was what i was trying to explain to the nurse and lactation specialist.  

overall, the lack of room maintenance, communication, and bedside manner were definitely subpar. i definitely would not choose this hospital if i have another baby, and wouldn't suggest it to anyone either.

here are the facts about what mountainview hospital is doing at this moment:

* a nurse is only given an n95 rated respirator if they are working directly with a covid-19+ patient that is undergoing aerosol treatments while the nurse providing care to this patient.
* a nurses is only allowed to wear a surgical mask around covid-19+ patients who are not undergoing aerosol treatments as well as all others that are presumed to have covid-19 but are waiting the 3-5 days it takes for test results to come back.

it's been awhile since i've written a review and since with the covid scare all the restaurants in town are closed i decided to try out one of our longest standing eateries, the powell valley health clinic.  since you can't just leave a single review at such a fine establishment, this is part 1 of 2.  starting off, i would say the curb appeal is better than in the past with multiple extra signs telling you exactly where to park which is helpful when you can't breathe, you're dizzy, and have no depth perception to begin with.  
   you're greeted at the door by what i assume is a welcoming smile behind that mask where you are asked additional questions to further accommodate you.  a hard dry cough, fever, and dizziness even gets you a shiny red sticker on your chest so that others know you've made reservations and you can use the disney-like 'fast pass' line.  a mask, some gloves, and bam! you're in!  
   the maîte d' is of course the first person you'll see, and as the position dictates in any fine establishment, they are very knowledgeable of past stays, have payment info and address on file, and will have any paperwork ready to go to speed up the process.  after just a few quick minutes of waiting...while staring at the assortment of magazines and wondering if i dared touch them...i was called in.  
   at this time i go back and they take measurements, height and weight, and then it's time to see my personal physician's physician's assistant.  some more vitals are taken here and then bam!  one step closer to salvation and feeling better!  next came the physician's assistant - finally! the person i was waiting for.  the physician is gone for the day, but the training everyone here has is impeccable..and if it's not, how would you know? 
     we went through the symptoms again and took a look at my tonsils.  then we called in a physician for a quick consult and take a swab of my tonsils and throat to grow a culture and wham bam, problem solved!  my problem?  i didn't wait long enough to see if it would go away!  silly me!  
     exiting was even easier than coming in with no lines or stops, and since they already knew where to send the bill for my visit i was back in my truck and headed home to try and not die!!  overall my stay left me feeling wanting.  i was in a lot of pain, hadn't been able to swallow since the night before, so no water or food but hopefully it would all work out.  i had no answers, only more questions, and pretty scared to be honest, but i have faith in the people put in place to protect me.  the staff was very pleasant in that small tight-knit country community vibe you've come to expect in powell, and so after saying very painful but socially required thank you's i was out.  
     i feel nothing but the best for this establishment and the people working hard to keep our community safe in these uncertain times.  they're at the front lines - not just when it's in the news, but all the time.  caring for you, your loved ones, and being there for all of us in our most vulnerable moments.  i came back to the powell valley hospital the next day, but as i am not yet done with my current stay i'll have to hold off on writing my next review - spoiler, this will include hotel and restaurant amenities!!

note:  i was seen today, 3/25/2020, during the coronavirus epidemic.

scheduling, i was given very detailed instructions on where to park, signs to look for and where to register when i was in the hospital.

the day before i was called to see about rescheduling for after the pandemic. i shared that i would need to call and reschedule because i was losing my health insurance. she didn't hesitate and said no way, they'd still see me.

right now things may be different. in fact, before i entered i was asked the covid-19 questions, if i had traveled outside the country and if i was feeling ok, throat, cough etc.

i went to the registration desk and was seen very quickly by the individual that is the reason i'm writing my review, rita w. i won't put her last name for privacy purposes but lisa is your manager and i hope you get some big kudos! she was fantastic. so patient with me and compassionate. i shared that i was losing my insurance and she gave me financial forms in case i needed them. she was just great. i know she was really busy and took time with me answering my questions.  i would imagine being in a position right now, working in the health field, these workers are exhausted. she was so friendly and nice!!  

i then went and sat in the waiting area for my tech, sara. i wasn't waiting long, i went to the changing room and was in and out within 30 minutes. sara was great too!  very nice and i thanked her again for letting me come in today. 

needless to say, if i ever need anything done and a doctor refers me to chi, i won't hesitate!

its taken me a long time to write this review, but finally here it is. a bit over a year ago, i had an outpatient urology procedure performed. i arrived on time and followed all instructions. what was truly amazing was the admitting nursing staff (i dont recall her name) who prepped me, started my iv, attended to me, made me feel comfortable (lots of warm blankets), and then others started walking in. just as attentive and concerned as the rn was, the crna's and anesthesia folks who hovered around my bed were equally worried and concerned about my well being and care. the anesthesiologist was friendly and explained everything. my urologist came in, explained things again (and always kept me informed), but her urology resident had no bedside manner at all. regardless, all went well, and i am so grateful to these incredible folks who made sure i was safe and cared for. i cannot thank them enough for helping me, when i was down and out.

these people here work for a check! very incompetent, rude and careless. unprofessional and ghetto. from the doctors to the nurses to the receptionists. they all need to work for mta or waiters at a restaurant because they are too incompetent to work at a hospital dealing with people lives. dr. guranchy (however you spell it) asked me a list of the medication that my grandmother takes and i told her that the ems worker noted it when we were in the ambulance...her response was "oh okay i should look there" ....so you're telling me you had a patient admitted and didn't even check their emt notes after arriving via ambulance?? disgusting. i'm not even going to share my other experiences with the other "caretakers". if you want to die by negligent "caretakers" go to kings county!!! fucking shame.

the care i received was horrible. i went in because i was experiencing an allergic reaction in my eyes and the swelling was getting worse. i was prescribed antibiotic drops and allergy drops and was sent on my way. the doctor spent probably 5 mins with me and didn't even do a full exam but told me that i will be better in 4 days. 24 hours later my right eye swelled up so bad i could barely open it and my left eye started to swell up as well. 

i called the nurse line to see to explain that my symptoms were worsened she told me that she couldn't tell me to come in and i had to make that decision on my own. when i told her that i was scared because i didn't know what was happening and i didn't know if this was normal all she said to me what that she couldn't help me unless i came in, when i said thank you she just hung up. she was extremely rude. i decided to go to another place and it turns out i was supposed to actually get steroids to help with the swelling. i'm really glad i decided to go somewhere else because if i just trusted this one doctor then i would of probably had to been hospitalized.

review: i expected them to take this specific pandemic seriously. i had 2 out of the 3 symptoms for coronavirus, and they red flagged me/put me aside. when i entered inside i expected tests to be done, and nothing was tested except variable questions. i've been here for a long time and did not expect the round rock hospital to take this so lightly. i've always used this hospital even as a kid, and did not think they would just do verbal questions for a virus that's global.. yall can do better. it just disappoints me to say this because they've been so good to me everytime i've been there but this is serious. and just to add to this. we went there primarily to do some check ups on my 8 month pregnant fiance and now i have to go home hoping i dont have it.. sad
