review: after five months of indecisiveness, i have chosen to write this review in hopes of dissuading you of choosing this er. the nurses and staff were amazing and great and it's unfortunate that they cannot be reviewed separately. that being said i brought my daughter to the er on january 9 because she was in excruciating pain from having strained her chest muscles due to coughing (allergies). she had gone the day before to the pc and started allergy medication but the cough got worse, and she was in severe pain. these deep muscles were having deep spasms due to over straining and it was very obvious to all that my daughter was suffering. the doctor, who belongs to longhorn medical, came into the 'room' and sat down without even looking at my daughter who was writhing on the bed and crying. he proceeded to speak with me, sent her to the x-ray to check her ribs, prescribed steroids, and he was done. i convinced the doctor to at least give her a shot to lower the pain but by the time she got home the effects were already fading. it was a nightmare that is only now beginning to fade. but this doctor was so cold, so rude to the patient herself by not addressing her and angling his body away from her as he spoke with me (her mother), it really shook us. why did this man choose to become a doctor? and why would a hospital that prides itself upon its compassionate care, have this person who demeans his patients on their er staff? the steroids alongside the allergy medication really did help my daughter's health improve- but that doctor was a terror and should not be allowed to practice his nastiness in the er.
fac_name: St Davids Round Rock Medical Center

review:
rockford is a horrible place! staff is told to trick people into coming, they deny patient rights, the place is filthy, food awful, cafeteria gross, and there is *no* individual treatment plan or care. it's nothing but a warehouse for exploitation of the most vulnerable people. 
it is part of america's largest psychiatric hospital chain, universal health services, or uhs. a yearlong buzzfeed news investigation published december 7, 2016 shows the corporation makes a 30% profit by cutting staff and services. the investigation and "raises grave questions about the extent to which those profits were achieved at the expense of patients."
this place and all uhs hospitals should be closed forever and the ceo put in prison. just awful!

if i could give this place zero stars i would. this was the absolute worse experience i have had with an er. took my son here because he gashed his head on a glass table and was told he would need stitches. came into a busy er tonight so i get. i'm not saying i have a problem waiting the issue i have is when countless kids with minor issues were seen before my son. he bleed though the bandage that was applied by the paramedics. i finally asked just how long they were going to take as i figured driving to my area of town to another hospital would have been faster. the nurse offered to change his bandage and realized how deep the wound was. that is when we finally received a room. these people were calling kids that hadn't even made it to the waiting area we were sitting in.i am so livid because this is ridiculous!!! what if i had never said a word were they going to let us spend the evening in the waiting room because my son wasn't crying?!? he is pretty brave for a 3 year old but that doesn't mean you just continue to overlook him attending every new patient coming into the er. mind you i'm sure they will bill our insurance as quickly as possible with their below acceptable service!!! 

update: we actually never received service after sitting in the next room 2 more hours which equaled 6 hours in total with my son bleeding out. i eventually left and went to another er which treated him within 30 mins. i felt like the worse mom for not leaving so many hours sooner. they kept convincing me any other er would be just as long. not true. unfortunately he now has a scar which could have possibly been avoided if he was treated earlier. this place billed me 1,100. 00 dollars and they did absolutely nothing. when i inquired about the bill and lack of service they stated did they take his blood pressure and temp while there. wow! so i basically paid these crooks to sit in their nasty waiting room. they try to force you to sit around er as long as possible in order to bill your insurance ridiculous fees. i will most definitely be fighting this is small claims courts.
if i could give them 0 stars i would.  i would not send my loved one to this hospital.  not a pleasant experience at all.

omg for real  people. this is the craziest hospital ever. a test that was supposed to be 45 minutes turns into a 3 hour ordeal, and no communication between the doctors/ nurses and myself. my mom went in for what is called a tilt tablet test. the test seemed to work but no one came to tell me she was having issues. 3 hours later and they just wheeled her out. no thanks. and valet parking is a joke, they let a lady park in the travel lane. while we waited for our car of 30 minutes, i bet she went back and forth with her child in and out of the car at least 4 times. and was still there when we got our car and left almost 30 minutes into our waiting for the car. why??? if we can't do it then they shouldn't be able to. 
i used to have my personal appointments there several years ago and i had no issues. i'm sure not going back there.

went to banner general on april 19th with severe abdominal pain. was reluctant to go during covid but it was so bad i knew i'd need to see someone.  all entrances were closed except the er, wirh respiratory cases physically separated in the waiting room.  no other guests allowed.  checked in quickly, triaged quickly, in an er room with pain meds quickly.  taken for ultrasound, explained everything.  then taken to ct scan, back to the er room and provided more meds for comfort.  moved to a room on 5, provided meds and allowed to rest.  diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, crazy painful.  after a couple of up and down days, started finally coming out of my own yesterday.  
all of nurses, aids, cleaning staff, doctors, respiratory therapists have been professional and very caring.

terrible reason for a review but definitely well deserved.  great job all around!

thanks for the amazing care, folks!

i recently delivered at banner gateway and i cannot say enough good things about my experience with the ob department. the staff was amazing and knew exactly what to do when my delivery resulted in an emergency c section. the resident doctor, terry huff, is amazing as well and i felt in such safe hands with him when my regular obgyn was unable to perform my delivery due to covid. i also had to be readmitted for gastro and infections issues post birth and the infectious disease doctor, dr. ooman, was most helpful. he immediately pinpointed my issues and got me feeling better within hours. huge thank you to dr huff, dr ooman and the ob staff at banner gateway.

banner gateway- i emailed customer service and never heard back. it's been over a month. who else do i need to email to be responded to? thanks for the help!

i had to have an emergency surgery to remove my gall bladder during the covid-19 pandemic and they were extremely caring and concerned. the staff had great communication and let me know what was happening every step of the way. i didn't know there was a difference in hospitals and now i know there is a huge difference. i would highly recommend them.

do not go to this er if you want any level of privacy whatsoever. i was very sick back in february and went to the er at banner gateway. i was put into a "room" with curtains instead of walls. there were patients on either side of me. i heard all about one gentleman's testicular pain and a young lady's suicidal thoughts. i am sure they heard all about my health issues as well. i can't imagine that this is not in violation of hippa. i will be consulting with my attorney to find out what more i can do to address this issue at banner gateway. 

additionally, do not go to this er if you would like to be seen and treated in a timely manner. it took the doctor over two hours to come and see me after i was put into my "room". once he had the time to talk with me, he stayed in my room for less than a minute. he ordered some tests (tests i didn't even feel were necessary but he insisted were). i waited for another 3 and a half hours with no testing conducted. nobody came to talk to me to let me know what was taking so long. so finally i just discharged myself so i didn't have to wait any longer. i went in to see a different doctor the next day and sure enough, none of those tests were necessary - my symptoms were pretty straight forward and all i needed were some nausea meds. 

i sent an email and filled out a survey about my experience at banner, and not a single person ever followed up about my concerns. so i will blast them everywhere that i can think of to prevent other people from having to go through what i went through. 

i will never be back to banner gateway again. this is easily the most unorganized, unprofessional er i've ever had the displeasure of checking in to.

if you're going to the er good luck. no privacy everyone in the waiting room hears what's wrong with you. also im sitting down and someone positive with covid comes in, checks in and then sits two chairs from me. again he seemed lost himself that that's where he was asked to sit. they don't separate and they did not clean where he sat. i asked two ladies if they sanitize and they said no. and i pointed where he sat and she said yeah they sit everywhere.

my elderly mother went to this hospital because she has coronavirus and every and joint in her body hurts and is on fire and she can barely breathe. my elderly mother only had two people in line in front of her, and they took six people that came in after her, instead of taking her when it was her time. my elderly mother sat in the waiting room for over 6 hours screaming and crying, and when my elderly mother told the woman she could barely breathe she said, well you are still talking so it can't be that bad. they took a younger woman in that was complaining of stomach and vagina pain but she was all right enough to sit there and laugh with her mom and play video games on her device and she came in way after my elderly mother. it is so unethical sad and disgusting how the elderly are treated there. i plan on getting a hold of the medical board and the insurance company and putting up any reviews about this horrible degrading treatment. my elderly handicapped mother on the way out to her car also tripped and got hurt and not one employee could help her i will definitely be getting a hold of my attorney about this terrible unethical company. please, this sincerely goes out to all the people that have elderly family, do not take your elderly family members to this location unless you want them to be miss treated by unethical employees, that do not care about patients.
thank you. 
banner gateway hospital higley road.

extortion..kidnapping..and rude people..
this is what you will get..
it took them 2 days to check me out..
they will tell you about yoga..meditation..gym..
nothing you will get..they are here just to kidnap you..and squeeze your insurance..
you will cry to go out. they will treat you so bad.
why does the state let this place continue to violate the law??

i went into enloe after sustaining a rock climbing fall that left me with what i thought was a fractured foot. they gave me an x-ray, glanced at it quickly, and told me i only had soft tissue damage and was fine as long as i stayed off it for a little while. i've fractured my foot twice before so i was skeptical, as i know what it feels like and this seemed like way more than just soft tissue damage. i went to a podiatrist the next day to get a second opinion and they confirmed that it was definitely fractured. enloe billed me over a couple grand for the x-ray and misdiagnosis...

my husband has also been there for a gash in his leg from a mountain biking accident. they stapled it back together. later, he had another doctor look at it, who told him they should have stitched it instead and at least told him to keep it moist. as it was, they had sent him away with no information or care instructions, so the healing wasn't optimal.

you're better off driving to sacramento.
it's a new york-"f u"-"you're just a number"-attitude combined with all the skills and benefits of third-world healthcare. it's only your health and your life. meanwhile, they will be standing around chatting while you're in pain and telling you that it's all in your head. oh and don't be dehydrated because they can't seem to spare ivs... those are for rich people with gold-plated healthcare.

this hospital killed my mom. dr. vinaymar paschal was the doctor overseeing my mothers care. she left me a voicemail at 9:17 am about getting a procedure and at 10:00am she was deceased. this hospital is a death factory. go in for dehydration leave in a hearse. i will not let them get away with them taking my mother from me. you better just get out of this business of helping people because killing them doesn't help anyone.

so this particular hospital has had a bad reputation over the years but i happened to switch here towards the end of my pregnancy because i had my 1st child at wyckoff hospital and the experience was awful so i didn't want to go through that a second time. also because i had seen advertisement for a new & improved maternity ward here so i thought i'd make an appointment for a tour. the tour was nice. i went into labor just a week after and i have to say the experience was amazing. cozy labor & delivery room. private suites after u have the baby and both dad and mother in law stayed. i asked to not be bothered with offering me breast feeding assistance and my wishes were granted. no students coming in & out constantly to ask and say the same things the doctor would eventually say. the baby stays with u at all times unless ofcourse its necessary to take the baby for blood etc. its a nice & quite ambiance at night with dim lights throughout the halls to give u a more homey feeling and your door remains shut for privacy. they even take a pic of your newborn and give it to you in a thank you card as a souvenir before u leave the hospital. the only downside was the food. not many options. portions are too small and not very tasty. no cafeteria neither. they should really improve this but other then that everything else was great.

horrible , horrible er experience , poor receptionist service , had my elderly family member there for hours without giving her any food/ snack !! never again and took very long for discharge . if it was up to me this hospital wouldn't get 1 star.

had both of my daughters delivered at mountain vista with dr purohit. she is the best doctor.  secondly both times the nurses were great too - before, during, and after. 

only negative is that if you're the partner and need to sleep with the pregnant person, that chair is a rough nights sleep. like sleeping on a 2x4.

as a former coworker, i'd give them 2 out of 5 stars. 
from what i have personally experienced, i would like to give them negative stars. but that would be a biased move.
most of the coworkers were kind, a bit stand-off-ish. 
i worked in the outpatient department and was treated horribly where i had to go to hr--they didn't do anything. and i emailed the ceo about what was going on. 
in the end, i was ridiculed, harassed, blamed, made fun of because i truly wanted to put people first. but they didn't see that. they cared about numbers and money. 
when doing my rounds of going to the floors to get signatures of patients with medicare, they explained to me how they wanted to speak to the head nurse or the doctor about their care. not all of my patients, but a big percentage of them. 
and i defended the hospital and the staff. and i apologized profusely. but deep down, i knew...i knew the patients weren't treated fairly. 
even in the emergency department. i would call their extension at times, and the receptionists or nurses would talk down on me, give me attitude, make me feel little. 
i can't imagine what the patients went through. 
the harassment, the lies, the abuse was too much for me to take. of the ceo and hr couldn't help me, then who could? 
i left because back then, they believed in numbers and money. when i believed in helping others. i helped an out-of-town patient get the care he needed when an ir surgeon happened to be on my daily duties. i went above and beyond for the doctor and the patient. my supervisor was watching me like a hawk. 
the surgeon then greeted me at first meeting me and from then on, we've became great friends. 
the two stars should be five for the hard-working people. but i have to give this a two. because the coworkers that i have confronted did not show empathy but judgement. 
and i do not stand for that.

i should of listened to the reviews.. and not go. i called to see if they did covid testing today, yes she said. went there and was told only monday-friday. i told her i just called. i was ignored. i asked do you know where i can go that's close to here? i was ignored again. they weren't busy, there were a total of 3 people in the emergency room. i felt not only stupid but was outraged at how these so called nurses treated me.
went in for feeling crappy. admitting nurse was incredibly sweet and my nurse was amazing! in these hectic times they all were upbeat and had a  sense of humor. i love this hospital!

this could be the worst hospital of all time. my wife had to visit the  emergency room.  upon  entering the hospital,  we encountered the most unprofessional staff that you could the of. it was like girls at recess laughing and goofing of. as my wife completed the  registration process, one young lady asked to to start signing forms with no explanation of what she was signing. after sitting for approximately three hours, she had remind someone that she had not been seen as of yet. we also could a gentleman complaining that he had been waiting for his sick wife to be treated after waiting over three hours. he had to remind them that she had recently suffered a  stroke. during my wife treatment, a p.a. prepared to  give her an injection and she had to remind him to wash his hands. his response,  
i forgot.  sad !

if you're reading this review trying to decide whether to go to this emergency room or not... stop! 

even if you have to drive farther ...drive farther even if you have to walk farther ...walk farther!

after experiencing the most traumatic and life-threatening experience of my life (next to childbirth) i come in to this hospital (code yellow) and didn't realize that my experience here would be almost as dramatic as the event itself. 
i don't use foul language and i don't typically call people names but i really don't have anything good to say about any of the people that were in their "helping me" ... and i can only think of mean names... 

i was crying almost to the point of hyperventilation almost the entire time... not one person tried to comfort me or assure me that everything would be ok(and in a real sense everything might not of been ok, and i completely understand that) or at the very least that everyone was working hard and doing their best. i was left in the dark about everything, my monitors were going off and they told me not in a kind way that if i could just calm down that's what i needed to do as they left the room. 

covid-19 has everyone walking into the situation alone and scared. and it is the most terrifying feeling to be so alone while you are experiencing the most trumatic experiences of your life and the guys around you are being jerks. 

i have no idea what their faces look like but hearing the people in the nurses station just laughing and carrying on and having conversations with three or more people while i'm scared to death and crying my eyes out alone in the room... waving for help for sometimes more than a few minutes... 

i would literally rather suture my own wounds and set my own arm then come back to this place!! it almost felt surreal because the people that i did see seem so normal like they might have an ounce of empathy. 

i will save the person conducting the mri was the most informative and kind of all of them.

my 80 year grandmother was admitted yesterday into the emergency room with complaints of heart palpitations and elevated heart rate. no guests were allowed into the hospital due to covid-19. the health violation i am most concerned about is admitting a patient into a hospital bed that had someone else's blood soaked into the mattress. my grandmother got out of her bed and noticed blood soaked on the back of her shorts that was not of her own. she then pointed this out to the staff and after an exam confirmed that it was not her own, but that it was "from her iv line" where no blood could be seen to be the source. she had to remove the sheet with blood herself and put it on the floor. a nurse walks in and noticed that her fluid line had been dripping onto the floor with a huge puddle (also a health concern). also, how do you know the correct administered measurement of fluids if half of it ends up leaking? the sheet had someone else's blood on it, was wet and was on the on floor and the nurse proceeded to try and put it back onto to the bed. i am in shock of the hygienic practices being conducted in this hospital, especially during such a time of necessary cleanliness due to covid-19. no food or water was offered during her 8-10 hour stay. upon discharge, the nurse never offered a wheel chair and left her alone outside in the 100 degree heat without the arrival of her accompanied ride being present.

my sister went in with a hemiplegic migraine (a migraine that basically paralyzes half of your brain) and she has a history of them so we knew what it was. we brought her in to help with her pain and they didn't believe us that it was a hemiplegic migraine. she count speak couldn't move couldn't advocate for herself, and she was all by herself because of covid-19. they gave her a ct and a whole bunch of test and when those came up negative they decided she was psycho and they were about to send her to a psychiatrist facility without speaking to us first. thank god my dad called and asked what was going on, or else she would be involuntarily in a freakin nut house. worst doctors, worst experience, never again'!!!!!

horrible hospital!! my mother was taken there via ambulance as they thought she had a stroke (closest hospital) stroke was ruled out during er exam. they had sedated her in the er and then admitted her 8 hrs later. - due to her dementia my mom does do well with sedation- fast forward to 7 days later my mom has not anything to eat or drink. no plan of medical action, she is awake, confused and scared. medical staff (with the exception of a couple of nurses) do not seem to care. it's as if the dr has already signed the death certificate, just enter date. unfortunately we are stuck; with the coronavirus situation we can't just transfer her to another hospital. then the staff has the audacity to tell us we can only stay 1 hr once a day. nope my brothers and i are doing shifts. we will not allow them to kill our mother!!
just because she has dementia doesn't mean she was not living a quality life, all it meant is sometimes she didn't know what the date was. 
the medical team has not done any assessments since she has been in. they have punctured her lung due to inserting a g-tube incorrectly.

the one star is just so i can't post this. 
if anyone from dignity or banner is reading this please reach out to me. we need quality care for our mother (btw she has a excellent insurance)

oh the entire ed except for girl at front desk. is j o k e!!

i had a laparoscopic bilateral tubal ligation. after waiting more than a decade i finally found dr.ahad who took me seriously and performed the surgery. he did amazing work.  one of the kindest most empathetic doctors i've ever had the pleasure of meeting. 

the hospital itself was well prepared and maintained social distancing, took temperature and required masks. i was a bit nervous due to the pandemic but i felt i was in good hands once i went into the lobby. 

ida worked incredibly fast and was friendly during registration as the new restrictions caused time delays and she was the only one doing check-ins. 

the hospital itself was clean and all the nurses were incredibly kind. nora and nabiha both were wonderful, they chatted with me in a way that calmed me down. but really all the nurses were amazing. when i came to, i felt a bit confused, i had  what felt like strong menstrual cramps and since i'm fairly blind without my glasses i started to panic. a very nice and kind nurse who i couldn't see was able to calm me down and stopped me from trying to put pressure on my lower abdomen which is what i usually do with cramps. confusion + pain + inability to see is a bad combo. i'm grateful to her for not allowing me to hurt myself. 

i can't say enough nice things about my experience. i'm always a bit scared going into surgery but the staff at this hospital are phenomenal, i recommend getting an outpatient procedure here.

this place is trash. literally the er room is disgusting. the bathroom was dirty, had blood on the toilet, and there was trash everywhere. i barely touched anything let alone needing to take a pee sample in that cesspool full of germs. i should've went somewhere else. medical records? forget it. my doctor cannot even obtain them and needs them to continue my care. they also tried to release me with no pain medicine. i had to ask for at least something more than typical tylenol. please go somewhere else.

very rude and inattentive nusing staff. they argued there is no federal law stating they must help anyone in an emergency. i recorded the phone calls and will be forwarding to my attorney. nurses are not doctors and should not speak to emergency calls as inappropriately as they do. they are a shame to the medical field. and have no authority to diagnose or turn away persons in need of help. if you have an emergency and care about your health or a loved one's health, this is not the place willing to help! they are unethical and do not care!!!!

horrible experience in the er at hillcrest hospital. blood had poured out of cut in leg, but i sat for over 2 hours in lobby getting nauseated and dizzy. no concern whatever, and extremely slow and uncaring staff.

beware!!! prisma had authorization from my isnruance company and i was told my portion for an echocardiogram was $1000.  surprise... received a bill for $1700.  they are rude when i try to get to the bottom of it and won't even consider negotiating the balance.  places like this are the problem with transparency in this country.  we will never use any practice if they're associated with prisma health, again.

the doctors and nurses in the er were amazing. they treated my brother with respect and kindness. they worked quickly and thoroughly to get him the medical care he needed.  they were also very kind to our family.

i have been aggressively pursued by telephone and by mail. i owe a balance of $125. my insurance company has paid thousands and thousands of dollars through the years. their lack of human empathy and respect is pitiful. also, we are in a world wide pandemic to top it off! unbelievable!!

review:

the dr. shawn (kaku) was truly wonderful! 

every, single icu nurse was a blessing! they had so much patience for us, it was so wonderful! 

after 3 weeks of icu and 1 week of a normal floor stay, our family member got to go home! 

thank you for the wonderful care! appreciate all that you guys did for us!

review:
hi,
on march 6th 2020 i was rushed to eden medical center.

review:
what a roller coaster.

coming in, the temperature nurse was really sweet and brought me a chair to sit in while filling out the paperwork. they brought me in after a few mins to get my history, vitals and blood draw to check my troponin. 

trust, i've been in and out of the er frequently for sob, palpitations, chest pain and heaviness due to my history of cardiac arrest. 

triage nurse and ecg tech were very friendly. nurse told me they're probably going to monitor me to make sure everything's okay. 
i head back out to the hallway and finish the paperwork..

1.5 hours pass and i'm nodding off in the hard plastic chair. butt is numb and i feel cold. 
i ask the registration if they could inquire if i was going to be monitored like i was told (and what usually happens when i go to er).

the nurse comes out and says they're gonna do a 2nd blood draw after 2 hours. i ask about the monitoring, and she says they're just gonna take my ecg again with the 2nd blood draw... this was news to me. 
we vibed well but it didn't help with the miscommunication.. the reason i wasn't getting taken in was cause they were full, but just a little communication goes a long way.

after waiting 2 hours, i asked registration if i could just know what my initial vitals and labs were. 
every time i spoke with the older lady, she made me feel like i was such a bother, when all i wanted was some communication. she literally told me nothing other than they don't see that info and the charge nurse never got back to her (only after i stood near the registration window for 5 mins, sat back down and asked about my results the second time 15 mins later!)
this was what really discredited my experience at bhh. 
at my hospital, they require us to maintain communication with our patients regarding any delays and reason for delays so they stay in the loop instead of sitting out there wondering and getting frustrated; to acknowledge patients without attitude. 

man, this made me wish i just stayed home. 

after i was taken to draw labs for the second test, i asked the rn if they could just call me if anything was up. i was cold, tired, and very uncomfortable. 

the er doctor, who was very cutthroat and straight to the point (i dig that), came to meet me after i mentioned i wished to leave. he ended up seeing me twice and said "i'm happy to share good news..."  

i believe that i'm a very patient person. i understand that extended wait times happen. miscommunication happens as well, but complete lack of it and attitude was not something i came there for. i come in respectful and optimistic about the care and experience i will have, but that really turned me off. 

so, all in all, mixed feelings about bhh, but i would not come back.

my mother in law was admitted to the bakersfield heart hospital due to low blood pressure after being treated in a skilled nursing facility.  her daughter hand-delivered the dnr that her mother created for emergency situations to ensure that her wishes were followed.  her daughter called the hospital to speak with her today and then found out that she had been admitted to the icu but no one had contacted her to inform her of this.  even worse, the doctor stated that he had no dnr on file for her and they administered unnecessary and unwanted medication and medical intervention which caused her serious pain and suffering against her express wishes that were clearly stated in her advance healthcare directive.  this is incompetence of the highest order which this hospital will have to answer to once this ordeal is over.

writing this for marty koch: the nursing staff was good but dr.ajay m. patel gravely misdiagnosed me. he said i had a pulmonary problem, ordered several tests for lungs that came back negative, and still told me it was a pulmonary issue. even when their own dr.vaghasia told him it wasn't. they did preform heart tests but still told me my lungs were the issue. thankfully, i sought out help from keck medical of usc. just from looking at the heart tests transferred from b.h.h. dr.cunningham of keck was very surprised no one had told me i had a heart attack that caused a ruptured 3 holes in my heart. i was diagnosed with vsr and had open heart surgery at keck. if i hadn't left bakersfield heart hospital i would be dead now.

do not take your loved ones to this hospital!  due to my mom's serious medical condition, she was taken to bakersfield heart hospital.  they have completely ignored her advanced directive and failed to communicate with her family, even after she was rushed into the icu, where she was provided unauthorized treatment. we are trying desperately to get her transferred to a hospital that respects her, her family and her advanced directive.   the care she is receiving is torturous to her.  she has congestive heart failure, extremely painful wounds covering her legs and bottom, pneumonia and dangerously low blood pressure.  we are not allowed to see her due to covid-19.  neither the staff or the doctor treating her bothered to check the paperwork that was brought in by the family with her directives, nor did anyone at the hospital take the time to even pick up a phone to call her family while she was in critical condition.  i found out my mom was in the icu from the florist who could not deliver flowers to her room!    negligent and scary... how else are they failing her while we are stuck waiting outside the walls of the hospital?

i was having postpartum depression and got sent here. originally, i was supposed to go to zucker hill maternity/postpartum ward, but last minute i was told nope, you're going to south oaks. i should mention i never experienced depression until i had a baby at age 19, and then experienced postpartum depression. i also have anxiety and have had it my whole life. i've tried other medications for anxiety and have had bad reactions to certain ones. the certain ones would make my symptoms worse, or even have suicidal thoughts. 
so here i am, a week after turning 20 sent here. i think, ok, i'll make the best of this to try and get better. boy, was i wrong. it's co-ed so they don't separate males and females. they also let psychotic patients roam free and terrorize the non-violent patients. i was there for a week total and i cannot even count on both hands the amount of times i was harassed, given death threats, unwanted romantic/sexual advances etc. men would sexually hears me and when i ignored them or gave them an answer they didn't like they threatened to kill me, shoot my family, etc. there was a minimum of 3 physical fights between patients a day with screaming, yelling, all of it. the more aggressive/violent patients would try to antagonize the others to fight with them for "fun" (for example one would repeatedly try to bait me into a fight by saying dumbass stupid bitch, fucking bitchass hoe white girl, etc after i turned down his offer of "wifing me up". there were a few patients like myself who weren't insane, just going through a hard time but were constantly scared and under stress of the aggressive patients.
i had a guy come up to me everyday telling me about conspiracy theories and his "secret pet monkey". the first night i spent and woke up my roommate was screaming at me in spanish calling me "el diablo" and poking me and trying to steal my belongings. staff moved me to be with a different roommate who was very kind and lovely. however with the constant fighting and screaming my anxiety was at an all time high. the dr at first refused to give me the medicine that works to calm my anxiety. they tried to also make me take ssris which had previously given me adverse side effects which i explained to them, yet they wouldn't budge. after my mom made a phone call to them and raised hell then they gave me the proper medicine for my anxiety. i was scared all the time in that place. most of the nurses treated u as if you were an animal at times. it was a very dehumanizing and terrifying experience.
i needed help at this point in my life, not to be further traumatized. the one good thing i can say about this place is they have good food. long story short though it's a free for all where violent and aggressive patients are allowed to go at you with little intervention, no protection from sexual harassment, and this is a sad reflection of our mental health system that a person like me ended up in the same place as some of these people. i demanded a 72 hour release paper and that's how i got out and am now going to my therapist and an actual helpful psychiatrist. also, there is no real therapy or therapists here. people just exploding and getting "booty juiced" (sedation vaccine administered through the buttcheek) all the time. i also will say the art therapists here who would lead programs where you would do art activities were lovely and wonderful people, and were some of the only actual staff who acknowledged the situation i was in and how i should not be there.

also: they don't tell you this but they don't release patients on weekends. that's why i had to stay 5 days rather than 3.

i was hospitalized in the adolescent girls unit in 2012 for depression and self harm, i was never violent or lashing out i was admitted because i was a threat to myself. while on the unit the staff was very rude and were not empathetic or caring in any way shape or form. they made me feel more alone there than anywhere i had ever been. the main reason im giving 1 star is because while on the unit i was attacked by a girl on the unit who was my roommate and she jumped on top of me, hit me, kicked me and hurt me pretty bad, a security guard and a nurse saw what had happened but did not do anything to punish her or anything!! and they wouldnt allow me to switch rooms either!!! when my parents came to visit that evening i told them about it and they were furious, they talked to the nurses and security guards and they said "they cudnt do anything about it". absolutely disgusting place which has traumatized me for 8 years. i hope this dump shuts down
i wish i always  didnt have to wait soooo long when i am waiting for an appointment. some of the docs are good tho.  others not so much.

fantastic doctors, nurses and staff. facilities are beautiful and spacious. patient rooms are comfortable and modern. we spent 3 days here and saw at least 15 different nurses, technicians, doctors, and staff- all kind, caring, and attentive. highly recommended hospital. only the best care in dfw.
fac_name: William P. Clements Jr. University Hospital

review: just returned from an awful emergency room visit. i have taken my parents ,daughter and myself to other ers and have never been treated like this. i was sent by my pcp because of chest pain. because of the covid situation it appeared to be vacant.dr. huang entered the room and the first thing she asked me is why i was there. my ekg was normal. i told her my pcp wanted them to draw bloodwork on me. she never examined me. asked a few questions and left the room.i felt like i was the biggest burden and was so sorry my doctor told me to go there.it was a terrible experience.i left feeling very depressed.
fac_name: William P. Clements Jr. University Hospital

review:
admittedly i'm high risk for visits to the er, as engaging in sports and other activities some consider nuts, it might make sense to just keep a retainer payment here. this hospital has grown over the years, but to its credit, parking here is a breeze compared to the fairfax campus. obviously there are times when it's not as easy as one would like, but with enough diligence you'll make it. my last visit was actually for lung nodules, discovered during a ct scan, and i'm relieved they disappeared on a recheck. it was rather stressful, but the doctors and nurses were superb. truly professional. the same goes for a recent blood test, as the phlebotomists have a wonderful sense of humor. 

over the years i've been in the er with broken ribs, and what appeared to be a hernia, but thankfully was a groin pull. admittedly not fun, but here you usually can get in and out of the er with relative ease. the er staff is exceptional. i'm happy with the level of care and also the kindness. this has been a great addition to the northern side of the county, and a excellent facility for outpatient surgery as well. am very happy to recommend this hospital. yes no one wants to go, but when you're in an emergency or need something checked, this is where to go.

i interacted with about ten different staff members, and every single one of them was helpful and caring. they all seemed to genuinely care about me and my recovery. this is the best i've ever been treated at a medical facility. i would recommend this facility to anyone and everyone.

had my 2 year old son pre surgery covid testing requirement today and i'm thankful for the rn manager and the nurse for being understanding and patient with me and my son. especially to the manager (i forgot to get her name) for even going the extra mile and going to the testing site/tent to help (due to some minor issue/ miscommunication) before testing. thank you!

seriously?  providence st. john's suspended 10 nurses who refused to work inside a coronavirus ward unless they were provided with adequate protective gear.  a co-worker had already tested positive for the virus.  this is very telling as to how much the hospital values its employees.  shame on you providence.

update: as you can see there was a response to my comment/review. i did drive down thru the hospital area and side street, and saw that the discarded masks, gloves had been picked up. thank you for the prompt action and reply.

while waiting for an outpatient surgery patient, i briefly stepped out from the waiting area to grab a bite to eat. when i returned, i knew it was a possibility that the surgeon may have been to the waiting area, so i called the phone number displayed at the front desk to obtain an update. accordingly, i was informed that the patient was still in surgery. after another 45 mins - 1 hour, a nurse named gayle b. approached me and stated that i could go see the patient. i explained that i hadn't spoken to the surgeon, so i inquired about speaking to him. aside from a general update on how the surgery went and follow-up care, i didn't have any major concerns, and i wasn't upset about anything. gayle b. responded by attempting to reprimand me from leaving the waiting area, and proceeded to tell me that i should've been in place to see the surgeon. although i understood what she was saying, her delivery was vile and extremely nasty. i don't understand why anyone with that type of unprofessional attitude would choose to work in a customer facing/patient facing profession. i really hope no one else has to experience gayle's nastiness.

the staff here were extremely rude. i went to a local medstop to get some help but was told to come to this facility. when i asked about co-pays and possible fees, they remarked that they wouldn't have a cost until the doctor orders tests. not only that, but they tried to get me to sign for treatment before even looking at my insurance card. now i'm no insurance expert, but in my past experiences, they've always taken my card and at least told me my co-pay and added that there might be other fees associated with tests. when i said i wasn't willing to sign for treatment without having an idea of cost, they became even more pushy and rude. they were so gracious to let me know that i could pay at a later date but wouldn't go into detail about that either. so i'm supposed to sign something for an undisclosed amount of money and an undisclosed date of payment? yeah, right.

i am soooo disappointed about how houston medical center is handling giving information to families about the patients especially during this covid virus flare. i called to find status or any kind of information about my mother who was admitted through the emergency room. it took me 5 times to call and still was not able to talk to the nurse who was taking care of my mom. they did not even ask for my number to call back...showing how inconsiderate and not caring environment of these staff. front liners should also care for the panicking families of patients!!! perhaps they will only call to tell me if my family is deceased.....

kind people and helpful but when i had to stay for a few days in recovery. it would take foreve for the nurse or any nurse to come then off the alarm or check what it is. like 5-10 minutes and instead i would hear them gossiping about whatever for that whole time instead of turning the alarms off

wow, night and day!    emergency room was orderly and professional. pre registration for imaging and coordinating a service in imaging was hours of torment. cassandra was kind and tried to help but where is the communication with registration. several days of trying to get an imaging appointment as requested by my physicians office happened! took a hard effort.  trying to get registration to see what my co payment would be, never happened. technical difficulties, lost in the q and several times ringing the department was lost time.  it's too much effort to deal with services!  i have insurance, a dr and just desire to be responsible by knowing my obligation. i feel terribly unimportant to this group of people. i'd rather travel further to get any kind of attention. a definite f!  i needed this service but got beat down.

i went to the emergency room with internal bleeding and in great pain. i ended up on the floor screaming and staff walked around me and informed me they had no where to put me. totally unacceptable. i could have died on the floor of the emergency room. don't go here if you can help it.

my 79 year old dad was transferred to banner boswell from banner del e. web on june 12th. since then, i have not heard from a single nurse, doctor, administrator, case manager, or customer care specialist. when i call the hospital it goes to a recording for an hour. then i'm transferred around only to be told the only person that can give me information about my dad is his nurse who is "out to lunch!" i ask for a name- they refuse. i ask for a doctor- they refuse. i ask for a call back- i'm still waiting! my dads cell phone is no longer charged or being plugged in for him and he is unable to do it himself. that do not tell me what room he is in, if he has a phone, offer facetime, nothing. this is appalling, more than upsetting, disgusting, and sub-human behavior. i have been hung up on, treated rudely & inconsiderate, been told my dad is an adult and can make his own decisions. i was told just today by a nurse named tasha in imcu that it's not her responsibility to charge my dads cell phone. she then hung up on me while i was still talking! what sort of hospital does this? is it not bad enough we can't be with our family face-to-face? i realize they are just another "patient", just another "room to clean" to them, but they are family to us! the only family i have....

would definitely recommend... if you're looking for a low-budget horror movie hospital experience.

i've had friends speak poorly about this place but never understood why until i visited. when i saw a hospital bed left uncleaned for hours full of (unidentifiable) liquids, with a nasty dirty floor left unvacuumed/unwiped potentially for days, with holes in the walls, that should've been my cue to get out. this place looks like the hospital from the hills have eyes, where the trailer dwellers from down the road get off their shift at walmart and then work evening shift as rns here. hospital staff are incredibly callous and antagonistic. i recall that we were in one of the patient rooms having a private conversation about the poor service of the hospital staff, and one of the rns (or whatever she was) came in after snooping in our conversation and started verbally attacking us. after many unnecessary hours of being there, the hospital staff seemed so knowledgeable and incompetent that they said they'd contact fresno hospital to see if we should be sent there instead. why keep us there for hours only to tell us you don't know how to handle our problem? we came here because it was allegedly a hospital, not a place that just suggests for us to go somewhere else. yeah, never coming here again. if i ever hemorrhage, i'd rather drive an extra 30 mins and risk death than come here.

where else would you like to spend your new years eve than here at wonderful evergreen?  yup, i signed up to have my bladder cancer surgery here to keep my cost in 2019.  
the check in procedure was very efficient, and evergreen did a very good job keeping me informed of where i was in the process.  i liked that they kept checking to make sure i was the right person/procedure.
the nurses were absolutely fantastic, even the night-time ironmaiden nurse who checked me hourly.  they even had a little potluck out there for nye in the ward, made it feel a little cheerful.
warm blankets galore.  responded when i hit the nurse button.  pain meds provided adequately. 
two names stuck out as being really superior, magda and cynthia.  no last names, sorry.
billing seemed to be accurate, complete, and everything went thru insurance.
food was really good, but that's reviewed separately cafe 128.
i know i shouldnt complain about environment, but its appalling how much plastic waste is generated here, wish they could try to minimize more.
i wouldn't hesitate to come here if needed, which, with my disease, i'll be seeing more of.

worst experience you could possibly get if you prefer to not give birth naturally. i asked for epidural when i gave birth to my son, it worked great at the beginning even though the doctor had to try twice to put it in, however, when it was getting close to delivery, i started to feel some pain but the nurse kept saying it was normal, it's just pressure, and would not give me extra dose. during the delivery i was in 10 out of 10 pain for two hours, i thought i would never be able to get the baby out, and when the baby was out, i did not even want to see the baby because i was in extreme pain. i ended up to have a stage 3 tear and when the doctor stitched me up, i could feel every needle going through my  body, and was extremely painful. i contacted the customer relation department about this and they did not give a damn.

ladies out there, if you are choosing natural delivery, it's a good hospital with good doctors, but if you prefer a delivery with epidural, i would say go to another place unless if you want the worst birth experience.

if i could give this place a 0 star i would. i went here when i was about 13 years old and it didn't benefit me at all, the staff just made me feel worse about myself than i already did. they made fun of me for my reasons of trying to commit suicide. the staff (mostly men) would laugh at me! i thought this place was suppose to help us with our mentally but they just treated us like bad children. last time i recalled this was a behavioral institution not juvie. i felt like i was going to jail because they made me strip, think about it, a underage girl undressing herself in front of a woman when i had already been checked off, that's uncomfortable. i tried my best to  participate in activities because i knew would get me out of there, i just wanted to leave as soon as possible, i stayed less than a week. the longest week of my life and i still felt horrible, i had to pretend i was better and get through the staff mocking me, i didn't have the best relationships with the patients but the staff, the people that were suppose to help me just teared me more apart then i already was. not only didn't we see our parents as much but we could rarely call them, the staff wasn't there for us intellectually. like don't get a job just for the paycheck and to get through your day actually do your job and help these poor children. this place is garbage and i hope they found actual people that want to help children with their mentally, children are our future generation, and helping them is the best we can do help our world be a better place. i am now studying social work in nau and when i'm a social worker i will make sure my foster children or any other children in need of help never come here!

if i could give this hospital no stars that would be the case. lately i had been coming to this hospital because the er is never busy and believed i would be in and out soon because of its emptiness. 

the fact is that their service towards patients suck! the nurses in general are plain rude, don't care, make fun of patients, gossip for hours and ignore you. on top of that, they don't even have a dam interpreter for customers who are not bilingual, instead they use a dam tablet!! what kind of hospital doesn't have interpreters for their patients. how is the patient to express their feelings/pain. 

these nurses are unexperienced! they can't even  find your vein to insert the iv, they poke you about 10 times and just say sorry. "like hello! you're making my pain worst!"  

there is no communication or control at dameron. 

i go in as a visitor, a nurse at the entrance does her protocol as we are in the corona-virus pandemic, when the nurse and i are halfway to the lobby the security stops us, "excuse me where are you taking her? there are no visitors allowed." the nurse seemed to be unaware and takes me back to the entrance. 

my family member happened to be at dameron from 6am- 830pm and could not solve the problem nor had answers of the x-ray done. answers were never clear! the answer was always "let me ask the doctor and i'll have to get back to you." i was never called back. i had to stay on track and call the nurse department because may i remind you they have no interpreters. we went through 2-3 different nurses and all they would did was gossip and ignore my relative. if it wasn't because i personally went in and took my relative out that hospital they would have been doing the same and my relative would have remained suffering. they are not attentive whatsoever!!! everything you ask them to do, they do at their own pace. you press the button to have a nurse come to your room and ignore it and again come at their own pace and time! we can be dying and they don't care!! 

we left the hospital and drive towards st. joseph's. my relative was immediately taken care of and asked for interpreter in order to express their pain since all visitors must wait in car. when i told them what we went through and the fact that there were no interpreters at dameron they all laughed! they were also amazed! my relative was out of the hospital by 11:30pm and satisfied that st. josephs was able to solve/help with the pain. 

i advise you!! 
please do not visit dameron! 
go to another hospital!  unless you want to experience for yourself. this explains why their er is always empty and there is no wait outside, but behind those closed doors is a nightmare when in severe pain.

i went to damron hospital last night with mild fever bad cough headache mild diarrhea and my body was aching then they took me back in this room all they did for me was took xrays they didnt draw blood or have me take a urine test nothin said i had bronchitis and took me out to the lobby this is at 1:30am then they said i will have to leave cause nobody is to stay in lobby they didnt test me for the corona or nothing on that note i give this place.  - 5 stars

this is the worst hospital in california, i had three of my children there and they were great for that then they closed their ob dept(the only thing were good for). the er is horrible, they don't listen to the patient and they act like they don't care

if you need to go to the er..dont go to this place unless you're ready to fucking die. #1 the rude loud interrupting bitch who answers the ph has no respect for you, trust me. just call her and find out. lol........... #2 i guarantee they wont help you. if you arent gonna die while you're there, they send you home. no 
diagnosis no advice no nothing. had bad chest pains and went there yesterday. ... they said well you're not having a heart attack now but it appears you may have had 1 in the past. that's it. no explanation no instructions except to call my doctor in 72 hrs when hes open. still hurt real bad this morning. called because i'm concerned about endocarditis. it can kill you if not treated quickly. asked the rude bitch who answers the er phone, tina, if any of the testing they did yesterday would show if it could be endocarditis... she said no but in real life she has no clue. she said call your doctor monday. hilarious if it wasnt so sad.. its well worth the drive to sutter roseville for actual medical attention. i'm sure they arent mcg better but anything is better that auburn faith.dont they think it's possible you may have an infection in your heart? completely and utterly absurd. dont waste your time w auburn faith, you'll just wind up at another hospital anyway if you want to find out what's up. ridiculous. very sad too. seriously, this is the wrong er. i'm getting in my truck and going to another er besides auburn.

i've been coming to methodist for my obgyn needs for a few years now.  in, fact i delivered my son here!  this review is a bit bittersweet as my current health insurance carrier is terminating their relationship with methodist, so looks like i'm going to have to seek out a new practice and that makes me grumpy!

anyway, as with most doctor's offices - wait times can be rather atrocious so i would advise trying to take the earliest appointment in the morning or the first available after lunch.  they do tend to run further and further behind as the day progresses (this is common with most medical practices), so just bear that in mind and bring along a book or your ipad (there's free wifi).  i've been a patient of two doctors in the obstetrics and gynecology department and i've been pleased with the interactions and quality of care i received.  even the front desk staff, techs, and nurses have been understanding and patient, even when i've been disheveled and bewildered (as a first time pregnant lady can sometimes be).

i was especially pleased with my stay in the childbirth center.  it's a smaller labor and delivery area compared to some other hospitals in the medical center, which i feel facilitated a quieter and calmer stay, and it enabled the nurses and staff to provide more individualized attention to me and other patients.  granted, i only have this one experience to draw my opinion from, but the nurses were just so extraordinarily kind and helpful during my stay here.  almost two years later, my husband still brings up how lovely everyone was to us during our brief three day stay here.  i had a traumatic (but not life-threatening) postpartum complication that was rather unpleasant to deal with and the nurses really busted their butts to make me comfortable as possible and continuously tried to seek a resolution to my issue.

anyway, highly recommend methodist - especially for the obstetrics and gynecology department and the childbirth center.  hopefully i'll be able to return to the hospital in the future, should my insurance get their crap together.

will never visit this hospital again. back on january 10,2019 my son had to go to the er here. it was a lot of nurses and patients with mask on before this covid-19 was announced. it was hot in hospital instead of cold. they were overwhelmed with patients they even had them in waiting rooms receiving treatment talking to doctors and even drawing blood in waiting room. i took a picture because my wife couldn't believe they were drawing blood in wait room. not long after my visit i got sick with symptoms i've never had before. it took about 3 weeks to get well. they didnt take proper measure to make sure everyone was protected.

do not give birth at this hospital. these people are inhuman. they tortured and harassed us for days, and then called cps on us for opting to delay giving our newborn a vaccine intended for drug addicts and prostitutes. scum of the earth. we've had two other children at different hospitals around the us, and were treated very well and respectfully at those other hospitals. this place should be audited and many of these people should be fired. what a black eye on my lovely lone star state.

this methodist system has resources,employees,funding but it doesn't matter if i had insurance or not there was only one time i had a safe and decent experience.the nurse was attentive,polite( i have a chronic condition).
they really need to look at all locations and make sure they are cleaning properly and monitoring patients correctly. this is my experience was not good despite i tried to patiently speak up.

terrible customer service. tried to make an appt. calling every week for 7 weeks! always telling me they will call me back in 2-3 days with a very rude tone and they never called me back, anyways. played this game for 7 weeks. i won't try to go there ever again.

very unhappy with services provide at one of the supposedly best hospitals in texas. what a waist. very unprofessional and nothing but the run-around. they can treat patients without insurance just fine but a hard working insured client they send you from 1 place to another before you get tired. please be cautious with the physicians here, they are not favored to certain ethnicities but will take a homeless patient any minute. shame and disappointed. i want to especially point out the bellaire location methodist urgent care.

my 28 yr. old daughter had severe vomiting and right lower quadrant abdominal pain and was up all night due due to recurring ovarian cyst problems. she was waiting 30 min to get put in a room, retching in a hallway, it took over 90 minutes to get a nurse in to insert an iv and 2 hours before they gave her any iv fluids or pain meds. i wouldn't call this emergency care, but lazy care. i'm filing a complaint with the hospital board, joint commission and state of california. we are about to purchase a home here and move, but am now reluctant due to so. shame on you, eisenhower!

absolutely the worst place to be if you're sick!!! rude unprofessional staff, and filthy facilities! went in for a serious sinus infection, in horrible pain, and was appalled at the unprofessional attitude. i sat in a filthy waiting room and waited for hours to be seen. the other folks also waiting were treated to nothing but neglect!! i was put in a hallway when they finally called my name. inside the er was worse!  i was put on a gurney in the hallway and had to listen to the staff make fun of patients.  doc who finally saw me never touched me, said it was probably a sinus infection, which i already knew, and left me in the hall with a prescription for an antibiotic!  never have i seen such unprofessional behavior. stay away from this place. not the place to be if you're sick! i wonder who runs that disgusting place!

in february i was treated in the emergency room for diverticulitis. the doctor and staff were efficient. they quickly got me into radiology for analysis and back again. after getting my diagnosis from the doctor and rx for antibiotics the nurse told me to get dressed and leave even though i still had an iv "thing" stuck in my arm. other than that little hiccup i have nothing to complain about. this is a good medical center. i recommend it!

prior to my surgery, i had to come in for pre-op labwork and registration, as well as be tested for covid-19 as part of their policy. all patients must do so regardless of whether they have symptoms or not. the nurse was very nice and gentle with me, explaining everything as she went, apologizing for any uncomfortableness i felt. she truly tried to make it as easy as possible for me. i got a phone call the next day with my results (negative of course) and was then explained currently policy for visitors and what i needed to do the night before surgery, as well as the morning of. 

surgery day, i arrived. i was called back quickly and got put into my gown and compression socks and put into a bed and nestled under a super neat inflatable warming blanket. all the staff was very friendly and kept checking on me while we waited my turn for surgery. the anesthesiologist (chris lambert) was super nice. he cracked jokes to keep me from being nervous, and said he would make sure i had zero nausea when i woke up, because i always do. he kept his word - not one bit of nausea when i woke up after surgery. good man, thank you! 
the surgery itself was done by my own chosen surgeon (dr. chris park) so i'll leave that part of the review on his page, but it's fantastic. 
after surgery, i woke up in my own room. i stayed overnight because dr. park said he prefers that after what i had done, because he knows my pain is controlled and he is able to pop in and check on me. it seemed like i good idea, and would've been, had it went according to plan. but it didn't. 
dr. park came in to check on me and tell me surgery went great. at that point, i was in no pain, which was good. he told me to go on and call the nurse to start my pain meds, and i'd get them every 4 hours. i set an alarm on my watch for every 4 hours (something i learned while fighting cancer) to make sure i wake up and take them on time to stay ahead of it. he said one the pain hits, it's 10x harder to get it back under control. i called my nurse for pain meds at 7:51pm. i called again at 8:30 because she never came. she finally showed up at 9:20 with my pills and an attitude. by then i was in tears from the pain. i refused to let my husband facetime me because he would see how bad i was doing and i knew it would stress him out. (hospital has a no visitor policy, so he had to drop me off at the door and leave, and then pick me up the next day when it was time to go home.) i took the pills and thanked her. i reset my alarms since that obviously messed up my schedule. 4 hours later, alarm goes off and i request my pain meds. nurse doesn't show up til nearly 2 hours later, again. i'm in tears, again. i ask her politely if my chart says every 4 hours or every 6 hours in case i was confused from anesthesia when i talked to dr. park, since she was bringing them every 6 hours. she said "chart says 4, but you're not my only patient, so you get them when you get them." that's how my night went. when dr. park arrived bright and early the next morning, he was surprised to see me in pain and asked what happened. i told him, and he left the room immediately. i heard words being exchanged, and he came back in and apologized profusely for the experience i had because that's not how it should've been. he said my entire reason for being there was so that wouldn't happen, and i could tell he was greatly upset by it all. needless to say, after that, things were different.  i had a different nurse until i was discharged. i was immediately given morphine to knock out the pain, then set back on my original schedule of percocet every 4 hours. once they saw it was working as it should be (as it should have been last night had it been given correctly) i was able to go home. 
my daytime nurse was a gem. super sweet, very attentive if i needed anything, but i try not to call unless it's necessary. the food was delicious. 
other than that one night time nurse, my entire experience here with everyone was wonderful. 

** i will not name the night nurse. i only know her first name and it's a common one, so i don't want to put negative light on innocent people with the same name. i found out later that she was reported for her behavior, so that's all i'll say about that.

it is now a over a year later so this is an update on sgmc. 
while i gave it a 5 star rating then, i will have to give it a 2 star rating now that all the dust has settled. 
sgmc was my first in-depth experience for heart/stroke related issues as a wife.  i learned a lot of lessons!  
i am now familiar with the care and urgency of such a matter so i see how important it is to have a patient advocate with patient at all times besides the spouse. we tried to have someone there all the time but a patient needs a person who is knowledgeable and will take the time and demand answers which was very difficult to get in our situation. they,  also, need to be present, throughout the day. 
my husband was alone  traveling to florida from kentucky when he had the stroke. 
being a stroke victim, who can hardly understand anything after a stroke, let alone being by himself makes for bigger problems. 
no advocate at hospital at the time and no direction available for him being a stroke victim left him very vulnerable, as you can imagine. 
he did manage to tell them he was a vet (they are not affiliated with va) and had his va healthcard with him as well as a supplementary insurance card. 
i was aware of his stroke and called the hospital but was not allowed to speak to him so asked to speak to nurse who gave me update. 
i then was connected to finance department and told them he was a vet.  
i drove down there the next day and things were so stressful for me, as well. 
trying to take in all the information even with a case worker was too much. 
people were coming at me from different directions talking about pt, ot,etc and how important it was to get my husband into both asap!! 
they were on top of it and i so appreciated it at the time. 
they were pushing hard to get him the proper services but we were not residents of georgia and lived hundreds of miles away . 
i'm not young a young person and have health issues of my own so this was almost too much. 
all i knew is he wanted to go to a va rehab facility. 
i tried to honor his request. 
the hospital head of therapy tried to to get him into va hospital but sgamc said there were no beds only to find out months later they weren't calling correct facility from what va told us.  i
needless to say, there needs to be someone assigned to a patient that will listen to him/or her when there are no relatives available on site. caseworkers just don't have the time nor the knowledge of how va works, evidently, too. 
long story short -knowledgable patient advocate to direct or help patient and family( wife) know what the next steps are in helping the loved one get immediately what he or she deserves right then and there. someone who a spouse can contact to ask
questions. someone who will talk to the wife or family and explain. an advocate who  follows the patient the whole time they are in the hospital. 
one person that checks on his condition daily, is explains finances, checks to to see correct insurance is used and really has the patient's  welfare in mind. 
no one did that for my husband except his family that flew in to various surrounding airports, from boston, ky, dallas to drive hours the valdosta. 
while it seems things weren't going quickly to get him in rehab at hospital his family was working hard on their end to get to va ( then they could transfer him where he was closer to family) or anywhere finally just to get him closer to home and therapy. 
don't  know who dropped the ball but my husband ended up at this hospital without proper therapy for 19 days feeling captive. someone dropped the ball. 

my husband said it was humiliating and degrading experience once he got out of icu and put in another room. he couldn't get help to the bathroom or even take a bath because of shortage of medical techs. the only way he'd get cleaned  up was only after accidents. 
my son and niece asked several times while they were there for my husband to receive a bath or have his bed changed. neither saw it done while they were there. 
my husband was bathed 3x's in almost 3 weeks (last one being the day he was privately transported long distance to another facility), no bedding changes but 2x's (and they were from accidents after he left icu) in 14 days. 

he did say, however, the therapists were very good to him when he got therapy which, as i said before, became minimal the longer he was there. 

and, one more thing. too many hospitalists. too many doctors and all have different ideas!! it's confusing to a patient, especially a stroke victim. drs should know better!! 
part of a stroke is the confusion of the mind!  

in the end no one should feel captive in a hospital and not receive the proper care. 
someone dropped the ball and my husband was forgotten. 
he's paid the price.

review:
i was struggling with depression and acted on impulse one night, putting myself in danger, which led me to api's inpatient psych unit. after 3 nights, i was discharged and agreed to enter the iop program they offer.
i had never been to therapy before, let alone in a group setting, so i really didn't know what to expect. i really needed them to focus on helping me through my depression and anxiety. but for whatever reason, they always had me in the addiction recovery group. 
just before my release from inpatient, i mentioned that i smoked a little pot. i stopped smoking marijuana in 2001 when i was 20, and i picked it up again 17 years at the end of 2018. i smoked maybe 6 times, not necessarily enough to call it a "problem". but they still insisted that i belong in the recovery group. i had asked my psychiatrist, dr. markman, about it, and he 100% agreed with me that i am not here for addiction. he made a note of it, assuring me that they will take me out of that group and put me where i belong. well they continued to put me in that group. finally i spoke up, and i was told that they'll make a change. nothing changed. this went on every day for the next 5 months. i finally got fed up. so i would go in in the morning to see if they made that change, and if i saw my name on the board outside of the recovery room, i would just get back in my car and leave. if they didn't want to take me seriously, then i didn't need to be there. i did this on my last week before being discharged from the program, showed up, saw that they have me in the wrong group, i left, and as i was driving home i received a call from the program director, she gave me a hard time about just leaving like that without telling anyone. i turned around and went back to have a meeting with her. she explained to me that the reason i was being put in the recovery group was because it says on paper that i have a marijuana problem. i never did. the entire 5 months i was in this program i didn't touch the stuff once, and they know that because they test us once a week. but she insisted that i was wrong. i tried to explain to her that i wasn't here for marijuana. i tried explaining that i was suicidal. not only did i empty a bottle of zoloft into my mouth, but two days before that i went to home depot and bought a hose to see if it's wide enough to fit around my muffler pipe. but she still insisted that i needed to be in this recovery group.
that was my experience with alvarado parkway institute- la mesa. i was discharged in june of 2019, and to be honest, i wasn't ready to be discharged. i am still struggling with my demons every day. i was supposed to be working on myself while at api and they just ended up wasting my time. i still need help, i am still struggling, nothing has changed. but to be perfectly honest, i am very skeptical to start any other sort of program like this one, regardless of which hospital. they didn't respect my needs. they received their money through my insurance, they got what they wanted. 

to anyone who may be struggling, maybe you will have a different experience. 

adam k.

i'm giving this place two stars because there are some good and bad. i had a serious suicide attempt and i had voluntarily committed myself to walden. i acknowledged that i needed help and i was open to it--in fact, i was looking forward to it. as the days went on i felt more and more demoralized for the following reasons: (1) i felt deliberately disrespected by the nurses, many of them are super unprofessional and would make nasty remarks while the patients are present. i've had culturally insensitive remarks thrown at me when my parents brought me, i've seen a patient break down because a nurse said the patient was obnoxious to another staff. i've dealt with another nurse pressuring me to take medication, rogue from the recommendations of the psychiatrist. (2) it felt more traumatic to be there. there was a lot of intermixing in regards to the severity of the patients mental illness. there were instances where i'd wake up to shrieking. i've seen a 16 year old patient being sedated in a violent manner. (3) another thing i really hated was during visiting hours a nurse pulled me aside for more intake stuff. i valued my visits because it was that one time i could actually reconnect to my world outside of walden. i'm not able to spend nearly as much time with my loved ones. i asked the nurse if it was possible to do it another time but she said she can only do it during that time (i highly doubt it). 
there are patients of all sorts of age range: from 16 to patients roughly in their late 50's to 60's. regardless of who you were outside of the hospital, your sense of dignity is ripped away. i felt infantilized and like i can't be trusted. i feel like recuperation from mental illness is being able to trust yourself again but it's harder to do that when i'm being gaslighted by certain staff. feeling self-sufficient is a luxury here. 
i felt more depressed the longer i remained there so i signed myself out because i felt that this place was jeopardizing any chance i had at recovering. there were good parts--any part that does not involve the nurses. i thought the psychiatrist was helpful. i felt comfortable opening up because for the first time i felt respected and sane. my psychiatrist was completely transparent and respectful of my boundaries. i also felt the mental health counselors to be very helpful because they listened and worked harder than the nurses. i felt safer crying and actually voicing my concerns and fears.
if there were some structure and transparency, if there was more effort to advocate for patients--this would have been a much better place.
