review:
this is for the physical therapy department only.  

i've had the unfortunate luck of having multiple joint replacements and other orthopedic surgeries (before becoming kaiser member) at a young age. the reasons why were never clear though many doctors have tried to figure it out.  the most common theory is that because i have hypermobility but was very active from a young age, this has deteriorated my muscle skeletal structure and started a domino effect. 

i had good physical therapy following my surgeries and the replaced joints are not a problem.  however, i continue to experience profound pain and discomfort on my right hip which is my one remaining major natural joint.  x-rays show no reason for this. i went to kaiser pt multiple times but found that the treatments actually worsened the pain.  when i eventually said this to the pt (actually a very nice guy) he basically threw up his hands.  

this issue has affected me greatly and i am in constant pain regardless of trying things like meditation, turmeric, foam rolling, etc. etc.  i've even had to resort to strong opioids left over from my surgeries even though i had weaned off long ago. i finally decided to bite the bullet and pay out of pocket for a place recommended by a neighbor.  i had immediate relief after the first session.  here's what they do that kaiser pt does not:

- you do the exercises with the therapist monitoring as opposed to going home with an exercise sheet. this allows you to report areas of pain or discomfort as you do the exercises and it also allows them to try other things while making note of your comments.

- hyper-mobile people have distinct needs, and therapy modes that work for most may well not work for them or have to be adjusted. i'm now working with someone who specialists in hypermobile patients.

- the new place truly deep dives into diagnosis.  muscle skeletal issues are complex and there are a diverse set of reasons why x may hurt.  you may have weak hips, but your issue may go beyond that and there may be a reason as to why your hips are perpetually weak.  kaiser pt is great for people who neatly fall into the bucket of widely known issues and common prescriptions, but for people who need a more individualized care it is a black hole. 

- i barely did any exercises in person with kaiser, so needless to say they did not help with any stretching whatsoever. in my case, though i'm double jointed there are a couple of tight areas that i simply cannot stretch on my own.  the new pt recognizes how crucial this is, and i can attest to the importance of this.

i really like kaiser in many ways, but in terms of pt the experience has been literally painful.  i've asked permission for an outside pt referral but if you're familiar with kaiser you understand how almost impossible that is.  this is a shame because i've probably cost them more money in terms of constant doctor appointments, mris, x-rays, etc. than what they could have paid for an outside pt for a few months. i could only afford to pay out of pocket for just a few sessions so i now spend hours each day doing self pt at home.  the personal cost of being in pain is enormous  - financially, emotionally, and socially.  i truly wish that an excellent organization like kaiser, which seems to genuinely care about public health, would take another approach to their treatment of physical therapy and pain management.

i was transferred to john muir inpatient from contra costa regional medical center's psychiatric emergency services (ccrmc, pes) located in martinez. john muir was definitely an upgrade, but i suppose anything would be better than pes.

i had 2 inpatient stays, both in february 2020. the first was from february 6 to february 10. the second was from february 18 to february 26. the first discharge was premature, but the second one was helpful in my recovery.

i was admitted on the second day of my 5150 (72 hour hold) as i had attempted suicide. the remainder of the stay was on a voluntary basis as i was willing to comply with treatment. the oak adult unit has friendly staff. most of them aren't licensed therapists, but they are still knowledgeable in various therapy concepts. i really enjoyed the groups, especially expressive arts. the registered nurses are professional and check in with you frequently to make sure you are safe. 

the psychiatrist i worked with, dr. mundi, is a jerk. when i shared what had pushed me to hurt myself, he was very dismissive. i made sure to let the staff know, and was assigned to a nurse practitioner during my second inpatient stay.

the food is really good. they really care about their patients health, both physical and mental. we had patio breaks throughout the day which was our only time to get fresh air. the nurses giving medication were very nice and helped me understand the specifics such as side effects and a time frame to notice improved mood.

naturally, i was home sick, but we were allowed to have visitors and access to a phone to call our family. the rooms had 2 beds, and a bathroom with a shower. 

the reason i was admitted again was because the first discharge was premature. the post discharge care plan did not work, and no one followed up with me despite me leaving several voicemails. fortunately, the second time around the post discharge care plan worked great and i was able to get a referral for further care at a crisis residental, hope house in martinez.

i give john muir behavioral health 4 stars. the facilty was clean, the staff was nice, the rooms were safe, and the food was good. there were rounds conducted every 15 minutes to make sure everyone was accounted for. it may affect your sleep, but the staff tries to be very quiet. safety is very important, so it didn't bother me.

on a side note, my very first inpatient stay was at fremont hospital in 2018. though the facilty was bigger and had a pool and court, i felt the staff was very impersonal. john muir behavioral health may not have all the extra features fremont hospital has, but quality is better than quantity. you are seen as a person, not as your diagnosis. 

we occasionally had students from samuel merritt take our vitals, all of whom were very nice. overall, this was a good experience and helped me grow. i doubt i will ever return because i now know how to cope in times of emotional distress. but i feel reassured knowing a place like john muir behavioral health exists. 

if i were to give any advice, it would be to speak with your social worker regarding care post discharge. this is very important. if you are troubled, you can talk with the staff. every shift each patient is assigned a registered nurse, mental health counselor, and social worker. they will listen.

thank you john muir staff.

review:
i went to the emergency room complaining of an increased heart rate, the onset of significant fatigue, nausea, and vague pain in my feet.  i was confused and thinking slowly. i told them these symptoms started a couple of days ago one night after work when i was trying to go to sleep. i thought i was having a bout of tachycardia as i had been diagnosed with svt in the past.

i was given an ekg, a chest x-ray, and two blood tests. on the way to get my chest x-ray, the technician was taking me back to the x-ray room and i suffered a severe abdominal cramp. after that subsided, i was taken back into the waiting room until a room had been prepared for me. once in the room, a pa came in and gave me a medical examination. i had to sit up in bed so that she could listen to my lungs. when i sat up, i again had a severe abdominal cramp. she immediately stopped the examination and said she was going to order fluids.

an iv catheter was inserted into my arm but the fluids the pa supposedly ordered never came. i laid on the bed clutching my stomach, trying my best not to move as i felt like any movement might set off another spasm.

eventually dr. zachary simms came in with the pa in tow. this was the first time i had seen or spoken to him at all the entire night. he immediately told me that i was having a panic attack and that my symptoms were psychosomatic. the basis of this diagnosis was that outside of the ekg, the other tests had come back normal, combined with a distant (about 10 years or so) diagnosis of generalized anxiety disorder. i told him i didn't think this was a panic attack, as i am familiar with how a panic attack feels. his response was a speech about how i was going to be in and out of emergency rooms for my entire life, i was always going to feel bad, and that i needed to go see a psychiatrist. he gave me a prescription for vistaril. he was explaining what the medication was, when i told him that i had taken vistaril before and was familiar with it. his response was condescending and something along the lines of "yes, i'm sure you have." i told him i wasn't there for pills, especially anxiety medications as i try to only take them when i feel they are absolutely necessary. i again tried to explain that i hadn't really felt anxiety in a while, which was met with further indifference. he told me one day i was going to have a real medical emergency and i wouldn't get help because of my panic attacks. it was one of those classic "if you weren't crazy, you'd agree with me that you're crazy" catch-22s.

he eventually just left and i was told to leave. despite still feeling pretty horrible, i did so, mostly because i didn't have the energy to get into some prolonged argument. i was provided with zero assistance. i slowly drove myself back to my house and, being exhausted, immediately went to sleep.

the next day i woke up with a severe headache, dry mouth, cramping, a racing heart, and nausea. i sat down in the bathroom and tried to take some tylenol, which caused me to begin dry retching. following dr. simms' advice that my symptoms were induced with anxiety, i powered through it and went to work at my job as a carpenter. i sipped water throughout the day as much as i could, but my symptoms just got worse. eventually i said to hell with it and decided to ignore dr. simms' diagnosis.

i realized i hadn't urinated in about two days at that point, and when i did, my urine was a deep yellow/brownish color and low in volume. it turns out a combination of a new diet, the recent heat, and the vigorous nature of my job had put me in a state of dehydration. after fluid replacement, my symptoms began to subside.

so to summarize, a man who works outside in the sun all day doing physical labor came into the er after work, complaining of an increased heart rate, fatigue, pain, and more or less just feeling like crap. he had a history of increased heart rate and a distant history of anxiety and depression. while in the er, he suffered two massive cramps. rather than going to the very simple conclusion of dehydration, dr. simms', who i can only assume at this point is the disowned love-child of carl jung and christian bernard, decided that i was deluded and suffering from a complex reaction to anxiety. i also can only assume that he told the pa to not give me any fluids, though i will be attempting to find out whether or not that is true monday evening.

unfortunately, as far as i understand it, this is not a case of malpractice; not because of how dr. simms' decided to handle this issue, but because i did not suffer any significant injury as a direct result of it. i will be following up with a complaint to the hospital and any relevant governing bodies that i can find, as well as posting this review anywhere that is applicable. i doubt anything will come of it, but it will at least give me a sense of vindication.

i've been ill and decided to get tested for covid-19 today. they had lines for people who were in cars and for those who were not. i had to wait in the car line, which probably took much longer than the other line, but i had no choice.

on first arrival, i was confused on where to enter the line and accidentally turned into the test site from the adjacent alley. they were about to let me go through as if i had waited my turn until i told them that i didn't know where to go. the healthcare worker i spoke with calmly told me where i needed to go. i was impressed because i know that if that were me i might be a little tense and impatient.

the car line took about 3-3.5 hours to get through. it might seem like a super long wait time, but i don't think i could've had any better or faster of an experience. it's the only free test site i know of that doesn't require some sort of permission from your gp. and when i say "free", i mean they don't ask for or charge your insurance company. it's a great resource for the city, especially the neighborhood the hospital is located in.

i tried getting tested at a couple other sites (one of which employs many of my regular doctors), but the instructions on their websites were vague. when i tried to call their lines were completely busy or their voicemail was full.

so i'd like to thank (with all my heart!) the loretto employees who are providing this service in the most convenient way possible. they truly made it as smooth as possible. i would've waited in that line for another three hours if i had to!

the whole staff is really sweet and nice! i can not get enough of my stay here and making me feel really comfortable as possible since my baby does not want to come yet. they answered and talk to me with all my questions and i'm beyond thankful and bless to have a great staff this past week.

dr lalonde performed a hysterectomy on me and left 2 bleeders. i never felt right after surgery and shared how i felt with the nurses on duty. i was answered with "you are not supposed to feel good". after 18 hrs post-surgery i was having trouble catching my breath and still ignored by the nurses on duty. i asked that a hematocrit be run - they refused -saying they would ask the doctor but that i didn't need one. then they began pressuring me to leave - for 3 hours i resisted - insisted that there was something really wrong. they ignored me and went so far as the literally yank the o2 hose and say (triumphantly) "you don't need this anymore". finally i consented to go - got up in altitude to go home and ended up feeling really bad. couldn't breathe - massive debilitating headache, peripheral vision going dark --- went straight to the local hospital and they determined i was bleeding internally after a ct scan. 4 blood transfusions and another surgery later, i spent a week in the hospital with a 50/50 chance of making it. i will lay money down that those 2 simply awful human beings known as nurses still work there, even though the hospital was made well aware of the situation and the nurses' complete lack of attention to a life threatening issue. dr lalonde - never bothered to follow up or even ask/call to see how i was. when i did contact his office, he could only tell me how excellent his surgical record was. he is arrogant and unfeeling. the whole experience was a nightmare - thank goodness for an excellent general surgeon who put me back together and the transfusion nurse who was an angel. they saved my life and i am grateful beyond measure to both of them. avoid memorial womens wing if you at all can.

(after hiring an attorney, i finally received the phone conversation recordings that both hospitals' cmo told me i would never receive.) the hospitalist at porter told the hospitalist at mercy that porter doctors did not have higher skill sets than mercy doctors, but still accepted the transfer.  brian left mercy on a flight for life plane in fair condition, but he actually had dangerously high blood pressure, a map reading with alert next to it and 9 out of 10 pain.  he was given an opioid for the pain right before the plane took off.  there was no plan for surgery when brian arrived at porter, instead he was assigned to an inpatient room.  he died in his bed 11 hours later when the pseudoaneurysm burst.   my son's autopsy shows that he died from the rupture of a known aneurysm.  brian actually died from lack of treatment by an inept medical system.  per john hopkins hospital study - medical errors account for 1/3 of hospital deaths.  as of today, there is a reported 60,726 covid-19 deaths in the us.  as of today, the number of deaths caused by medical errors is probably much higher, but these deaths are recorded as the condition the patient had, not the medical errors that caused the death. medical errors are a silent, rampant epidemic

i was just traumatized at the memorial er hospital in southbend today.  i had been exposed to the coronavirus but was told my results would not be back for 7-10 days.  meanwhile, i got worse but then i got better, but then two days ago, i had taken a turn for the worse--fever, chills, cough, etc., all those symptoms came back with a vengeance. so, upon hearing that it could take up to 10 days for my results to come back, i looked at my sons and told them i couldn't wait any more. i had to go to the er. we called the cdc to see what we needed to do. they told me to call the er, so they could prepare for me. 

i called the memorial hospital er, and they told me to just go in and register. however, after self-quarantining for 8 days, i was not about to go into a public population and possibly expose anyone if i had the coronavirus. my brother called the hospital  and they gave him different instructions for me to follow, which was call them when i got to the er, and someone would come out to me. 

none of this protocol was followed once i arrived. i was told to just go in. yep. i refused to go in, so my brother called the hospital again, and the lady informed him that if someone is telling me to go in, then i should just go in. (all recorded by the way.)

now, i'm going to move directly to the er room with the doctor, and this is where i was completely traumatized, accused and made to feel like a criminal. (i'm a 56 year old professional--educator). 

the doctor came into the room and goes to listen to my lungs. he twists my shoulders away from him. (i get it, and i'm okay with it.  he didn't  want me to breathe on him), but then he used his elbow to turn my head so it faced the door. then after he had listened to my lungs, he started asking why i came to his hospital to expose people if i had the coronavirus . (i forgot to mention that an iv had been put in my arm but not taped down because the nurse had forgotten the tape, and at this point,  i totally understood that they wanted to spend very little time in my room in case i'm positive--and i'm okay with it up until this point.)

i had mentioned the iv to the doctor when he first came into my room, and i even told him that the iv looked like it had twisted in my vein.  while this doctor was on a tirade, blaming me for being at the hospital and accusing me of spreading sickness to everyone, he reached across the left side of my bed and jerked, not pulled, the iv out of my right arm. he then left while i was bleeding in that room. 

i called my brother, crying and panicked, and my brother told me to take pictures of everything. because of my hysteria, i had only taken two pictures when a nurse came into the room, telling me to calm down. i showed her my bleeding arm and told her that i couldn't calm down informing and showing her what the doctor had done to me. (by the way, my brother was still on the speaker phone.) the nurse then threatened to call security to take my phone if i took another picture. my brother then spoke up and said no one better not touch my phone or they would be sued. 

while i was still upset and crying, my brother called the administration of the hospital and informed him how i was being treated. 30 minutes later, the doctor came back into my room to apologize because he said it had been years since he had done an iv, and he didn't know that when he pulled my iv out like he had done that i would bleed like i did.  he then proceeded to say everyone's nerves were on edge because of the coronavirus. i continued to let him try to explain why i he had treated me so horrible. 

when he finished, i then reminded him that i had complied with everything that i had been told to do while awaiting my test results and that i had come to the hospital because i was getting worse instead of getting better--only to have a doctor accuse, blame and make me feel like criminal--when all i was seeking was medical help.

i still don't know if i'm positive or negative. i'm still waiting for my results to come back, and i've been on self-quarantine for 8 days. my nerves are also on edge, and a medical doctor traumatized me when i needed reassurance.  i'm the one who has done everything i've been told to do--not going out partying, gathering in groups, etc..  

i have self-quarantined for 8 days now, and i needed reassured that i was going to be okay today. attached are the two pictures of how the doctor left my room after jerking the iv out of my arm. today, i needed a doctor who was at his best to take care of me, not a doctor who was stressed whose nerves were on edge. i had gone to this hospital for medical treatment, but instead, i left completely traumatized.

review: i was an employee and started this review when i left so knowing they did demolish and rebuild a section which personally, i felt had so much history yet the rooms not being used were very very dated, i still gave it a 4 because i dont know if the intended plan for the assisted living building to be built has been completed or new changes. however, don't let that affect your opinion of my review. i worked there 2 years in the therapy department, separate company so keeping that aside as well, with over 15 years of experience working in healthcare facilities across the us at the time 2016 i can truly say that this facility was one of the best places i have worked and let me just say i have worked in some really low and high quality locations and would have definitely sent my family there for recovery, long term care i'd have some questions if in san francisco. possible disadvantages finding which door to enter was a little confusing. if you did not celebrate jewish traditions, and those that were orthodox, small things like food during traditional practices were given to all patients but i believe you could have special requests.the people who were in the other building for long term, were in dated rooms and mostly non english speaking residents so if you want your loved one to socialize in a long term facility i would ask which building/floor and the people showing the facility were nice. also, it had a somewhat high rate of employees coming and going mainly to pursue dreams after getting experience to go work in hospitals or lower their commute. also, the few days where it reached 90 degrees..for some reason it seemed to take forever to have the air turned on in the patients rooms. otherwise the temperature was comfortable year round. also parking was an issue but thats more for employees, guests could pull up front. possible pros a shuttle bus from the bart, wasn't labeled at the time. they had fold up beds for families to stay and meals, a cafe,  a gift shop, a huge library, a pharmacy, x ray machine, and doctors that came in constantly and sometimes student doctors. i personally liked all the doctors however 1 seemed a bit too honest and one thing in recovery or medicine in general everyone heals differently and i over heard the doctor tell a patient's daughter their loved one was not going to walk again (this was in passing and i did not hear the entire conversation however i do remember a bit of a language barrier so perhaps in an attempt to help the family member not set her hopes so high the doctor may have tried to narrow the language gap) with that said their loved one did walk again with help and that is a good feeling to have and see. the staff was friendly and if i was a client i wouldn't have felt nervous asking a worker walking by a question as you would in some facilities. they had 3 or 4 gyms, and as an employee you could sign up to use 1 during specific times. camera's and guards surveillance at the entrance  who also walked the perimeter ensuring safety. in the end a lot of changes were occuring but i would like to think it was for the best.

i am 45 years old and i went into acute renal failure about a week and a half ago. i went to centennial hills hospital and stayed for 6 nights, since it was close to my home. i wasn't given any information why this happened to me. the communication to patients from the centennial hills hospital staff was horrible!!! all they could tell me is that i was dehydrated and they needed to pump me with fluids for 6 days. they also told me to stop my blood pressure medication. and i never saw a cardiologist while i was there. centennial released me with no post care other then to follow up with my primary physician and no medication to treat my hypertension.  
i scheduled to follow up with my primary care doctor. thankfully i was able to see them 4 days after they released me. the morning of my appointment my symptoms came back and my blood pressure was extremely elevated. thankfully my primary physician group, internal medicine specialists of las vegas, (dr. milne, dr. petersen and dr. silver) examined me and directed me to go to valley hospital immediately. they called valley hospital er department and gave them a heads up that i was coming. i was there within 10 minutes and getting care from the staff. 
the er staff at valley hospital was so caring and so attentive to me and really showed that they care about their patients! callie rn and makenzie rn, that helped me in the er were amazing! thank you both for making me feel calm during a very anxious situation for me. i also saw a pa and a resident from internal medicine specialists in the er. they were very helpful and were very interested in solving my case! they communicated with me and my spouse the plan of action, they made sure we were well informed of what they were going to do and never once did we have to ask for test results. the pa was always keeping us informed. i got admitted into valley hospital for further testing and was transferred to the 4th floor. every nurse and every certified nursing assistant that handled my care has been outstanding! i would like to thank matt rn, ron rn. stephanie rn, tina rn, ebony cna, rahel cna and denise cna for their efforts of making my stay in the hospital very comfortable. they made me feel like something was actually being done to get me the help i needed to get past all this. 
the ultrasound technicians and radiologist technicians were super sweet as well. valley hospital has been around for years! i live far from the hospital but for future medical emergencies for me or my family i will always go to valley hospital! thank you so much to the whole team there and for the quality of care you have given me!!!

fac_name: Barnabas Health Retail Pharmacy at Saint Barnabas Medical Center

review:
after having my dad go to the er with signs of a stroke i have to admit the doctors and nurses here done a fantastic job helping him. the majority of the staff, with the exception of a charge nurse in the er was very pleasant and helpful; it's all about how you speak to people and when the people are already stressed out because of uncertainty, don't come at them with attitude, no matter your position. 

my father was well taken care of and even yesterday after having been discharged we were called to ensure my dad was doing ok. that means a lot. 

keep up the great work but train the charge nurse..

i came into the er for low blood sugar via an ambulance. my nurse was okay and my doctor was awesome and friendly. the reason they are getting one star is when i was rushed to the er it was morning and i didn't have my contacts in. i asked when i was discharged how to get the the er exit, the lady laughed and said follow the signs. i said i don't have contacts in should i go left or right at the end. she said it's not that hard follow the doors and you'll find yourself outside  good luck. the rudest thing someone who is cleaning out trash bins in patients rooms could say. as well as this a patient next door to me was fighting (physically) with a nurse and i'm not sure who was at fault but after it settled down. all the nurses were gathered being extremely loud outside the room talking about the patient and expected her to not react when 8 ppl are standing there talking down on her. long story short dont go here unless your desperate. because this place is empty and
dead, there must be a reason.

i visited the er extension in harrison, ohio. i was seen fairly promptly but that was the only good thing i have to say. 
the visit required that blood work be done. results of the renal function indicated that my creatinine level was high and the doctor was admitting me to the hospital. he later advised me that mercy west had no beds available so they would check at mercy fairfield for admission availability but that i would have to pay for the ambulance service from harrison to fairfield. after deliberation and finding that it wasn't the level was not unreasonably high and that i would have to pay for the ambulance service, it was decided to go home and drink lots of fluids and follow up with my pcp on monday. while preparing me to be released the nurse removed the iv from my arm and the tape used actually tore my skin off in 2 places revealing raw flesh when i removed it. i had to treat it with antibiotic ointment and covered it with gauze and non adhesive wrap.
my pcp agreed to fit me into her loaded schedule. she repeated the blood work and treated my arm from the iv tape.  the following day i received a call from her office indicating that blood work looked ok but to continue drinking lots of fluids.
i went to my chart to view my test results.  i found the test results from the work done by my pcp and the results of all the blood work done at the harrison er except for the renal function results. i called
i called my chart who advised that i needed to call the er doctor to get the results posted.  i called the er, waited on hold for 12 minutes and hung up..  they told me to call central records.
i understand not able to be admitted because there were no beds (flu season was at its peak), but for me to have to pay out of pocket to be taken to the fairfield mercy hospital was ridiculous. my chart could be a useful tool but only if has correct information and is kept up to date.
i will do everything in my power to avoid anything to do with the mercy hospital system.

i am a 18 year old transgender woman and i was discriminated today by delware country memorial hospital. for 1 i asked to by called zaria (due to covid-19 my court appointment was delayed) and to be addressed as a female. they put it in my chart but yet only 20% of the staff addressed me properly and i keep telling them and they didn't listen. i went in with chest pains and abdominal pain and got 302! they held me against my will as it stated in my chart because i'm 18 and transgender! they worded it as such. if they were concerned about the side affects of my medication they could have said "due to the medication and the patient's depression we suggest...". i told the doctor i suffer from depression and i get discriminated against because i am a 18 year old african american hispanic transgender female i am absolutely disgusted and will be pursuing legal matters. please see attached doctors notes. i was in the er for almost 48 hours waiting for there crisist center to have a bed. once they finally had a bed i was taken there and released! the psychiatrist told me he was not going to up hold the 302 and that doctors should think and ask more questions before 302ing someone. he told me the 302 would not be in my record because he didn't uphold it. and my real reason of going there for my medical issues wasn't even resolved. they told me all the test was negative but didn't even let me speak to the doctor after my exam when the test came back to see what he thought it was. the doctor who wrote the note was dr. michael dumin. i am highly upset!

i was just here on may 6, i've had emergency c-section and it went very well. nurses and doctors was very responsive, kind and caring . personally i want to shout out to nurse belinda that work on 2nd floor for labor and delivery. she took very well care of me thru out her shift and i forever appreciate that. other nurses that was there also did a wonderful job as well , i didn't want to take that away from the others. also i want to give so much thanks to the nicu nurses for caring for  my little premie baby.  without you guys  there is no hope for lil babies like mines. thank you west houston staff!!!!

the worst experience ever

do not come to this hospital 


my sisters got in to a head on car accident. they were rushed to hca west houston on richmond street
the staff was very rude and they were being  rushed to get out my sisters out from there as quickly as they could from the er.

they even give us wrong discharge papers from another patient that wasn't ours, that's how fast they wanted to discharge my sisters.  the nurses were not helpful at all, complaining why they were there. 
please save yourself and go to another hospital where they will take care of you.

i used to love hocking valley community hospital, but recently have been so disappointed with them. they have inept billing, and refusal to work with their patients to get to an agreement, they would rather send to collections with meade and associates that will harrass you, yell at you, and scream at you and threaten you than actually help the patient. during covid 19, they have decided to take things a step further and sue me for medical bills. i am an rn, a front liner, risking my life, but apparently hvch needs money right now! they want to garnish my wages and here's the worst part, this is from 2013 and to my understanding was already taken care of. i am beyond disappointed!  if i had medicaid, these bills would be done, but since i'm working, i'm penalized. i will never ever recommend this hospital again. they have adamant refusal to work with anyone in regards to payments. their ceo and cfo would rather have money. patient care has gone out the window at hvch. 
sincerely disappointed

i got to spend two nights here recently. luckily i wasn't the patient -- but i kept my man company after his surgery. i actually slept on two chairs bedside while he was there. 

i've been here before myself, but they seem to have upped their game. in addition to taking all the extra precautions for covid, every person we came in contact with was very professional and enjoyable to deal with -- from the cleaners on up to the doctors and nurses. there really was a great team effort. and it shows. 

each shift change, they came in and introduced the new people. they went over the necessary info and posted it each time on a board by the bed. each patient has a phone with the number to call to reach the attending nurse, the assistant and floor personnel. it's a very efficient system. and they are very informative to prepare the patient for what's going to happen and how to manage your pain. 

the food here was surprisingly way better than average for hospital food. every morning starting at 6:30 am you can call in your breakfast order from their menu. it takes about an hour or less to get your hot breakfast. you use your phone to call the kitchen extension. (hint: they're busy. don't hang up. just hold til they answer.) choices included various omelets, eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes, breads/cakes, fresh and canned fruits, juices, cereals, etc. the only thing they didn't have was toast! you also call in for your other meals at least an hour or so in advance. lunches, too, were good as well as dinners. there's a lot of variety and they try to accommodate all requests if possible. two standouts were their fresh sliced hot turkey with mashed potatoes and gravy and their mac n cheese.

the hospital offers free valet parking which is helpful as the lot fills up. 

the only downside was the day we came their computers were acting up so it  took longer to register and to be processed during pre-op. and a longer time than expected waiting for a room to be available. 

no one really wants to be in a hospital, but if you do need to be, this is one of the better options in town.

the miscommunication, misinformation, incompetence, stolen items and more from hcsfl and their staff is absolutely inexcusable and is a sorry excuse for a hospital! 
to go into detail...
this place is terrible. every time i thought the incompetence and miscommunication couldn't get any worse, it did. started when my fathers bag with his personal items (cell phone, eye glasses to see, ugg slippers clothes, etc) were stolen. we tried endlessly to track them down to be told by multiple people they can't do anything to help us. while in his room getting his mobile chest x-ray, a maintenance painter came in and started painting a wall in his room when he was already having trouble breathing from an infection caught from them! skipping to the end when they called us to say my father had died, only to be called back saying sorry we read the wrong chart he isn't dead! at the end of the day, i blame this hospital entirely for his decline into hospice. if you want to live do not go here.
(not to mention their covid protocol during our time there was a joke and staff did not even follow procedures often like wearing gloves or masks. unacceptable.)

my dad has leukemia, he spiked a high fever so i was told to bring him to the nearest hospital, i had options but chose holy, i had 2 children their and many of our doctors are affiliated. we got to the er and there was no covid tent, reluctantly, i took him in. i am an rn at another facility and we all have "covid tents". my neutropenic father was with the general population, triage was not visible. after 30 mins, i chose to leave, risk my father and go to another facility. i am extremely heartbroken and disappointed in holy cross and the direction it has gone. i will continue to see our beloved mds at their facilities but would not consider going inpatient after what i saw.

dr. cappezzuitti is the best ! i have been seeing her for years and couldn't be happier .. her bedside manors are amazing and she always takes the time to listen to you .. if you are in need of a new doctor i highly recommend her :)

emergency room -   while under influence of some serious pain meds was wheeled up to xray.  no one put my large purse on my cart and while left in my er cubicle, someone went in and stole my credit card wallet.  i found out when i got a text a few days later that someone was attempting to use two cards.  i made a complaint on my survey and a head nurse called.  he said "make a police report".  that's the level of concern.  the osteo they referred me too wrote a prescription for the wrong side of my body.  really?  such incompetence,
serves gourmet meals. nice setup. regimented physical rehab.

review: so weird to post this but best blood draw ever. i have told i have "rolly polly" veins and i also am super scared of needles. add to that the whole covid thing and i was a little leery even though i needed to get labs done. aiza was my phlebotomist this morning and she was awesome! got it on the first stick, which literally has never happened for me!

i can only say good things about bolivar medical center! the website provides a wait time for the emergency room, which is fantastic. while there is a hospital in the town i was in, i drove 45 minutes because i know the service and knowledge of the physicians is so much better here. i was quickly taken back, triaged and the doctor came shortly afterwards. the facility is super clean and, since i'm germaphobic, i never felt unsafe or concerned. the nurses and check in staff were so professional, courteous and made me feel like they really cared.

i am a fan of the recently opened, drop-off that they have installed this previous year.  in my previous post, trying to drop off handicapped elders was quite the stressful experience. i see a huge difference in this new set-up that includes:
(a) more spots available for cars to wait for passengers
(b) a level ground to ease the patients' transition from vehicle to walking aid.
(c) more kp personnel standing by to help assist with handing off wheelchairs or providing support to persons needing a hand in or out of the vehicle.
(d) traffic personnel helping to move cars in and out of open spaces.
looks like kp put a good deal of thought into redesigning this active space and i appreciate the value it brings to patients and their families who visit.
great efforts made by the medical staff despite the chaos outside with covid-19.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
my wife is pregnant and has severe anxiety. it is reported in her medical record that she has adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depression.

i am not allowed to accompany her on the appointments. i am not allowed to be with here during her ultrasounds, and i wasn't even allowed to be on video chat during her last ultrasound. i have been excluded from the experience of having my first child. i am extremely disappointed.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
i've always liked the woodland hills location of kaiser. except for the recent construction and their parking garage with all the miss directing signage, it's always been pretty good.
so now i'm scheduled for a medical procedure. they require i do covid testing prior to the procedure. no problem i go in and do that, and extremely unpleasant experience by the way. then i get a call the day before my procedure telling me that the test results have not come back in for the covid. i have two choices, come in in the morning and i will do a rapid covid test just before the procedure. or go ahead and do it without the test results. 
i asked them if the people performing the procedure have gone through the covid test? they informed me they have not! that doesn't make any sense to me. that combined with the fact when i was recently in there picking up my prescription there was some kind of meeting going on in the pharmacy area. a group of hospital employees huddled together discussing things. and the person that seem to be leading the meeting was wearing his mask with his nose hanging over it. hospital staff! i asked the young woman behind the plexiglass and she confirmed yes they were hospital staff. he obviously overheard me and pulled his mask up over his nose..
i'm not surprised when i see this out shopping, but none of this makes any sense at the hospital. this affects the professional credibility of the facility. 
i ended up canceling my procedure.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review: this is a review for their obgyn dept.  - my wife gave birth there and the nurses were like headless chickens, they never cleaned my wife after giving birth, the room was also never cleaned, we were in a room surrounded by bloody tissues and bloody utensils, they didn't even clean/remove all the left overs from inside her.

review: love coming here had my child here they treated us very well! the staff here is so kind ! very caring and respectful.

review:
i have been fortunate to have had caring and compassionate practitioners for decades at this location however i have recently noted a disparity in care, communication and clinical aptitude with my most recent provider. i speak specifically of steve loh in physical medicine. at no time during my months i was under his care did he make any attempt to address my chief complaint or aide in managing my symptoms. the only interventions were repeating expensive testing and talk of referral to other departments for consultations. 
i sincerely hope that kaiser is not losing it's seasoned and clinically competent doctors during this time when we need them most. should they continue to replace physicians with those of dr loh's aptitude, i would think that many people myself included will seek care elsewhere.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
be aware that kp prefers that you use their pharmacy, and will go so far as to not send your prescriptions at outside pharmacies.  i needed a scrip faxed to my local pharmacy but their policies prevent that from happening, but they wont tell you that, you just won't get the meds. keep that in mind if you are considering using kp. i have never heard of a doctor/hospital that could not fax in a prescription to a local pharmacy and then get dumb about it when called about why it did not happen. and never call in early, you will get passed around with no help, leave them to have their coffee and donuts, call in later in the day. kp is ok for checkups but if you have a serious issue, they will fail you.
so i check the website to get a phone number for the 24 hr pharmacy and there is none, i drive 30 minutes to pharmacy only to be told that the dr did not enter the prescription correctly so it can't be filled. they will try to reach the dr but if not they will call me so i can come back later to get the pain meds. even though a private dr can fax a script to the pharmacy kp can't. that way you must use their pharmacy only. if it's urgent kp fails. i get a call from a nurse who tells me i should know this script can't be faxed but her coworkers don't know. kp does not want to fill pain med they font care. plenty of excuses but no resolution. i can't make this crap up! epic fail.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review: we have a love hate relationship some of the experience felt like the dr was negative and condescending but another dr saved my life literally and my pcp is amazing.   just remember to advocate for yourself until you are listened to.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review: i went to the er here for tooth pain one night. i knew i had to see a dentist asap not knowing what it was, however i was just hoping to get prescribed strong pain medication in the meantime as none of the over the counter medication worked, i was in tremendous agony, and all my local urgent cares were closed at that time of the night. i waited for about 3 hours just to be seen (which sucks but was expected). when i got inside the emergency room, i waited another few minutes before the doctor finally came to see me. the doctor literally just asked me to rank the pain, didn't even bother to look into my mouth to see if its something she can identify. she prescribed me pain medication and was with me for less than 3 minutes. the payment process took longer than her seeing me. i paid $150 on my credit to get a prescription that night, which sucks but i know the er can't be free. where kaiser has gone too far is when i recieve a bill for $800 7 months later. they're essentially asking me to pay $950 (+ $150 i already paid) to prescribe me pain medicine with absolutely no professional diagnosis. to add salt on the the wound, i tried to dispute it but they said i needed to start a claim within 90 days or so after my visit, even though they sent me the bill 7 months later..i had to fight for them to let me dispute it. once they agreed, they "reviewed it" within 2 days and denied my dispute. absolutely horrible experience in this er. would rather go through the agony again then to deal with this er service. in what world is it ok to charge almost  $1000 just to prescribe medication???
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
i was taken to caromont hospital and while in the er the doctor was very unprofessional and rude, 2 of the 4 nurses acted as though i was a burden instead of a patient in need of medical care. the xray techs were friendly and professional tho. ( i was only in er and not admitted.)

now the big deal, unapproved scans against medicare and insurance rules- i got my bill and it was for more than $20,000 and then i got a letter from my medicare insurance company stating " caromont billed nearly $6,000 for tests not medically required nor appropriate. plus they performed 1 test 3 seperate times for blood work. this sounds like fraud to me, but my insurance company stated to "not pay for the excessive and unapproved testing.

systemic medicare and insurance fraud seems to me as not acceptable yet may be occurring and in just this one incident $6,000 or so was improperly bill

i'm finding it difficult to review this. three stars just because of staff. oh my goodness. they are truly truly top of the line! i have had plenty of nurses in my life. i don't say this lightly. 
as far as the doctors, and this includes today's (erika robb). have any of you physicians had migraines the last 15 years of your life? have you tried to keep a job throwing up and with pain so bad you have to go on disability? have you felt the worthlessness of that? my seizures are not a fluke. however, it seems that i've gotten labeled a drug risk. erika, i do not have narcotics at home. when my migraines started in the beginning and i went to the er i was treated with narcotics and given an rx. when my migraines got severe enough, the er did the same. when i was made aware of the rebound affect, i weaned myself down slowly. i have been telling them if i have to go in, no narcotics. but with this new (small dry brain bleed) i needed something.  so, i'm sure when you dig in my chart you'll find something about "drug seeker"
i would now be interested to hear dr.  boudrueaux's thoughts on my seizures.

since moving to columbus roughly three years ago, my health has been a little all over the place. i needed to find a primary care physician, a rheumatologist, and a handful of other specialists (gi and urology) as soon as possible and going with ohio state was easy. it's close by, there's several facilities all over the city, and the main hospital is about a mile from my house. while right away i noticed that there were a few things that could be improved, my experience was still way better than the ones i had in chicago at northwestern. needless to say, i was content. 

that was until i found myself in the emergency department twice, admitted twice, surgery twice, and two full months of illness. without getting into all the details, i can say that the treatment i received was rather awful. from an eight hour wait in the ed to being rushed into surgery, to poor communications between doctors, and a lack of ability to manage my medications, the entire ordeal was exhausting. the first experience was so bad, that less than a week later when i needed to go back, i waited a little too long out of fear of what would happen. 

since then, i've gone back for a few procedures and a tonsillectomy. things weren't as bad, but i was still anxious and on pins and needles just walking into the building. overall, i would say the majority of my doctors and normal visits are great, but the ed situation is one i pray i can avoid in the future.
fac_name: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center

review: wexner medical center is the best hospital ever. i once hit my head and needed to have stitches in my face. i thought my life was over. i thought i was going to look like frankenstein and have to pay thousands of dollars for the rest of my life to have the scar treated, smoothened, and lightened. it was my worst nightmare come true. however, wexner medical center saved me. matt, an rn, gave me 11 stitches and to this day i have had no work done and people cannot tell that i ever had stitches there. once i tell people i had stitches there- they literally stare at me trying to figure out which side has the scar. my family members even entirely forgot that i had stitches there because of how excellent the scar healed. i went to a specialized plastic surgeon 2 weeks after i had the stitches- just to check and make sure everything was going okay. he looked at them and said he could not have done a better job himself. i will be endlessly thankful for wexner medical center. this could have easily been a scar that ruined my life but instead i look in the mirror and don't even see it myself. thank you wexner. i tell everyone i know how great you are.
fac_name: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center

review:
my husband had back surgery here recently and post op/ discharge were the most horrible experience i've ever had at a surgery center/ hospital.  the rn who was there to help my husband in recovery/ post anesthesia was annoyed with my husband's questions and was extremely condescending and disrespectful. my husband had surgery at 3 pm. i was updated via text once, recovery rn called me at approximately 5:15 to let me know he will be able to see me in approximately 30 min. i was picking our daughter up from soccer and was back at the hospital at 5:30 ish. went to the doors and they were locked. walked completely around the building and finally went into the er for assistance who weren't remotely helpful and kept vaguely telling me how to get there. after several attempts to get to surgery waiting a very kind janitor (wish i had gotten his name as he was the only good thing at this facility) was able to get me there. 

post op/ discharge was slightly horrific. rn we had was abrasive and didn't really even know what procedure my husband had and was unable to answer any of our medical or mobility questions. considering he had back surgery, you would think the discharge rn would be educated on the procedures her patients have had. she wasn't able to tell me where exactly the incision was (there was a large bandage over most of his back). she didn't know how to put on the back brace so another rn came into our room and gave her an in room class on how to do this. during this impromptu in room back brace class my husband had a question and was completely ignored. little knowledge regarding pain management meds and had to check twice to articulate what the proper dosage and timing. there were literally too many disturbing to post in one review. 

note: i'm a super positive person who rarely writes bad reviews. typically i'd give feedback on a bad experience (there haven't been many) in hopes that establishment is able to use the information to improve and prosper. i generally give people the benefit of the doubt (i don't know what they are going through etc) but this was just an unacceptable experience. i've never written a review this long or negative but our experience was just so horrible i'd like to save anyone willing to read this whole review the experience we had.

had a terrible experience here. went to l&d due to alot of pain and my baby not moving as much. ive been here many times during my pregnancy as im high risk and its my first. iwas taken care of first by a nurse named lacy, she was so sweet and nice to me and made me feel really comfortable. but 2 times now that ive been to l&d to be monitored the male doctors are very rude. i was told multiple times to go to my hospital to be seen and not come to their er! i live in caldwell and my hospital is in boise so going to their er is easier and faster for me in an emergency and thats where my ob tells me to go when i need to be monitored quickly. not only was i told that but also treated poorly by 2 male nurses and they did not listen to my concerns at all. not returning here again and im so happy im delivering at st lukes now!!!!

last night i fell and hit my head which required stitches. my husband took me to the emergency department at st. luke's, and we couldn't have picked a better place. i was brought in almost immediately, ct scans were taken, and the doctor examined me and meticulously put 10 stitches in my head. he, my nurse, the registration and the triage people were super nice, and i was out of there within an hour and 15 minutes. 

i only have good things to say about the rest of the hospital, since that's where my babies were born many years ago.

took my infant to the er here after calling my pediatrician and describing her symptoms. she's had a fever for four days, lethargic, inconsolable crying, weak, distressed and in pain. she was having a hard time breathing normally and that's what i was most worried about. 

the receptionist was very friendly, took our information and we waited. the waiting room was nearly empty. due to covid 19 they only allowed one parent in w my daughter so my husband waited outside, even though there was a mom and a dad with their baby in the waiting room. 

they took us back to triage and left us waiting. finally a nurse practitioner came in, not friendly at all, almost annoyed that we were there, looked in my baby's ears and down her throat and said as she's walking out that they'll do a swab test her for flu, rsv and strep. she left and i hear her talking happily w another nurse right outside our door. would it kill her to be kind or friendly to us? oh well, i figured, not a big deal, i just want to take care of my baby. 

they take us to a room. 

shortly after that a nurse walks in and listens to my baby's heart. she said she needs to go see what tests need to be done and she leaves the room. 

we weren't waiting long when someone shows up to do a chest x ray. a chest x ray? the nurse practitioner had said nothing about that. i didn't even know they were going to get x rays. i wondered if they had heard something when they checked her a few minutes ago. of course my baby is freaking out the whole time. the guy is kind and we get it done.

my partner ross died in huntington hospital after waiting a week for an operation when dr. tiner, the oral surgeon the hospital provided, would not accept his dental or medical insurance and insisted on payment in advance first. this was after ross was admitted to the hospital via the er  and diagnosed with endocarditis from a strep infection. ross told dr. cohen, his heart surgeon, about dr. tiner but dr. cohen defended dr. tiner, saying he had spoken to him in the past, and he was the only one the hospital uses, and he's a "fine surgeon." nothing more came of that. 

i found out later that the "oral surgeon" the hospital had provided wasn't actually a licensed oral surgeon or dentist; he was a plastic surgeon, and the hospital did not provide anyone else after ross complained about it to dr. cohen. i tried twice to pay for it with a credit card. dr. tiner scheduled the surgery but when the first credit card declined the charge, he canceled the surgery until i offered a different credit card. by the time that was approved, ross had a stroke, and now neither surgery could be done. he was put on life support.

dr. cohen told me if it were up to him, he would stop treatment now because it was "very costly and risky" and the odds of survival were slim. i wouldn't approve of that yet since nothing had been done, and if there were any chance at all, no matter how slim, i would give ross a chance at life. i thought that was what doctors do, that's what hospitals are for. so the very next day, guess what happened...?  dr. tiner showed up and he finally pulled ross' teeth, even though he was now on a ventilator and on life support, in far worse condition than he had been the prior week. that took slightly more than an hour.

what was the medical reason for why that couldn't have been done ten days earlier, when ross was not on life support? why did huntington hospital allow a doctor to wait so long when they knew this was a serious, life threatening infection? and why did they bring in a plastic surgeon when he needed a dentist, preferably one who can bill a dental insurance plan?

i must have asked those questions a dozen times to different people between march 5 and march 15, but i never got a consistent answer. every time i asked, i either got an evasion or a change of subject. nobody gave a medical reason for making ross wait a week or why payment in advance came before saving someone's life. in fact, dr. enriquez from palliative care told me this was "standard procedure;" those were her exact words. ross never came off life support and he died in that coma on march 15. at least he was spared knowing. 

so if you take a loved one to huntington hospital's er and he gets admitted because he needs an operation to save his life, i recommend the following:

1. make sure the doctor they provide is licensed to do it first, don't assume it;
2. bring extra cash in case he isn't licensed and therefore can't take your insurance;
3. don't waste your breath complaining if he insists on being paid first, it won't do you any good; 
4. if you pay out of pocket, make sure you get a receipt before he dies.

i've been trying to get the records for ross' treatment so that the insurance company will reimburse me for my credit card, but the hospital refuses to give me any proof that they performed an operation that i paid for. i could have used that money to give ross a decent funeral and burial. just think - if i had taken him to a different hospital, i might not even have had to bury him at all.

want to hear a real kicker? the mortuary cost less than the surgery, and they even gave me the paperwork to prove it. nothing to hide there. 

my advice: go to any other hospital if you can. the staff and nurses and junior doctors were all great, but the two lead doctors? i don't know what they were thinking, i can't imagine what they were thinking, or how they sleep at night. i wonder how they'd like it if this happened to one of their family members. all i know is they didn't do anything until it was too late, and since nobody wants to answer my questions, i'm left to come to my own conclusions: one thought his money was more important than ross' life, and the other was content to not do anything about that even after the patient asked, and palliative care said that's "standard procedure."  i don't know if she meant standard for the entire industry, or only for huntington hospital, or just those two doctors; that part wasn't clear. 

this wasn't a medical mistake; it was a financial decision. if someone from the hospital can explain it another way and in person, i'm willing to listen. but i want answers to specific questions, no deflections, evasions or tap dancing acts. 

otherwise, if you can afford first class insurance, huntington probably pays attention to you, but if you can only afford third class, good luck finding your way to the lifeboats.
