dr. reeve once and she was not willing at all to adjust my medications and wanted to wait until the meeting at the end of the initial assessment period. it makes sense but when you're paying over $1000 a day you would typically expect your doctor to be a little more engaging with their patients. during my stay i do have to say that they had a great support team, but not everyone was there for the right reasons (staff wise). now heres where it gets screwed up... i completed the 5 to 6 hours of testing they required me to do and then at the end of all of the testing they had a talk with me basically saying everything that came up on my test and a lot of it did not sound like me at all. the doctor understood this and said that sometimes it happens and so crossed off some things on the list. however when i had my meeting with all of my doctors at the end of my 10 day assessment, dr. reeve and all of the other doctors at the lindner center who were on my patient care team decided to ignore my, the patient's, perspective and rather completely rely on the tests, the paperwork, and what the personality tests i took told them about me without listening to me, as the patient, at all. it was a very embarrassing session, i was barely allowed to speak and i felt like my voice was not heard and that they did not care about me at all but we're only speaking about what they thought i was like instead of actually taking a second to understand who i really am as a person. i think of it like this, if you go to the hospital your doctor should always take the patient symptoms and perspective into consideration as well as the bloodwork and the tests and put two and two together and come up with a comprehensive diagnosis that encompasses both the patient's perspective and the tests that were run in order to gain an accurate diagnosis. this was never done at the lindner center for me, they never took the time to listen to me as a patient which is extremely concerning for a medical facility. please take this into consideration when you are considering the lindner center for your care.

if you need any kind of imaging take your order and go else where as there are many stand alone imaging centers available and at a much lower cost! i just got my bill for a 10 minute ct scan without contrast for a whopping $5,184!! stupid me checking around i could of got the same thing at another facility for $139! a ct scan is a ct scan! what a scam! guess the hospital is trying to make up for lost income with all the elective surgeries being cancelled due to the covid hysteria and remembering that they are for profit and a hospital doesn't stay open for free!
thank you very much every nurse every doctor big respect i'm never forget your help you guys soldiers god bless you all:

i intended to deliver my daughter here. upon my horrific experience when admitted for monitoring i switched my care to a different hospital where my experience was consistent and night and day compared to overlook.

i found the maternity staff to be condescending and cold-hearted. the head of the department lacks any bedside manner and has a callous persona.

one of the nurses threw away my tray of lunch while i was using the restroom in my room (with no assistance offered and much needed) after i had been starved for hours and finally got the ok to eat by my doctor. 

if you want to be treated like scum, well sure, this is the place to deliver your baby.

a few weeks ago, i lost my dad to this horrible corona virus. he went to the overlook hospital to the er a week before his admittance only to be told to self quarantine. meanwhile his chief complaint was difficulty breathing.  shortly after he had to return to the hospital for more aggressive symtoms of covid, he was intubated and put in icu and that was the last time we saw or spoke to my father.  my mom would call all the time to inquire about his condition and even asked if she could speak to him but was always denied.  she, along with my aunts, were only allowed to "speak" to him when he was essentially dying and obviously unresponsive. 
after my dads passing. my mom tried calling the hospital to retrieve his personal belongings which included a brand new i phone.  this has been going on for three weeks now.  even today  my aunt tried calling family support center to  speak with a social worker, no one returned her call.

my family understands that it's an extremely difficult time for all right now especially those working in the medical field but we who are not trained in medicine or social behavior would like compassion, honesty and integrity from those who are such professionals.   all we wanted was my dad's belongings. his phone has his last messages, pictures, texts.  little things that we could cherish.  well, in our opinion, overlook hospital doesn't quite stand up to the professionalism and integrity one might expect especially after losing a loved one and in a pandemic that hasn't been seen in 100 years. 
think twice before you choose overlook.  looking back, we would have.

horrible birth experience. patty and michelle don't know what the ferguson reflex is. they said it's a "midwifery term". they scolded me like a child to "stop pushing" while my baby's head was coming out when, in fact, i was not pushing at all (ferguson reflex). had to defend myself several times due to their lack of knowledge of natural occurrences of a woman's body in childbirth. awful care. i will never forget these women for as long as i live. go to las cruces or el paso to give birth. due to covid-19, i was facetiming my husband during the birth (multiple nurses standing around, and not 1 offered to hold the phone) and patty screamed "put your phone down" as if it wasn't the father of my child watching his baby be born on the other end. indifferent staff with no compassion. they treated me like a burden while i was in the most vulnerable state of my life. lots of eye rolling at me, talking down to me, reminding me of their masters degree and that this wasn't their "first rodeo". horrible horrible experience. these women (night shift) have no regard for the sacredness of childbirth. it's just another day on the job they clearly hate.
oh also, here's a direct quote from an encounter during my stay here.

*nurse preparing to test me for covid-19 while i'm in labor*
me: what if i decline this test? 
nurse: then we're gonna treat you like you have it and put you in quarantine.

me and my husband had to bring our 2 year old son in to the emergency and they would only let 1 parent in which is really messed up. i will never go this hospital again. if i could leave a 0 star i would but i had to put 1 so i put 1

these drs saved my life .. thanks nicole, megan and dr grayden for taking care of me all week...truly grateful you guys are heroes!!! even tho the stay wasn't fun i got the help i needed and i'm thankful for being treated with respect and taken good care of....ready to move along now!!!

the majority of my experience has been with their php/iop program so that is what i'll be speaking on. i had an overall amazing experience with this program. it's hard to fathom how much their staff cares about their patients. you are not just a number on their caseload you are an actual human being. i was just discharged from the program today but taking part in this program was one of the best decisions that i have ever made. i've been made to feel so loved and i will never forget that. shout out to the case manager brenda!!!! she stood by me no matter what was going on and for that i will be forever thankful. so, if you ever find yourself in need of outpatient mental health services this is the place to go.

amazed! just went through a 5 day intense detox... i had super low expectations due to other reviews i read prior to coming. my experience was life changing! the staff- each nurse including wen, denise and others went out of thier way- yet don the head lead nurse was more than encouraging and accomidating. the food was delicious i.e. ceaser chicken salad was top notch!! ( not to mention i am a super picky eater ) many times i broke down in tears just needing some trusted help. whoever put this team together .. thank you! i will be leaving here with renewed hope and courage to move forward. from the bottom of my heart i am truly, grateful. unfortuntely, i must give laura, the social worker assigned to me on friday 6/5/20 a one star due to her abrasive, condescending attitude who seemed to care- less about my recovery plan.. just cruel and cold. nevertheless, college hospital was a god send in my life for me and my family. thank you!

i am so surprised that this place has such terrible reviews. my experience here was absolutely wonderful. the nurse i had the day i came here (i was admitted for detox) was an absolute gem. super bummed i can't remember her name. she and don (he is phenomenal!!) made me feel so welcome and comfortable. they were both super friendly and they made me feel like they really genuinely cared about me and their other patients. i was there for 4-5 days and all of the nurses i had were wonderful - no complaints. bryan is another nurse worth mentioning. so friendly, so attentive, and also makes you feel like he genuinely cares about you as both a person and a patient. these staff members had impeccable bedside manners and i would highly recommend this place to anyone in need of detox or mental health services. can't say enough wonderful things about bryan and don. my boyfriend was there detoxing with me and i left a few days before he did. at one point he told me that he was on the verge of leaving, and don got down to his level, looked him in the eyes, and told him that he would do whatever he needed to do to make my boyfriend comfortable and get him through the remainder of his stay there. he also gave me a cloth mask on my way out since i only had a disposable one with me (not at all something they're required to do - he did it out of kindness). these nurses care! five stars for the nurses at college hospital. you guys rock and i can't thank you enough for your genuine kindness!
best nurses ever.   from start to finish they did everything right.  there were a few minor errors but they were all over it.  so happy to have been taken care of here.

the covid 19 pandemic creates extraordinary circumstances for all businesses and medical facilities. we recently had a requirement for a procedure and ecmc made the process seamless.

5* for rapid response to the referral and the outstanding courtesy of the person from scheduling
5* for the entry process to the facility (bonus points for the free chocolate bar!)
5* for the outpatient check-in
5* for the attentiveness and care during the procedure, along with the thoroughness of explanation for the procedural process

we're experiencing a time of elevated social stress; you wouldn't know that from the care and courtesy of this medical facility. every effort was made to make the experience comfortable.

understanding the current pandemic environment, the inability of both parents being permitted to accompany my daughter inside was tough but not completely unexpected. my daughter was treated very well and the 5 hour surgery was a success. 
that being said, the treatment of the family by the registration/ front desk staff was deplorable. on a 90 degree day it would have been nice to be able to social distance somewhere inside the 1 st floor waiting area that spans the length of the facility. not only was i denied access to that area, i was told i must wait out in the parking lot. the public restroom was also off limits for the 5 hour wait. 
working in healthcare myself, including during the entire pandemic, i understand the necessities of infection prevention. there are steps that can be taken to ensure the safety of everyone and create an environment of care for family members of your patients. the importance of care for the entire family cannot be understated. the front desk crew was an epic failure for that part of the experience.

this is the worst place to receive medical treatment in sc. use roper...i am going to work hard to get this medical center shut down. never go there unless you want to waste your money on underpar medical services.

this hospital needs to do better when it comes to hospitality with patients. i was treated like sh*t when i walked in the er yesterday. security guard was rude, and was on his phone the whole time. the nurses who took my history and vitals had no sympathy, and couldn't care less as to what was wrong with me. woman who registered me also seemed like she didn't care about anything either. 
i couldn't imagine if i had something serious going on, and was treated the way i was. it was a very awful, and a triggering experience. i've been going to kmc for treatment for years and now i'm trying to figure out if that's where i want to continue going. i choose kmc because location is super convenient and family works for the company. it's a shame because i know they have the best trauma unit, but front staff truly ruins it for the back staff. do better.

the hospitality here is garbage especially at night time i just left kmc i went in with a fever of 109 they basically ask questions for covid and check my temp!! they made me wait outside cockroaches everywhere even crawling on me mosquitoes biting me they came out 3 more times to ask the same questions over and over finally put me in a room to ask me the same bs so i told them to test me just waisting time she said i'll get the doctor another nurse heard me and told me to go get test some were else because he basically said they weren't gonna test me he said go home get some rest cuz your just gonna waist time here so my point is why don't they just test patience before even assuming they have it i could have bronchitis, valley fever , or some other problems. they refused me a test and i ask for a supervisor and they shut the door on me !! unprofessional!!

my wife was transferred to this hospital after 21 days in the icu with covid-19. kindred hospital came highly recommended for transitional care and was highly rated online. i'm not sure how they got these ratings because the care that my wife received at this hospital was substandard at best. five times in two weeks my wife had to call me in the middle of the night to tell me that her nurse was not responding to the call button, or that the call button had been moved out of her reach and that she had either urinated or defecated in the bed. so i had to call the nurses desk to inform them that my wife needed attention. pretty pathetic that my wife has to call me so that i can call the nurses station to tell them to do their jobs. my wife was receiving dialysis after which she would become incontinent. one of the night shift nurses yelled at her because she could not hold her bowels long enough waiting for the nurse to arrive. another night she called me at 2 am crying and having a panic attack because 25 minutes after pressing the nurse call no nurse had come and she wet the bed. so do yourself and your loved ones a favor and avoid this hospital like the plague if the need for a transitional care hospital ever arises.

after places started opening up due to covid, hubby decided it was time to get out and enjoy a ride in the country on his harley motorcycle.  a dog came out of nowhere and decided he wanted to play a game with the motorcycle.  so, the dog won, and hubby went down on his bike at 40 mph.  brought him to the emergency room and they were shocked that he walked in on his own.  one broken arm, 4 staples on other arm, one fractured rib, and about 50% really bad road rash.  the er staff was phenomenal.  courteous, efficient, and very professional.  thank goodness i am educated in wound care, but they took the time to answer all of our questions.  thank you integris er staff.  we are home and doing wound care which is for those w a very strong stomach.  btw, i told hubby that as he is 70 years old, maybe it was time to get a trike or just quit riding.  as usual, i will not win that argument.  thank you god and jesus for placing him in your hands as he was taken care of by the fantastically professionals in the integris i-35 emergency room.

the mrs chose integris edmond as the hospital to have our first child. the rooms were large, comfortable, quiet, and very relaxing. the dr.'s and nurses were very attentive and we were never stuck with an unanswered question or unmet need. as for being our first delivery my wife asked possibly 3 million questions and the nurses never showed any negative emotions or responses and always answered truthfully and accurately. the wife has decided already that if we were to bring anymore beautiful children into this world, integris edmond would be the place they first see. thanks again, you made it very easy on a first time father!

let me start by stating that the medical staff, in their entirety, were absolutely great, professional and polite.  my largest grievance falls at the feet of the facility,  it's poor upkeep, and those responsible for the facilities shortcomings.

i went to the er for a post medical infection.  the er took me in quickly and listened to all of my concerns.  the er physician recommended that i stay over night and voiced his concerns.  i agreed and was quickly taken to my room on the 3rd floor.

again the nursing staff were polite and professional  and did everything they could to make me comfortable.  that's were the problem began.  from the moment i got to my room the constant noise of the hvac unit and the incessant, ear piercing hum of the air bed made it impossible to sleep.  it got so bad and so uncomfortable that i had thoughts at 2am to call in a nurse, sign an ama and walk out.  i stuck it out through the night but informed the day shift nurse that i was leaving regardless for the staff dr's recommendation.  in fact by that time i was so aggravated i became less than courteous and demanded  my discharge.  

the medical treatment i received was premier but i would have to give serious consideration before staying at the edmond facility ever again.

please be careful of patronizing this hospital if you are not white. when we visited there, they were quite racist to us. not only did they not want to let us into the emergency room when my son was visibly acutely ill, but the doctor did not want to touch my son to examine him. the hospital claims values of respect, integrity, and compassion, but they did not extend those values to us. as for the hippocratic oath, that was not honored either. this was one of the most virulent examples of anti-blackness that i have experienced in the modern era.

my 88-year-old mother presented to the er 5/8/20 for leg pain and weakness. at the time she was at full mental capacity, ambulatory with walker assistance.
she was admitted to the hospital with our concerns expressed to the hospital that we feared for her life and safety since we would not be able to be there with her due to covid 19 as there were several reported incidents of abuse and neglect during her january 2020 stay that occurred in front of family members and the condition that we found her in when we would leave and come back.
on 5/10/20 we found it very difficult to reach her, her phone was not answered in her room and it was difficult to get in touch with nurse's station. we expressed our concerns about this. by 5/11/20 she was totally incoherent and unable to answer her phone. at times an aid would answer and we heard her screaming in the background. when they held the phone to her she was unable to speak and she had no idea where she was. she believed she was home. the dr. (raza) told me on 5/11/20 that she was on hydrocodone for pain and when i expressed my concerns about her wellbeing he informed me that her bloodwork was good and she could be discharged 5/12/20. on 5/12/20 we were informed by nurses that she had not had any pain medication since she had been there other than 1 tramadol and she was diagnosed 5/12/20 with a uti and was beginning treatment. on 5/13/20 we were told it would be yet another day due to possible small area of pneumonia. we insisted on her discharge 5/14/20. upon picking her up she was brought out in light summer pajamas, a blanket no mask and turned over to us and we thought they had made a mistake and brought the wrong patient out. we did not even recognize what was sitting in that wheelchair. the nurse stated that what we were seeing were probably residual effects from the ativan that was given to her to "calm her down" why did she need to be calmed down and why was she given ativan? we were rushed along and given no real discharge instructions. upon getting her home she laid in fetal position for the first 3 days crying for her mother. she was covered in bruises showing all signs of severe abuse, trauma and suspected sexual abuse. at first the home nurses though that she may have been catheterized for the urine sample and that was painful and traumatizing for her but we later found out that they never even did a urinalysis and she never had a uti that they claimed she had and was treating her for. after a few days she began to come around a small amount and she could only cry and ask why they had done those things to her in the hospital and why they hurt her. we also found out that she had a 14mm kidney stone that was never addressed or told to us. my mother went from being of total sound mind and ambulatory (only experiencing some pain and weakness) on 5/8/20 to now being on end stage hospice care.
we have had several incidents with this hospital that have always fallen on deaf ears.  in researching the many websites, we have come across several similar heart wrenching stories from patients and families in this hospital and i am currently corresponding with a woman who saw my post about her father in law who is currently in that hospital suffering abuse and neglect. i have every intention of contacting medicare, state board of medicine, health dept. and any other agency that will shed light on what happened to my mother in that establishment.
i have worked in the medical profession myself for the past 20 years and have never witnessed anything like this hospital. i am contacting the large benefactors for the hospital, the press and anyone that will listen and help me to stop another human being from suffering this type of tragedy and abuse in this facility. i also will fight as hard as i can to get the license of dr. raza taken from him. i want whomever abuse, assaulted, and basically killed my mother held accountable.
**update since this was first written.
on june 9, 2020 exactly 27 days after she has suffered the abuse, assault, medical misdiagnosis and gross negligence my mother has passed away.
also, the man i mentioned that his family had contacted me due to similar complaints of neglect and abuse was scheduled to be released from that establishment 6/8/20 but had passed on 6/5/20.
i will fight until i take my last breath for my mother, this man and all who walk through the doors of olean general hospital that are unable to speak for themselves.  there has to be change, people have to be held accountable.
i have been in contact with the hospital and melody stuckey informed me that an investigation had been done (it took a day) and that they asked everyone on the third floor if anyone had done anything to my mother and they all stated "no". did administration actually expect someone to step up and admit that they abused, neglected, assaulted, drugged, misdiagnosed and wrongfully treated / medicated an 88 year old woman?  this hospital takes nothing seriously

i would give a negative review if i could.  this has to be the worse hospital to receive service.  twice i have been charged for items that i did not receive and the last time was for $314.00 for 2 antiobiotics which were never given to me and they won't won't even consider what i have to say.  also there was a host of other issues which makes this the worse place to receive medical attention.  you have lost my business,

it's corona virus season and i understand this is a time where a lot of people are under stress but i think sometimes people forget compassion/customer service is why they're doing this job. it's 7am so i definitely understand most people aren't completely awake. at any rate, it's 7am! i ain't tryna be here but i walk into all of these departments with a warm good morning and a smile (under my mask of course) instead of being greeted with the same response i'm looked at with funny faces and no responses, then of course back to their normal "keke". i automatically feel like my presence bothers these employees. i'm not writing this post to bash anyone's work ethic but i think people in these roles should be reminded customer service is everything.
absolutely fantastic rehab center! loved one was transferred here to rehabilitate after stay at st johns tulsa. care here is amazing. we could not have imagined anything better.

this facility restored my faith in the local healthcare system. my mother was admitted in december 2019 amidst the busy holiday season. her care was nothing short of excellent, especially being a new patient with no established record of care in the area. i only had a long stay in the emergency room. i was forgotten about due to the flu season and many patients already waiting with more coming in. by the time i arrived to the hospital, my mother was receiving care in triage and being prepped for admission. 

my mother was fed well and treated respectfully although i know she can be difficult to work with. she was clean every time i saw her and all of her needs were met, which didn't always happen with hospital stays at other facilities. nurses were polite and gracious. visiting hours were ample and the facility was easy access with plenty of free parking. the facility was clean, modern and used brand name healthcare products as part of their hygiene regimen. 

i was very pleased with the level of service provided. the hospital administration and their staff deserve full recognition for all that they do for the community. thank you!

(1/6/20) this er just keeps getting worse and worse & i came in, in severe pain. on the positive side i have had an ultrasound and been given some pain meds. on the negative side i had to wait 2.5 hours because triage is non existent. some of the people i spoke to had been there for 5 hours waiting on lab results.

the ultrasound tech was nice. i think her name was brenda. i have no idea who brought me back here. 

i just had one of the most asinine explanations of triage from some nurses aide. they also managed to lose the urine sample i gave them about an hour and a half ago. i highly doubt that i will come back here for any reason.

(6/17-6/18/20) my wife had kidney surgery yesterday through the outpatient surgery center. she was admitted for observation and is awaiting her doctor to remove a stent. the surgery went well. everyone in the surgery center was nice and friendly.

when i arrived this morning there was a young lady doing temperature checks at the main entrance. she located my wife's room and i got a temporary visitor badge from the front desk. the room is large and clean. there is a bevy of tech on the wall behind her bed. there's also a longish couch and the standard recliner.

my wife was not happy with her nurses during the day yesterday. she kept referring to them as the demons in the room. the tech that just appeared was asking if she'd had breakfast when there was no evidence of a tray. 

apparently the night crew is leagues above the day crew. my wife believes that communication is spotty at best between the shifts. hopefully she'll be leaving sometime today.

i was in here for feeling really sick twice in the last week. last week, i was in an out in three hours. and the call ladies were nasty to me, and everyone i saw except my male nurse and doctor were acting like it was such an inconvenience for me to be there. clearly not fit for the job. i get it, they're stressed. but they should know better than to take it out on their patients. it was disgusting. 

the second time i came, i told them about my chronic health issues and how i wasn't sure if that was it and they pretty much dismissed me for that. they were more concerned about serious stuff that clearly wasn't the issue. i even told them i was fine just having an iv and oxygen but they kept wanting to run tests. they really just wanted more and more money!!!! 

the only good part about this whole experience was my amazing nurse, paul. that guy deserves a bonus check and pay raise. he was amazing, and funny. and he knew what to do to keep me calm. he didn't lie to my face once. 

what angered me more than anything was how the ladies at the desk answering the calls for me wanting my nurse were. whoever that was is horribly rude and shouldn't be dealing with patients on phone. i didn't even call that much and every time i did she had a major attitude problem. she was downright nasty. it took everything in me to not be rude back, but i am too nice of a person. 

she also kept raising her voice and i could hear her sigh right before she hung up. it was downright disrespectful and she clearly hates her job. you need better staff who do the patient calls. 

i wasn't going to go here because it's known to be the busiest, but this is by far the closest to me and is the only er i've known and i was wanting a familiar place. but except for my nurses i wish i went elsewhere. ridiculous!

i would've gave y'all only one star, but because of paul, i gave it two. they're the only nice people i dealt with. and paul understood my sensitivities with food and my allergies. nobody else seemed to care, they didn't even tell me if it was safe to eat after they said they would ask. 

if my mom was there maybe they would have listened. they don't take me seriously enough and i told them at the very beginning i didn't want too many tests done, preferably none.

i've personally experienced the high quality of care provided by california hospital on march 10th 2020. i was an employee turned patient when struck by a car in front of the er on my way to work that day. the coworkers rushed to my rescue before the ambulance came and brought me directly to treatment followed by series of tests. the efficiency and professionalism of those who worked at the medical center is truly impressive.
i was transferred to the seventh floor for observation and pain treatments, and would like to express my most sincere gratitude towards jin and cheol, the nurses in charge of taking care of me, they have been nice and patient, especially jin, when i'm bed ridden with pain, she would ask me very often wether or not i need help with the bathroom, and routinely check on my pain after every medication. the pain evaluation and management was through and professionally done. even when i was being released jin did not cut corners with informing and educating me about my medications, it's effects and how to manage my condition. her kindness and thoughtfulness was to aspire to as a fellow medical personnel.
i would also like to give my thanks to my coworkers on the 8th floor and my director imelda. cowden coming to my assistance in my time of need, helping me manage my condition along with processing my break from work. and my gratitude also go towards our cno, trudy johnson who took time out of her extremely tight schedule to make frequent visits even after i was transferred to recovery room, constantly asking to provide me assistance.
these attention care was really touching and made me feel like a part of the big family that is california hospital. i am proud to call myself as a member of the family and can not wait to recover so i may be back to my post, to contribute to the patients care, to give them the same level of attentiveness i was given.
last but not least, speaking as an employee as well as a patient, having experience all aspects of the hospital, i have but one thing to say. "california hospital, you are the best"

review:
i came in around 1am on june 3rd, 2020 already in labor. i was taken to get checked if i was in active labor before giving me a room and allowing my partner to come in. 
after confirming i was 6cm dilated, they settled me into a room and allowed my boyfriend to come in. 
the first nurse poked my left hand trying to find a vein for the iv but was unsuccessful so she had to come around and use a thinner needle on my right hand. the iv was meant to be on my left hand so during my whole stay i had wires across my bed and in the way because it was on my right hand. 
the first thing i told the nurses was i did not want the epidural. we discussed different pain medication options but didn't settle on anything but eventually i asked for pain medication through the iv. 
although i clearly specified no epidural, it was offered to me at least  6 times before my boyfriend stood up for me and told the nurses to stop asking me because i wasnt taking it. 
while checking the baby's position through an ultrasound , i asked my boyfriend to take a picture and the nurse rudely told him pictures were not allowed?!
we have no pictures of the delivery due to this nurse! we later found out we in fact were allowed to take pictures so i don't understand why that nurse said that?!

fast forward to actually giving birth. i had midwife (i believe her name was emily carter?) and a student help me through. she was great! she was positive and never touched me or did anything without telling me what she was doing . "i'm going to be checking you , i'm going to touch you here, my fingers are going in. " she asked me questions, gave me options and considered my feelings. 

i pushed for 35 minutes, no epidural and birthed a 9lb2oz healthy baby boy!  my first baby! 

right after the placenta came out, the midwife let me know she needed a second opinion wether i had a second or 3rd degree tear. 

this is when this disgusting doctor comes in ..unfortunately, i did not get his name
he comes in and without an introduction, a heads up nothing, he aggressively starts poking around in my vagina. now i now i was extra sensitive since i had just gave birth but when the mid wife was checking me, it was not as painful.
 i asked him to please stop and give me a minute the doctor has the nerve to get up and walk towards the door and say "i can leave you looking like that or do you want it to look pretty?!?!" (referring to my vagina!!!)
i was in complete shock that a doctor could say something  so disgusting and disrespectful like that to a patient . 
the doctor had the audacity to repeat himself and say "well there's not a lot of time, do you want it to look pretty or not?" 
i was in so much pain i could barely speak but luckily my boyfriend stood up to him and told him "i'm sure there's a better way of saying that!"..even the nurses and midwife had a look of shock on their faces. 
the doctor seemed mad, told the midwife "second degree" & left the room. 

the midwife went ahead and gave me stitches again being very vocal about what she was doing which i appreciate. 

after being moved to our room, everything went as expected. mediocre food, uncomfortable recliner for your support partner..nothing out of the ordinary.
nurses were nice but none exceptional.


overall it was an ok experience. the midwife and her student made my experience so much better hence the 3 stars but honestly, i am still thinking about the comment that doctor made days later. my boyfriend and i talked about it later and i realized i wasn't just over thinking it...it tainted the whole experience for me.

i hope that doctor reads this and is more considerate of the woman who have just gave birth next time around. 
don't be the reason a beautiful memory is ruined because you were an a-hole!!

review:

also, one of the employees was showing some symptoms and was sent there to get examined. he was seen and examined while i just sat there and no one told me anything or checked up on me.

i'll go straight to the point. on march 28th i left work with sob ( shortness of breath).. the doctors i work with was concerned because i had surgery on the 5th of march and during the following weeks my legs started hurting.. the left one swelled a little bit but not much.. within the following weeks i couldn't talk without stopping to take a breath every other sentences.. i went to the er and i tried to explain the pa gregory barnes, but ignored my symptoms..my nurse at the moment keep appearing out of no where stating "so i heard you telling barnes this and that.. so she can verify all this her name was "bobby" i asked him to do labs to see if i had a clot. he said he was gonna order blood and xrays.. well he did ordered a cbc and cmp, not a ddimer which it would show if i had a blood clot.. he got the xrays he said he didn't see pneumonia or anything wrong but he was going to put me on antibiotics..i'd asked him if my labs where normal.. he said yes.. i asked for a copy. i went home, he did order the covid19 test ( which was negative). two days later i can't sleep laying down, i had to sleep sitting down in my bed with pillows.. had a severe headache.. and my fingernails where turning purple.. i called my doctor that i work with( i was quarantined so i couldn't work) i told him about my symptoms and what the pa said. he was very upset ( all the doctors i work with work in the trauma center in the hospitals here in las vegas)he checked my records ( i screen shot my paperwork that i got from the hospital and texted it to one of the nurses at my work)withing half an hr, he sent a co worker to pick me up sent me back to the hospital, another pa saw me,  (collene raether) was very attentive and said to me " well, under the circumstance and the way you sound and look i'm gonna skip the ddimer and order a cta..an hr later.. she came back telling me that there was a blood clot in my left lung aka pulmonary embolism! i could've die at home if it wasn't for my doctors! i understand that everyone is in panic with this covid19 situation.. but the manager of centennial hospital should re established their rules and regulations and remind them to focus on pt's symptoms and don't discard those little details.. i ended staying in the hospital given blood thinners, and iv antibiotics.. i have to take eliquis for 6 months now. i hope you all stay firm and request doctors to pay attention to your symptoms.. do not let them do to you what they did to me.. stay safe  people #vegasstrong!!

a few things to note:
-the hospital/echn has excellent prenatal and postpartum programming, from their pregnancy/infant care class and prenatal fitness to their new mothers' group that meets weekly (currently virtually on zoom!). they've also got a remarkable doula program (shannon made a huge difference in my birth experience, she's amazing). 
-delivery & recovery are in the same room which i found to be a total asset. plus, the room is huge with plenty of room for nurses, bags, partners, visitors, etc without feeling cramped. 

i live in the hartford area but my midwife practice only delivers at manchester hospital, which is how i ended up here. it really made all the difference in having such a supportive experience.

my wife and i have been to this hospital twice, once when our daughter was born in 2016 and again when our son was born in 2020.

in 2016 i would describe our experience as average.  we had some good nurses and some pretty lousy ones, the doctor was fantastic, the food service employees were rude and awful.  altogether a pretty middling experience.

when we returned in 2020, it was clear that a lot of changes had been made.  every nurse we had, day and night, was incredibly friendly and helpful.  my wife, who is very introverted and has trouble with new people, took to them immediately.  in particular she absolutely loved our night nurse in postpartum, anny.  the delivery nurse, nicole, was also outstanding - she didn't leave our room for the final 4-6 hours of labor and basically acted as a midwife.

the room service staff was also excellent; they made sure that both of us were well-fed during our time there, and were very polite on the phone.  food was delivered promptly, they would call the room around meal times if we forgot to do so, and the food was pretty good - you certainly wouldn't come here to eat if you weren't in the hospital, but it's much better than you would expect from hospital food.  lots of healthy options, and the fruit tray is clearly fresh fruit and not canned.

we were visited by multiple doctors, pediatricians, nurse practitioners, and the hospital's lactation specialist, who were all very patient and professional and spent significantly more time with us than i expected - they didn't leave the room until they had answered every question we had.  we never felt like we were rushed so they could go to the next room.

the facilities were great.  the delivery room itself was comfortable for both of us, and it's clear that improvements have been made to the postpartum room because it was also much more comfortable, including a better sleeping space for dads / partners.  it used to be a chair that did not recline, now it is a chair that folds out into a makeshift bed.  you could do much worse spending the night in the hospital.  also of importance to dads / partners - the wifi is very good.

excellent care was taken of my wife and child; although we don't plan to have more children, we would still recommend this hospital for medical needs.  it is also clear that the hospital takes feedback very seriously - we were asked by the heads of basically every department if we had any criticisms or areas of improvement, and several of them mentioned that they had been making some changes in the last couple of years to make patients and guests more comfortable and happy.

after our 2016 visit we weren't impressed, and the only reason we came back in 2020 is because my wife loved her doctor and nurse so much and wanted to deliver with them again.  i'm so glad we did come back though - it was a completely different and completely wonderful experience for all three of us.

i'll try to make this as short as possible.  i had hip replacement surgery in november 2019.  i was so disgusted with the surgeon.  i used to have private insurance and now have medi-cal because of my disability.  i've worked as a unit clerk at oroville hospital, had front office and back office positions before becoming a case manager with butte county social services.  i am very well aware of being treated differently with private insurance and medi-cal.  maybe this is why that surgeon reserves a separate office for private insurance patients and may see his medi-cal patients for five minutes in the "clinic' office.  this is appalling.  i had to have labs done before surgery (probably a cbc and a chem panel).  my platelet count was 765.  i'm sure you know that the normal is between 140-400.  hmm.  after waking up on the surgery table, my lower back felt worse than labor pains. not the hip, yet.  i tried to tell him this and he kept walking out of the room and didn't even respond to me.  by the time i got to the floor to a room i was experiencing pain as i had never had before.  my blood pressure began to drop and i couldn't stop shaking.  one of the nurses said he knew where the dr. was and needed an order written for pain. i will commend the nursing staff and physical therapy.  they were all very pleasant.  i did not appreciate a male nurse telling me that pain medications were not the answer and i needed to try to do my part instead of being high on pain killers.  this was at the same time i couldn't couldn't quit shaking all over from no pain medication after a 12 inch cut into my hip and nerves.  what!? well, it has been just under 4 years since i was admitted here as a patient. it is still uncomfortable to remember and discuss this time in my life which triggered the most massive upheaval of my life, i've experienced to this day. i stayed here twice in less than one year. 

     one lesson i have learned by being admitted to a mental health facility is that the brain is a delicate, fragile part of you and what happened to me could happen to any person at any time; that's the concerning part.

     i've decided to go into a little more detail about what i experienced because i believe it will help even just one person; maybe even the family and support system for a person staying here. there is no shame in living with a mental health condition. try not to let the stigma get you down. did you know having depression and or anxiety is a mental health condition? many don't but it is a fact. 

     i've always been an upstanding member of society and kept to the laws in place; i was a functioning member of society and consciously and pleasantly aware of that fact. in the winter of 2016, i suffered a psychiatric breakdown. it's quite common you know. one common culprit is stress; severe ongoing stress. i without my awareness slipped away from reality and entered the land of the lost. a very scary and uncomfortable place to be.

     i was under an immense amount of stress due to personal situations, relationships and events that occurred suddenly. i had filed for divorce and was making the necessary arrangements transitioning into that next phase of my life when it occurred.

     one minute i am me as i've known myself to be for over 40 years and from that place of comfort i lost all touch with reality. no fun. i do have some memories of this psychiatric hospital as it's common to not be able to recall memories when one experiences what i have. with time some memories are returning. i do recall not arguing nor fighting with any of the fellow patients here nor staff. this hospital is a locked facility.

     i also recall some areas that need attention: the restrooms in each patient room need work.  the shower heads? nope there aren't many of them so the water sprays all over the place. a nice pair of shoes would have been wonderful for me to wear as you have to walk around in socks on the dense linoleum floors. staff will remove the laces in shoes brought for patients, same with hooded sweatshirts and sweat pants. 

     you have to make your own bed which is excellent. and they give you clean linens to do so. the meals were good & you get 3 a day; plus snacks. once they know your not a threat to anyone or yourself and have been behaving yourself, you are given the option to leave the ward in a organized group with fellow patients and a professional leading; and head down via elevator to the the cafeteria and dine. another experience is the gymnasium. if your on your best behavior you may be asked if you'd like to go to the gymnasium and play basketball and other indoor sports. sometimes i went and other times i abstained. there is a phone for patients in the hallway and it works which is helpful. 

     not one employee here treated me unkindly. when i asked for something my request was granted if at all possible. the mental health technicians were very kind and friendly to me as well. i appreciate this even now nearly 4 years later. i feel this hospital is a safe place for anyone experiencing acute as well as chronic mental health conditions and/or complications, even if they have not been diagnosed yet. the rooms are kept clean but just to be fair, its important to understand that this is a psychiatric hospital therefore the patients who are occupying the rooms commonly are not cognitively healthy at that time so it is expected that they may elicit (just like me) odd, strange, bizarre behaviors preventing them from up-keeping their room.  

     in closing, one piece of lived-experience i will share is the mind is a very delicate creation and does not like stress. give it enough and any one persons brain chemistry can change (happened to me), altering your behavior. what i lacked during this experience was a supportive, loving, caring, intelligent empathetic spouse to help me through this unexpected and horrifically frightening experience. i hope for anyone that may experience this or something psychologically unusual for you that you have a great family and/or friend support system. i found mine once i received the necessary treatment and was able to return to my healthy cognitive self; but it took time. this hospital kept me safe during both stays here; and that's what i needed.

    if a person winds up here you/they may not be healthy cognitively at the time. maybe choose to view the situation this way verses the alternative which is they could be ill living on the street. i met homeless persons here too; they were really nice.  sierra vista is a much safer therapeutic option than what is listed above.

nothing strikes more fear in all of us during this era of covid-19 (well, except for the virus itself), than the thought of a trip to the er.

under normal conditions, an er visit is very stressful, but in the era of covid-19, it's incapacitating.

yet, here i found myself on a monday morning after experiencing lightning streaks coming out of my left eye all weekend. it was mystifying and scary. 

a quick trip to dr. google led me to a possible diagnosis, a detached retina, and these words, " seek medical help immediately." 

i live smack dab in the middle between two ers. i found out the hard way, that while one will offer a slick, state of the art environment, you will encounter indifferent, uncaring staff and wait times up to 8 hours.

the other er features a setting reminiscent of the tv series, m*a*s*h, all due to ongoing construction of brand new facilities.

i chose the latter. why? 

because a previous visit 18 months earlier showed a well-oiled machine, despite er patients lying on gurneys in hallways. the staff were attentive, nurturing, and very efficient.

this er, providence cedars-sinai tarzana medical center, proves that it's not the setting that matters. it's the staff!

and this is where tarzana er excels. from the friendly check-in to triage to the er doc, everyone was top-notch.

especially the doc. 

i'm a veteran of many er visits, so i know an exceptional er doc when i see one, as in the case of dr. gregory scott brewster. 

i have not met a more compassionate, attentive, sympathetic and driven er doc. ever.

he goes far beyond what is required. i listened for two hours as he not only took care of at least a dozen patients, but chased down specialists and patients' personal mds on the phone. 

in my case, it took him 2 hours to find an ophthalmologist willing to see me. yet he never gave up.

overall my experiences at scripps encinitas have been relatively positive for having to stay in the hospital. i've also stayed at scripps encinitas about 6 times over the last 3 years, so i know how the process works, and knowing what to expect is helpful. 

positives:
1. treated quickly (this has to do with the condition i have), unfortunately, if you have a broken arm, just like most hospitals, it will probably take longer to be treated.
2. er is a major improvement from 10 years ago, private rooms with doors.
3. good experience with every doctor i've had.
4. i've only had to share a room 2 out of 7 times, however this also had to do with my condition. 
5. they allowed my boyfriend/fiance/and now husband to stay overnight with me when i was in my own room.
6. 90%+ of nurses i've had here have been helpful and sweet.
7. the billing process has significantly improved through online portal.
8. access to medical records and tests as well as communication online is helpful.
9. pcu and the standard hospital rooms on that floor are very nice. 

possible negatives:
1. possibility of not having a private room. this is huge for me. if you are sick, in pain, and recovering, you want your own space and a space for someone to stay with you. all new hospitals in the san diego area are required to have their own rooms now, i'm sure they will get there and understand it's a big undertaking, but it makes a big difference for experience and patient care. 
2. nurse response time - this can be long (i never experienced longer than 20-30 minutes at any given time), and i understand that there are tons of other patients to care for, however, if you are not allowed to get up to go to the bathroom by yourself or your pain really spikes 20-30 minutes can seem like forever. overall, the response time was adequate. 
3. lack of communication between doctors & nurses. i felt like i had to advocate and/or repeat for myself on several occasions. maybe notes weren't written down, maybe doctors don't always read them, who knows. my surgeon also has privileges at this hospital but is not based out of scripps encinitas, so there may be some gaps due to that.
4. not all of the hospital is updated. some floors and areas are, but some feel pretty old.

after my friend fell in january of 2019 and was not found for over three days, she was in dire physical condition and required a tracheostomy to stop recurring pneumonia infections. once stabilized, she was moved to barlow respiratory hospital, one of the best facilities of its kind in the country. here she had the medical and physiotherapy attention she required as well as a staff willing to take the time to understand her.

this was a woman who had no family and no medical coverage (although i had applied for medicare on her behalf at this point). this made no difference to the quality of her treatment by the people at barlow.

although her body had betrayed her, her acute intelligence was still there, something other facilities ignored. as a result, even after she improved to the point where she was breathing on her own and able to talk with a pmv and was moved to a nursing home, she never ceased wanting to go back to barlow.

six month later following more episodes of pneumonia, she did get to go back.  and, again, received the same great medical attention, the same personalized care by the staff and, again, her condition improved to the point that she could communicate with people even without the pmv.

eventually, all her determination could not will her body back to health and it finally gave out but, to the end, she appreciated the doctors and staff at barlow who took care of her physical challenges and made her life worth more than just existing and, especially, those who enjoyed her twisted sense of humor.

if i could rate this place zero stars i would, the visit was a nightmare from start to finish. i came in to the er on a weekend with agonizing abdominal pain. i'd heard the horror stories about this place but i was very new to the area and was in such intense pain that i just wanted to get the closest care possible. i was triaged and put in a waiting room where i was left to sit in pain for an hour and a half. then finally, i was brought back to what i thought would finally be my room, but i was just placed in another waiting room where i sat for another 30 minutes. i appreciate that there is a lot going on behind the scenes that contributes to long wait times in the er, but this hospital was seemingly empty, with staff just standing around talking. 

finally i get brought back to a room and see the doctor (oluwaseye acabi). nobody asked me for a list of medications i was currently on or for any sort of medical history. i explain to him that i was having severe abdominal pain and that i had an iud and a history of bad ovarian cysts. i told him that i was afraid that either my iud had migrated or i had a cyst that was causing my ovary to twist (which would need to be treated immediately if that were the case). he proceeded to tell me that the iud migrating would be impossible after having it in for a year already. 

he then asked me if i wanted a pelvic exam and/or an ultrasound, which i thought was odd considering he was supposed to be the expert and should know what he needs to do to figure out and solve the problem. i said yes to both. he started the pelvic exam and it was by far the weirdest and most uncomfortable pelvic exam i have ever had. it was clear that he didn't know what he was doing, but i'll leave out the graphic details. 

he then tells me that i am welcome to wait for an ultrasound but that i "wasn't a priority" and would be waiting all night. at this point i was so fed up, tired, and in so much pain that i just wanted to go home and get in bed, there were no beds in the rooms for me to try and get comfortable in while i waited, so i told them to discharge me. 

they came in with the discharge papers and they'd given me bs diagnoses of pelvic inflammatory disease and dehydration. he also prescribed me antibiotics (which i didn't take because i had a feeling i didn't need them, and my obgyn confirmed), and muscle relaxers. mind you, they never took down my medications so they would have never known if i had any medicines that would interact. 

as i'm being discharged, he comes in and tells me "oh by the way, during your pelvic, i couldn't find the strings to your iud. i didn't look any further because i didn't want to inconvenience you." i am still confused as to how he would have "inconvenienced me" by doing his job and investigating the problem that brought me to him in the first place. 

so i went home and stayed in extreme pain until i could get in with my obgyn. within seconds, my ultrasound tech was able to tell me that my iud was embedded in the wall of my uterus and needed to be taken out (something the er doctor told me was impossible, if you remember). when my doctor came in she did a pelvic and was instantly able to see my iud strings clear as day... the ones the er doctor claimed he couldn't find. 

i've been to a lot of bad doctors and hospitals and had a lot of bad experiences but this one takes the cake. i paid $500 to wait around in pain and to be treated with extreme negligence and incompetence. stay far away.

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

once in the er, which was set up efficiently because of the virus, the er doctor immediately explained to me that they will not send my covid-19 test off to be tested unless i was admitted to the hospital.  his main concern was not diagnosing my problem but explaining that i would have to go somewhere else to get tested for covid-19.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.  

i was discharged and walked to my car still struggling to breath just the same way as i walked into the hospital.   

that was saturday, march 21st. fast forward to wednesday, march 25th and i was not feeling any better, in fact, i felt worse. i called my doctor both the 25th and 26th and left messages. her nurse called my back on the 27th and informed me to stop taking all allergy meds immediately and that she had reviewed the labs and x-rays and they believe that haze over my right lung is pneumonia.

pneumonia?!!  so i had pneumonia in the right lung for an additional 6 days without any treatment?!  why would dr. parker say i was "all clear" and ignore the haze?  i had to take additional time from work to heal whereas if dr. parker would have just taken the time to explore my results for something more than covid-19, he could have treated me correctly and i could have returned back to work without taking additional time.  

lastly, once i got the bill, i saw that i was billed $273.50 for a pregnancy test!!!  the admitting nurse asked if there was anyway i could be pregnant, i immediately answered no and explained why i couldn't be.  so why would you give me, a 49 yr old woman with a valid reason a pregnancy test?  especially for $273.50.  over billing???   yes!

i will never go back to memorial hermann sugar land emergency room.  the care of the treating physician was below sub-par and i could have saved way more time and money going to another facility.

review:
where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!
