the pandemic created issues.  trying to find where to go proved difficult.  staff seemed reluctant to assist, and many staff had no idea where to go.  no one appeared to be in charge anywhere. there were a lot of puzzled people, patients and staff alike.

the procedure went fine, and the imaging technician was professional and pleasant.

i'll go to a different facility in the future in hopes of finding one where the staff seem better trained

banner desert medical center has excellent phone communication during covid-19. when my son was in the emergency department, nurse megan m. took my call and answered all my questions pertaining to my sons health with a friendly attitude. my son's surgeon, dr. susan r. cortesi even called me after his surgery and explained all her findings in detail, she was very pleasant and helpful. floor 2b nurses; morgan brown and missy took my phone calls with great patience and care. my son had a very positive experience with this hospital, i'm very pleased with the exceptional service that was given.

the nurse at the door seth as he so eloquently spelled his name was extremely rude. its obvious he hates his job. 
 in addition it took seven hours for them to do one test. didn't find they literally shot me up with two doses of morphine and have me some antibiotics. 
 really for extreme abdominal pain that's lasted over 24 hours? 
 what a joke. do not come here unless you want to be talked down to by some punk kid named seth or just have them do nothing. 
 oh i did get to heart then talk about covid. they even were showing other nurses their covid wing. 
i felt like they were showing a new car. they were so excited..

the condition my mother was discharged should be criminal. she went in able to care for herself and came out close to a vegetable. proper home care was not communicated nor set up for her tremendous needs on discharge. this is during the pandemic lockdown, so i could not witness her deteriorating condition. no doctors or nurses ever initiated a call during her 11 days. calls made to nurses would routinely get disconnected, and other times when they would say they would call me back, not once did it happen. there's just too much wrong to write about. hopefully, you can get the gist.

the staff is very kind and friendly! nikita took my information and was so lovely to talk to as well as my phlebotomist, hailey, who kept me nice and distracted while she took my blood. i was in and out this am in less than 15 minutes! thank you for your great patient care! i won't dread getting blood draws anymore coming here.

i delivered my youngest son at kingman regional medical center. while there were some problems during delivery and recovery, most of the doctors and nurses were good. my biggest issue is with the awful billing department. i thought i was done paying in 2017 when i had my son. over two years later, i received a large bill. i paid that in full, was told there had been an issue with the billing department and that i was now done paying. well, i just received another large bill 3 years after i was told i was done paying. i would definitely not recommend krmc based on their billing department.

krmc is a good medical facility. their pot of gold is their employees, caring and professional. i've been a volunteer there, a patient, rehabilitated after a stroke for 7 weeks in acute rehab, watched my beloved great-granddaughter born there, had the heart-wrenching experience of holding someone's hand as they slipped away and experienced lives saved in the er. i never experienced a problem not immediately resolved. i recommend their care from urgent care, physicians care, acute care , emergency department and their cafeteria is reasonable with excellent food.

i don't think they deserve any stars. my brother was in there for nine days. because he came from a big family we would call the hospital they told us not to call the hospital anymore. because he's not the only patient in the hospital and we can't answer the phone. but with the coronavirus going on. and you can't visit the only contact is to call. they told us to call his cell phone which was always charging across the room he could not reach it. we would call for updates.they would always say oh he's the same but his oxygen was going down daily. he was always filthy he would tell us he messed his pants and nobody would clean them right away. when he came home on hospice again he was messy did they care no so please avoid being sick in this hospital you may not survive. some of the nurses are very rude and uncaring.and the doctors office next to them is just as bad.they also said they would give us updates when he got worse. boy did they they gave us updates when he had five hours left of his life. when they should've notified us couple days sooner he was on hospice for two hours at home and passed awaythe hospice nurse gave him a bath because the hospital refused to clean them up before he left.
the best, absolute best hospital! they took amazing care of my son after a serious mva. surgery was successful and staff was magnificent. very pleasant and clean environment.

"sprawling" single story facility off 424 on the east side of town; casual entrances south and east plus emergency around to the west. hospital staff are pleasant and professional, did a quick time and temp thing for plague before i could enter and use the facility so that's a plus... then did a courtesy room check to make sure i wasn't going to disturb anyone with a phone call.
got the all clear and was informed dinner would be served shortly so i went around to the window to chat with my uncle and see how he was doing. room seems comfortable and well appointed with plenty of room for visitors if they were allowed but they ain't. a nurse (aid?) helped him get around to the window seat and left us to visit for a while. my uncle was recovering from his hip thing pretty well, he was in good spirits but a little tired so i got on my way after chatting for a short hour - was kinda like a zoom meeting but with a bigger screen and the video is less choppy. gotta do what you gotta do.
it's plague season everywhere so currently each patient is allowed one specified in-room visitor as a reasonable compromise between the extremes of hysterical over-reaction and the potential for infectious under-reaction.

easily one of the worst hospitals i've ever been to. i received two bills in the bail and total i had to pay over $1000 for an x ray. i was confused why it was so much, as i was there for fifteen minutes, was told my wrist was not broken, was given an ice pack and then left. i called the hospitals customer service and she told me that the first bill ($508, over $800 before insurance) was the bill from the doctor, and the second ($540, $740 before insurance) was the bill for the facility and what i used while i was there. so i guess sitting in a room for five minutes on a chair and getting an x ray done would've cost $741 before my insurance. the lady on the phone told me that i should've just went to urgent care instead because it would've been cheaper, but i did and the wait was over four hours so i caved and went to the er because i had to work. i will never return and i do not recommend anybody to go either.

what a wonderful staff! i've been here since 5 in the morning and it has been such a pleasure. the facility is spotless and dying this pandemic i really feel safe. they really haven't missed a thing and are very thorough.
i feel very blessed to come here.

omg!!! i cannot even believe what this place has posted on their site!!! i'm seriously furious right now!!! to start with, if you care about your loved one do not send them there! this place provides zero therapy and only keep patients there as long as insurance is willing to pay. i just checked their site and they moved my one star rating far below their preferable ratings from 4 months ago. 
now to my point... they are not doing anything to prevent the coronavirus spread at all!!! they allowed an elderly elderly woman in not even knowing she had a pneumonia, she disclosed it to us during a break.their patients and employees are complaining! please please help me stop this place from hurting anymore people!

we tried to get my friend into here because he gets suicidal and has a very back drinking problem. they turned him away when he was at rock bottom because he didn't have $2,000 up front to pay. they would not work with him. what the heck kind of place does this when they say they are there to help people. really? places like this give no hope. all for the money.

19 years ago my wife and made an emergency visit to this hospital, she was 1-2 weeks pregnant and had been spotting, since it was after hours and her regular doctor
was closed we made the decisions to go to the er till now i have no idea why we chose this hospital.
after she was examined and did ultrasound the nurse who i wish i knew her full name told my wife that the baby was going to be born with no limbs and dwarfism 
she had to abort it and directed her to her primary doctor who is out of whittier hospital. the next day she whent to see her doctor she told him what occurred, he examined her and said the fetus was fine and told my wife that there was no way of that nurse knowing how the baby would come out when it was a small fetus, he called that hospital to file a complaint and was told that there was no record of my wife making the visit in the er also no records of any nurse examining my wife. my son was born healthy he is about to turn 18 and just graduated from downey high going to college 
i am not a hateful person but god might punish me for saying this but i hope that the nurse that was there night is dead and burns in hell. now to reason of my complaint 
my father in law who is 87 was @  nearby rehab getting better due to a recent minor heart procedure he had done, he was to be released this past saturday 06/13/20
but 2 days before he had lost consciousness and was taken to the same er now called pih they took him there because it was nearby the rehab center he was @, after they examined him we found out he had uti and would be ok, today my mother in law got there and they had hooked him to a respiratory machine beecause they "think" he has fluid in his lungs and had problems breathing and wanted to inkebate him and put him under and should start preparing for the worst.
my mother in law was furious and told them he was fine 
and that they are not to do any procedures with out her approval nor his regular heart doctors approval
i have no idea why this hospital is stil there, 19 years ago they had no idea on what they are doing and till now even thought they are under pih they still have no idea on what they are doing, this hospital should be shut down due to inaccurate and false doctors examinations that can lead to death cause by this hospital.

thank you

after a long day of picking up and transporting covid deaths i went to this hospital. in staffing office some employee named dennis berated me for my appearance for not having a suit and tie on. that's the kind of "thanks" the funeral industry gets dealing with these difficult times. i am proud to say i have much love, respect and support for the medical professionals dealing front line with this unknowing virus, we have to wear ppes as well and it isn't fun.

so if you meet desk clerk dennis in the staffing office please do not expect much.

wow, a god-loving, christian hospital? sign me up!

i love their refusal to take care of my friend during her pregnancy even when there were very concerning symptoms showing up one night, because she's on medi-cal. 

i commend the nurse's loving, caring, and concerned warning that, "if you didn't get assigned here by medi-cal, then we don't get paid when you come in".

i appreciate the cautious, wonderfully crafted lie they fed to my friend that "even if you're in labor, we'll have to send you home because it's not considered a medical emergency" (which she said to ensure we wouldn't return.)

i was astonished, no, impressed when my friend had another emergency during her high risk pregnancy (past her due date, nonetheless), and showed up again only to be told the same lines by a whole different set of nurses, who openly place the value of some extra money over that of two human lives.

i will be even more excited to sue the living daylights out of this joint if anything goes wrong and it's shown they could've solved the problem (but didn't).


what an absolute joke. they should be utterly ashamed to call themselves christian in any capacity. presbyterian hospital? more like pre-historic, when my lawyers get through with them.

the emergency is a complete joke i went in to clean up a post operation area and all they did was stick the filthy bandages right back on w more tape not even caring about the infection i already had...they were quick to collect my 100$ co pay tho.

worst experience in a hospital we ever had my family member came in had a extended stay they thought she might have had "the corona virus" put them in isolation left them should in bed didn't give her medication wouldn't answer pages all the nurses sitting in nurses  station no visitors can check up on patients they just sit doing nothing. the fact that they are a co-worker didn't matter not until they found out their son was administrator and the dr she worked for notified nurses supervisor they got care this has happened with 2 family members i work in radiology 34 yrs never seen worse patient care than at this hospital

my grandfather is a non covid patient at whittier hospital medical center. they are not allowing visitors to see him even though he is end of life. administrators please help me, your nurse supervisor, diana, isn't coming out to update us after she said she would come and what she is saying is against your own policies. she stated that my aunt who called 911 yesterday saw him before they put him in the ambulance so she "doesn't need to say goodbye". please we only want a chance for his children, who are nurses and educators, to say goodbye and say i love you.

wow,  three stars is far to kind and high. please get your family out as fast as possible.  they are liars to say the least. pih downey first lost his clothes and specially made diabetic shoes. they conned my into letting them transfer him to the whittier location for rehabilitation. don't waste your time or think that will happen. he arrived on a wednesday and the first attempt for therapy was monday. now when he arrived they asked why he didn't have clothes and shoes because they would need them for walking him as part of his therapy, we had to explain that downey had lost his clothes and shoes "his only pair of shoes". whittier asked that clothes and shoes be brought for therapy. so we were told he was to be home today friday at 430. this afternoon they asked why he didn't have clothes to wear home, which was shocking be they were there 8 days ago for therapy. now at 615 he still not home because the ambulance that was busy. we know this because we called them at 530 and asked if they lost him. no, was the answer. that was when we were told of the ambulance issue. oh, when or if he will show up we don't know they don't know and they are not smart enough to call us. so don't be shy run for your life.

come on in, the water's fine. spent the evening with the fine people at the erd. from the security guard that greeted me warmly at the door to the attentive staff and caring medical professionals, i was treated with kindness and respect. thank you one and all.

horrible hospital for the elderly...i am extremely upset because my dad has a heart condition and he was just diagnosed with a blood infection, the hospital hasn't even had the infectious disease specialist come in yet and they turn to the patient and ask him if his heart stops -during his stay at the hospital, not even during any risky procedure...which is a standard question in such cases...if he wants to be revived-resucitated, they didn't even bother consulting the spouse...my mother about it, to see how his psychological condition is, of course my dad said he does not want to be revived if something extreme happens...he has been going through a lot lately...but if he was already giving up, he would not be at the hospital...and they they go and put a bracelet with the initials dnr -do not revive-resucitate...just so he can look at it every freaking moment of the day and night and remind him and the family about that! it is so sad to see a hospital making this type of decisions without them considering the impact of it on everyone...they are giving up on him without even trying...not professional, no compassion, hope they never go through anything like what they are putting us through...please if you can avoid this hospital for elderly with chronic conditions do!

i can't not believe what the nurses at pih whittier have put my family through today. my grandmother had a heart attack and became very sick very quick. we have had to make decisions very quickly regarding the end of her life. they are limiting the visitors to 2 people at a time... making it so that her adult children can not be at the bedside as she passes, citing "hospital policy" numerous times. the charge nurse mae on the critical care unit and jose the shift supervisor were un-empathetic and spoke without any compassion for the situation, which i find very sad considering their positions. each one more rude than the next. when i asked to speak to the shift supervisor mae stated in a condescending tone "i would loooove for you to talk to them". i wonder why she would speak to be that way considering the situation. they actually had the nerve to ask us to facetime my grandma during this time. they have taken something away from our family and a piece of healing during this time that we will never get back.

i'd give negative stars if i could. 
these are trying times, corona virus has many of us nervous and hospitals are overwhelmed. as a health care professional myself i am more then sympathetic and grateful to those who are still working right now to help during this pandemic. my grandfather is at pih right now, and recently has been receiving the worst possible care. as an elderly patient who cannot advocate for himself (non patients not permitted inside during these times), he seems to be completely written off by his doctors and nurses at pih for weeks. he can't sleep due to his overwhelming pain, he gets sent home us being told it's nothing severe. his leg has been swollen and red for over a week and they sent him home with antibiotics and were very dismissive of him. now it's purple and swollen and cold. if they would have been so dismissive of an elderly man who can not advocate for himself and if they cared for his patient it wouldn't have gotten this bad. 

only reason for this review is because of a conversation between her and dennis (health supervisor at pih). my mother is concerned and scared for her father, this is his last year, we all know it. we will be lucky if he last till the end of this year, needless to say he is in poor health. and doesn't help that he is not getting the best care at pih. forgetting to give him medication he needs and not watching over him since she can't be there. 

while calling to complain about his care and asking if he could be watched over more frequently (grandfather recently calling her frantic at the hospital confused and believing he is being held hostage) i heard a man named dennis being not only dismissive of my mother, but utterly rude. 
me and my sister were disgusted by this. 
patient care?!
i understand they are tired and maybe overwhelmed, but how he spoke to her and then clicking on her. all this man did was scare her even more that he is not getting the best care and that pih does not care about her father or patient care. 
after hearing that conversation even i now share her fears, pih is where my grandfather will more than likely die. due to their lack of care.

i lost my grandmother at this hospital, yesterday. due to a stemi she had to be sent there. she normally would go to pih - downey... where we've experienced so much more compassion and empathy. in all my experiences at whittier the nurses lack human connection. they have an air about them as if they are better than their patient population. i've even overheard them talking poorly about patients or visitors. this was evident during our experience yesterday. my grandfather who was losing the love of his life (73 years together) had to make the difficult decision to turn off her machine keeping her alive. part of him felt comfortable making that decision because he was going to have his 3 children with him while she passed. at some point during all of this there was a change of shift. as the ccu day shift charge nurse-mae came on, she decided to really tighten the visitor restrictions. they told us we had to do 2 at a time and rotate out. after trying to explain that this was a change and not our understsnding, she did not have one ounce of human compassion. we asked her to think of our position and please explain why the change. she just copped attitude and said it was hospital policy. her inability to humanize our situation was unbelievable. she said i cannot answer for what happened on night shift but this is the policy. the sad fact was my grandma was dying during day shift. she was trying to use the fact that she told my grandfather the visiting policy and he was fine with it. he was completely grief-stricken and you could have told him anything. he was just pleading for his wife to be saved by some miracle. when we asked to speak to someone higher, she snydly remarked-- oh i would llllooove to get you to the hospital manager. jose-shift supervisor  was even worse....he had put us on speaker (unknowingly) so his colleagues could hear us. when we asked his name he spelled it, as if that was even necessary. please know, we were grief stricken and our instinct was to be kind. we did not approach any of these people in a way that was rude, we simply wanted them to show us an ounce of human compassion. in return we got nothing but a huge power trip and unrelentless use of the words "hospital policy" and told us to facetime. my father stated when mae came in to tell them the visiting rules changes, she seemed to almost enjoy it. that's a terrible perception. pih-whittier nursing is robotic and unempathetic. can you teach empathy? is this where burned out nurses go to thrive? in addition, during one of my rotations out of visiting my grandma in her final moments i heard the clerks in the nursing station talking poorly about our request to allow 4 people in the room. making comments like we can only have 1 visitor. i just wonder if their family was dying would they be ok with that kind of treatment?

my partner comes to this location to have physical therapy once or twice a week. is there a pest donna is really knowledgeable and gives us tips on how to maintain strength. during the covid 19 outbreak the pool has been closed so we have not been able to do pool therapy hopefully that will change in the near future.

not family friendly 

i don't know if that's the cdc's fault but if you ask me it way oversteps their authority and kinda steps on my rights to be with my loved one especially at their time of need. 

the lines are spaced out the door but there are no lines.
no visitors allowed 

kinda reminds me of a church i went to once that didn't want to allow these disreputable types in.

i know the caretakers are brave souls but isn't that what they signed on for? they look well protected. and you're given a mask on entry. 
and they are rightfully the first to receive new vaccines. i love them all 

the case worker was the most helpful.
she was an exceptional coordinator.

the staff and most of the employees are great and most appreciated 
they are doing things to keep us connected but in health care , to me , you need that personal touch 

doesn't bother me to go wash my hands after.
doesn't bother the dr., he does it consistently and constantly anyway. 
but because of the covid police you're not allowed in.

i cannot stress this enough, if you are in pain, they don't care at all about finding the cause of it.  all they care about is treating the pain and sending you on your way.  the care team is entirely insensitive to you and your pain, they just want to get you out of there as fast as possible.

even with an empty emergency room, they wouldn't allow anyone in, someone not in pain, someone with a clear mind, to properly advocate for her.

my girlfriend went to the emergency room the other day with extreme shoulder pain.  the copay is a few hundred dollars to go to the emergency room and she would normally never go because of that, but she bit the bullet and went, hoping to have some kind of imaging exam, to find the root cause.  they did nothing.

they diagnosed the problem as a muscle spasm gave her an injection and sent her on her way.  no crap it's a spasm!  but why did it spasm?  was there a cervical spine problem that caused it?  who knows???  the didn't perform an x-ray, ct, mri......nothing.

the nurses there are insensitive. with all the pain my girl was in, they never offered any assistance in sitting up, getting off the table, nothing.  she's struggling to move and they just stood by.

go to another emergency room.  go to another hospital.  see other doctors and other nurses.  it seems like this hospital's administration fosters an environment of non-caring, poor patient treatment, and expedited "fast food" patient care.

i am currently a patient on the behavioral health unit, 32 south. my "doctor," kenneth a. hetzler, has continued to maintain that i am an imminent threat to myself and others based on instagram art posts that i made while peacefully at home and quickly took down. i have been kept here for nearly three weeks against my will with no access to fresh air, off-unit time, visitors, or personal effects. what passes for mental health care in this hospital is nothing short of obscene. right now, i am awaiting a judge's decision to know if i can return to the home i own and maintain safely. dr. hetzler lied to the judge. you read that correctly. to add frightening insult to injury, hetzler has never set foot on the unit while i have been here. his absurd opinion is based entirely on only three, hour-long zoom mtgs. with me and staff notes. despite the fact that i developed an inability to walk without the assistance of a walker and the horrific side-effect of akathisia, he continues to order haldol to control my "homicidal and suicidal manic" urges. you are reading a true but nauseating to read tale. if i don't receive a sensible judgment soon, all hope for humanity on this unit is lost. other staff members are decent and kind. many think what has happened to me is offensive and wrong. the night-shift head nurse brian anderson spoke with the worcester police department to corroborate that what is going on here is a human rights disaster.

review:
horrible experience here.  staff was very rude.

without getting into personal details, one would expect a little accommodation for family when a family member is near end of life.  nope.  

i will make sure that no family uses this facility ever again.

i could not recommend this hospital enough. 
i gave birth here in mid april 2020...at the height of the covid crisis. needless to say, i was an anxious wreck the whole month before. i'd never been in hospital before and the one time i need to go, there's a once in a century pandemic happening. 
but i really shouldn't have worried because literally every single employee that i encountered at lenox hill is an angel. amazing at their jobs and with such nurturing and caring demeanor. i had incredible care from everyone here and now i fully understand that healthcare is a calling for these people...you couldn't do what they do day in and day out ...all of the stress that comes with it if it weren't. 
we couldn't leave our room because of covid but the nurses were so accommodating with everything we needed. l&d rooms are private and i recommend paying for a private room if you can swing it for after birth because i couldn't imagine having to share a room in the state i was in post birth. 
the only negative i will say....we did the hospital tour in jan or feb and i really didn't like the nurse who ran that session. she was a very straight shooter, no nonsense type. to the point where she was downright rude to some of the women who had questions. one of the women i felt so bad for...she asked a question and the nurse was sooooo condescending and made the woman look like an idiot who had asked such a stupid question. like i literally would have cried if it had of been me. it's like, i get that this nurse has delivered thousands of babies so she knows everything and it's no big deal for her but for us women, we've never done it and it's our bodies that will be going through it so it's obviously a scary time so it would be nice if the nurse running the session was a little fluffier and more considerate of the fact that we have very little idea of what to expect and want our minds reassured. to be honest, i was very turned off the hospital because of this nurse (i literally looked into other options because of that) so i do think they should definitely reconsider who runs this session because that nurse (think her name was lisa) was not at all representative of everyone we encountered when it was go time and is a poor "face" of the l&d/maternity department for lenox hill.

i just gave birth 2 days ago , and i have to say this hospital is the best .. everyone of the nurses was well attended , doing their job . checking on me 24/7 seeing if i'm okk. answering all my questions with no problem . food for breakfast and dinner was the best .. i have nothing bad to say , but to say i'm so thankful that i had my little princess in this hospital. will recommended anyone that want a safe and fast and want to give birth in a nice private space , should give birth here .. the best !!!! god bless the nurses and doctors at labor and delivery !!

serious accident happened while in nyc and a great friend/local suggested the er at lenox hill. to say we were nervous only begins to describe how we felt. (broken bones will do that) 
early in life, i learned being quiet and polite in er ..later, i learned it can work against you. upon arrival, the guard at the door got me a wheel chair. in a timely manner, i was checked in, seen by dr ghandi  (great name!) she sent to get myriad x-rays. everyone we dealt with at the er was top notch: cordial, smart, efficient and sensitive to the severe pain i was experiencing.
at the completion, i was given sheets of relevant docs to refer to and pass on to my ca dr. impressive. greatly appreciated the post-appointment health suggestions. well done.
when i returned home, i had to call to request copies of x-rays and dr notes.  the records dept was extraordinary - so helpful, cordial and professional. ( silly me, i thought i might encounter the surly ny-er you see on tv. i was so wrong.) 
hands down, best care and kindness rendered.

i would rather be paralyzed than go back to this hospital. when tomorrow's surgery got moved here, yesterday, i canceled it.

i had two major surgeries here in march.  i was in the hospital from wednesday through monday. i was supposed to stay until thursday, but i had multiple infected iv lines, wasn't fed, and didn't get meds, so i asked to leave a few days early.  my last day, i sat in feces until my husband came to take me from the hospital.  

just called the patient advocate to find out if they've improved. i would like to have surgery so i can walk again. i am an optimist and hoped they had changed their culture. after speaking with taschiya, i have less faith in lhh. i could be offered no assurance that my roommate would not have multiple guests who would not wear masks. that means i would be sitting in a room, possibly for days, breathing in random unmasked civilians' sars-cov-2. when i had surgeries with them, previously, they refused to enforce their own rules or the government's rules about covid-19. just an fyi, a lot of cases of covid-19 do not have fever or cough, but they are still contagious and spread has been documented from these people. according to lenox hill it's just fine for these people to breathing in my tiny room with me without a mask.

i previously held off writing a review or complaints because, i figured, i didn't see the staff on a good week.  if you have similar problems, skip the patient advocate, and go straight for the new york state department of health centralized hospital intake program and the joint commission's office of quality and patient safety.

if you're thinking about coming with to this hospital, shoot me a message. i'm happy to give you plenty of information to dissuade you from coming.

i've included a picture of what my wrist normally looks like.

the er at this hospital is the fastest and best in new york city!  what a great group of dedicated md's! and nurses!  i refuse to go to any other hospital while i live in my city of new york!
  lenox hill hospital of northwell health is literally the best hospital in the entire state of new york!

i dont know if anyone reads these reviews, but be careful in there with a doctor named michael togo! i ended up there after a bike accident, with a fractured tooth and pretty beated up arms and hands. he comes in to the room very sassy and grabs my arm for me to extended it, cause he grabs one of the bleeding wounds aggressively, i pull back and say ouch. his response it, 'ugh! i will go get you a woman doctor who has patience for this kind of shit" and walks out. unbelievable. luckily the doctor that came after was kind. what kind of a sexist unprofessional attitude is that? do doctors have the right to treat people this way?

if i could give this hospital a negative rating i would. one star is being immensely generous. 

my animals received better care from veterinarians than my spouse received from the physicians at this hospital. 

i would rather die at home than to seek any type of care from this hospital. even from the sars-cov-ii virus. 

stay far away from this institution if anyone desires even a modicum of compassion. because none will be given from the staff at this hospital. 

i can name names of the cold, heartless and sadistic physicians at this deathcare institution. but i won't. for now anyhow.

this review is specifically for dr. bridges.  she's awesome!

it's so nice be listened to, heard and given the courtesy of  direct and clear replies to questions.

spine surgery is a big deal.  i've had  two consults before where the doctors pretty much said "here's what you need" and then just expected me to do it without questions, research and serious consideration.  dr. bridges is the opposite.  she flat-out said high risk, gave me real numbers on complication rates, discussed options even if it wasn't in her wheelhouse and referred me to someone who specializes in an option i want to explore.

no detectable ego which makes her more credible in my eyes.

i'm well aware weight is always a factor in surgeries and since my colon resection and the unexpected consequence of the high carb post op diet, i'm all too aware of my current size.   i don't sugar coat it.  she doesn't sugar coat it.  need to keep this stuff real.  she wasn't rude, just matter of fact.  i really appreciate that.

review: i have been to this hospital three times now in the past two years and it's high time i leave a review. my family and i have experienced nothing but incredible care and compassion from the angels that work at this hospital--from cleaning crew to doctors, everyone at this place is so wonderful and caring. when my dad had his heart attack a few years ago they were so loving and understanding throughout the whole process. last year, i broke my arm and i experienced the same level of care and professionalism from every single staff member i encountered. yesterday, i took my dad to the emergency room due to a back injury and because of the covid 19 situation i wasn't allowed to be with him throughout his visit, but the check-in staff and triage were so wonderful that i felt like i was leaving him in the hands of angels. i truly don't have the words to express how wonderful this hospital is. we are so lucky to have this center just a few minutes away.

what a joke!! they need to get some doctors that care in the er!! took my hubby last night with shoulder pain. they did a x-ray and diagnosed him with a pinched nerve. they didn't run any other tests, no medicine to relieve his pain, only saw the doctor one time and was told no for a mri when he asked for one. he woke up this morning after not sleeping last night. in worse pain. they gave him a prescription last night for muscle relaxers and something else which he couldn't get filled until today. all i can say is thanks! it's no wonder people go crazy!!

my wife and i came here and gave birth to our beautiful baby girl and they were just amazing. all the nurses that helped us were just wonderful but i have to give a shout out specifically to arielle who worked with us on two separate days as we went in several times before actually giving birth. she was just so sweet and easy to get along with. our midwife ramona is such an empathetic person she was just so helpful and sweet. she gave excellent advice to help my already exhausted from 38 hours of back labor. over all just really helpful staff and really sweet people. only issue was it's just freezing in there. bring your own blankets and pillows as they'll just be that much more comfy.

my dad recently stayed here for almost 3 weeks after he had a stroke. the entire staff at encompass is so awesome! from tiffany (patient admission),debrah (case manager),eiesha (medical records), physician,pt,ot and st everyone went above and beyond to help my dad to recover and accommodate him. my dad kept asking me if he can stay there longer. he loved the staff there as well as the physical therapy activities and the two gyms.
during this special time i wasn't able to visit him in the facility which really worried me at the beginning. on top of that my dad speaks very little english which didn't help the situation. i expressed my concern to debrah,the case manager. she ensured me that they have some type of translation tool and they will make sure to take good care of my dad. and they did!
my dad made great process while he stayed there. 
eiesha from the medical record department went out of her way to help me to request medical records from the previous facility my dad stayed while she could easily say sorry that's not part of my job. she is so organized and had everything ready for me on my dad's discharge date.
i am so grateful for those wonderful wonderful people who take great pride in what they do and passionate about helping others!
highly recommend it if you are looking for a rehab place for your loved ones.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Tustin

review:
i had a unfortunate accident on the 2nd day of a new job in oct. 2019. it messed up my neck face & body pretty bad. i had to have surgery june 2. 2020. from the excellent surgery center in orange i was transferred to encompass in tustin, ca., on the 3rd. as much as i hate to say this, they really sucked. they weren't familiar with someone coming to them so soon after c-spine surgery. i was told by a couple of my doctors & through some testing that i absorb medications quickly. the nurses did not understand this. i guess because of the "oxy-demic" they made me feel like i shouldn't be taking so much, even though my dr/ surgeon prescribed them. they went through all my things & searched all the drawers, cabinets & bathroom as if i was hiding something. iwas in so much pain & they made me feel like i was an addict!!
on the positive, i give great thanks & praise to the pt department. thank you pedro..
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Tustin

review: my husband had back surgery three weeks ago and was sent first to fountain valley hospital where the care was awful. since there are no visitors they don't get the attention needed. i wouldn't even give them a rating. without asking me they were checking him out and making their own decision where he was going and no way was that going to happen. he had to stay there a couple more days, however; it was worth it. we got him into encompass acute therapy in tustin and there isn't enough stars for this place. larry said it was like heaven. everyone was so nice and went out of there way to make his staff as pleasant as possible. mark called me on that monday and rushed all the paperwork so we could get him into their place. he couldn't even get out of bed when he got there. he still needs help because of the back surgery and i might also mention he has parkinson's and that isn't easy either. he had not had a shower for 8 days and that is one of the first things they did and put clean clothes on him. they treated him like a human being. they would check on him often and keep in touch with me also. some of the names he mentioned was the supervisor, dr nicole and therapist nicole, barbara, darrell, rosa, denise and the case manager, cecilia, was so helpful getting everything arranged for him to come home. hopefully, the home care we will have helps him to continue his recovery. since i couldn't go and visit i felt comfortable knowing he was in such great hands. i would recommend this place to anyone who needs this kind of care. i also want to thank lisa for the couple showers she gave him. there are too many great people that work there and all were great. i want to thank them and appreciate all they did.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Tustin

review:
we don't recommend kindred at all.  if any other place is available - don't choose this place. we're not going to waste anyone's time with the litany of wrongs our loved one suffered in their care, by their obstinate staff.

what kind of hospital does not call the family members and lets them know their relative has been discharged? i have never heard of this. wow. and for the neurologist not to call us back after numerous messages. very shady!

went in because i had a fever for three or four day's straight, and cough. this is during hot time of covid19.
saw michele winchell. never ever see that woman. there was me there and no one in front of me. took way over an hour to see her. she came in and just brushed everything off, in three or four minutes she sent me on my way not doing a single test or prescribing not a single medication. simply said try flonase. soon as i got home my temperature spiked to 103.4. called her back and demanded medication! she finally prescribed an antibiotic an hour later after i had already left. now i have received my 305 dollar bill. and am most pissed about it all. why was i charged 305 for a three minute talk and no test and no medication even prescribed?! my visit with the actual doctor there doesn't cost me 305 ever, and he always prescribed me something or runs test for something. 
also don't expect to get in an out quick. you'll be there at the least an hour. that's just before you get called back. then you'll sit in the back do another 30 minutes prolly more.

dr. tong and lisa crouse were part of my son's care team while he was recently hospitalized, and it was very comforting during a very stressful time, to know they were kind to him. due to covid-19, i was not allowed to visit my son, so it helped me a lot to be in communication with the capable and caring medical staff at mad river community hospital. i was very impressed with their overall quality. thank you!

obgyn nurses and doctors are pure evil:  i looked through the glass to be held captive against my will then complained "thinking of" child robbery for looking then they frauded trespassing then interrogated me for 2 hours all of which i had no representation or help while they forced me to sign no lawsuit papers- i had a legit pass and my alleged crime was looking because i was not white. i kid you not. i didn't bother fighting because psycho is psycho. they are pure evil psycho: last i heard reading minds is only for discriminating vilifying terrorizing con jobs scamming cover up for hate crimes.

i waited 6+ hours in an empty/almost completely empty er before getting in. after the person i was with actually got a bed, it was an additional 2+ hours of them sitting and waiting for an actual doctor to see them. the nurse who took their information made them take tests they didn't need. humboldts heath system is a joke and this place definitely adds to that idea.

avoid this hospital at all cost! 
my mother was admitted to nazareth hospital....i was there most of the time for 10 days and what i saw is just hard to believe!
few "care" details i experience: 
one day i came and noticed few pills on a bedside table. since my mother could not move, all meds should be given to her by the nurse. i took the pills and went to the nurse's station. i asked for the nurse who take care my mother.... i was told she is with another patient... 15 minutes later i was told that she is on another floor... another 15 minutes later i was told she is on a meeting...when i asked who taking care the patients while she is not, i was told that they have somebody. after i insist that i want to talk to this "somebody", the woman i was talking went to the nurse at the computer and whispered something to her, then turned to me and sad that this is the nurse who is covering. when i asked what meds prescribed to my mother and when they were given, i was told that she is only covering and need time to figure this out. when i insist, saying that it should be recorded and she can look it up on a computer, she did, and told me the list of medications and time they (all meds) was given. it was recorded that all meds were given! i show her meds in my hand and ask her why they are on a table... she said that i better talk to the nurse why responsible for my mother.  finally, the "responsible" nurse came to her work station. i guess she was not informed that she was with another patient, on another floor and at the meeting, as she told me that she went out because she needed a break! for the meds, she told me that my mother did not want to swallow them! i understand the possibility that my mother would not swallow, but why it is marked as given???? 
after more that a week in a hospital, thursday, late evening, i was told that my mother will be discharge on saturday. i reminded that home care agency needs to be informed, hospital bed, oxygen tank, lifting equipment etc delivered and installed. i was told not to worry! next morning  (friday), while driving to the hospital, i received a phone call. i was told that my consent is needed for special iv line for my mother, as she must be on iv medication for 4 days. i was confused, as this totally contradicted what i was told only few hours ago, so i said that i need to talk to somebody to understand what is going on and will be in a hospital in 30 min or so. when i came to the hospital..... i was told that my mother discharged today and i can take her home! i asked about the iv line etc and was told that she can take meds in a form of pills. i went to the room to see my mother. cardiologist made his rout, and told me that she is not responding to the meds and not getting better. i told him about meds on a table, about "discharging" ordeal, and he was very disturbed by it and sad that he is not discharging patient in this condition! few minutes later a man walk in the room and gave me paper to sign for portable oxygen tank to be use while transporting my mother home. he said he got order for it as my mother being discharge!
few days later, late afternoon i was told again that my mother discharged and i should take her home. i asked if home care agency was notified and all necessary equipment (hospital bed, oxygen tank, lifting equipment) in place. i was told that they not sure about home care agency (i found out later that nobody informed the home care agency), but all equipment delivered and installed in my mother's apartment. i asked few times if she sure and was told that she is as this is stated in the record. i asked to talk to the person who recorded it: i wanted to know how they manage to deliver and install equipment in my mother's apartment while it is locked and nobody is there!
avoid this hospital at all cost!

ms. gupta (i refuse to call her a doctor of anything other than being cocky, rude, and careless) was the most terrible medical professional i have ever came into contact with. never had a plan of action for the treatment of my father besides allowing him to lie in his hospital bed confused and uncomfortable. i did everything i could to have her removed as his doctor and finally had some success after having to contact the patient advocate and having two different care conferences. gupta is the most unprofessional, rude, and to be blunt, not the brightest. she was wrong with every single diagnosis she suspected. demand another doctor if she is yours or your families.

it has taken me awhile to decide if i was going to share my mother's story while hospitalized at peacehealth.  i've decided it's important to do so in order to let the community understand what happens within those four walls.  my mother was admitted april 27th, 2019 with severe sepsis.  she was admitted to the icu by dr. chen, at the time of admission it was asked kris keough (hospital ethicist) not be involved in her care.  after 24 hours in the icu she was transferred to the fourth floor.  my mother had been admittted to this floor before and it had always been a nightmare, we should have requested a different or better yet be transferred out of this hospital.  april 29th my mother was working very hard to breathe, mind you my sister and i are both nurses and we know our mom's medical history and we know her very well.  we told the evening nurse, she told the physician and no new orders.  this was dr. eric yang. shift change came and again we were persistent that she was working entirely too hard to breathe and told the nurse shelly a. multiple times and requested her to be evaluated by a physician.  the nurse kept telling us the physician was doing an admit and would see her after.  we went to the charge nurse several times.  finally when my sister went to the charge nurse and asked for hospice medications to make my mother comfortable because that's where we were heading a physician magically appeared, it only took three hours.  upon obtaining my mother's medical records shelly had time to document how upset we were but not time to advocate for my mom.  my mom continued to decline over the next few days and despite our continued verbal concern to physicians and nurses it seemed to fall on deaf ears.  on 5/2 i spoke with the evening jacqueline m. and i requested medication for her breathing, she did request the medication but also had time to turn up my mother's oxygen to 4 liters (my mother retained co2) turning up her oxygen only caused her to retain co2 as she was already retaining fluids and working to breathe.  the next morning she was transferred to the icu with chf and respiratory failure.  the physician following her was chi-chang yen who told us on her icu admission he felt he could pull her through this.  we were very present in the icu only leaving at bedtime and back in the am.  our only mistake was asking kris keough the ethicist not to be involved in my mother's care. we only saw dr. yen on her icu admission and never came back at all during her admission to speak with my sister or myself, we were both her poa's. on friday may 3rd physician rounding was taking place and visitors are asked to leave.  kris keoug went into my mother's room and told her she was dying.  she told this to my mother alone with no support person in the room.  not only doing this to my mom there was never a family conference to discuss my mom's care or she may not survive this hospitalization.  kris came to the waiting room, blindsided us and stood over us with arms crossed and stated, "you're mom has chosen to go to hospice and she will be there by one o'clock and everyone will be much more comfortable."  my mom was very upset and we were so blindsided and couldn't think to say no let's slow down, she had been in the icu less than 48 hours.  kris was not the doctor and dr. yen never once said my mother was dying to my sister or myself.  upon obtaining medical records dr. yen falsely documented there was a family conference held and it was a family decision for hospice.  it was a forced blindsided decision in my opinion.  i did dispute the documentation and dr. yen again said his documentation was accurate.  i was told by the qi coordinator molly b. "everybody has a different definition of a family conference."   there was not a family conference held the risk manager dan is well aware of this and he stated "kris felt she knew you and your sister and felt it wasn't needed."  she didn't know me and knew my sister on a professional level only. i met with senior leadership and there were changes that came out of my mother's hospitalization and death, two of the most important family is no longer asked to leave the icu during physician rounding and  there is a phone number in each room on the white board to call if family or patients feel they are not getting the care they need.  hopefully there  were  more and nursing staff and kris has learned from this situation and the outcome. our parents do not live forever and i completely understand this but how this was handled made everything traumatic for my mom and her family, something that is almost unforgivable.  i would not recommend this hospital and wish i would have taken my mom elsewhere unfortunately it wasn't an option as sick as she was.

this hospital has really turned themselves around. they are very patient oriented, take great care and pride in the daily workings and want nothing but good results for patients. their staff are super helpful and kind and if they can't assist you they will find someone who can. so glad i stayed in town rather than risking the drive some where else.
er staff was not helpful and oblivious to our concerns. not surprised so many people took the time to get on yelp to say the same. terrible.

i was in the er today with a diagnosis that i pretty much handed to them. they were told several times that the doctor i have been consulting with was in the same hospital, at that moment, doing surgeries and that he wanted a ct. well, they did the test and told me multiple times it was completely normal. well, not only did they not consult my doctor with the ct results, but they told me that my ct was completely normal. i received a phone call after i was discharged from my doctor telling me he actually was looking for me in the er, but i had already been discharged. there was actually something shown in that ct that not only could've turned out to be life threatening if it had been worse, but also is most likely going to lead me to an operation that will save me from future symptoms like this and from sooo much pain and time we have spent on this diagnosis. there were other concerns i had, but this was major for me. i was sent home in tears, again, because we didn't have an answer, yet again, for something we've been trying to figure out for 2 years now, just to find out that they really did have the answer the whole time and just ignored it. they even knew i was frustrated and wanting to know the cause of my symptoms because i made them add two tests. the only reason why i went and will ever have to go to skyridge is because that is where the best gynecological oncologist operates!

in response to hannah b. -
the er director and i had a discussion in the middle of me trying to figure out why my heart rate was jumping from the 70's to 160's. i wouldn't say the conversation was excellent. that was also before i was given the true results of my ct. if the providers would have actually read, or even just traced through, the whole report, they would have seen that what i told them was correct! i told every person in that room what my doc and i were looking for and it was right there the whole time! the 2 tests the director witnessed me request could have been avoided if the ct results were actually read through. i also could have most likely had it repaired and avoided the pain and other symptoms i've continued to have since. 
also, my doctor was able to see my records from the visit the whole time i was there to track my visit (which is what i call a great provider, by the way). now that i have a follow up with him, my records from the visit aren't accessible in your system. it is time that skyridge hospital take responsibility for their questionable care.

i can't speak to the services at rwj rahway hospital, itself, nor the quality of patient care you can hope to receive.  however, i can speak to the amazing community programs the hospital runs.  if the support groups run by the hospital are indicative of its patient care, i have to say the organization is truly invested in health.  

rwj rahway, at one of its namesake gyms, rwj fitness & wellness, offers community-based support groups.   i personally attend the fibromyalgia support group & i can only describe it as a "life-saver."  before the covid-19 pandemic, we were already a close-knit group who discussed the countless lifestyle/medication/nutrition/exercise changes we'd made to improve our situation.  but, when we all went into lockdown, we had unique issues.  

led by an rn who could not care more about us if she tried, our meetings are a mix of scientific information (some unfolding & yet untested) & anecdotal experience.  

i've seen an amazing increase in my health from (regularly) attending these community meetings.  but, & more importantly during this crisis, i've had the support from people who understand our special risks & needs.  people i'm proud to now call "friends."

during this time, rwj & mindy, our group coordinator, have made zoom support group meetings.  it has been a lifesaver, when we can't be physically close, to keep this sense of emotional community makes it seem less abnormal.

my wife had a procedure done on the endoscopy floor at atrium health shelby on november 7, 2019, it was to be a egd with bravo but once we had gone in and prepared for this and she went into the procedure room they decided to not do this but to do a egd with an ablation, which my wife had had done at cleveland ambulatory on november 13, 2018 which told us that she had acid reflux  and doctor rybnicek prescribed 2 medications that one worked for the reflux and the other did not. we did not desire the test to find out the same thing it was to tell us why my wife was spitting up her food at every meal. this egd with ablation cost us three times more  at atrium health than the one at cleveland ambulatory and we got no satisfaction for my wife she is still ill. we are moving on to another health care provider once we pay the few thousand dollar bill at atrium and the other services we had to pay for a unnecessary test. barbara thompson

i couldn't not have been happier with doctor oleg and his staff.  my 76 year old mother had been in a nursing home for several years because of a severe case of parkinsons disease which left her bedridden and unable to move.  this led to bed sores, blood clots, and eventually a stroke around new years day leaving her unable to speak.  she was taken to encino hospital for the first time and we could not of been happier.  the place is very clean, the rooms are very quiet and it was very easy to visit. that is when i first got to spend about 30 minutes face to face with dr. oleg. i was extremely impressed with him and his caring attitude toward my mother as her condition deteriorated.  over next five months, she returned to the hospital three different times for various problems.  each time, the staff could not have been more accomodating.  even as visits became restricted,  i could talk to them on the phone without feeling rushed and still get the information i wanted.  sadly my mother contracted covid19 in the nursing home where she was at in early may.  dr. oleg called me personally several times that last week to share information as the end neared and even allowed me an end of life visit the day she passed away.  i am eternally greatful to dr. oleg and the staff at encino hospital for making a difficult situation just a little more bareably.  if you are in need to be in a hospital, i would strongly recomend this facility.

last january 2019, i checked into the er because my financial situation brought me to the brink of suicide.  i recovered after receiving treatment, somewhat.  i moved to henderson, nv in may of 2019 because it was a better opportunity financially.  having paid my $400 co-pay, i assumed i was done.  according to mission viejo medical associates, they sent 2 letters to me on june 5 & 10 of 2019 stating that i owed $1286.  since i had already moved, those letters never got to me, and i did not call, because i had no reason to believe i owed anything.

today, i checked my credit score, only to find out that they sent me to collections.  wtf?? they have ruined my credit score.  i lost my job in october, and had finally found one, only to have the offer taken away because of covid-19.  i am destitute, and i now cannot get a job in my profession because i have taken a huge hit on my credit report, and i need good credit because my industry requires it.  mission viejo medical associates has had my telephone number the entire time and never once attempted to call me about owing anything!!!   now they have ruined my credit, and my prospects for attaining employment.   there is no reason they could not have called my back then when i still had a job.  now my financial situation is worse than it was then.  and now those thoughts are quickly back in my mind.  mission hospital is there to save lives, yet they will probably cost me mine.

i have been going through a rough patch the past few months with really bad back pain. i had it under control most of the time but unfortunately it's with pain killers. it's a temporary thing but very much needed. i also have daily abdominal pain and discomfort from my past cancer surgeries that they already had be on the pain killers for. this back pain over shadows it. so they just have me take more for this. i recently moved and my new doctor wanted to try me on the pain meds he likes. unfortunately they didn't seem to take away any of the pain and it by the time i figured this out and told them i was already in very bad pain. then they took some time to respond due to the doctor being out. a little too long. this pain completely changes my life. i can't hardly get out of bed or do anything. i have my laptop in bed with me trying to work and it's rough. so i didn't know what else to do. especially with the covid situation. i wasn't sure. so i called the closest hospital to me, st. john's. they said come right down, they'd be happy to see me. it was a rough ride but at least they are very close to me. i got there and no one was in the waiting room. i thought this is great, get right in! so i got signed in, told them the whole story and went back to the waiting room. i then spent two hours curled up in pain on the floor of the waiting room before my pain doctor came through and they just put me back on the meds i was on before that were working. it was a rough ride but i got the prescription and took them and was back to life again. this was 4 hours after the time i arrived at the hospital.

it was a day or so after this that a friend of mine told me that they probably though i was an addict. this is the reason for this review. i am a clean cut professional, i can't even believe i could throw out that kind of vibe but he said that there are clever addicts that exhibit the same persona. all i can say, this is some of the worse pain i've ever experienced and i've had a lot with the gi issues from my past cancer. i was wondering why two different people came into the er after me and got right in. they just kept telling me all their beds are full. so i guess it's true. i will do all i can to avoid this place if i can. unfortunately it's the only hospital around me from what i'm seeing. but i am new to the area. i'll have to explore more and ask around.

admitted into the er in 2016 b/c i was experiencing tightness in my chest, irregular heart activity, dizziness and shortness of breath.  staff hooked me up to an ekg machine and iv drip, when the nurse checked my bp my heart stopped and it felt like a grenade went off in my chest.  ekg machine started to beep maniacally at which point the nurse said "oh sh!t" and turned the machine off.  about an hour later my organs started to spasm violently and i went into shock.  eventually my blood work came back unremarkable and i was discharged.  for some reason they prescribed me xanax.  i could barely walk out of the er under my own power.  days later i returned to the er with same symptoms but my condition was far worse.  after more blood work and imaging one of the er doctors told me that i had gerd even though the xrays revealed no evidence of ulcers.  i was released again, this time they prescribed various gerd medications which i threw away after trying one dose.  a week later i was back at the er a third and final time because i was still suffering severe chest pain and tachycardia episodes (and blacking out).  during this visit the doctors and nurses gave me the third degree, pressuring me to admit that i am a drug addict with suicidal tendencies.  i explained to them i never did drugs in my life but for some reason they ignored my feedback and clung to that narrative.  one of the younger doctors actually mocked me when i tried to articulate my symptoms.  my case manager said they would not admit me into the henry mayo hospital but she would try to transfer me to downtown la.  i waited about 4 hours while she "negotiated with my insurance".  at one point i received an unexpected visit from a social worker who probed me about my non-existent drug problem and depression.  after the social worker left i was discharged without explanation.  my condition continued to get worse but i was finally able to consult a cardiologist who determined that i had fluid building up around my heart (pericarditis & heart failure) and he instructed me to go immediately to ucla.  i was hospitalized at ucla for three days and they put me on a protocol to reduce the inflammation around my heart and within a few weeks the issue was resolved.  i find it interesting in retrospect that the nurse did not report my ekg incident as this was not in the doctor's report, this should have been a critical clue to help diagnose the problem.  i am also perplexed as to why they did not perform an ultrasound of my heart which is how another hospital determined that i had pericarditis.  it's a shame hm got to bill my insurance over 100k for basically doing nothing, and i am disgusted by their misguided efforts to profile me as a suicidal tweaker.  fortunately ucla knew what they were doing and identified the problem without gaslighting me and playing games with my health, i guess that is why my providers say ucla is the best and to avoid henry mayo...

having had a severe sore throat, cough and congestion for about a week, i went to my doctor (wearing a mask they gave me) yesterday.  i was told that i likely just had a severe sinus infection (non-contagious) but that i should probably consider being tested for covid 19.  they suggested that i go to the drive through testing at baptist east; so i did.

there was a quick drive through triage with two stops to determine that i "qualified" for testing.  then they instructed me to park my car, where i was called on my phone and told it was my turn for testing.  this all took no more than 10 minutes.  when i arrived at the first of two stops at the testing tent, i was asked for my insurance card and asked how much i wanted to put toward my $1400 deductible.  when i asked what the cost would be for the test, they told me that they did not know but that i would need to pay "something" toward my deductible for the emergency department visit.  emergency department visit!  you have to be kidding me!   those visits cost hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars and i was in a rickety tent in a parking lot trying to do my part to determine if i had exposed anyone to a terrible virus.   i got nowhere when asked why this was considered an emergency department visit instead of a minor medical or minute clinic visit.  i also told the payment staff that they should disclose the approximate cost at the very beginning of the testing process.  nonetheless, i put $50 on my credit card and proceeded to the second section of the tent to be tested for the common good.

two nurses swarmed me as i sat down in the testing section of the tent.  one took vitals while the other gave me a new set of sinus windows with five different swabs.  when i asked why so many, i was informed that they are testing for the flu, strep, covid 19 and one or two other tests.  five tests in all.  i told her that i had no idea they were going to do all those tests but she said that's what they are testing for at the current time.  and i am sure they are profiting for each and every separate test for each and every person being tested.  i went back to my car, a bit stunned from the encounter, and comforted my bleeding nostril with a tissue.

the covid-19 testing at baptist east took less that being in line at chic-fil-a and should definitely not be billed as an emergency department visit.  i feel that the hospital is taking advantage of the pandemic instead of doing its share to help those affected.  they should know better.  and they should be ashamed.

review:
this is a pretty top notch hospital.  i guess during the coronavirus crisis, not many people were at the hospital.  parking was pretty empty with no one to man the posts.  we came here while i was 3 cm. dilated.  since i wasn't in active labor, they checked me in and then had me walk around for an hour.  this was the most painful one hour walk that i've ever had.  i cried.  but all the nurses were really nice and supportive.  

after i started to become more dilated, i was checked in immediately and then they flew me down via wheelchair to my room, which was spectacular with an ocean view.  the anesthesiologist came in pretty fast to give me the epidural.  our dedicated nurse was super nice and helpful.  whenever i wanted some popsicle or some chicken soup, she brought it for me.  she was very informative too.  what a blessing to have a great nurse!

they were really efficient too, when i was in active labor, a herd of nurses came in to help out.  it was pretty awesome.  everyone knew what to do.  no one was super chatty, which was nice because i would have gotten annoyed.

the after care was awesome too.  the nurses again were all very helpful and kind.  the after care room was pretty spacious.  we really enjoyed the food offered at hoag. they gave us a celebratory dinner, which was so generous and thoughtful.  the food was very delicious.  we order the filet wrapped with bacon and had some cheesecake.  all in all, it was such a luxurious stay.  it was way better than the hospital that i delivered at for our first child.

hotel hoag is the best place to deliver. from the nursing staff to the service staff, customer service is top notch. i had an emergency c section 2 years ago with my son and was trying for a vbac with my daughter i just had 3 days ago. everyone was on board with the vbac and didn't make me feel pressured to do anything else. i ended up having a successful vbac with dr. illeck and it was the best redemption birth i could have asked for. giving birth during a global pandemic is scary and the whole experience was warm, inviting, and first class.

i had my baby here, i have to say a very nice hospital and very caring staff. from my labor and delivery team of nurses to mommy recovery unit they were all amazing. i want to give a shoutout to the nurses in labor and delivery annie, amanda, and i can't remember 1 (the 1 with curly hair) were very caring and understood my pain that i was going with! thank u for all of ur help!!!

also shoutout nurses in mommy baby unit casey, adrienne, julie, shannon and all their ma's; thank u for help and kindness. 

the hoag team made my experience a real nice 1; 1 to cherish and share with my loved ones!!

please hoag keep putting patient importance 1st; as i have learned from somewhere else "it's not healthcare it's human care!" please always improve and never become like some hospitals where patients r just numbers!

o how can i forget my epidural was amazing!!! it worked and i was relaxed; i don't remember who it was but he was amazing. it's very friendly and helps u through it so ur not scared and overwhelmed. he has a 3 year old and twins. 

well thanks again for everything!!!

my elderly father was admitted to las encinas after a diagnosis of dementia in about 2003 after an emergency visit to the er.

i wasn't comfortable with our communication level with his las encinas physician.  i was skeptical about the precision of the physicians diagnosis, and his recommended pharmaceutical regimen with respect to geriatric dementia care.

my father was placed into a "locked" facility with suicidal, drug abusers, and other mental patients of all ages where he complained of abusive fellow patients. i expected las encinas would exercise due care and responsibility for my fathers well being by placing him in a dedicated ward for geriatric dementia patients.

i retained a geriatric psychiatric specialist at ucla medical school to undertake an independent examination of my father which confirmed an advancing dementia, and, the ucla physician prescribed an alternative drug regimen.

las encinas was eager to discharge my father due to limitations on his medicare coverage. after consultation with county regulators and medicare, we we're provided enough time to find a replacement facility.

although i cannot recommend las encinas for dementia patients based upon my fathers care many years ago, i caution you to examine carefully las encinas or any psychiatric institution claiming to have expertise treating elderly dementia patients. it's my belief that early, specialized geriatric psychiatric care, is pivotal to prolonging the quality of life for these patients.

my father passed away two years later in a hospice, unable to recognize anybody, eat, drink, or swallow.

i wish you good luck with your loved ones in combating this dreadful disease.

i'm writing this review not only as a current employee(who gains absolute nothing by leaving this review), but as a previous family member of a patient as well. 
as an employee i drive by two other hospitals and dozens of therapy clinics where i could work and probably like it there, but i choose to drive 20 miles one way, to work at a hospital i love. as of june 2020 this is the longest i've worked at one place in my life, and i feel like i just started, and can't fathom the idea of not working here. is this place perfect? no. could things be better? absolutely, but what in life is perfect and couldn't benefit from improvement. in healthcare nothing is as ideal as we'd like it to be, and healthcare workers are humans too. we have lives, families, restless nights and stress just like everyone else. at abrazo central i've never worked where everyone is so connected. it's like we all know when our co-workers need a little help and vis versa. i've worked and been on every floor, almost every department and many group functions, but regardless of what your badge says, everyone is willing to stop and help however they can to ensure our patients are taken care of. i've never heard anyone say "that's not my job" or refused to help because the task was "beneath" them. i truly love the moral, environment, and people who work at acc. even our administrators are not afraid to roll up their sleeves and help out during a crisis. not everyone can say that about the people towards the top.
as a previous family member of a patient, i brought my dad here last year because i knew he'd be well taken care of despite me being an employee. to be honest i didn't tell anyone in the ed(one of two areas i'm never in so no one knows who i am) that i worked there. the dr's and nurses made sure he had enough warm blankets and comfortable. ensured he understood what was going on regarding his health and their plan for getting him better. even my dad said this hospital was far better than banner thunderbird where he was the wk before. he loved that the nurses were so attentive and kind. i made it a point to not blast the fact my dad was a patient for alot of reasons, as a result he got great care not because of me but because the people here truly care about the patients.

the next day, surprise!, i don't have covid-19 and they are going to move me from the covid-19 section to another room.  i get a cardiologist who basically tells me i am ok to go home even though i am still having some shortness of breath @7am (also absolutely nothing had been done at this point since everyone was waiting for the results of that test).  they move me to another room on another floor @10am where the bathroom floor is always wet because the shower is leaking (where they give me toiletries finally - luckily i had someone drop off my phone charger, toothbrush and toothpaste, etc the day before so i didn't need anything).

granted, i do understand some of this because of the covid-19 virus going around, but even when i was moved to a regular floor, i couldn't get answers and i got discharged with a shortness of breath diagnosis and a diet plan.  i asked for the echo results to give to my regular cardiologist and was told that i couldn't have them because they hadn't been read yet

the nurses were nice enough when you saw one ...
and the food was not bad (except for the turkey sausage - don't ever get the turkey sausage) but i really hope not to return to this location especially not during the pandemic, but probably not ever
