after calling to review these charges with bon secours customer service they informed us that we would have to take this issue up with the billing department of the doctor's office.  once we spoke with the doctor's office they said that it was a bill from saint mary's hospital and would have to be handled by them.  after calling bon secours back, they gave me the name of a contact that all billing complaints go through.  they refused to give me her email or phone number.  they said all issues must be through hand written letters.  we contacted her stating our issues and after some time received a letter back.  the contact only offered services which are openly provided through customer service (pay balance right now 15% discount or set up monthly payment plan).  wrote contact back trying to get explanation of charges and cited local health care cost averages for ultrasounds.  stated that these charges were billed unethically (as if we were admitted in the hospital) and that costs of services were not within market value and were not discussed with us ahead of time.  we waited a couple months and heard nothing back.  we called their customer service and they told us our letter was received and under review.  we waited a couple more months and a collection notice came in the mail from bon secours.  we called their customer service back and let them know about this issue and that it had been under review.  they stated the bill was unpaid and therefore sent to collections.  we were never able to speak with anyone with autonomy, were billed extremely unethically and nobody from their organization would directly communicate with us about their bill.  my wife and i have high credit scores and always pay our bills in accordance with our responsibilities.  this company refused to openly communicate with us or explain their absurd billing practices.  buyers beware!!! there are many other companies providing the same services in our area with far better customer service and for far cheaper.

via christi rehab center at 1151 n rock road is where i learned to walk, talk and function again after my brain bleed stroke almost a year ago disabled my right leg and arm, and affected my speech.  i knew what i wanted to say but just was not able to put sentences together.  they put me in a room and the rehab team came to my room and told me that they would be the ones rehabbing me.  it would be pt, ot, and speech therapist. they gave me a schedule to follow each day.  i was fitted for a wheelchair, and tray for my disabled arm to rest on. two nurses would come in at 5:30am to take vital signs, dress me and get me up for breakfast. wheel me down to breakfast.  i was unable to communicate so a nurse  came to help me butter my toast, open my milk, put a breakfast bib on me. what a first experience that was.  nurses were very attentive to my every needs.  my first hour was with kim the lead pt. she took me down and put me on a 6x8 mat table to try and rehab my leg, with exercise and trying to get the muscle back.  she even got terry a pta to assist in taking me up and down the long hallway.  they would stand me up, while terry held me up, kim went along on a rolling stool to assist me using my right, physically putting it forward each time i went forward.  first time we went a short way. then we went to the locomat a machine that utilizes a treadmill and a suspension harness for unweighting.  after hooking (trussing me up) in a upper torso harness to suspend me over the treadmill, they strapped my legs into the robotic portion of the machine to make my legs move like i was walking, and lowered me down to the treadmill.  it was pretty intense, looking in the mirror and watching my disabled leg moving and not be able to get it to work under my own power. lookiing into a full length mirror and watching me do this was pretty weird.  needless to say my first experience was pretty scary, but the therapists were right there with any indication of discomfort, pain or anything they responded right away.  went to ot so they could work on my right arm. doing some exercises to strength my muscles and retrain the nerves in my arm.  to even lift or move my hand was futile, for that week. then was off to speech.  she gave me some flash cards that had various people on them for me to describe.  she had me write ( ha, scribble my name and address on a piece of paper with my left hand. wow was that an eye opener.  when i would go back to my room to rest, i would try to do the exercises that i was trying to do with the therapists in bed. eventually, the second week i was getting some movement in my hand and some in my leg.  they kept me for 4 weeks, and intensified my rehab the last week that i was there.  wheelchair, to walker, to a cane.  i walk without a limp, write, move my right arm naturally (still some weakness in some movements) and talk normally.  i owe it all to the fantastic rehab team of via christi rehab center.  kim, terry, jerri, speech therapist, nurses, and the whole facility.  i would recommend them anytime you have a stroke or mobility problems.

during the pregnancy, we attended a meeting with a dozen other couples.  this was held in a large room in alta bates, and the wives were taught breathing exercises and other things that they needed to know during delivery.  during these exercises, the wives reclined on the floor, and the husbands knelt nearby.   and so, when the time arrived we drove to nearby alta bates located on ashby avenue.  when delivery was eminent, the female doctor exclaimed, "let me put on my baby-catching clothes."   a male nurse was on hand to cut the cord.  they allowed the husband to be next to the wife during the delivery.   

the outcome.  we spent the night in a recovery room, and the next morning returned to our apartment with our new burrito (i mean, our new burrita) wrapped in a cloth blanket.  the attached photo shows our little one posing with soap bubbles.  

stupid advice regarding diet.   alta bates has a second location in berkeley, and this is the herrick campus on dwight way.  we went there only once during the pregnancy, and this was to hear a lady give a lecture on what to do during the pregnancy.   the lady advocated vegetarian diets.  i raised my hand because i needed to make a comment.  i said, "if a pregnant mother eats a strict vegetarian diet, the infant could get irreversible nerve damage."   the lady did not like my advice and so she replied, "i never heard of that."  i do not remember the job title of this lady, but it is my guess that her title was, "professional dotard."  i was not in the mood for a confrontation, and so i did not say anything more.  

at the time, i had just published nutritional biochemistry, elsevier, academic press.  pages 519-521 provides the narrative, "the woman gave birth to a child who was exclusively breast-fed by the vegetarian mother.  symptoms of b12 deficiency presented in the infant within a few months of birth.  the symptoms included anemia, and neurological problems such as flaccidity, poor muscular control, twitching, and an abnormal electroencephalogram."   my book cites this article:  higginbottom et al (1978) neurological abnormalities in a vitamin b12-deficient breast-fed infant of a strict vegetarian.  new england journal of medicine.  299:317-323.   

i acquired my ph.d. in the dept. of nutritional sciences at u.c. berkeley, and i have 20 research publications, most of which concern folic acid and vitamin b12.   and so, i am qualified to conclude that the speaker at alta bates is stupid.

we had our baby at alta bates and we were so impressed by the level of care we received. i have to admit, i was a bit apprehensive after taking a hospital tour a few weeks before my delivery. the maternity floor could use a major facelift and the rooms we visited were small and dark.

i went into labor several days before the shelter-in-place order was announced but the hospital was already taking precautions to ensure that everyone was screened at the entrance. 

every staff member we met throughout our experience was professional, kind, and caring. the triage nurse was warm and made me feel calm in what could be a nervous start for a first time mom. our labor and delivery nurse was dedicated to us during the entire labor and rarely left the room. there were a couple of instances where the baby's heart rate dropped and our nurse had to call backup. within seconds, four other nurses showed up and they quickly rectified the situation. the nurses clearly have strong working relationships with one another and demonstrated the type of teamwork we all strive to achieve (but rarely do).

once the baby was delivered, i was wheeled to the recovery portion of the floor. there, each new shift of caretakers - nurse, nurse assistant, charge nurse, and lactation consultant came to check on us and made sure we had everything we needed from diapers for the baby (and me) to water and food for my fiance. we were extremely well taken care of.

what made my experience even better was that the rooms i was assigned to were a huge upgrade over the ones we had seen during the tour. our labor & delivery room had a jacuzzi tub and was one of the largest on the floor. the recovery room, where we spent almost three days, was also spacious enough for baby, fiance, guests, and me. we visited friends at kaiser when they had their baby and while that hospital is more modern, their room was much smaller than what we had here.

overall, no complaints at all and i'm really satisfied with my experience.

this is another long overdue review. i gave birth at alta bates in 2018 and although i had a quite traumatic delivery, the staff really made it easier. the nurses were compassionate and effective. the doctor who delivered the baby and sewed me up did a beautiful job. they really cared for me after the delivery. i am so grateful that i was in such good hands.

i went to the emergency room and was astounded to see staff at the nursing station not wearing masks nor physically distancing.   this is a hospital?

i came in an ambulance with a heart attack. i am still alive today because of these fantastic nurses and doctors. i love them, and i can't imagine anyone giving a bad review about this great medical place. even when i went upstairs from the icu the nurses up there were awesome. i love alta bates berkeley.

i would rate this hospital five stars but my last experience i had was when i was going into labor i had no one to support me in the delivery room besides my 13 year old son due to my fiance not being able to make it on time because of work and the distance at the time. the rn nurse i don't recall her name told me to please don't have no more kids that she didn't want to see me in the delivery room anymore that she only had two kids and that two kids was enough. i felt so bad not only were my hormones all messed up but that was not for her to decide neither was it any of her business i didn't want to be rude to the lady because that's just not my style but she really made my delivery very uncomfortable for me especially when she face time her husband while i tossed and turned with contractions. alta bates is not a bad hospital i just wished the training they give their staff would be more educating and more serious so that the staff can take patients serious not just as a pay check but to give support especially during stressful times..i pray that what happened to me does not happen to another expecting mother and that the support is not like the support i received.

if ur a drug addict sutter health is perfect place. its amazing how easy the prescribe pain meds then send you on your way without really helping situation but they offer pain meds on a regular.  i much rather they help with a medical issue rather than pushing pain meds. i'm grateful they tried to help but wasn't helpful. i now see why america has things like opiod crisis when you go to hospital to try and get "fixed" but instead just pain meds and sent on way....its :/. also when comes to er no matter what u go in for and what they do minimum charge is 3,000. had one first where all i did was get blood draw then waited on burney in hall to be transported... 3,000+.  and people wonder why america has high suicide rates and addicts.

my mother-in-law and i were next door to the hospital touring an assisted living care facility. when we were leaving she was having trouble breathing from the walk and needed her oxygen so i helped her put on the mask and she asked for help to get into the vehicle. i ran in and found two employees to come and help me. when we got out there to help she was coughing awful and then all of the sudden passed out so we laid her gently on the parking lot. 

as the workers called 911 and i called my husband my mother-in-law, karen, was starting to turn blue in the face..she wasn't waking up...more employees were starting to gather. it took 17 min for a small fire truck to come and start cpr, why hadn't any of the staff or i start to do this sooner? everything was going so fast except the ambulance they took forever!! when they did finally show up we got mom to the hospital right next door!

the doctor and nurses had her in an emergency room while i was answering questions in the back and handing over her medical cards. they brought her back thank god, but then she passed right back out, she did this several times. i was told i had to wait in the waiting room where i had to answer the questions all over again. then they wanted me back again and was asking more of the same questions then back to the waiting room, then back to the e.r. it was crazy! when i was told to go to the waiting room last my husband showed up and we could both go back, then they offered us drinks. it felt like they had no clue what they were doing at all. 

the doctor kept coming out of the room and doing different things, talking with other people and then they asked if mom had a d.o.r. in place? really!! i would've told them a long time ago if she had..is there no communication here? after mom had come back to us 4-5 times then shut down again the hospital decided to medi-flight her to the okc heart hospital. they brought her back and told us that she was having seizures from going without oxygen for those 17 awful minutes waiting on the ambulance. with the seizures mom would never be the same and she would be on machines for all of her remaining life, she wouldn't be the same. we had to make that tough choice to say goodbye and let her go. she had already been through so much and we knew she'd never want to live as a vegetable or have machines to keep her alive. 

if you ever have any other choice use another hospital!! this one has absolutely no communication. the doctor was out of the room more than he was with his patient than needed help from him. i don't have anything good to say about the ambulance or the living center next door to the hospital either. with those employees working at a place where the elderly spend the rest of their days you would think someone would've dropped down and started cpr!!

if i could give methodist charlton hospital a zero i would. i first came to their emergency room department nov 2019. it was horrible since then every visit is horrible. i have a on going medical condition that causes severe flare ups. here are some things i have encountered while a patient there. no pain relief and once they give you what they feel even after you kindly explain that doesn't work, they never come in and ask are you ok how you feeling they just give me discharge papers and send me on my way. they have no privacy among the patient a female urine was not marked the nurse allowed her to go through all the samples which one was mine until she found hers that is hippa no no!! i took pictures of the area a doctor came and asked where a patient was nurse while searching for apartments on company computer looked at him and said " i don't know". one nurse was eating popeyes chicken and left the container on the desk there was trash under the desk and on the floor. i have pictures

came in for ruptured cyst and severe pain they did nothing for me at all had me waiting for 3 hours just to tell me i can go home they didn't run test only a ct scan and i never saw a doctor once only nurses. i will never reccomend or come back for pain anything else like the flu yes but pain no!

i went to have a procedure with dr.koro on mar 31. i had the procedure done but still had complications swallowing. i have been to the er twice had a barium swallow done and now am getting a ct scan done. the unfortunate thing is. i had to track dr koro down for help as he seems very unresponsive and so is his staff very disappointed.

had my daughter here 2 1/2 years ago and the experience still baffles me. the nurses there were extremely rude and had horrible bedside manners, especially towards someone in labor. then after i had my daughter they tried to force me to breastfeed, judged me cause i decided not to, then refused to discharge me until i watched a video on breastfeeding. not only that i was 17 when i had my child, and was judged and treated poorly based on that as well. hopefully all those horrible women have been fired, but i'd never have another child there, and wouldn't recommend anybody else to either.
i hate to give them a not so great review but as a patient, i have had some not so wonderful experiences here.  mostly in the er.  at one point they missed a blood clot.

unfortunately a lot of the nurses here know me, because i've had a lot of complications recently. as they come into my room they greet me and say that it's great to see me, but not under these circumstances, of course. (of course!) then they ask where my husband is. they all know him as much as they know me, and i just say that he's not allowed to stay because of the new rules.  several nurses have told me that you can literally get an exception made for him to stay because *other patients* are having exceptions made for their spouses. i tell them we've tried but they won't let him stay still. 

this seems completely unfair to me. i really would like to know why exceptions are made for other patients and not us, especially when my husband and me are never apart from each other like this. 

the rules (which aren't posted anywhere as i have screenshots of in my previous review) do not show the arbitrary 6-6 time for visitors, and even if they did- allowing some spouses exceptions and not others is just cruel. i'm literally just trying to deal with these rules and then a new staff member goes "you know you can get an exception?" 

apparently only if you're not us. ‍

my son has surgery appointment at crown point this morning.  we walked to the front desk at the entrance to parker adventist and asked where crown point surgey center was located.  she said read the sign on wall.  she said crown point is to the left outside hospital.  just clueless and this was the hospital information desk.   blind leading the blind.  
when i explained he's having surgery today it shouldn't be at a office building.  she said i guess you can go to admissions desk.   as we walked towards alpine entrance, she said that's alpine not crown point.  we headed to admissions and they redirected us back to alpine doors.  
other than front information desk being "uninformed", the doctors are great.  patients will get to experience this if directed correctly.

i just want to say thank you to the whole medical team that are very care to each of their patient also especially to the very first man that is in emergency department that is always greet with love and care. 
this hospital is the best!

i know this post is long but bear with me....trust me.....

if you are a travel rn seeking an assignment in or around denver, co, i highly recommend avoiding this facility. i was recently a travel rn for parker adventist during the onset of the covid outbreak. right away the staff and the work environment were very off-putting. my "welcome" to the unit was anything but welcoming. the management and leadership were rude and didn't provide me any direction or answer any of my questions. i couldn't get the nurse manager to answer my emails or return my calls once in the few months that i was at the facility. a good portion of the nursing staff were cold and never offered assistance when a fellow teammate was struggling (i was in icu....you know we all need help in icu). on top of the nursing staff, the doctors were ignorant, impatient, and most had "god complexes". i was consistently ignored, talked over, and/or cut off when i had important information regarding my patients. not to mention, an anesthesiologist put his hands in my face for being "too slow" when drawing up the correct dosage of medication for my patient (it had only been maybe about 30 seconds at this point.....). lastly, what really got me frustrated was that i was told that i was going to be "let go" from my travel contract if i ever took another day off when i had to take a few days for strep throat and the passing of my grandfather. i am only talking like 2-3 days here in the six months that i was at the facility. after the way i was treated for taking a few days off for my mental and physical health, it was apparent to me that i was very expendable and just another warm body for this hospital to control. again, i highly recommend searching elsewhere. 

thanks for bearing with me. i just wanted to save my fellow travel rns and our patients from having to go through a similar experience at this facility. (:

unfortunately some establishments only get a review when a customer has 1 bad experience and wants to get revenge on the entire complex. so here is my 5 star review. i have always gotten top notch care and i come here every 8 weeks for treatments. i have not spoken to one healthcare or support staff who hasn't been courteous and professional. every person wants every employee to pull out all the stops for their relatives. but i know that these doctors do everything within their policy and abilities to get the care needed. if look deep down and you were less than cordial, that's on you and you most likely created your own misery.

my wife spent 8 days at pah after being admitted for recurring pneumonia.  emergency room staff saw her within 5 minutes; performed an upper body ct scan and determined she had fluid in the pleural cavity and pneumonia in right lung.  over the eight day period she saw numerous consults; required a chest tube and numerous antibiotics to clear up a nasty blood infection.  happy to say she is home and well on the mend.  the doctors and nursing staff could not have been more professional and caring and were on top of her condition over the entirety of the stay.  her care could not have been better.  i highly recommend parker adventist hospital.

i just wanted to adjust my review. i was helped by heather and she was amazing. she looked in the system, figured it out for me and things are worked out on the er side. she was very understanding and even made sure to ask her manager if everything was correct. i'm waiting to see if the physician sends me anything. it would be weird seeing as though nothing happened w her. but we will cross that bridge when we get there. i'm just so happy that what i once thought was such an amazing hospital .. and then not... can now be amazing again!  thanks again heather!

i just under went hernia surgery at bi milton hospital.  the surgery was performed by dr. rahul gupta.  i was very happy with the excellent treatment i received at milton both before, during and after surgery.  dr. gupta is an outstanding physician, kind, caring and very "in tune" with the illness and needs of his patients. both dr. gupta, and his excellent staff of nurses, are to be highly recommended for their work, care and consideration during my stay at the hospital. i highly recommend this hospital, and dr. gupta. i thank you all for the great care. god bless you all in your work.
admissions is badly managed and abusive to this prospective patient.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Rock Hill

review: you're working your nurses to death.... they walk around looking so exhausted. you expect big ratios that work at big hospitals but don't give the nurses the auxiliary staff to even come close to achieving those feats while maintaining customer satisfaction.
the worst service i ever seen take 1 hour 22 minutes to write a prescription and release
i wish i could give no stars they said i can't see a doctor and they can give no help at all no questions. chose a more professional place to get a doctor.

my daughter was in this facility.  physical rehab, occupational therapy and speech therapy appeared to be very good. after a week it showed not much therapy was happening. 
 
the nurses ( most not all) lack empathy & caring skills.  not all seem to read charts or personal information. every shift has different ways to go about taking care of patients medication schedule.  a schedule is a schedule! 

my daughter was ignored having serious physical symptoms and i had to talk via facetime to the nurse since they were on pandemic lockdown.  i explained her symptoms that were a serious warning that something was seriously wrong!

after my being given a hard time by her nurse and being told "she knows her name and who the president is, "she's just fine"   well, she finally called the doctor on call. my daughter ended up in the hospital needing medical care immediately. 

if they would take the time to talk to the patients and get to know them, they would see something was very wrong!

the nurses lacked in the area comfort for my daughter.  like leaving the nurse call button, drinks,tv remote and bed controller within reach is important to those with physical limitations. most therapists get  it, the nurses do not.  

as for the nursing assistants, my daughter has some very thoughtful caring ones that she adores. they show patience ,brush her hair and tend to her needs, which can be a lot at times. then there are some that just don't want to be there and she feels like a burden when they walk in her room with a snarling face.

when my daughter was slipping out of her wheelchair, she had to have siri on her phone call me. not one person on that floor could hear her yelling for help! i had to call the reception desk! yes, she fell after the nurse arrived. pain meds took a bit after that.

i would not recommend this particular facility for rehab with patients that have memory issues and are unable to move their arms unless they are across from the nurses station!

after being home under my date my daughter made better progress.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of the Mid-Cities

review: horrible hospital. has treated me numerous times, every time was disrespectful & despicable. after my car accident, they thought i was just wanting pain medication. i was sent to another hospital & discovered i had fractured vertebrae as well as serious issues with my shoulder. another time i was taken there by ambulance, the nurse treating me told me that if i wasn't acting so dramatic, i would see that it's not a big deal.

i've given birth to both my girls here in 2007 and 2012 and will be giving birth here for the third and last time due in march. the nurses have always been helpful and kind however, after giving birth, i feel like they need to give us moms a break. this review is based on my 2012 experience. they come in just about every single hour for every little thing when you're trying to rest after being in labor and pushing for however many hours. i chose to breastfeed my kids but at one point with my second daughter, i asked for some formula so that my husband could help just so i could sleep a bit because baby didn't want to get off my boobs and cried the whole time if she wasn't on it and the nurse refused and kept telling me i had to keep her on the boob even after seeing how exhausted i was and crying. i find it so damaging mentally and emotionally to basically tell an overly exhausted mom that she pretty much cannot sleep because if baby wants to be on the boob 24/7 (regardless if you already nursed 15-20 mins every 3 hours) then she needs to just be on the boob 24/7, no formula. no pacifier. formula or breastfeeding should be a mother's choice, not something forced upon by the hospital! and if a mom who just went through labor asks for formula just to get 2-3 hours of sleep, then they should be able to grant that. my last hospital stay was overly draining and i plan on packing formula and bottles and a pacifier with this birth because i can't imagine having to endure 2 1/2 days of no sleep again and being told i can't do something


update: i would love to thank all the nurses who helped cared for myself and my son these past few days. i had an amazing experience with em all. can't remember everyone's name i encountered but to list who i can remember - giselle, stacey, brooke, erika, ana (so thankful for your extra kindness on my last day), anna, angie, maria, sally and a handful of others. 

to the awesome rn's i got the pleasure to have encountered in nicu - idonna, lina, kayla and dr. tan. and the two secretaries/receptionist in front; you guys are truly a god send. there aren't enough words and praises in this world to describe how amazingly badass you women are! especially idonna and kayla who i felt really wanted my son to get better quickly and went above and beyond while also having their hands full with other babies. thank you, thank you, thank youu from the bottom of my heart!!!

the only thing i would really want to inform other expecting moms is that memorial is big on breastfeeding. i went in for sure wanting to strictly breastfeed however going through what i did with my son - your baby truly does not get very much from colostrum which is what comes out the first 2 days. i pumped and literally only 2 to 3 veryy tiny little drops came out. this is why babies lose so much weight the first week because they push breastfeeding only. it should be mandatory to supplement with 1-2 oz of formula after breastfeeding!
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review:
i'm only giving this hospital 1 star because they made sure my son was happy. 

my kids and i were in an accident. because i refused treatment for myself, dr. wittenberg and social worker carole said i had an attitude. having panic attacks and them knowing i have anxiety, they did nothing to help ease my mental state. instead they threatened me with dcfs if i didn't admit my younger son (although he was cleared by the doctors in the er) and they kept me from my son who was injured in the accident, they kept me away from him for almost 3 hours! i was in shock, my ptsd was triggered, and i had just experienced a traumatic accident that totaled my car. no one in this ward asked if i was ok. they never tried to calm me down, instead they coerced me and filed a claim with dcfs causing further trauma! 

i do not recommend this hospital at all and if you can, go elsewhere.

review:
so disappointed. i came a few years ago and my son was seen by dr. jensen. he was amazing. 
now my new baby is sick and i drove over 45 minutes just to come here. i was seen by dr. jennifer lim. she seriously has no compassion or patience. she wouldn't even let me get out all of his symptoms before she cut me off. she said "ok sounds like everyone else in here".... like i don't care about everyone else!!!! she asks if he's been throwing up i said no. 
10 minutes later a nurse comes in with zofran to stop his nausea and vomiting. what?!??? i just told you he wasn't throwing up. 
i have not slept in over a week! i have been pounding my baby with medicine for a month (fever straight for 9 days) going through bottles of tylenol and motrin just this week alone. 
i ask her if it's something in my house because we're remodeling, she disregarded it. 
i told her my older son has asthma if this could be hereditary? she ignored me. 
he hasn't eaten in 36 hours now, asked if he should get an iv. she said no .. he's had diarrhea straight for over a week. 
my primary heard him 5 days ago, took his time, listened, and said he hears some wheezing in his chest. to keep an eye on it. 
the nurse heard wheezing. dr lim listens for 2 seconds and says nope don't hear anything that it's probably a virus. i asked if we could do xrays she said it's not necessary. i said i will not leave until xrays we're done. ).
stop rushing! realize that you may see this all the time. it as a mother seeing her child not sleep, eat, fever for days, at least act you care even though you clearly don't! 
.. they ended up taking xrays and my son had pneumonia in both lungs!!! 
i swear this woman was so inconsiderate and had absolutely no compassion!! i will never take my children here again! it's a children's hospital for gods sakes! we don't go to a regular hospital but we wants understanding people to take care of our babies! this was the worst experience ever. 
i left, went to little company of mary and he was admitted for a week. he is now doing much better no thanks to doctor lim

review: the charge nurse, karissa, in the emergency room is a horrible human. i was sent around and around from my pcp to urgent care and then the emergency room. no one could help and kept sending me to different departments. i even told her i had my infant with me driving around and around and begged her to help me. she was so unhelpful and slammed the phone down on me mid-sentence. i asked to speak to her supervisor and she wouldn't allow it.

review: delivered my first baby here at long beach memorial! my experience here with the nurses, doctors, and faculty members was one to remember. i enjoyed every second of my hospital experience and the care that was given to me by each individual at this hospital. with everything going on at this time, the last thing you want is unnecessary tension/anxiety. the nurses were the sweetest most caring people who made me feel at ease throughout my whole labor and after.

review: my daughter was recently born premature and was placed in the nicu. the doctor (dr. mcnolty) caring for my wife through the very rough pregnancy were phenomenal and extremely attentive. they monitored my wife's situation on a daily basis and when the time came that the womb was no longer a safe environment for my daughter they took the correct steps to begin and execute and flawless c-section. although my daughter was born early she was sent to the nicu dr. fritsell was assigned to her and has been hand down the best doctor i have ever worked with. thank you to all the nicu nurses caring for my daughter around the clock you truly are an amazing force.

review: it's been as almost 10 months and i can honestly say the doctors and nurses have been wonderful. we have had an issue or two, but if you make your concerns known to the staff they do try hard to make things right.

i had been experiencing an issue that began on a thursday afternoon, hadn't resolved by sunday morning, and seemed to be worsening. not wanting to wait another day for medical attention i went to the walk-in clinic at 10:00 a.m. on a  sunday, prepared to wait an hour or more in a crowded waiting area. but that was not the case at all. there was only one other patient checking in as i walked in. there were two receptionists so i did not have to wait. five minutes later i was escorted to an exam room and promptly seen by craig elsner, pa. i was nervous and a bit frightened. he was kind and compassionate and patiently explained to me what the likely cause of my symptoms were and his recommendation for treating them. i was probably there close to 1/2 hour and left with a prescription already submitted to the pharmacy and some notes about my condition and how to manage it. it was an exceptional walk-in clinic experience.
fac_name: Wenatchee Valley Hospital & Clinics - Confluence Health

review: during this time of emergency due to covid-19, i completely understand that the frontline is exhausted, overwhelmed, and frustrated.   i know this because i am on the frontline as a healthcare provider myself.  however, no matter what the situation presented to us, we are to be empathetic, compassionate and respectful to each patient that we treat.  i did not experience this from dr. mendoza or stacy, np (sp) during an e.r. visit with my daughter on march 22, 2020.  stacy was very dismissive, argumentative and continued to minimize my daughter's condition.  no matter what my daughter told her, the bottom line is that stacy was not actively listening.  because this was the second time within two days that my daughter had presented to the emergency room with these symptoms, this was an urgent situation for us.  who would go into an emergency room where there is a greater chance to be exposed to corona if it wasn't an emergency? in my experience, a patient knows their body and how they feel and we as healthcare workers should listen and not dismiss what they are saying.  we are not always right and don't have the right to tell a patient how they feel.  stacy comes in to discharge my daughter after barely assessing her a few hours before.  there was no end result except to go home.  no.  the problem has not been resolved.  the reason why we are back here a second time is because of the dismissive attitude  presented before.  apparently there is something seriously wrong.  i asked to speak to the charge nurse but somehow dr. mendoza, who never treated my daughter at all, found her way into the room.  she, just like stacy, refused to listen to our concerns and basically in a nutshell told us that they would not be doing anything for my daughter and for her to go home and 'stick it out'.  for hippa related issues, i won't go into detail my daughter's condition but it involves constant vomiting, diarrhea and severe stomach pain.  she cannot even keep down water.  severe dehydration is an overwhelming threat at this point.  dehydration leads to other medical conditions like heart problems or kidney failure.  because i have a healthcare background and know that there is a standard that should be met when taking care of people, my mind is completely blown by the behaviors of these two healthcare providers.  again, i understand the stress that we are all under but at the end of it all, when you are present with a patient, be present and actually be of help and not hinder an already stressful situation.  i have had pretty good experiences at south sub before so i am extremely disappointed and will be requesting that if myself or any family member is in the e.r. again, that these two not be in charge of our care.  they need sensitivity and active listening training asap.  if something worsens with my daughter's condition because of their insensitivity and dismissals, there will be legal action taken.

with the scare of covid19, i called the covid hotline and explained my symptoms to the nurse on the phones. she instructed me to go on to the er to be seen and possibly tested. i went to this hospital because they did amazing when my mom was transferred there after having 3 heart attacks. 
when i got there, everyone was confused and a little irritated that they didn't know what all was going on. this didn't bother me at all because i know it's a very scary time to be a nurse or dr right now. this covid19 is new and the rules keep changing. i appreciated everyone's demeanor and positivity. everyone. from the ladies at the screening desk, to the triage nurse, all the way back to the nurses elise and anne (i think were their names). i got taken back to a special area where they were screening for covid19. it was a little scary because they were wearing plastic robes over their clothes... 
elise was the nurse that took care of me and she was so amazing. super sweet, and did a good job of keeping my mind off feeling miserable. these doctors and nurses are working their butts off. i mean, elise had to write my info down on a paper towel bc they didn't have all the supplies that needed. everyone i saw was working double time, and staying positive for the patients. i could over hear conversations from my virtual bed, and they don't have it easy at all. please keep this in mind when you see a a nurse or doctor and they look worn out. they've for sure earned a gold medal during this time. i wasn't able to be tested bc i didn't meet criteria. but i still have to quarantine for 14 days. thank you, seton, for trying your best to stay ahead of this virus going around.

my father was recently a frequent patient here as he neared the end of his life with several health complications.  the entire staff was incredibly kind, caring, sensitive, and patient focused.  ellen in the er was especially great.  no emergency room/hospital visit is a good thing but the good people here make it as pleasant as it can possibly be.  i hope and pray for all the good people here to help get us through this covid19 mess.

i was admitted to ascension seton on 38th street on wednesday, june 10, 2020, with an infection which triggered a multiple sclerosis flare up.  i am on the 5th floor, being cared for by the nurses and clinical assistants from the 5th floor nurses' station south.  they are amazing. even in these dangerous times, with half the hallway reserved for covid19 patients, nurses and clinical assistants have shown me unparalleled amounts of compassion, kindness, understanding and concern.  even at end of shift, their attitude, never changes.  they remain patient, kind, caring. these nurses and clinical assistants are true heroes, flesh and blood angels. i pray that god showers each and every one of them and their loved ones with an abundance of blessings, good fortune, excellent health and a long life. i pray that god looks after each of them and their loved ones and keeps them safe. i wish i could do more to express my gratitude and appreciation.  i am humbled by their grace and generosity.

i hope you don't have to recover at this hospital after a major surgery!!!

the surgeon and physical therapist were fine. the one star is for the doctor overseeing her case and the nursing staff. my sister had a complete knee replacement, and due to covid, i was not allowed to visit her and be her advocate. 

she was not given her pain meds at the correct times so she would be in excruciating pain with no relief. she was never able to stay ahead of the pain. she was made to feel like a drug addict for asking for the pain meds she was allowed to have. one nurse was not even able to help my sister test her blood sugar because she could not manage to get the blood strip to my sister's finger.

the doctor did not seem to understand anything about my sister's type one diabetes and how to deal with her high blood sugar. the doctor also misread the chart and told the nurse to give my sister potassium. her potassium levels were fine, she was wrongly given potassium when she did not need it. 

i'm not sure if it's incompetence, not enough staff, or just laziness- most likely all of the above.

this is the worst hospital ever for medical bills! they owed my daughter over $300 for three months. thank goodness for the time off because she's had time to talk on the phone or hold on the phone for hours and hours. do you not give you them your money until you know you owe it to them. if she owed them money of this sorts they would send bill collectors out for her. this all started to before the virus and it is a matter of money not the hospital. thank you to all the front line workers! the billing department should be ashamed of themselves or get someone in there that doesn't lie!!! sad
patrick with eurology can go suck one. what a pompous prick.

in these days of heightened awareness of inequality, ihc (the organization) is a staunch holdout for good old fashioned bigotry.  i'm sure it's fine if you are straight, white, cis gender, etc.  anyone else, you'd be crazy to go there. heaven forbid you are gay or black or anything outside of their mold. although they are no longer owned by the church, they are very much part of it (even the lawfirm they use is the church's law firm), with all the judgment and hypocrisy that entails.  sure, there are some good people but overall they are bullies, the proverbial 800 lb gorilla.  and for being a "non profit", boy are they into taking your money.  if you ask providers outside of their network, they will tell you ihc is the worst organization they work with, greedy and hypocritical.

#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!
