thankful for the ppe we are provided here! we have had everything we need to stay protected during the critical time.

i was here overnight after surgery. i was told my daughter could be there during my pre op until they took me to surgery. they did not allow her back and actually had my family go home. the doctor came out to talk to my family and was not told they were not allowed to stay. everything went well until i was taken to my room. i was ignored. the iv machine beeped for 20 minutes. i could not get anyone to come help. i finally pushed every button till it was turned off. i was told i needed to walk to go home that day. no one came to help me.  i begged the nurses to help me get up to walk but no one came. i had to spend the night when i could have gone home. the nurses only came if i needed meds or to take my vitals. another patient screamed all evening and i was told by my nurses they were looking after her. i was ignored because she was screaming. if my family could have been there i could have gotten something to drink or gone to the bathroom. if you will not let families stay because of covid-19 then nurses need to pay attention to their patients. i owe more money because i had to stay the night when i wanted to go home.

my best friend had a heart attack and spent a week in the ccu, i have unfortunately been to many atlanta icu's and regular units over the last 5 years because of elderly parents, while 99% of nurses were great, cameron at wellstar was truly unbelievably good. i have never seen someone so caring, and in such a way that made myself and family feel so much better in an otherwise terrifying situation! if it we're my choice i would intrust my life and well being with her before anyone else, and knowing her manor with family makes a patient so much more at ease! i truly wish there was more i could say or do to thank this wonderful person! -joey griffin

not sure where to start.  my wife was brought here by emergency vehicle after a bad fall in september 2019.  we received adequate care overall, but had big concerns including a missed broken wrist that they failed to x-ray, pumping her full of opiates instead of the nerve block they did in previous surgeries with anesthesiologists lying about the sequence of events, and now bills for services 7 months ago, after being given a final balance due and setting up a payment plan.  

dr. reddy was the lone bright spot here, as his reconstruction of her face was flawless.  it seems like he will have a lot of work to do to fix this place.  the daily staff on the floors was very caring and helpful.  hospital administrators, some doctors, and some surgeons left a lot to be desired.  

thankfully, after good care at home at osu surgery centers and local pt/ot practices, she has made much progress to overcome the lackadaisical "care" offered at wellstone, and is mostly on the road to recovery.

wow,  i've never had such a fantastic er experience.  my daughter came home from school early with a fever.  i gave her motrin before bed and thought she'd sleep it off. to my surprise,  she woke up at 11pm screaming with a fever of 104.5. i quickly looked for the closest er on yelp and headed out. this er was more than i could've ever hoped for! they got us in right away and took great care of my daughter.  that even dubbed her the "cutest patient of the night". it was great start to finish.  thanks to all who helped our family in our time of need!!

i arrived in the morning because a family member was having surgery. 12 pm rolls around and i need something to eat (diabetic),so i go to the cafeteria and order a spring mix salad with chicken. after i receive about 5 ounces of salad and chicken, i asked if they had dressing or do i get it myself. it was already on the salad and not diabetic friendly. i was offered a salad with lettuce and fruit instead. no thanks,  i don't want the sugar from the fruit.  i don't expect to be catered to, but for a cafeteria in a hospital? it would be easy enough to put dressing on the side for a tiny five dollar salad, i'm sure. they sure have plenty of starchy garbage though. i paid for the salad and threw it away. it's not like they could serve it to anyone else. if you eat there, ask about everything before you buy. i didn't want to hold up the line.
switched over from northside to kennestone for my 2nd child. so far i love the obgyn staff, the hospital, everything has been a much better experience overall.

i was admitted to kennestone after having major surgery. the  day nurse assigned to me was lacking on basic knowledge she did not know how to turn the lights on or off at the bed  she told me it could only be done by the nurse at the wall switch. she did not know how to unhook the compression device on my legs she constantly asked her tech how to do everything  i was very uncomfortable since she was administering all of my pain medicine. that evening the night nurse was awesome she checked on me numerous times and showed a special interest. then the day nurse returned it was not the same individual but this nurse was worse. she never came to check on me unless she had to take stats. after the doctor came by i was ready to go home when my oxygen level reached 90 or above that was around 8:30 my level went passed 90 and i was ready to go. the day nurse told me she would have to get the iv team to take my iv out i waited until noon and no one came. then the nurse told me the doctor had not signed the release and would have to wait on him  after another two hours i inquired about the doctor she said he was a surgeon and probably in surgery she could not bother him   after several hours i was still there she then told me i would have to pass the breathing test again at that point all i could do was cry. i had no cell phone or anyone to help me i felt like a prisoner with no options. it wasn't until my husband contacted the doctor that everything changed suddenly the release papers were signed the nurse took out the iv (the iv team never came) and i was ready to go  that is when i saw the tech for the second time since that morning not once did anyone check on me or try to help me with my problem. the next day i called and placed a complaint. that was over a week ago and i have heard nothing. it was after 5 before i left

dr pardo in er was great. dr mastromichallis was outstanding. 
sam, kim, amber, and esther were excellent nurses on the 5th floor. 
dj in the kitchen was so thoughtful and nice.

terrible staff communication. i am out of state. my sister is in the icu, i am listed in the hospital chart as one who can be given her health information but because the primary next of kin. her son, is unavailable i cannot get a pass word from him that enables me to get this information, information that i am entitled to!

the manager of the icu flatly refused to give me any help except telling me to contact the unavailable son! 

and my sister is lying in the icu critically ill!!

terrible, terrible insensitivity!

i typically avoid the er at all costs but having kids there have been a number of times we have had to go to various ers over the years. 

this time i was by myself during the summer of covid and went to loma linda feeling rather anxious having to be alone and in so much pain. 
i was quickly evaluated, treated, and cared for. 

i wanted to write a review because i feel that i was treated with such dignity and exceptional care. 
my provider was rick oldenburg and my nurses were carrie and alexis. 

all three of them had plenty of patients but from what i saw they made each of us feel comfortable and did their jobs with a smile. i can only imagine how difficult these last months have been on healthcare workers yet here they are showing up for us in all the ways! bravo to llmmcer staff! thank you for your bedside manner in a sensitive time when as patients we don't have someone to hold our hand- it really means a lot!

brought my husband in tonight around 6:30 because he had a swollen gland in his neck and complained of lethargy.  he doesn't have a fever or any other covid related symptoms but yes let's jump to that conclusion.

i've been waiting in the car in the parking lot since he checked in....it's now 10:35 and i'm still waiting.  an hour ago he's was waiting to be discharged. 

good heavens how effing long does it take to discharge someone? 

this hospital is a joke.

just had my second surgery in a year at loma linda in murrieta. the 1st was a neck fusion in april 2019. all went well. attention to patient care was above average. i needed regular pain management and the wonderful nurses saw to it i was medicated within minutes of requesting it. all went well.

now less than year later, the downhill slide in patient care was startling.  it took 30 to 45 minutes to get taken care of with pain meds. i had rotator cuff surgery, and was kept in the hospital for 3 nights to qualify for skilled nursing facility per medicare. i thighs the nurses at ll hospital were fine. but very understaffed and over worked. i would not go to loma linda in murrieta again if another surgery is, unfortunately necessary. i hope they change. soon.

this is the best care i have had since moving to this area !
i can not believe how mindful the staff is about cleaning and keeping patients safe. they are professional and went above and beyond !
i have 4 kids and we are always at the er! this is my go to hospital!! we are always in and out of there. the staff is so nice and helpful!! we have never had a bad experience.

the operator at the nurses station on the fourth floor her name is stephanie is extremely rude and very unprofessional. this woman was very aggressive and not willing to help with providing basic information, the information i was requesting was not in anyway violation of phi or a hippa breach. there should be some type of standard of communication and respect that must be maintained.

in the er with a friend for her gall bladder. the 2 front desk ladies who were working in the er on 1/30/20 from the hours of 6:30pm on were absolute monsters. they were belittling people who were asking about being called back, they continuously rolled their eyes at everyone who came to the desk, they sat with their feet up and talked about other people. rude doesn't even describe it. they never checked on anyone to ask if they were ok. they gave out paperwork to  a woman in a wheelchair and never asked if she needed help getting it back to the desk. their attitudes are not helpful and they don't know anything about customer service. the saving grace was the nurse who was taking vitals at the front. she took all of the patients aside and helped them independently of the desk. it sucks that she had to intervene and smooth things over with every single person but if it weren't for her nothing would have been done. thanks mystery nurse!

er isn't the best sometimes because the wait time is longer than usual just because it is a small hospital i'd assume they don't have much stuff/room to see so many patients at once. i've had to wait up to 30/45 minutes before. aside from er i will say that this hospital has one of the best labor & delivery departments i've ever seen. coming from someone who has worked in a few hospitals before. the staff is amazing as well. my obgyn delivers here and i was skeptical my whole pregnancy about giving birth here honestly. i was googling and looking into larger hospitals like uchealth hospital in aurora or good samaritan in lafayette and i'm glad i didn't end up going to those hospitals.  i just gave birth recently (march 18,2020) and i have zero regrets choosing this hospital to deliver at. from the moment i went in to be checked if my water really had broken at home to the time i got discharged with my newborn. i had to stay a few extra days due to random blood pressure issues i hadn't had before on my end and every nurse and doctor i met with/came into my room answered every question i had whether it was regarding me or the baby. i highly recommend this labor and delivery department if you're looking around where to give birth and if you're skeptical as i am i hope you'd take my word for it!

i had emergency surgery after a tubal pregnancy ruptured my.fallopian tube and ovary. although the response intially was slow, as soon as things became very emergent, they did not mess around. i was admitted and taken inro surgery one hour after my intial triage amd er admission. the gynecologist on call was amazing. she saved my life. the nurses and doctors were attentive and i recieved immediate pain relief before surgery and pain was manahed beautifully after. i was pushy anout beinf discharged post surgery and they did allow me to go home soonwe than probably normal but staying would not have been an issue. the after care i recieved was exceptional. i see a lotnof bad reviews for this er however, they acted quickly with my emergency and i will assume that those who had to wait forever probably either werent that sick or could have gone to urgent care. drug seekers clog the ers and actual emergencies are delayed because of it.

make sure they actually treat what you come in for before checking in!!
this could be a 5 star as the facility and staff have been fabulous, but they need to be more open about what they treat when you check in. when i took my 10 year old here for symptoms of appendicitis, we went through triage and several hours later had a verified diagnosis, but then we were informed that their surgeon on duty doesn't operate on children. we were told we had to take an ambulance to another hospital (or be discharged against medical advice meaning they wouldn't be able to transfer records to them and we would start the entire process over, with 2 hospital triage bills). this costs us lots of extra time and money, and appears to be a fairly common problem at this hospital from the other reviews. it's completely unfair to the patients.

on the other hand, i have given birth twice at this hospital and really appreciated the accommodations and staff. the food is great, but my favorite part is that they monitor when you are sleeping and come in to do vitals and check ups based on when you are awake- thank you for giving new moms the chance to rest! this is definitely a good place to have a baby (from a mother who has had 9 in 5 difference hospitals).
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review: i went in for covid-19 testing and was treated like pure scum of the earth. the nurse "jim" drilled me and asked why i was out so early getting a covid-19 test and why did i come to the er and not call my doctor? i told them that i had shortness of breath and i keep having the chills. i work in a warehouse that has had numerous cases of covid-19 over the last few weeks and it's possible that i was exposed. i was then advised that because i did not have a fever that i didn't have it. i was also advised that because i was not falling on the floor from shortness of breath that my shortness of breath was not serious. i then grew angry from the way the nurse was talking to me and left without testing. he would not even give me his name when i asked for it. not trying to make this a race thing, but studies show that when people of color visit the doctor our symptoms are often downplayed because we're not supposed to feel pain or that we're not truthful. the two clerks also told me that they didn't know the nurse's name that was giving me the hard time. how do you work with an extremely small group of people and not know your colleagues name?  i will be contacting the hospital later on today to speak with a supervisor.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review: update: mar 30: there has been no response nor any update from baylor frisco to this. i put in all information to the link they replied back with. i now have to deal with payments to their er, the doctor and the ambulance service - all separate payments that is over couple of grand, for nothing really. they could have just send me to baylor plano right away and i'd be impressed with the honesty. instead, i have a bad taste in the mouth, and a hole in the pocket. deceptive practices!
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Medical Center - Frisco

review:
i had the fortunate opportunity to be a patient here at the end of february, 2020. yes, right before all elective surgeries were cancelled due to the corona virus, or covid-19. the staff was absolutely wonderful! check in was easy, as you go up to the 2nd floor, and the check in desk is right there by the elevators, you can't miss it. the waiting room is comfortable, with nice seating, and plenty of it. there are tables there for your use as well. free coffee and tea too.

they have a nice system in place, where there are rooms that you are taken to, once surgery/procedure is done, and your family/friends talk to the doctor/surgeon about how things went. this is done in private. there is also a board where your family/friends can watch the progress of your surgery/procedure as well, all by the number assigned to you when you check in.

the hospital is big, very big. it's clean too. there is a nice cafeteria, and a daz boggs as well. there is a gift shop on the first floor, and a baby joe's gift shop, if i remember correctly, on the 4th floor as well.

parking is easy too. there are several garages with free parking. or, use the valet service, which is right there by the front door. 

the staff is wonderful, as well as all volunteers, and basically, everyone. 

my stay at the hospital was a good one. i was always in good hands. i never needed anything either. the room was comfortable, and i had it to myself, i didn't have to share it with anyone. the food was good too.

if i ever have to have surgery again, i wouldn't hesitate when told that the surgery would be at st. joseph hospital. thanks for the excellent care!

this is specifically about the er. i went in for having covid symptoms that were irritating my asthma. they basically took me back to a room and scolded me for being there. the doc even admitted how shaky the test is. they didn't listen to my breathing or anything. i went home and had an asthma attack but was too scared to go back and face rejection and humiliation again. eventually went back and was hospitalized for covid. hospitalization was better than er but the er needs to rethink their priorities. this is a pandemic with a deadly virus and inaccurate test, treat all your patients with respect and listen to their symptoms, not their false negative. future hospitalization could have been avoided if you cared the first time.

by far the worst hospital experiences in my life. and i've lived all over the country. i recently went to the er with severe back pain, was told to sit on an stretcher that was in the middle of the hallway, which i complained about due to the pain, but it didn't matter. i was not administered any pain meds for what i was suffering from, was not even seen by a doctor, was taken for x-rays on the stretcher that i was very uncomfortable on and told i couldn't walk there even though it was far more comfortable to walk, which shows they don't care if you're in pain, was given prescriptions and told good luck and never given a diagnosis. then there are the coding issues. every damn time i've had to go to this poor excuse for a hospital, they have incorrectly billed me due to coding "errors", which i believe aren't errors at all, but rather they're trying to con and milk me out of as much money as possible, and have had to contest my bill every single time. i have never seen a more dysfunctional, mismanaged medical facility. the staff is very unprofessional, incompetent, and i recommend that nobody goes here. putting "northwestern medicine" in the name doesn't make it any better. it's still the same ole shitty kishwaukee hospital. if you can, please go to delnor in geneva. you'll thank me.

i was in a car accident , went there and they can't seem to send my company insurance a correct bill. the adjuster is willing to write a check he just needs proper paper work which they said they can't find because they move . they just don't want to do there job and now it's on my credit because they can't do there job correctly ! they are lazy , horrible at there job and just don't care about who they screw . i will never set foot in a mercy hospital ever again !!! horrible service !

i can't say enough good things about this facility and staff! everyone did their best to make my sisters stay here as pleasant as possible.  my sister had a stroke and i saw her make improvements no one thought possible thanks to a very professional, competent and enthusiastic team of drs, nurses, therapists and case workers.  i would wholeheartedly recommend this facility as would my sister, who was a patient here.  she will definitely be back as an outpatient to continue the excellent therapy she received at encompass.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Scottsdale

review: my husband had to go to the er because he had severe abdominal pain. turned out he needed his gallbladder removed  due to having several gallstones and constantly having gallbladder attacks. he went in on sunday and got discharged on thursday. as we all know,  nobody wants to be in the hospital,  but let me tell you what.  all the medical staff were extremely friendly and caring. they all went above and beyond for the care of my husband. especially halit! the surgery team did amazing too! answering all if our questions and checking to see how my husband was doing.  even the dietary and patient techs were incredible! thank you to everyone who helped care for my husband,  it really helps when you have amazing nurses and medical staff!

this hospital is extremely under staffed. we took our family member here during the covid 19 crisis and there was example after example of a barely functional hospital staff on duty here. the communication between departments was atrocious. the dietary staff never asked about food allergies, and simply brought the meal of the day to include  unripe fruit. prescriptions were not sent to our pharmacy. these were just some of the things that we experienced. 

it seems like the hospital is understaffed and the small logistical issues are being forgotten or brushed aside. 

as far as medical care. we were satisfied with the medical care and experience of the surgical staff.

in the future, we will be driving the extra 20 minutes to a different hospital.

my girlfriend had a total hip replacement done over this weekend. operation and overall recovery has been good. care from the nursing staff has been excellent so far. we had one issue with a dr that had poor bedside manner and that has gone to patient advocacy. not a lot of specialist on the staff here though so don't expect it. facility is clean if not just a little dated. had issues with the bed not functioning properly and a cantankerous serving tray. overall i would recommend opmc for the basics but consider it a gateway only for more serious medical issues. so if you fall into that category there are better options. "small town hospital" sums it up from my perspective.

i'm only writing this because when i sent my child here i had second thoughts after reading the reviews. there are many horrible reviews, and my heart goes out to those children and their parents if those reviews concerns were genuine. my experience was although not as beneficial to my child as i would have hoped, the physicians and staff were very professional in our interactions except for one time, and they did not try to keep my child to "milk" all they could out of my insurance. my child is home where she needs to be as directed by their psychiatrist, and we are moving forward with the guidance of del amo to help my child in the out-patient setting.

back again, lol.... ugh. just shut this place down already... do not come here! do not even call this horrid place!!!

the goal for uhs facilities is to hospitalize as many patients as possible and keep them locked away for as long as possible to make a profit. people who werent a danger to themselves or others were brought to the hospitals under false pretenses that they would be evaluated and diagnosed, not locked away and fed a mind-numbing amount of meds. 

please check out this 2019 article about how uhs (the company owning this "health" center) agreed too a $127 million dollar settlement to the department of justice. uhs hospitals (like del amo) upcoded the condition of their patients so insurance companies would unknowingly reimburse the hospitals with excess money. in other words, del amo falsified records so they could profit off of the patients. 

https://medcitynews.com/2019/07/uhs-agrees-to-127m-doj-to-settle-behavioral-health-investigation/

uhs continues to profit hundreds of millions of dollars a year. absolutely f''king evil.

when my family member was transferred here 8 days ago my heart sank when i saw the reviews, but i vowed to keep an open mind. 8 days later, i have not been able to get a doctor to call me once. there are 3 patient phones in the unit but 2 of them are broken. no visiting at all due to covid19.  nice nurses did get my relative on the phone twice, after i kept calling, and my relative told me he had given permission for the doctors to talk to me. and still no
calls.  what kind of quack doesn't talk to family members who have information about a patient's history?   the people whose loved ones have landed in this place need to get together & press for action.  maybe media attention would be useful here?  local press might be interested in a story about substandard mental health care provided during this time of crisis.

my 18 year old son was put in del amo hospital. communication with the family is very poor even with a release. he saw the psychiatrist for less than 10 minutes everyday. very old facility. we saw rats just outside the front door. if you have any other choice , go there.
my son is now 20 and still having mental health issues. i would never put him at del amo. they charge my insurance thousands for being there .
the doctor talked to him less than 10 minutes a day and charged for a full session which is fraud.
someone should sue and shut this place down!!

can't even get thru a phone call to get information on my son he's been there 3 days and no one has called me to give me any kind of information. they were just quick to call me and ask me for my insurance info.

i am a licensed therapist - lcsw, phd. i had to initiate a 5150 hold on a 12 yr old boy last wed. as a professional with 40 years experience, i have to say that del amo demonstrated a remarkable degree of incompetence, lack of professionalism and caring for my patient and his family. i have worked in several large medical centers and psychiatric hospitals during my long career and i have never written a scathing letter about a facility to anyone. rest assured, del amo, its owners and administrators and state licensing will be hearing from me. this place is a prime example of the disastrous state  of the mental health care in this  country.

0 stars. incredibly disorganized and awful. no follow up calls from doctors or social workers; the nurses station says they leave my number for the dr./social worker to call me, back but that's hard to believe as no one ever calls back and it seems that each nurse who answers the phone doesn't look at the record of my loved one and the calls and notes i've been leaving. incredibly rude staff (minus maybe 2 helpful employees) who think that patients/families should already know the ins and outs of the system, so they are very snappy on the phone and try to rush you off. i wasn't even notified when he was switched to a different department. i understand that you are busy and stressed, but i deserve respect and straightforward answers regarding my loved one's wellbeing. he is being held here against his will and he did not commit a crime. he is no longer having any mental/behavioral symptoms and needs to be released immediately. his notice of certification from the state of ca health of human services agency has incorrect information. he has a home and he and i have given his address multiple times, but apparently, the itu thinks he's homeless and did not put that information on his notice of certification. additionally, he never received this notice of certification until he asked for it today, which is 6 days after the notice was signed by staff. absurd. during his hearing, he had a patient rights advocate named debbie who didn't even speak to him before the hearing. additionally, she called me before the hearing, and cornered me into saying an answer that i didn't want to give. i repeatedly told her i was confused and to please explain what she was asking and why, but as soon as she got the "answer" she wanted to hear, she ended the conversation. i tried getting a call back from her and the patients rights office to no avail. no one told him that the hearing was happening until they brought him to it. this certification was falsely signed off by doctors/staff as jonathan never received any of this information regarding the certification or his hearing. i have left messages on their contact form (http://delamohospital.com/contact-us) but no one is helping. this is wrong. my loved one is being held here against his will without any serious mental illness symptoms and he needs to come home and back to his job, family, etc. he has always had a self care plan in place but this place refuses to listen to him or me. there are so many more nightmarish things going on that will eventually be heard through a lawsuit.

very grateful new mommy, the experience i had was exceptional and positive. i want to recognize rn jojo, elisa, ginger dr. purdom and all the wonderful ladies in labor and delivery that took so good care of me and my little one. they went above and beyond to make us feel safe secure and in very good hands.  having a baby is a life changing experience! the one provided to me definitely deserved to be commended  not only for their professionalism in which they took care of us, also highlighting the warm genuine sweet friendly manner of true care for their work. ladies from postpartum carlene cindy.

from the bottom of my heart  thank you

i had surgery the other day and just am so impressed by all the staff at this hospital. from the front door employee to admitting, to lab, to surgery you all were just amazing. being there alone was so difficult because the no visitor policy due to covid, however you all made it a little less stressful for me. dana my pre op nurse you are an absolute gem!! thank you for talking with me and helping me through my nervousness!! thank you to the entire surgery staff for making me laugh and keeping things real but light!! i can't tell you what a difference it makes to have people around you make you feel comfortable in such a scary place! thank you from the bottom of my heart!!

i don't care what the bad review says, i love this hospital.  both of my kids were delivered here, 99% of the nurses here are super nice and super helpful.  my grandparents have stayed here during their surgeries and recoveries as well.  i literally have nothing bad to say about this place.  heart to all the doctors, nurses and staff during this corona virus crisis!  bless you all.

i was seen in the ed this last monday for severe back pain. i was taken immediately to a room by jordan castro who was very caring and empathetic of my pain. i was very shortly seen by a pa named james. he was very kind and listened to my concerns. within minutes i was provided with morphine, zofran and prednisone. i was sent home within 30 minutes with a prescription for prednisone and pain medication. it is now wednesday and i have not felt better. i will always come to whmc for my medical needs. you are all the best. 

lori chaves

my husband had an unfortunate fall last week and completely separated the ac joint in his shoulder. during these unprecedented times with covid19 going around we didn't want to have to pay the er a visit but when i saw his shoulder deformed and him in severe pain, we had no choice but too. we had to bring my 2 year old son because i have no child care. as soon as we arrived there was a nurse who screened us and checked us for a fever. we felt very safe. our nurse joseph put us at ease, started my husband's iv. the doctor came and ordered a ct and examined him. joseph splint his shoulder and was very patient and took care in making sure not to cause my husband any unnecessary pain. we were in very good hands. the clinical manager sara made her rounds and made sure my son and i were okay. we had a very pleasant experience with each person we interacted with including the radiology techs, admitting clerk. i just want to express our gratitude and appreciation for the excellent care and service.

just want to say how kind and wonderful everyone has been to my mother. she was sent to er, i arrived shortly after.  diana sun greeted me at the waiting area.  after explaining our special circumstances, she allowed me to go in and sit with my mother while she was being attended to in er.  i am truely gratiful for ms sun's sympathy and kindess, especially during this difficult time. i am grateful for all the staff members. thank you all for every thing you are doing and all the wonderful care you are giving my mom.  bless you all.

back on 9-1-2019 i had a really bad stomach flu.  i went into the er, and the overall experience was great.  in november i got my co pay paid and doctor seiler sent me a bill that my medical would pay.  the last statement was sent in december.  now in may, the hospital is sending me a new bill for the same doctor stating that my medical didn't cover the doctors visit.  so i call my medical care company...and they told me that the hospital didn't bill them till april 23, 2020 and they only had 60 days to submit billing to them and that is why the payment was denied.  now the hospital is expecting me to pay.  apparently someone didn't do their job in the billing department and i'm now having to pay for it.  not cool!  keep an eye on your bills with this hospital.  they are dysfunctional and for such a small hospital.

having a lifetime disease, i have been to many hospitals,  and this is by far the best experience i have ever had. 
even with covid 19 in full force, i was treated like the only patient there. not a single rude employee. i was a person, not a #. in and out in under 5 hours through the er. 
kudos to the entire team. you made a stressful situation just a bit better for me. 
thank you.

i am currently a patient and have been frequently for the last 60 days. i have estimated i have spent 11 out of 50 days at sharp grossmont. the very first admission was at the end of april. i was rushed off from er who said i would be admitted. 2 women dressed like hazmat officials started poking, prodding, and pushing and pulling. the general dr. walked and told these two woman to stop i was not positive for covid and no patient deserves that treatment. i was crying because nothing that was ailing me had been addressed.  the following day i had my first of 4 surgerys. the nurses at sharp are wonderful and so sweet. unfortunately i had a fistula grow and returned a week later. this time i received a new surgeon who has a poor bedside manner. he rushed to get me home and although i was assigned home health they never came so that was a fiasco which had me back 4 days later for a 3rd surgery which i could tell wasnt right. however, i did recieve after care and that was awesome. but not awesome enough 6 days later i woke in a pool of blood and pus and was definitely pissed. i wasnt surprised when they announced yet another surgery in which he would...... im not sure what he did i had google it to find out. it to date has been the most painful thing i have ever endured. here is my ratings
1-5 5 being the best
nurses in er and on the floor. 5

on may 28th, 2020, i went to the er experiencing extreme pain. 

i arrived at the er at approximately 3pm. i was checked in and vitals were taken, blood pressure check, temp check, brief interview, blood work done, and paid $400.00 copay. all this happened fairly quickly.

afterwards, i was sent back to the waiting room to wait for an available dr to see me, without being given any pain meds.

approximately 2 1/2 hours later, i'm still sitting in the lobby waiting to be seen or at the very least given a pain medication. 

at that time, i went to the nurse at the check-in, informed her that i was in a great deal of pain, and requested a refund of my copay, since i had not been seen by a dr, so i could go home and lay down and address my escalating pain.

the nurse told me that she could not give me a refund but politely asked if i could wait just a few more minutes to be seen. against my better judgement, i agreed. 

approximately 2 hours later, nothing had changed. i had not been seen or administered any medication to address the escalating pain.

i again approached the same nurse, again requested a refund, so that i could return home, lay down and address my increasing pain.

i was again told they could not give me a refund of my $400.00 .

she again, told me they don't give refunds. she went on to say i could go home but i would not be getting a refund of my $400.00 copay. she added  they don't collect the copay until after services are rendered. i then presented her with my receipt of payment. she then gave me a business card and told me i need to contact billing and dispute the charge!
overtaking by pain, anger, and disappointment i left.
approximately 4 hours in the er, without treatment or any type of pain relief, for the price of $400.00.

this is not the way to run a er or any service oriented business.

i am extremely disappointed in grossmont hospital and will never return for any reason.

i suggest all consumers and future patients go elsewhere for your medical needs.

i am writing this review for a nurse named sahar on 5 west! yesterday morning my grandma was taken to the hospital by ambulance. she was very out of it, delirious, and does not speak any english. my worst fear is that she would be alone and confused and misunderstood. given the current situation right now i understand that we can not have any family members with her at the time. the thought of not knowing where she is and if she if okay was terrifying to my family and i. we followed the ambulance and were told me could give our information to someone outside and they would call us with any information. i do not want to get into my experience with the man outside because it was terrible. the man had no compassion for our situation and told my aunt not to bother explaining. we just wanted to make sure a translator could talk to us since she was so out of it. anyways this is not about him. we waited in the parking lot for a few hour waiting by our phones to hear any information and decided to leave. i was up all night thinking about how my grandma was alone and if she was confused and scared. i woke up this morning to the best news that my grandma was okay. i heard she was even singing to the nurses! this made my heart so happy. to have a language barrier and still bring someone this much comfort and joy is very special and i just really wanted to say thank you! i sent flowers as a thank you from my family and i, and i really hope they get to you! i know right now especially is an extremely stressful time to be working in the medical field and your commitment to making your patients feel special is not going unnoticed! god bless you and thank you so much for taking care of the most important person in my life!

i was in the hospital for 20 days! i've never experienced so much trauma and distress in my whole life. when i say this i don't blame my doctors and a few nurses. complaint 1: i was introduced a new nurse every 12 hours. usually at 7am and 7pm. each rotation the debrief the new nurse about the patient. i want to say within all nurses i've seen about 4 were amazing! they knew their stuff, did their homework on me and came to me knowing everything i've undergone through, dates, test results in hand just in case i've asked, how long i've been there, why, when and how. the others asked how long have you been here, what's your condition, just stupid simple questions when my records are easily displayed. 
complaint 2: around day 17, at this point i haven't seen my children since my admission. due to flue season i completely understood. a charge nurse notice how depressed i was and set up a time and date for me to be rolled downstairs to the lobby for a quick visit. i was excited! it was written on my whiteboard. i reminded every nurse i had just so everyone was onboard. the day came, kids were in the lobby waiting and nobody knew what i was talking about. it was not possible they said. after talking to the new charge nurse, many nurses and my attendant physician with tears in my eyes begging them to let me see my kids i got to see them. my kids waited 3 hours for me to come down for a 15 visit. 
complaint 3: my attendant physician dr elias sucked! he only came to see me a few times and every time he came in was to talk about my insurance (medical) and to be transferred to ucsd. i would here him in the hallways yell at other patients about insurance as well. and about their personal stuff. i quote "you hadn't shit in 4 days, you need to shit". 
complaint 4: one day i was out of my room showering. it was around 12 pm. that's was normal for me. when i came back to my room, my cell phone and flushable wipes were stolen straight out of my room! they checked everywhere. i kept calling my phone and a low voiced male answered once and never did again. someone came in my room and still my belongings. the hospital acted like it was my fault. keep in mind at this point i am practicing non mobile, i had to be assisted everywhere. i talked to patients relations and risk management. both admitted it was my fault and that it anyone can go into each others rooms. there's no cameras in the hallways. my upset question was "so anyone can just sneak in my room at night and kill me with no trace of video" and was yes. apparently theft happens all the time, and still nothing is done about it. i am now stuck with an almost $650 bill to replace the phone. 
complaint 5: me scared to leave my room to shower i didn't shower for two days not one nurse asked me if i wanted a bed side sponge bath. which i needed every day because i had a central line on my chest which you need to have a special bath to keep it sterilized. so day two of not showering i got fed up and asked for the nurse if i can shower he said yes and that his assistant will come in and cover up my iv and central line area, seconds later his assistant came in which at that night was a extremely large very deep voice male. he came in charging at me with his hands in the air and said "i'm not gonna shower you it is too early and i have a dead body to put in the morgue" i thought he was joking so i asked him again can i shower. he didn't raise his voice and said "i'm not playing i'm not gonna shower you i got a dead body to put in the morgue" at this point he seemed frustrated and angry. i got very scared and started to panic with tears. so i asked if i can just have some towels in a wheelchair i can do it myself. he then repeated himself again and said no then i just asked him to leave my room. i literally had a panic attack nurses had to come in to call me down offering me medication to call me down i just asked to be alone and cried for hours and hours. the nurse excuse was that he was just a very large male with a deep voice and he didn't mean to startle me. he then just was just asked to not come in my room. i didn't shower that day because i was afraid i was going to run into him in the hallways. 

other than all of these complaints most nurses are very poorly trained. when you call for a nurse they take forever to reply. my room was constantly filthy from bloody gauze dropped on the floor, caps, dirty gloves, just things that never got to the trashcan bin. they were very bad at recording my p intake and dumping my p bucket. my restroom was filthy they hardly took the trash out. house cleaning was just a crappy job. most days i would have my breakfast tray and lunch tray in the room at the same time. these are just a few things. i came home so traumatized. i couldn't sleep i can still hear the hospital in my head i have nightmares about that hospital.

i can't even begin to express my gratitude to the staff in the emergency department, and all of the other nurses, doctors, and technicians who treated me with extraordinary patience and kindness during my stay at mercy general. 

i went to the emergency department in serious condition (both physically and mentally,) and due to the covid-19 crisis, i was skeptical that the hospital would have the energy, means, interest, or (wo)man-power to address my medical and psychiatric needs. that skepticism soon vanished after experiencing the care and thoughtfulness of each and every nurse and doctor who treated me during my 4-night stay.

what's more is that my insurance partially lapsed and would only cover one night of care. the hospital ate the bill for the remaining nights, which saved me much heartache and financial strain down the road. it was an unmerited act of mercy. this hospital lives up to it's name!

in addition, i had no family that was able to pick me up due to the shelter in place ordinance, so i was concerned about traveling back home to santa cruz on amtrak fresh out of the hospital from a severe illness. once again, mercy stepped in to save the day- they arranged a ride all the way home to santa cruz.

i have been hospitalized on two other occasions in my adult life, and this experience far exceeded all of my other visits, and the attention to detail and empathy of the staff here far surpassed my expectations. i am so grateful for all of the providers who helped save my life. thank you all!!!

this has to be the worst emergency department in sacramento, with methodist coming in a close second. be prepared to wait many, many hours in the waiting room... just to be sat in the hallway for many more hours. it's an extremely small ed and they are limited on beds and space for that matter.

oh yeah, i almost forgot to mention that all the communication were through the rn's, a doctor never even spoke to us once during the second visit. patients are almost completely neglected here. it's as though... if you are out of their sight, you are out of their mind. 

thankfully her ppo healthcare plan allows her to have other options.

this place is a complete and total rip off. i just found out i am pregnant and went in to get basic labs which were ordered through their women's center which were in-network with my insurance company, they didn't talk to me about what labs they were going to do (i could have told them not to order any sti screening or blood type because i already know all the results for that since i was last pregnant) so i go in, they take 4 small vials, and no one even calls me with the results, it's been weeks, no i get a bill tho that says they are charging $2500 for what i could have gone to lab corp and paid a fraction for? and then i call their financial help line, and the woman was just like "oh, your insurance company is saying you have to pay this because you have a deductible" oh, fuck me right? low income, pregnant, at home and out of work because of covid with a toddler, and they aren't going to do shit for me, very cool! fuck this place, fuck their service, all they give a shit about is getting paid. i am not going back, i refuse to deliver here, canceling all my prenatal appointments i had with them.

review:

 i was picked up by an ambulance in the early am of 6-20-20 for an attempted overdose and requested to be taken to my own facility, baylor, scott, and white. i was told "you're going somewhere else". i still don't know where they took me, but i was taken to cch around 2:00 pm for admission, i waited 4 hours before finally being admitted and was told by one of the staff that i was the most patient of all the patients that day and she laughed. 
monday:
their induction manual stated that a  hospital patient "has the right to request a discharge from the hospital. if you want to leave, you need to say so in writing or tell a staff person.if you tell a staff person you want to leave, the staff person must write it down for you." i requested the release from tech jacob twice and told i would have to see a nurse the  second time.the nurse said she would have to ask dr. baez, still no help. i later met with baez and asked again and he told me i had to wait till tuesday.  had only underwear and a dirty t-shirt to wear and asked for some scrubs, which jacob ignored my requests all day. also requested a razor and soap which jacob ignored my requests also because he  had to watch me and he didn't have time.    
tuesday:
met with baez and asked again about the form, baez said in a flippant tone: "it's too late now i've already put you under the custody of the court and there's no judge in  their right mind is going to let you out of here you'll get a summons later in the week." not only lacking compassion for a patient but deceiving them as well.requested shave all day from jacob again to no avail.
wed:
received a summons for 2 court hearings, thur. 6/25 and thur 7/1. evening a patient in an adjacent ward spent nearly 2 hrs. beating on the door and screaming 2 women's names and "i want to go home". finally 2 orderlies were sent in to subdue him and carted him away.very disturbing.finally got a shave when baez gave staff an order to get it done.
thurs:
hearing was scheduled for 1:00 pm and finally came to order at 2:07 pm. baez had been making daily short talks and i had told him i was less depressed and slept better. when the judge asked the patient advocate regarding my progress, she read that baez had said i was more depressed and not sleeping well. i said nothing because my court appointed lawyer had spent about 3 minutes on the phone with me and told me not to say anything but answer what they asked. judge and county attorney decided i was nonchalant(?) and denied my release.
fri:
short meeting with baez again and i told him i was confused by his statement that i was depressed and not sleeping well to the court. he said "no i didn't say that, my statement was that you were improving daily, even your blood pressure and vitals." i asked him if my vitals had improved today and he said  "yes they have" i told him they hadn"t been taken yet because an incompetent nurse was trying to draw blood from both my hands and the nurse taking vitals moved on to the next patient. he said "be glad she didn't go to your feet." he then took me to get my vitals done. seems like more "deception" to me.
sat.:
at breakfast another patient was choking on some food and went to the  floor gagging and choking with no response from any of the staff. finally after a couple of minutes of screaming from the other patients around him, an orderly came over and knelt down and said "what's wrong, you ok?" no one rolled him over or attempted to help and he finally stuck his own fingers down his throat and vomited which dislodged the blockage. very disturbing. meeting with baez, he said i might get to go home monday or tuesday.  requested a shave from weekend staff oliver who took care of me immediately.
weekend staff in my case was light years better than weekly staff. particularly elizabeth, erica and oliver were outstanding in patient care. i was finally released on monday after 8 days while most patients had been released after 4 or 5 days. i was told by an employee that you're better off not asking to be released because they will automatically put you in the court system. beds were little more than wood frames with a four inch piece of plastic and foam. had a bad back going in and much worse coming out. no regard for the already fragile state of the patients.this facility appears to  be a cash cow for someone and should be investigated by the state. other patients were subjected to the same treatment as i and i believe are/were too scared to speak up.
update: i am from austin, not san francisco. didn't mention the fact i received maybe 30 minutes of actual counseling in 8 days. time was spent maybe 3 hrs a day of group therapy,the rest watching tv or watching others color, staring at the ceiling in your room because it was slightly warmer.

review:
so i go into the er because i'm having full body weakness that was almost full blown paralysis and slurred speech for over 30 hours. 
some background: i'm a 21yo female with a history of migraines, a hole in my heart, family with multiple neurological issues including brain cancer, restless leg, epilepsy, etc. i also have two chronic illnesses known as ehlers-danlos syndrome and pots (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome). 
i told them i was driving when i started having lapses in my memory before starting to feel super weak and dissociated about an hour after the memory lapse episodes. it turned into almost complete paralysis and i almost couldn't talk. the dr tried to make me make a fist and i literally couldn't do it. 
so they drug tested me. when that came up negative (i'm a criminal justice major going into law school for criminal law. i don't do drugs) they didn't know what to say. 
then they told me it was just depression and 
sent. me. home. 
so i go to my neurologist. he runs an eeg and tells me i have pretty moderate epilepsy and what i had was a partial focal or partial complex seizure while driving (they don't make you fall on the floor and shake).
the paralysis is known as todd's paralysis. it's pretty common after a seizure. 

so these er doctors can't even tell the aftermaths of a seizure. but since i'm a relatively normal looking, young female it's clearly just "all in my head."

be careful. cuz all that cost us $15,000.

that's fine. do you want to stay with your loved one until midnight? that's fine. does someone want to spend the night in the room with them? not only is that fine, but they also have a pull-out bed for your convenience! since you're allowed to come and go anytime you want there are many security measures. you have to go through multiple checkpoints where you speak into an intercom and tell them what patient and what room you are trying to walk too. i thought this was great and prevented some random nut from just walking in and doing whatever they wanted. this whole complex is a modern, impressive facility. they even have a seriously impressive gym in the building next door that is open to the public! if it wasn't for their hours open (i'm a night owl) i would have joined. the only thing i thought was incredibly odd was that there is a "healing garden" outside, but the door to reach it is one way only. it locks behind you and you can't go back into the hospital through it. so to get back inside i had to walk completely around the building and through a loading dock at one point. i didn't see any patients in the garden. in fact the only people i saw were employees going to the parking lot. as for my emergency room experience i was only there for a couple hours. the doctor who discharged me had a terrible bedside manner and seemed genuinely annoyed at the handful of questions i had about being released. i'm going to chalk it up to just being a bad apple. they treated my loved one so well over so many days that i would not hesitate to come back here myself for care.

although we encountered a number of amazing staff members, aaron sticks out to myself and my family for our own reasons. i know we were not always easy to deal with during that frustrating time, and aaron was always composed, empathetic, never left us in the dark, and always made us feel like our time was extremely valuable to him.

oh gosh! i'm crying now, so let me wrap this up. aaron, if you get to read this, i just want to say how incredibly grateful we are to you for being the nurse that you are, but more so, for just being the kind-hearted human being that you are, which isn't always easy to find these days. your mom raised an amazing young man, and never change k. happy national nurse's day. 

with love, from our family to yours, 
amy

i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!

as pleased as i was with dr. sebastian's work, i was extremely disappointed with the results of my diep flap breast reconstruction performed by dr. alex mesbahi, who was one of the three plastic surgeons recommended by her.

 as with any large organization, there are a few who could benefit from sensitivity training and a refresher on compassion. i have addressed this with the appropriate supervisors.

review: rude unprofessional unethical staff here!!!!!! prepare to wait all day and night to be seen and finally discharged!!! never ever come to this hospital. super dirty and contamination on all kinds if you come to this emergency room!!!!! how this place is staying open after all the violations mind boggles me. avoid this hospital even for a simple procedure.

if i could give negative, not even zero stars, i would. this hospital is an utter mess with the most rudest staff i have ever seen. they cannot even help you with simple directions to the bathroom, cannot help you be seen until your 5th hour in the er (and that's only for a consultation). if you try calling, good luck! the lady who answers will either hangup on you after 5 secs of you speaking or talk over you then hang up. surely everyone is busy, but the fact that i had to call 10 times and still get no where was absolutely uncalled for. imagine if instead of hanging up or talking over someone you just listened to their concern and what they needed help with. i cannot express my discontent with this hospital enough - this hospital is by far the worst i've seen in my life! please do not go here, choose a different hospital that will take care of your needs. even if this is the closest one, go to a different hospital to seek help. the brooklyn hospital center should be shut down or at least hire a completely different staff. i wish you the best of luck for anyone who is in serious pain; please seek help elsewhere. this hospital will be a waste of both time and money. also, with all the attitude from staffers and negative energy in the hospital, i don't think it's okay for anyone to even enter the building.

if i could give this place negative stars, i wouldn't hesitate. i have severe food allergies and ended up in the er a few months ago because i was having an anaphylactic reaction. i had already taken an epipen and walked in because i wasn't too far away. my eyelids were swollen shut and upon telling the receptionist that i was having a serious medical emergency she asked me to sit, sign papers that i couldn't see because of the swelling, and wait. every second during anaphylaxis is valuable, any nurse knows that waiting isn't really an option. even when i was taken back, a nurse or doctor hadn't talked to me for 20 minutes, or taken any of my information! the nurse who walked in was shocked to see me because she had no idea anyone was there! in that time as my condition worsened, i self-administered another epipen to save my own life. on top of it all, once i was seen, the nurse asked me if i had done this to myself on purpose and didn't believe me when i expressed how unbelievably uncomfortable i was after vomiting, struggling to breathe, and having swollen eyelids. i can't believe the lack of care and understanding from an emergency institution, they didn't offer much help whatsoever and billed the max amount. had i not been more aware and not had other allergic incidents, i'd have died from their malpractice. never again in my life will i think about going here.

zero stars. my boyfriend is currently in icu. due to covid, i am unable to be with him. the entire staff, with very few exceptions, has been awful to me. he has been chemically restrained for 10 days and now his hands are tied for 2 days. i sent him via 911 to the er due to alcohol withdrawal with psychosis. this place won't even let him get better. every time he gets agitated because he wants to go home, they shoot him with more meds. do not take yourself or loved ones to this hospital.....ever!

i was so upset that my arm was hanging down straight over 5 hours which should be put ice and elevated in the hospital and was treated as last patient just based on a desk lady's false judge regardless my mention about my fracture and real condition.  after the billing department smoothly obtaining the first payment from my insurance company, the department harms my credit by refusing to bill to my insurance company, but let a debt company to handle...... the emergency front desk service and billing department really impress me and give me such negative memory. i heard from my friend that the hospital provides poor service. i got the same experience.

review:
this review is for the labor and delivery unit. i work in healthcare, so i have a better understanding of how healthcare systems work compared to most people, and as prepared as i was to understand the finances and logistics of my pregnancy and childbirth, even i was unprepared for the problems i would have during childbirth.

first i had an issue with their billing. i called the billing department to verify that the hospital was considered in-network under my health plan, so i thought a normal vaginal delivery would be fully covered. however i was surprised to receive bills following my delivery from the anesthesia provider, who was out of network, the pediatricians who did the newborn physicals and hearing exams were out of network. overall, giving me a headache by having to sort out bills during the time i should have been bonding with my baby, rather than spending hours on the phone. as someone who is very diligent about making sure i understood everything forward and backwards regarding the cost of my delivery, i still was misinformed. lesson is: ask your insurance health plan specifically if the anesthesia providers, pediatricians, and any other providers you might see are in-network. personally, if i could do it again i would have opted to deliver at kaiser or ucla, where you know that you won't have any providers who are out-of-network. the experience of dealing with insurance providers and these other private providers have been painful to say the least. 

secondly, their "baby friendly" designation is misleading. i was very open to the myriad of possible events that can happen during childbirth, and that a lot of things are unpredictable, especially as medical events can alter the course of action. however, i felt  their nursing staff have so many traveling nurses in their unit, some who are unaware of the policies or full extent of services available in the unit, that i felt that most of them did not fully understand the services available during childbirth. for example, i asked to use the tub for pain relief, which i knew was available because it was shown to us during a tour, however there was a nurse who had no idea that there was even a tub available. i also found that the obstetrician who delivered my daughter, dr. mia sanders madati, was slow to come to my bedside once the baby started crowning. the nurse who was helping me to push literally had to tell me to hold the baby, while we waited 10 minutes for her to arrive to my bedside. as any woman who has every had to deliver a baby vaginally, every minute feels like eternity. then when the baby came, instead of putting the baby immediately on me, she took her sweet little time cleaning off the baby's face and body, when all i wanted was the baby to be on me. lesson is: you are your best advocate and also get your partner to advocate for you. understand that things may be out of your control, but don't blindly just assume what they tell you is always right. you never know what your experience will be like until you actually deliver. 

overall, having your baby is a truly special, once in a lifetime experience for some people like me, where i waited so long to have a baby. i am grateful to have had a healthy baby girl. however, if i had the chance to do it all over again, i would have chosen a different hospital to deliver.

i have had both private and kaiser insurance, so i feel qualified to comment and compare the two systems.  been to private physicians in the bay area (including stanford and ucsf), have had lab and radiology services, and hospitalizations up and down the peninsula over the past 30 years.  i realize people have individual experiences that may not be like mine.

kaiser ssf is designed to handle large volumes of people more efficiently, so it is in some ways less personal medicine.  one can sometimes feel like cattle. however, i don't need a lot of hand holding, and i love kaiser ssf for its relative efficiency.  i've been going to kaiser now as my primary insurance for over 15 years, because i find my coordinated care to be far better than through private insurance.  i like the fact that i can see another doctor in the kaiser system in a timely fashion if my doctor is unavailable.  i like having my meds mailed to me. flu shots are super easy.  your preventive care schedules (immunizations, colonoscopy, mammograms etc) are tracked and you are informed in writing.  

at kaiser ssf, i have never had to wait more than 5-15 minutes for an x-ray or mri or ct or a blood draw.  er was reasonably quick the one time i was there -- i was able to check in and be seen and get a ct, then out the door in about 90 minutes.  the er doctor was kind but also very businesslike and to the point, which was appreciated. the er staff also scheduled an appointment for a specialist for the next morning, so that i wouldn't have to do it myself.  i really appreciated their thoughtfulness. in private practice facilities, i've had to wait over 2 hours for a pre-scheduled simple chest x-ray; over 30 minutes for a lab; and weeks for a doctor's appointment. 

quality of doctors --- i have had some really great doctors over the years at kaiser and outside of kaiser.  (exception: i liked my obgyn and dermatology doctors outside of kaiser better.) my internist, oncologist, and surgeon at kaiser are as knowledgeable and skillful as the ones i had outside of kaiser, but unlike the others, my kaiser doctors talk to each other so the care is coordinated each step of the way.
