review:
most of my experience with this va has been fairly positive. every time i take my mom to the er they're pretty quick compared to most civilian ers i've been to. when it came to getting my new va id and getting transferred from the salem va to here, the process was quick. the nurses there are cordial and the travel area has someone there that's actual pleasant to talk to.
the pharmacy has been a hit or miss. sometimes it's quick and other times you have to check up on them to make sure your medicine is even being processed.
i've only had one experience with my primary care physician and it was horrible. i got stuck with team 30 and my first visit was via telecom due to the coronavirus. sure seemed unempathetic, didn't care that not all of my records transferred from salem to hampton, and basically told me that i'm exaggerating my pain. one of the "lost" records was from a civilian chiropractor explaining why i'm having back and neck pain and the va conveniently loses those during the transfer. she was great to get me referral's i needed and actually doing her job, but her "bedside manners" were atrocious, even to the extent of implying that the chiropractor was wrong even though she didn't have his xrays and explanations in front of her. because it was telecom, my family overheard a portion of it and even they said she sounded extremely rude and inconsiderate.
i've had mostly average experiences sprinkled with a few impecable and horrendous experiences, that's why in giving an average rating of 3. the salem va deserves at least 4 and the hampton va is lucky in giving them a 3.

as a united sates veteran, i really do appreciate everything that the va does for me. i don't come here often but when i do they really take care of me. they give me where i need to be and with who i need to see. the only knock i can give this place is that whenever i do come here i know it's gonna be a all day experience. i usually have to take a day off from work to come here because of how many people i need to see and different places i need to go. there's like an assistant for the assistant for the assistant. often times i'm left feeling like just another number, because you literally take a number and wait to be called. parking here is another whole experience. often times when i get here i feel like i'm parking at a football game or a basketball game and even then it's better parking at those events. i feel like they need valet parking or something to alleviate how bad the parking is. overall i think this is an ok clinic and i again appreciate everything that they do for me.

i had the unfortunate experience of having to visit the er for my teenage son last night.   i was headed straight for dell children's, as all parents of children should, but he was complaining of horrible dizziness and he had a head injury, so i did not feel comfortable driving that far with him.  in hindsight, i wish we had gone to dell.  

screened at front door for covid and masked.  no problem here other than we were not given any introductions.   from screening, through initial triage, i don't have any serious complaints.   my son was identified as a "trauma alert" in triage, due to the mechanism of his injury, and we were quickly wheeled back. i am uncertain of anyone's role up to this point as all staff who came into contact with us failed to tell us their name or role (with the exception of being told we were  "in" triage, no name or role to the person who completed that task.)

once in the room, my son was taken for ct within 5 minutes.  he had been wheeled to the room, placed on a monitor and left lying in a cold, wet swimsuit. upon return from ct, the pa came by to see him.  she was attentive and concerned.  she gave him a thorough exam, but had trouble finding any nursing staff who could assist her to roll him properly to clear c-spine.  throughout the duration of our stay, the nurses were much less than attentive.  there is an informative board on the wall that tells you the date.  ours read yesterday's date and it is unlikely the male nurse attending to us was named paige or esther, as identified by the board.   

the nursing staff was very disappointing.  they were standing at the nursing station conversing about the 6 year delinquency of required trainings for one of the nurse's at work that evening.  never offered a call bell, had to search for a nurse every time, the bathroom floor was covered in urine, my son was never removed from his wet clothes, taken off the wet fitted sheet (despite multiple bed transfers), never offered a warm blanket (standard of care for trauma alert). they did not operate as a team.  if i asked for something, the other nurses relayed the request to our assigned nurse rather than offering to help. when my son left for mri, evs actually assisted mri staff with the bed transfer because the nurses were sitting at the nurses station and did not offer to help.  

the pa was attentive.  if it were not for her, this review would be 1 star.  the pa
took pictures and relayed them to her attending physician, who was apparently involved in care but never came by to see him.  my son was never asked to rate his pain.  no follow up for the tylenol i requested he be given.  the nurses never asked him about his symptoms.   they did not ever assess him.  the only true assessment was completed by the pa and one by a triage nurse.  discharge instructions by the nurse included reading me the titles off the papers and i was told to fill the cephalexin, "which is an antibiotic, i think", the nurse said.  yes- it is.  nurses make all of the difference.   unfortunately, the nurses this evening showed the difference it makes when they don't take pride in their work.

i wish i could leave zero stars. the nursing staff is horrific. they don't dilute their medications. they blew my veins 5x in 6 days time. that has never happened anywhere else. the nurse threatened me with a midline and said if i refused i was not going to get iv meds anymore... when i'm there for an infectious disease that causes dehydration. i had a horrible reaction as i was leaving and the nurses refused to contact the hospitalist. instead the same nurse threw my discharge papers at me.. and tried to refuse to give me my prescriptions as i was leaving. she said they were sent electronically. 
i am someone who is chronically ill. i know that narcotics can not be sent electronically. as soon as i said i was calling the pharmacy, she comes running back in my room with my crumbled up prescription. which the doctor has already left so she was withholding it out of spite. 
i have been hospitalized a good amount of my life due to autoimmune diseases from gallbladder dying to chronic pancreatitis, liver disease, blood clots, internal bleeding and chronic c diff. 
i will never go back to this hospital. truly. don't go here.
the charge nurse on the fourth floor is up to no good, even the other nurses and clinic assistants told me horrible stories about her. only two nurses on the whole floor are genuine and even apologized and said they didn't know why that young girl was a charge nurse. 
my first day admitted, she was laughing with another nurse because she left an elderly woman on the toilet by herself because she was tired of waiting for her. 
you are better off driving to austin another 15 minutes for quality care. 
5 hours without anyone checking on me one day, they skipped time sensitive antibiotics.. then 2 hours of throwing up without any nurse coming in. you're lucky if they check your vitals once a day. 
i am glad i was able to fight for myself. if you have an elder parent or young child.. do not subject them to this type of care. there is a reason for the other negative comments. 
if you are reading this, it's probably because you need medical care and i hope you feel better soon. but this isn't a family hospital. this is an outrage.

so after speaking with the patient care advocate, mcall washer, the billing issues were all resolved. i would give her 5 stars for her compassion. she really worked hard to make things right. it's rare that you find someone that goes the distance for you. thank you again for taking the time to improve the care i received. you a good person and it shows.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

switching to kaiser permanente is definitely on the table right now.

i went to the er on february 28 the service was horrible i had to sit in the hallway for hours, i told the doctor i was very dehydrated and didn't even get anything till 5 hours later that i ask if i could get an ivy and only had it for less the  5 minutes because the doctor went home and the nurses just gave me some papers and send me home.. ooh but the 11k bill wow for not even getting anything.

nobody from this facility has contacted me 2 full days after my wife transferred there, and when i call, they refuse to even acknowledge if she is a patient there, even though i was the one who had her transferred there from a kaiser hospital.  kaiser nurses assured me prior to the transfer to this location that i would have full access and be able to advocate on my wife's behalf.  apparently, even though this is a kaiser-contracted facility, they have their own rules and totally disregarded the information provided to them by our health insurance provider who contracts with them.  i even dropped off clothes while my wife was still being admitted (the front desk took them and told me she'd get them when she was done admitting), and also they told me someone would call me that day (never happened).

when you call this place, you better have the patient code or they will not even acknowledge the existence of the patient, but even with a code, there is a consent form they make you sign or nothing can be released, so if your loved one is catatonic or in a coma or other type of frame of mind that is not rational and is unable to sign the form, be ready to not hear from anybody for an extended period of time.  my wife has been there for 2 days and not one person from this facility (doctor, nurse, case worker, etc) has contacted me to update me or speak about my wife's situation.

once i was given a code to receive information (and they actually acknowledged she was a patient), they transfer you to the nurses station and phone rings for hours before anybody picks up.  when a nurse finally did, he told me the code is useless because the consent form isn't signed.  i told him wife is catatonic and cannot sign anything, and then he hung up on me.

my wife has sleep apnea and needs a cpap machine nightly.  the entire reason she was sent to this facility versus others, was because they are supposedly equipped to handle breathing emergencies.  so the first night she was there, she was not provided her cpap.  when my wife finally called me early on the second evening, i told her to ask the nurse for her cpap machine and it was given to her.  then the next morning my wife called me to tell me that all of the electrical outlets in all of the patient rooms weren't working, and the only room that had working outlets was the game room and they would put in there if she wanted.  unacceptable!

they have one phone for the patients to call out on, but when my wife uses it to call me, patients routinely walk up to her and harass her and there is zero privacy for patients who want to speak to loved ones.

once it became clear that this hospital was not "cpap friendly" as they proclaimed they were to our health insurance provider (kaiser), they could not get rid of my wife fast enough (it was great!).  rather than keeping her for a prolonged period of time while they "balanced her meds" or ensured she was safe and ready to return to her home (for those of you in similar situations, you know exactly what i'm referring to), they discharged her without even having a doctor sign off on the discharge form (apparently it must have been done either after she left or remotely, because she was not seen by a doctor the day they discharged her, which is basically unheard of).  

in fact (and to date its now been two weeks since my wife was released and also since i began writing this review), we have never heard from one single medical professional at this facility.  not a doctor, nurse, or anybody else regarding my wife's hospitalization.  the only person who was nice enough to reach out to me while she was still in their hospital, was a social worker who facilitated the quick release.  

the last thing i want to mention is that all of this went down during the current coronavirus event.  you would think that under those extreme circumstances without any visitation possible, that they would ensure the patients and their loved ones (ie i'm her husband who had her sent there!), would have as much access to the patient as possible (via phone, etc).  this place wouldn't even acknowledge to me she was their patient for two full days while i stressed out and worried incessantly, and then i find out that she was without her cpap for her entire stay.  these people are damn lucky i don't sue their ass.  (but i have filed a nice grievance with the major health plan that they contract with, so we'll see how that goes)....

my body decided to go haywire on me this morning. i was concerned that it could possibly be a very high glucose level, so i headed to the er.

before entering, my temp was taken, and then i checked in. i was only in the waiting room for about 10 minutes.

after i was taken back, i got in my gown, settled onto the gurney, and then shortly after, dr martinez came in.

she has a great bedside manner, and she talked to me about my symptoms, and explained what she was going to do. she then said the nurse would be in shortly.

i was expecting a long wait, because that's how it goes in hospitals, but then about 10 minutes later, nurse jenny came in.

y'all, she is awesome. very nice and funny, and i did not even feel the needle when she drew blood and started an iv. a+ phlebotomy skills. she sent me off to the bathroom to get a urine sample. i told her i didn't know if i could give her anything because i had just gone before i went to the er. she told me that she actually doesn't need much, and that she laughs whenever people give her a full cup back, because it's just overkill. so after i returned with a fuller cup than i expected, i said "i got more than i expected" and she laughed and said "what did i tell you?! i only need a tiny bit!"

anyway, she took my various fluids to be tested, and i settled in with a podcast, anticipating a long wait.

but about 45 minutes later, dr martinez arrived, said my test results all looked great, and determined that the cause was the cough syrup i had been taking for an allergy-induced cough that i've had since march.

she said to follow up about the cough with my primary care, and said she was ready to "bust you outta here."

i got dressed, jenny came in with a note for work and my discharge notes, and off i went.

all in all, i only spent 2 hours in the er. i think that might be some kind of record.

so, if you have to go to this er, and you get dr martinez and/or nurse jenny, you'll definitely be well cared for. if you get both of them together, you've hit the freakin jackpot.

review: hospitals are mostly miserable places but the three experiences i've had here -- two for mom, one for me -- were purely inexcusable.  first, a bit shabby and unkempt when you look closely, and not as clean as you want a hospital to be (an aide and a friend of mine agree with this).  when my mother was an in-patient, the doctor argued arrogantly with me when i knew i was right (does he know my mother? who does he think he is?), so we left ama (against medical advice -- they hate that), and she improved rapidly at home.  as for their er, do not go.  do not.  you will wait . . . and wait . . . and wait . . . and wait to be seen and tested, although of course they'll get your insurance information almost immediately.  expect to be there for a long, long time. while you're waiting, you may notice old dried blood on the bed rails, like i did, and bits of paper trash in the hall that won't get picked up for a couple of hours.  if you're lucky, someone may ask you if you want an aspirin.  after that, nobody will look in on you to ask if, perhaps, you'd like some water.  you'll have to go out in the hall and holler; how else are you supposed to get any attention around there?  maybe you'll complain, and someone will give you the old song and dance about "very busy day" and "we're short-handed."  short-handed?  busy?  then call a few off-duty nurses and technicians and have them come in and pay them overtime.  is that difficult?  there are no excuses for this place.

feeding and managing stomach regulation was a week. after a week with no tangible post operative recovery achieved (her bowels were not yet working) out of frustration, pain and stress she removed the ng tube and refused to have reinserted. the doctors then told her she was healing slowly but well but due to swelling needed the ng tube for another week to complete the post operative process and to get her bowels started,

 also shared so many potential negative complications without emphasizing their professional opinion that she would recover well and live relatively independently with another week with the ng tube. she became more depressed telling me she would need a colostomy bag which was not the case at all. she was believing things that we're not true. great medicine north shore. since mom sounded coherent the doctors abided by her wishes against the wishes of her medical proxy - my brother. this was on a friday. however this was not my true mom who was saying this. my brother requested a social worker meet with her immediately and asked for mom to be put on antidepressants knowing that she would likely change her mind on the ng tube when she was not so depressed and disoriented. we couldn't get this to happen until monday since the social worker was not available on weekends. thats a good protocol in a life and death situation. does the hippocratic oath mean anything?? in the meantime her doctors told me and my brother that they would start some iv feeding and give her liquids orally. these did not occur until her condition rapidly declined because of handoff delays. apparently the handoff between internal medicine and medical intern doesn't work here. huge medical failure. north shore is a hotbed for miscommunication,
lack of medical follow through and poor medical judgement by monday, mom was on a death spiral and she passed on a wednesday.  if you are looking to heal, i highly recommend avoiding this place. if you have corona go to a professional hospital not here where you most likely will die! god help anyone that goes here

review: my doctor is wonderful but the office experience is horrific. i don't blame the staff, i understand we are in the middle of a pandemic and things are tough right now, but my experience with this clinic has been nothing short of traumatic, and it's clear there's something structurally and systemically wrong at this clinic. i've had to go to the emergency room twice because of the sheer amount of time i had to wait here. one time i went 12 hours without food or water because i spent half of it waiting in this clinic and then was sent from this clinic to the er and hadn't ate or drank all day because i was waiting and couldn't leave. (shoutout to the one nurse who remembered me and who was really nice because i had to keep coming back). despite being a mt. sinai clinic, there's no integration with the mt. sinai system and no access to my records electronically, so they don't communicate with the rest of mt. sinai. again, my doctor is great but i always feel rushed, making appointments is a labyrinth, and i have to go through 3 different appointment desks to make different kinds of appointments so i have to often miss work to come to the clinic. if i didn't have flexible work hours or an understanding boss, this clinic would be a nightmare. they didn't understand why i didn't want to come to the clinic three days in a row one week for three separate appointments just for tests because they can't coordinate amongst themselves, despite the fact that i live all the way across the city, am at a high risk for covid-19, have to come here alone because of mt. sinai covid rules, and because of the nature of it being an eye clinic, have reduced vision. not to mention the cost of travel every single time i have a separate appointment because this clinic's administration doesn't makes sense. sometimes they will make appointments for you that you didn't even make for yourself and you'll find out in a text days later. i cannot imagine what navigating this clinic would be like if i struggled with english, didn't have good health insurance, my vision was even worse, or i wasn't young or white or looked fairly ambulatory. overall, i regret starting my care here and not somewhere else because i feel stuck here. starting somewhere else would be a huge hassle, and i really like my doctor here, but the experience has put me off even the rest of the mt sinai system. do not come here if you truly don't have to.

renown medical center delivers a ridiculous amount of babies every day (4,063 in the year 2016), especially with being one of the main hospitals in reno (next to st. mary's) and from experience, i can easily see that they know what they're doing.

i'm the mother of three children and two of them were born at renown medical center.  my experiences were nothing short of amazing.  the ease of check in, skill level of the doctors, nurses and staff, resources available, and level of comfort all contributed to my amazing experiences and i would easily come back to renown if i ever planned on having another child.

my second child, arrived in half the time as my first child. instead of 12 hrs., he arrived in 6 hrs. i was at home laboring it out when my water broke and i knew he would come out shortly.  my dear sister zoomed us to the emergency section of the hospital knowing i wouldn't have time to check in and upon arrival, someone with a chair wheeled me into the delivery room.  the nurses heard me coming down the hall and my sister said they all quickly flocked together in a group, waiting to receive me.

they transferred me to the bed and immediately called the doctor.  the doctor arrived promptly and was very skillful with how he delivered my baby.  he did a technique that prevented tares and i couldn't have been happier since my first birthing experience left me in pain with a third degree tare.  asking your doctor ahead of time about ways to prevent tares could be beneficial so as to minimize healing time post delivery.

after my baby came out, the nurses quickly wiped him with towels and placed him on my chest.  bonding occurs right away and it is said that skin to skin contact also helps calm babies while keeping them warm and helps trigger your milk supply for breastfeeding.  they also applied antibiotic eye drops to prevent eye infections.

while holding my baby, the doctor came in and made sure the placenta came out.  one firm press to my stomach did the trick and the placenta slipped right out.

shortly after, the nurses took him to a table right next to my bed. there, they suctioned out extra fluids to help him breath better, took some measurements, and made sure everything was normal.

after being asked some questions, i was transferred to my recovery room.

in recovery, the nurse assisted me with my first bathroom break and gave me some instruction on how to care for myself.  the bathroom was fully stocked with everything i needed-underwear, pads, wash bottles, gowns and towels.   after, she offered me an ice pack for my bottom and i was so thankful since it was so soothing.

with my second baby, my husband went along with the nurses for his first bath. with the third baby, i was able to watch my baby's first bath.

they monitored me and my baby closely to make sure our vitals were on point and to make sure i was feeling ok and that i wasn't bleeding excessively.

a lactation consultant visited me to assist me with breastfeeding and any questions i had.  renown does have alternatives and resources to breastfeeding of you're unable to.

my doctor visited me the following day to see my progress and gave the o.k. to go home.  they monitor you for a minimum of 24 hrs. to make sure everything is fine but mothers usually stay 24-48 hrs. after birth.

it took a total of 10 minutes from the time i arrived to the time my baby came out.  with such little time, renown was able to deliver in all areas.  i was so impressed with how prepared they were.  there's nothing more comforting than knowing you have people you can depend on to get you through your birthing experience.

i gave birth to my three children without epidural and i wouldn't have done it any other way.  of course i was scared of the unknowns of pain that i would experience but i knew it was pain that i could handle and pain that would be worthwhile.

there are many options available for pain management at renown and different methods of giving birth.

with my second delivery at renown, i made sure to allow extra time to check in.  i went in through the front of entrance of the hospital and was checked into a screening room where they determined that i was far along to be admitted.  this time around, they called my doctor (information on hand from pre-registration) who made it just in time to deliver my third baby.  i gave birth yet again and couldn't have been happier with the service given.

renown's doctors, nurses and staff exceeded my expectations.  the beautiful hospital allowed for my husband to sleep overnight with me and the snack room (accessible to only mothers), was a pleasant surprise.

review:
so, i would have given encompass health rehab hospital 5 stars because they were amazing when i was there for two weeks in october. you won't find more caring doctors and nurses. honesly.

i continued with encompass home health when i got home -- and til the pandemic, i was crazy about both my physical therapist and my occupational therapist, both from encompass. then, when the world shut down and we were told to stay home, i asked for teletherapy. and, that's where the problems began.  encompass insisted that medicare required an in-person visit to accompany teletherapy. what?  you want me to be exposed to your therapists who are in nursing homes and with possible "compromised" patients every day? what?  i am 74 years old -- i cannot do that and you shouldn't be asking me to do that  -- an, btw,  medicare repeatedly told me that what encompass home health was claiming was 1) untrue, and, 2) impeding my recovery process. by the time i fired encompass home health, i'd gone more than 6 weeks with no therapy -- and my progress had basically stopped.  i have someone new now -- and he's great -- and is pushing me so i can hopefully make up some lost time. 
 
but if you want ongoing, consistent therapy, beware of encompass home health -- i cannot tell you how many excuses they came up with as to why they couldn't provide what everyone in the whole world was advising:  virtual care whenever possible and minimal exposure to outsiders. getting their reimbursement became much more important than ensuring my continued recovery.  i haven't even hugged my daughter for almost two months -- i was not about to allow "in-person" visits from encompass.
 
also, i found out later that my pt was in fact exposed and quite ill about two weeks after i stopped her from coming to my house.  not that encompass would have ever told me that -- and i wonder how many patients have unnecessarily been exposed to a potentially lethal virus because encompass misunderstood the medicare rules. just sayin'.....

review:
a practice manager objected that i was "sleeping" on a bench just outside. i was merely resting in a position that eased my stomach pain, eyes closed, but opened when anyone passed, with my head on my rolled-up winter coat as it was 20 degrees outside. i had earplugs in to attenuate the incessant yick-yack of cnn coming from the waiting room. i had two appointments that day, was seen by one specialist at 8:30 am and was waiting around for the start of this next appointment. i awoke with stomach pain but did not want to cancel at the last minute. all i wanted was a place to rest and chill out while waiting hours for the second appointment. if lying down on the bench was such a great sin, then i should have been instructed that only sitting was allowed, and i would have either moved or complied. i know from a log, she immediately called the cops on "a sleeping homeless person." the interaction left me with ptsd and a delayed scheduling for surgery at a different hospital for a likely cancerous condition. the trauma not only left me unable to enter that facility, it left me shaking when approached by security at my new hospital clinic provider. 

i felt like prey for two hours as i was followed all over by two security guards. matter of fact, when i went to sit in the east pavillion, security came over and harassed me about whom i was there to see--again--and i pointed out why not ask the other three women who were seated in the area the same question. after i told the police i had an appointment at 1:30 and a scheduled transport to my home at 5:30, security and the police hung out near the main entrance to see where i was going and what i was doing, or prevent me from leaving, i suppose.

when it was 1:20, i took a route around the police and security gaggle to get to the waiting room. once i was there and tried to check in, the police were right at the waiting room entrance!  i called out the practice manager as the source of my issue and was arrested on the spot for telling the security person he should be ashamed of himself. i was taken away to be booked. i barely made it back in time to catch my ride home, one i own for the record.

i am unclear how an ill, quiet person waiting for an appointment is a criminal offense!  i was discriminated against by a place of public accommodation. i find it really, really chilling that i was apparently singled out for the third degree and not others (the other women in the east pavillion).  oh, i later learned if i was ill, i needed to run the meter in the er (my words). funny how that option was not offered that day. why the two appointments in one day? i said no to this arrangement by the 8:30 am provider three times and he wore me down. had i understood the risk of having two appointments in one day, i would have pressed for the cancellation of one or the other, whichever provider would yield.

i adore mrmc! i am always taken care of when i need it. i have never called for an appointment and had to wait. they get me in right away. i love angel johnson. her bedside manner is loving and she listens. dr. bird has always greeted me with a hand shake and always makes sure to find the problem and get me back up and going. i can't say enough about how much my family appreciates that we don't have to drive to greatfalls if were sick. little hospital, big help.

it's very rare that i write a rating, but this was too good not to share. in january 2020, my husband and i had a phenomenal experience with the labor & delivery, maternity unit, and nicu at wellspan ephrata community hospital!!! as a nurse, pilot, and with my first delivery, i was just so blown away by how amazing the staff treated us, how beautiful and clean the facility was, and all of the effort by the staff to make us feel comfortable.

i was transferred to the ephrata for stalled labor after being awake approximately 30 hours. the staff gave me medication to assist me to get some sleep, while progressing my labor. during this time, they brought a reclining chair and cot into the delivery room for my husband and best friend, provided regular updates to my parents along with taking them to a monitor to explain what was going on, and delivered pillows and blankets to the waiting room. my husband and best friend were guided by the staff in how to best support me and be involved in the delivery. the midwives, nurses, and other staff worked to preserve my goal for a regular delivery with minimal site trauma.

when we transferred to my maternity room in the middle of the night, the staff already had a reclining chair and cot set up for my husband and best friend. thankfully i asked our nurse to take the baby since we were exhausted and not safe to care for a newborn. a few hours later our baby had a seizure. the nurse recognized it right away and immediately took him around the corner to the nicu. during my maternity admission and the baby's week long admission in the nicu, we continued to be amazed by the wonderful experience with the pediatricians, nurses, lactation consultants, and staff. the nurse to patient ratio and dedication of the staff facilitated individualized personal care. they all took the time to personally interact with us and provided a wealth of knowledge to set us up for success. in my experience as a nurse, we are stretched severely thin with balancing multiple priorities and often there just isn't enough time to get to know our patients. 

what we experienced at ephrata hospital was truly amazing and life changing. the staff were such a blessing and we are forever appreciative. we will definitely be back for the delivery of our second child! thank you, thank you!!!

i went out for a jog and fainted fracturing my shoulder. i was treated in the er and cant thank the staff enough for the kind and professional treatment i received. i need to send a very special thank you to maria howard and pam at the front desk and prudence who was my xray technician. prudence you are phenomenal at your job but more importantly you were kind. you all are beyond essential and please know that you absolutely make the world better. positive attitudes create positive minds. thank you all again. i'm home healing.

i've been to huggins hospital about 6 times in the last two weeks and have never felt more at ease and comfortable than i did with nurse mike in the er he is awesome! thank you so much for the quality care and compassion!

this was back in september 2019 my husband was brought in by ambulance into the er for vomiting neck pain and eye pain , he was dx with shingles! he is only 26! but let me tell you the nurses that took care of my husband were amazing they answered all my questions, roxy and a male nurse that i didn't get his name. great nurses thank you for all you do! also to dr diaz - thank you so much for the difference you make in the lives of your patients! your kindness, sincere caring, and concern make everything better and are a great encouragement. thank you so very much for taking care of husband. but other than that everything else is pretty shitty! the thing that really had me concerned was that they had a ct machine in a trailer outside?! with my husband vomiting and headaches you roll him outside ???and plus there was a drunkie outside trying to talk to us while they were rolling my husband out to the ct machine! like come. it's sad really sad to see this hospital as our neighborhood hospital ! the hospital itself needs a upgrade ! we stayed there for 3 nights...& nothing in our room worked! just unacceptable!

if i could rate this place with negative ratings, i would. i had my mom sent there due to being unconscious and cyanotic...the first hospital the ambulance would take her to was here against my wishes but it's protocol. the nurses kept changing names when i called for updates, they discharged my mom without proper information nor advising me amongst the covid-19 pandemic (they wouldn't allow me in the er which i understood -- however, i asked to be notified of her progress). the nurses never told me what was going on nor called me with updates/ not even a call that she was being discharged. nurse victoria (at the end they finally agreed on one nurse name) lied to me multiple times within a phone call. i wouldn't even recommend my worst enemy to go here. so unsanitary and unorganized. very unprofessional staff on the phone with attitude and lies. if you could drive yourself to another hospital do so, coming here is asking for a death sentence.

my mother was brought in by ambulance to this hospital and the er doctors and nurses were fantastic.  she's been there before about 5 years ago and that was not a good experience. it seems like there are new people there  now who are happy to be there, smile often and are kind and considerate and answer questions. roxy was our nurse and she alleviated any anxiety in being there and made us feel we're being taken care of well. when my mother was admitted for several days i was with her almost the whole day and only witnessed caring and compassionate personnel.  the only con is that one must share a room with another patient. this is not good in this age when people need peace and quiet to recuperate and not hear other people's tv nor their visitors.  i am hoping the hospital has been working on the atmosphere created by the workers because it is working. it is an older hospital with its financial issues, so beds and things are far from new, but i would not say it is a bad hospital as its previous reputation has been.

review:
my review is based solely on l&d and nicu. also this review should've been posted 4 months ago but time got away from me. 

i went into the emergency room at 2 in the morning because i was in labor. admitting was quick and easy, and the staff was friendly. 

when i actually got into the triage room for l&d i was asked if i wanted the epidural. i said no, but the nurse had other plans, seems she just didn't want to deal with me. 

i was moved to the delivery room and shortly after my water broke. the doctor was not present so i was surrounded by nurses (very attentive and i'm thankful). i ended up having my son without pushing. because he was small, nicu had to take him. i was moved to the ob wing, which i feel was bc i didn't have my baby with me, so it was made easier for me so i didn't have to hear the others an be so upset for not having him with me.

the nicu nurses were amazing, all except one. i don't remember her name but she was a night nurse, juvita or something along the lines of that, and she was extremely rude and demeaning. i know i look young, but i'm 27 and she made me feel like a teenager. having a child in the nicu is hard enough without the nurses judging. other than her, there were a few that stood out, amy was one of my favorites for sure. i also got along really well with the physical therapist, although i don't remember her name either. 

thank you parkview nicu for taking care of ez!

now x that 1 star out.....yes they are that bad. by own personal experience, bp 386/192, headache, difficulty breathing (before i left my house), repeated to admitting. i was given forms to fill out, take a seat. could not fill out forms, my head pounding & the er just had a office partition to separate the waiting area. sooo loud, i couldn't think. once they called me back, i seen where the noise came from. er super yelling commands, beds separated by portable curtains on wheels so the beds were smashed as close together as possible. after being told stand here, this patient will be leaving, then again at another & i gave up. slammed the unsigned forms onto the counter for the er sup & left without any treatment!  got a bill in the mail!  don't sign any forms till you are actually in a bed & if at all possible, go anywhere except parkview smh

i gave birth about a week ago and had the best experience at parkview. every single nurse i encountered was top notch!! especially anji, who was completely committed to my care and made me feel comfortable by being so down to earth and explained everything every step of the way. if i have another child, i will 100% be returning to parkview. i am  so grateful for my experience there and am bringing them baked goodies today to show my appreciation.

got the best care from rn gumaro and pa monica a few months aso.  they are fast and efficient and very compassionate with care.  dr richardson stopped by and was also very thorough and answered all my questions and concerns before i left.  really loved the new er and how all the rooms were private which also allowed you to close them.  super nice staff, would definitely recommend!

my family and i have visited the ed at parkview community hospital 3 times in the last month, like many families right now, it has been a rough year for ours. each and every time we have received excellent service. no one ever made us feel bad for coming in, they took care of us like we were the only people there, all our needs were met, service was prompt, the nursing staff was very attentive. shout out to kathy, meli, allan, karina....lisa was great too. the pa, i can't remember his name but he goes by "zazie", was also very attentive. the discharge teaching was excellent also. zazie gave us all the recommendations that we needed to get and stay healthy through this difficult time, and he took time with us to really explain things. all in all it was a great experience, if you got to go to the er, this one is at the top of the list. thanks again.

had to go to the er here a couple months ago bc our daughter had a high fever. we were seen rather quickly, the pa and other nurses/techs were helpful. after the fact when we received our bill, dina in the business office was very professional and super friendly and helpful! definitely recommend asking for dina!

ive delivered all 4 of my boys here and i had the best experiences especially being a gold member and new beginnings member. had my own room and extra snacks throughout my stay. had the head nurse in charge come in every morning to make suré they were doing their job n keeping me happy n comfortable. only thing i didn't like was feeling rushed to leave other than that good experience

i've been home about two hours now. i've debated for two hours whether i wanted to say anything or not. i've been sick since monday; it's saturday. it started out a little cough here and there. it progressively got a little worse. i started running low grade fevers and then would get chills. my nose was super stuffy. i thought ok i'm coming down with a sinus infection. i got antibiotics. they didn't work. as a matter of fact i started feeling worse; run down, fatigued, my body has been aching. today i started feeling short of breath. my chest hurt but not in that way you would think would come with a prolonged cough. more like a heavy, achy feeling. i've struggled to regain my breath several times today but i still didn't feel emergent. i weighed the options of getting health care with covid 19 so rampant but because i started struggling with air today and after asking the opinions of my triage professionals ( yes i work in healthcare) i decided i'd go to the er after i finished my shift. once i got to the room the dr explained he was ordering a flu test, a strep test (even though i had no sore throat at all) and a chest x-ray. results came back negative for everything and chest x ray showed no pneumonia. the dr tells me they won't test me for the corona virus unless i am admitted to the hospital and the only way for that to happen is if i had more emergent breathing issues. even though i was struggling to catch breaths my o2 sat was 99%. he tells me though that with all my symptoms he cannot rule out the virus and i was to return home to self quarantine until april 13. today is the 4th. upon discharge a different nurse that i hadn't met came in to give me my papers. i asked her, "how do i know if i need to come back?" this is why i'm writing. her answer floored me. she told me i shouldn't come back unless "i'm so out of breath (i) can't talk or if i'm turning blue." i asked if she was serious. she tells me "yes but if you're turning blue call 911 so they can get you oxygen on the way here." y'all i've been in healthcare for 15 years. i also have chronic health issues that have had me in and out of drs and ers and never in my life have i heard something so outrageous or felt treated so insignificant. i know there's a pandemic. i'm essential so i go to work and come home. i don't go out unless i absolutely have to. i heavily weighed wether i should go in or not and the care i received was what it should have been. they weren't full of patients, in fact it was pretty empty for 20:45 on a saturday. i know they are tired and over worked but something more needs to be done because if this is how we are screening patients for this virus that truly have all the symptoms no wonder people keep getting sick.

this is our 2nd baby born here and me and wife are 100% satisfied with the special care and comfort we get at reston hospital center. the staff are very kind, caring and attentive to your needs. even during this covid-19 pandemic, they make you feel at ease and safe. they have every kind of doctor on-hand at all times in case the baby needed any checkups. thank you staff, great job!

was taken to the er yesterday by ambulance following a minor accident. the staff was friendly, and the nurses were wonderful. dr amin was very professional and knowledgable, and answered all of my questions. an x-ray was taken and read immediately. for those concerned about covid, everyone was wearing masks, and the facility seemed very clean.

i have been an er patient here twice in the last 18 months (once for kidney stones and most recently for severe respiratory issues).  both times i was lucky enough to be treated by dr. aminah shahid.  she is a very thorough and kind physician with a patient bedside manner.  she gave me excellent care on both visits and explained everything in detail.  the nursing staff (notably rn anthony) are also kind, knowledgeable and hard working. 

very glad to have such a good hospital so close by.

stay away if you can, especially for pediatrics. my son was seen in the er for an infected bite and high fever. the er care was decent. the one star goes 100% to anesthesia services and interventional radiology (but i have friends in both departments so maybe we received better care than others might have) as well as the housekeeping staff. 
once he was admitted the quality and professionalism of the nursing care was negligent at best. nurses so unhappy they don't think twice about telling a scared mom how bad things are in the department. float nurse from the nursery whose hands were shaking as she flushed my child's iv, tells me, don't worry, i just don't do this much in the nursery. nurses fast pushing iv antibiotics that should be administered over several minutes. ignoring my concerns that his iv was infiltrated so that when i finally demanded another nurse to assess, his arm was black and blue and swollen twice the size. this same nurse telling me iv's aren't really "her thing, and it was flushing fine" (yeah, into  his arm not his vein) a nurse who read an initial blood culture report (without the md) and told me my son had mrsa, scaring us to death, unnecessarily. (turns out this wasn't true, it was too soon to tell, and it was a skin contaminate) 
i was ignored when i requested for transfer to inova. 
i had to request consults from infectious disease and surgery - these were not offered because they don't have pediatric specialists on site. turns out, they don't even have pediatricians. the hospital has 1 and they are staff the er room, so if "its really busy today" which i heard twice when they did not respond to my request for updates or nurses questions, you don't see them. all but one looked 20. 
i had to ask to speak to the unit nurse supervisor to request a certain nurse not continue caring for my child as she was horrible, just horrible. (made me feel bad asking for linen to give my son a bed bath. i provided 100% of his care, other than giving his meds, which i was happy to do, but c'mon.) gave antibiotics 4 hours late, told me his pulse ox (oxygen level) which was reading 85 after he returned from surgery was "probably just notreading right" but was fine once i requested a new piece (his had been on 3 days straight) 
i could go on and on, but really...unless you know your kids just has strep throat i would steer clear. 
kept waiting for my survey but since i never got one, i decided to post.

i'm a 79 year old cad elder patient with many fine experiences with staff at gulf coast and health park over the years. last october i missed my veteran nurses. they were  replaced by much younger staff. in er, they were training youngsters like mad. some knew their stuff. many did not. sad so many veterans have left or retired. please explain why this has happened? . 

two weeks ago had worst er experience ever. it was at gulf coast. arrived 9 pm with painful urination. 
they scoped my bladder and took blood twice in three tries. i still have the bruise from one failure. surprised they took no urine samples.  my wife and i were also shocked at sad conditions of rest rooms. at 3 am, a very young doctor finally showed. i asked her to look at my urine, please. she did and came back at 3:45 am with a uti diagnosis from urine sample. blood told them nothing.  i arrived home exhausted and disoriented. fell asleep in my bathtub. when i woke up, one hearing aid was missing. my wife found my wet, ruined cell phone in the kitchen.  i must have knocked it in the tub while asleep.

review: i am having surgery on wed.  i have had several surgeries at top hospitals.  the pre-surgical testing was the best i have ever experienced.  very friendly and courteous staff and they were organized.  had all my testing in one exam room besides the chest x ray.  i was in and out in an hour.  i have had surgeries at nslij, nyu in manhattan and winthrop.  this was by far the best pro op testing i have ever had.  i will update after my surgery on wed.

great hospital with wonderful doctors & nurses. especially the nurses. they were so nice & caring with me during my almost 2 week stay at the hospital. they always came in my room to check on me. such a lovely hospital with an appropriate name.

i went to sierra tuscon treatment center last year. it saved my life. was it perfect, i don't think any place can be perfect for all people. in the beginning i was very rude to most staff, i had meltdowns many times, but i felt safe. i got the right medication i need at this time in my life. everyone was very pleasant and nice, i might not have seen it at the time. i was unhappy about a lot of things but i can see now how much i needed to go through my emotions and self pity to start to heal. i learned to self advocate. i can't wish for a better place to be safe during my beginning of my healing.
with a step down program in california and a strong support at home i am having a normal functioning life.
i could wish for a better exit day than i had, but at the same time, it made me stronger, i learned i can handle things that comes up.
if i ever need a treatment center again, i would definitely choose sierra tuscon.
i went to sierra tucson for treatment. unfortunately they lost a bunch of my clothes and still haven't returned it. also, they didn't return my blow dryer and flat iron.

only day 2 but you should be aware that when you get there, you are put into a building with lots of people with different issues. you are strip searched and everything is taken away from you except your clothes.
